Result: A pool can be initialized at MIN_SQRT_PRICE, where the tick is MIN_TICK (Pool.sol:100-107, TickMath.sol:127). From that state every zeroForOne swap reverts, because the limit must be below the current price and above MIN_SQRT_PRICE (Pool.sol:323-330). oneForZero swaps and liquidity changes work, so nothing is locked. A swap cannot bring the price to MIN_SQRT_PRICE or MAX_SQRT_PRICE, because the step target is the nearer of the next tick price and the limit (SwapMath.sol:20-37) and the limit is strictly inside the bounds, so slot0.tick stays between MIN_TICK and MAX_TICK - 1 and the decrement at Pool.sol:431 never produces MIN_TICK - 1. About one third of the 28,000 fuzz sequences started within 2,000 ticks of an end, and the tick and price relation held after every operation. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:100-107, 322-359, 409-439; src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:20-37; src/libraries/TickMath.sol:121-129
- all 21 networks, cycle 1. Hidden characters, import targets and duplicate definitions in the files of this unit. Result: A byte scan of all 84 Solidity files under src found bytes outside printable ASCII and line feed only inside comments: the multiplication and division signs at FullMath.sol:8 and 104 and UnsafeMath.sol:18 and 23, and a dash character at Pool.sol:74. There is no carriage return, tab, bidirectional control or other line terminator that could end a comment early. Every import in the 18 files is a relative path inside src. The only import in non test source that leaves src is solmate Owned at ProtocolFees.sol:9. Each of the math libraries is defined once in the repository, and remappings.txt redirects only library prefixes outside src. Evidence: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:8; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:104; src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:18; src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:23; src/libraries/Pool.sol:74; src/ProtocolFees.sol:9; remappings.txt:1-6

## Established alternative L1s

- Polygon, cycle 1. Whether transient storage of the PoolManager (lock flag, deltas, synced currency and reserves) can leak from the last user transaction of a block into state sync calls that an attacker reaches through FxPortal. Result: Safe since the Austin fork at mainnet block 91949700. PrepareStateSyncContext calls StateDB.Prepare before every record, and Prepare replaces the transient storage map. Before Austin the reset was missing. Even then only a stale synced currency and reserves could survive, because unlock relocks at src/PoolManager.sol:113 and requires a zero delta count at src/PoolManager.sol:112. A stale sync credits only balance that arrives after it (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and no third-party token flow into the PoolManager happens between the last transaction and state sync. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.0/consensus/bor/statefull/processor.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 1. Whether Parlia system transactions run with transient storage left over from the previous transaction. Result: Safe. applyMessage calls state.Prepare for system messages once Cancun is active. System contracts do not call arbitrary contracts, so they would not reach the PoolManager in any case. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/consensus/parlia/parlia.go
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether PUSH0, TSTORE, TLOAD, MCOPY and SELFBALANCE exist on each chain (A10). Result: Safe. An eth_call contract creation that runs all five opcodes returned 32 bytes on each chain. Evidence: rpc eth_call with data 0x5f5f5d5f5c5060205f5f5e475f5260205ff3 on the three RPC URLs in networks.json, 2026-11-22
- Polygon, cycle 1. Whether one POL can be credited twice, once as address(0) and once as the 0x1010 token (A3 siphon). Result: Safe. settle rejects msg.value while a non-native currency is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356). sync(address(0)) clears the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283), and a later sync(0x1010) records the balance that already includes the native payment. The PoolManager has no receive function, and an eth_call that sends 1 wei with empty calldata reverts. A take of native POL between sync(0x1010) and settle makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-365
- Polygon, cycle 1. Whether PIP-88 storage repricing together with the transaction gas cap can make a swap or a liquidity removal impossible to include (A9). Result: Safe. Cold SLOAD costs 5460 gas, and the per transaction cap is 2^25 gas, twice the Ethereum cap. A swap stops at the caller's price limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so large swaps can be split. modifyLiquidity touches a bounded number of slots. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.0/params/protocol_params.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 1. Whether the BEP-652 transaction gas cap or the BEP-703 payment lane can block PoolManager operations (A9). Result: Safe. The cap is 2^24 gas, equal to Ethereum since EIP-7825. The payment lane withholds at most 10% of an 80 million gas block from general transactions. Evidence: https://github.com/bnb-chain/BEPs/blob/master/BEPs/BEP-652.md
- Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether charging max(gasUsed, gasLimit / 2) and counting gas limits toward block size can freeze liquidity (A9). Result: Safe. It raises the cost of over-estimated gas limits. The block gas limit is 80,000,000 and no opcode price changed. Whether a per transaction cap below the block limit exists was not confirmed. Evidence: https://docs.avax.network/docs/primary-network/exchange-integration
- Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether an atomic import that credits AVAX to the PoolManager address outside the EVM gives anyone a delta (A2, A3). Result: Safe. Native payments are credited from msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). A balance increase that arrives without a call is credited to nobody and cannot be taken. An export needs a signature from the debited address, which a contract cannot produce. The export signature rule was not read in source. Evidence: https://docs.avax.network/docs/primary-network/coreth-architecture
- Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether any caller can have msg.sender equal to address(0), the value of protocolFeeController on Avalanche, and so pass the checks at src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and src/ProtocolFees.sol:48. Result: Safe as far as documented. The C-Chain accepts only signed legacy, EIP-2930 and EIP-1559 transactions, and atomic transactions do not run EVM code. No system call with a zero caller is documented. The new VM source was not read, so this rests on documentation. Evidence: https://docs.avax.network/docs/primary-network/exchange-integration
- Polygon, cycle 1. Whether the PIP-74 StateSyncTx, whose from field is the zero address, can call contracts with msg.sender zero. Result: Safe. PIP-74 states the transaction executes no EVM code and changes no state. State sync calls use the system address 0xffff…fffe as caller. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maticnetwork/Polygon-Improvement-Proposals/main/PIPs/PIP-74.md
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 1. Whether permissionless fee collection through the fee adapter while the PoolManager is unlocked lets a caller gain funds. collectProtocolFees has no lock check in this code (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57), and _isUnlocked declared at src/ProtocolFees.sol:60 is never called there. Result: No gain found. The recipient is the adapter's token jar. The amount is bounded by protocolFeesAccrued through a checked subtraction (src/ProtocolFees.sol:55). The synced currency guard at src/ProtocolFees.sol:49 blocks collection of an ERC-20 between sync and settle. Native settle uses msg.value, so a falling native balance does not change credit. On Polygon, collecting native fees while 0x1010 is synced only makes the caller's own settle revert at src/PoolManager.sol:360. Fees accrue at swap time (src/PoolManager.sol:238) and the swapper must still settle before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Passed to the code units as a lead for a second reading. Evidence: src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 1. Whether the CAS20 Asset multiplier rebases balanceOf at the PoolManager (A2). Result: Safe by specification. BEP-702 section 3.12 says balanceOf returns the raw unscaled balance and the multiplier changes only the scaled view functions. To be re-checked against the client after Jenner. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/BEPs/master/BEPs/BEP-702.md
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether EIP-7702 changes A7 on these chains compared with Ethereum. Result: No new hazard. Polygon and BNB Smart Chain have the same set-code transactions as Ethereum. Avalanche rejects them. A delegated account used as a hook gives its owner the same power as an upgradeable proxy hook, and permissions still come from the address bits (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:337-339). Evidence: https://docs.avax.network/docs/primary-network/exchange-integration
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 1. Whether the hardcoded NanoBlackList can freeze the PoolManager today. Result: Not today. The list holds three addresses and the PoolManager is not among them. The check applies only to the top-level sender and recipient of a transaction, so calls that reach the PoolManager through a router would still execute. Adding an address needs a client release adopted by validators. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/types/blacklist.go
- Polygon, Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether Circle USDC treats the PoolManager differently on these chains than on Ethereum (A6). Result: Same control as on Ethereum. isBlacklisted(PoolManager) returned false on Polygon USDC 0x3c49…3359 and Avalanche USDC 0xB97E…8a6E. A blocklist entry would freeze every USDC pool, as it would on Ethereum. Evidence: rpc eth_call isBlacklisted(address) on both USDC contracts via the RPC URLs in networks.json, 2026-11-22
- Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether the native asset precompiles at 0x0100…01 and 0x0100…02 can move AVAX or give AVAX a second token face. Result: Safe. Coreth v0.10.0 deprecated Native Asset Call and Native Asset Balance, and they concerned non-AVAX native tokens. Evidence: https://github.com/ava-labs/coreth/blob/master/RELEASES.md
- BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 1. Whether BNB or AVAX has an ERC-20 alias at a system address like POL has on Polygon. Result: None found. The BSC system contract list has no token wrapper of the native balance, and WBNB and WAVAX are ordinary contracts with their own balances. The Avalanche precompile list was taken from documentation and release notes, not from client source. Evidence: https://github.com/bnb-chain/bsc-genesis-contract/blob/master/contracts/System.sol
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 2. P1, native take to a special address: does any precompile, system contract, burn or fee address, bridge contract or wrapped native token accept value with empty calldata from the PoolManager and leave the caller owing less than what left. Result: No. take debits the caller the full amount before the call (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). Value is accepted by: on Polygon the three burn contracts, the coinbase contract, WPOL, the precompiles 0x01 to 0x08 and 0x0100 and the empty address 0x0a; on BNB Smart Chain ValidatorSet 0x1000, SystemReward 0x1002, TokenHub 0x1004, RelayerIncentivize 0x1005, Staking 0x2001, Timelock 0x2006, WBNB and the precompiles 0x01 to 0x08 and 0x0100; on Avalanche WAVAX, the precompiles 0x01 to 0x08 and 0x0100 and the empty addresses 0x0b to 0x11. None of them returns value to the PoolManager, which has no receive function. Polygon 0x1000, 0x1001 and 0x1010, the BNB Smart Chain precompiles 0x64 to 0x69 and the Avalanche blackhole, native asset and Warp addresses revert, so a take to them fails as a whole. Evidence: rpc https://polygon.drpc.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 97768181 to 97768920 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 135095182 to 135097639 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 101077659 to 101078834 on 2026-11-22
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 2. P1 into the wrapped native token: sync(WPOL, WBNB or WAVAX), take native to the wrapper, settle, in every order, to see whether the wrapped tokens that the wrapper credits to the PoolManager can be claimed for less than their value. Result: Zero sum. A simulation on Polygon and on BNB Smart Chain shows the wrapper crediting the PoolManager with exactly the value sent. If the caller synced the wrapper first, settle credits that amount of wrapped currency to the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360) and the native debit of the same amount from take remains (src/PoolManager.sol:294). The caller must pay it with msg.value before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Without a prior sync the wrapped tokens stay in the PoolManager as an unaccounted surplus and the caller still owes the native amount. The PoolManager cannot be made to call withdraw, so the reverse direction does not exist. Evidence: rpc eth_simulateV1 on https://polygon.drpc.org (block 97768920) and https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (block 135097639), two calls from the PoolManager: 1e18 value to the wrapper, then balanceOf(PoolManager)
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 2. P2, token take on a special address: does any swept address answer transfer(address,uint256) from the PoolManager with nothing or a 32 byte true while moving value that pools hold. Result: No. Only WPOL, WBNB and WAVAX return true, and they are ordinary pooled tokens whose take is debited in full. Addresses that return empty data (the zero address, 0x01, 0x0100, Polygon 0x0a and 0x1002, Avalanche 0x0b to 0x11, the system address 0xffff...fffe, the not yet active Jenner addresses) move nothing, and the caller is left with a debt in a currency whose balanceOf call cannot be decoded, so it cannot be settled and the unlock reverts for a nonzero amount (src/PoolManager.sol:112). 0x02 and 0x03 return a hash and 0x04 echoes the calldata, which fails the success test at src/types/Currency.sol:68. Polygon 0x1010 returns false for every nonzero amount. Evidence: rpc https://polygon.drpc.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 97768181 to 97768920 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 135095182 to 135097639 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 101077659 to 101078834 on 2026-11-22
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 2. P3, sync on a special address: does any swept address answer balanceOf(PoolManager) with a number that an outsider can raise between sync and settle without paying it in. Result: No. 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 return a constant derived from the calldata, so settle credits zero. StakeCredit 0x2003 and GovToken 0x2005 on BNB Smart Chain return zero and their tokens cannot be transferred to the PoolManager by a third party. Polygon 0x1010 returns the native balance, which rises only through a forced transfer that the sender pays. The wrapped native tokens return real balances. Every other address reverts or returns data too short to decode, which makes sync revert (src/PoolManager.sol:285). Evidence: rpc https://polygon.drpc.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 97768181 to 97768920 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 135095182 to 135097639 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 101077659 to 101078834 on 2026-11-22
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 2. P5, hook calls to special addresses: does any swept address accept an IHooks selector from the PoolManager and return at least 32 bytes that start with the same selector. Result: Only the identity precompile 0x04 echoes the selector, and its address has the afterSwapReturnDelta bit without the afterSwap bit, which isValidHookAddress rejects (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:111-112). The special addresses whose low 14 bits form a valid combination are Polygon 0x1000 and 0x1010, BNB Smart Chain 0x64, 0x70, 0x1000, 0x2000 and 0x3000, the P256 precompile 0x0100 and the address 0x10 on all three chains, WPOL, and a few addresses without code. Each of them reverts or returns fewer than 32 bytes, so callHook reverts with InvalidHookResponse (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154). A pool created with such a hook address fails on the flagged operations for good, for example every liquidity removal with hook 0x0100. That is the hook finding of cycle 1 with actor pool-creator and needs a victim who joins such a pool. Evidence: rpc https://polygon.drpc.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 97768181 to 97768920 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 135095182 to 135097639 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 101077659 to 101078834 on 2026-11-22
- Polygon, cycle 2. Faces of POL: sync, settle, settleFor, take, mint, burn and fee collection across address(0) and 0x1010 in every order, with the call results of this cycle's sweep. Result: No order credits more than what entered. A native credit is always msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). A 0x1010 credit is the rise of the native balance between sync(0x1010) and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). In that window msg.value is refused (src/PoolManager.sol:356), sync(address(0)) clears the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283) and a new sync(0x1010) reads the balance again, so only a forced transfer raises the balance, and a native take or fee collection lowers it. A 0x1010 credit can never leave: transfer returns false for any nonzero amount without value and the PoolManager always calls with zero value (src/types/Currency.sol:73). take(0x1010, to, 0) succeeds, records no delta (src/PoolManager.sol:369) and only makes 0x1010 emit events. The contract has no approve, transferFrom or permit entry, and its deposit and withdraw paths send POL with a 2300 gas transfer that the PoolManager cannot receive. Evidence: rpc https://polygon.drpc.org, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, blocks 97768181 to 97768920 on 2026-11-22
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 2. Whether Jenner gives BNB an ERC-20 face through CAS20 or another reserved address (critic lead from cycle 1). Result: Not in the client source. The CAS20 token dispatcher keeps balances in the token's own storage and has no entry that reads or moves an account's BNB balance. Every CAS20 entry point reverts when value is attached. The factory, policy registry and activation registry are the only other routed addresses. The millisecond timestamp precompile at 0x70 was found in the precompile table only. Its source file was not located, so its answers to transfer and balanceOf calldata are open. To be re-run on chain after 2026-12-08. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20.go
- Avalanche, cycle 2. Whether the storage slot alias of the C-Chain (bit 248 cleared) lets anyone make two slots of the PoolManager collide. Result: No. The fixed slots 0 to 6 have a zero first byte. All other slots are keccak256 outputs or such an output plus an offset below 7 (src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:324-326, src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:66-73, src/ERC6909.sol:15-19). A collision needs two hashes that agree in 255 bits. extsload exposes the alias for reads only (src/Extsload.sol:10-15). The transient slots are not rewritten. Hooks and tokens with hand-picked slots are covered by the finding of this cycle. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go
- Avalanche, cycle 2. Where the Continuous Execution engine discards transient storage between two transactions of one block, and whether end of block operations run contract code (critic lead and unit lead from cycle 1). Result: saexec.Execute opens a new state database for each block and applies each transaction with core.ApplyTransaction. libevm's TransitionDb calls StateDB.Prepare for every message (core/state_transition.go line 436) and Prepare assigns a new transient storage map (core/state/statedb.go line 1335). End of block operations are balance and nonce writes (hook.Op.ApplyTo). FinishExecutingBlock moves non-AVAX asset balances. Neither makes an EVM call. A stale sync therefore cannot survive into another transaction. The public endpoint has no eth_simulateV1, so this rests on the source at tag v1.15.3 and the pinned libevm commit. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/saexec/execution.go
- Avalanche, cycle 2. Whether any execution path on the C-Chain gives msg.sender the zero address, which is the stored protocolFeeController there (src/ProtocolFees.sol:36, src/ProtocolFees.sol:48). Result: None in the engine source. The only call that is not a signed transaction is the EIP-4788 system call, whose caller is 0xffff...fffe and whose target has no code on the C-Chain. Cross-chain transactions never run contract code. A signed transaction needs a signature that recovers to its sender. This replaces the documentation-only basis of the cycle 1 item. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/saexec/execution.go
- Avalanche, cycle 2. Whether a cross-chain export can debit the PoolManager, and whether an import that credits it gives anyone a delta. Result: An export input must carry a signature whose recovered address equals the debited address (verifyCredentials), which no one can produce for a contract. An import adds AVAX to the named address with AddBalance and runs no code, so the PoolManager balance rises and nobody is credited, because native credit is msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/tx/export.go
- Polygon, cycle 2. Whether the protocol-level balance credits of Bor (base fee to the burn contract, tip to the coinbase) can reach the PoolManager balance between sync(0x1010) and settle. Result: No. Both credits go to addresses fixed in the chain config (params/config.go, BurntContract and Coinbase maps) and are applied after the transaction's execution ends (core/state_transition.go lines 634 to 644). The PoolManager is neither address. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.0/core/state_transition.go
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 2. Whether transient storage of one user transaction is visible to the next under the client source read this cycle. Result: No. Bor calls StateDB.Prepare at core/state_transition.go line 550 and resets the map at core/state/statedb.go line 3051. BSC calls it at core/state_transition.go line 623 and resets at core/state/statedb.go line 1532. Bor state sync records get the same reset through PrepareStateSyncContext since Austin, and Parlia system messages through applyMessage. This agrees with the two transaction simulation the critic ran on both endpoints in cycle 1. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.0/core/state_transition.go
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 2. Opcode differential for the call patterns of the PoolManager: CALL with and without value, the copy of return data into memory, calls to addresses without code, TLOAD and TSTORE, in the three clients. Result: The bodies of opCall, EVM.Call, opTload and opTstore in Bor v2.11.0, BSC master and libevm d398bc4dbe41 follow the go-ethereum pattern. A call to an address without code that is no precompile returns success with empty data, and return data shorter than the output area leaves the rest of the area untouched, which is what the success test at src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 expects. BSC adds a branch that skips the value transfer when the caller is the system address and a prefix route to CAS20 native code after Jenner. Avalanche adds the precompile override hook and the storage slot rewrite. MCOPY, PUSH0, SELFBALANCE and gas forwarding were not re-read in source and rest on the cycle 1 probes. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/instructions.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 2. Known weakness: the validator counting flaw in the light client precompile 0x67 fixed by BEP-682 in Pasteur, and the staking and governance fixes of BEP-695. Result: They concern the BNB Chain bridge and validator administration. The PoolManager never calls 0x67, and a call from it with any tested calldata reverts. A forged bridge message would affect bridged BNB supply and token issuers, which is outside what an ordinary account can turn against pool funds directly. Evidence: https://www.bnbchain.org/en/blog/pasteur-hardfork-arrives-on-bsc-mainnet-on-august-25
- Polygon, cycle 2. Known weaknesses disclosed for Bor in 2026: the Austin fixes (unbounded state sync gas, unbounded TxDependency field) and the Uburu and v2.11.x security releases. Result: The disclosed Austin issues are denial of service paths in block processing that a block producer or a sender of many bridge events could use. They delay all transactions and do not change PoolManager state. The v2.11.0 and v2.11.1 notes list state sync fetching, span lookup, witness and header checks. None changes how a transaction executes against a contract. The notes give no detail on what Uburu changed inside the StateReceiver, which stays an open lead from cycle 1. Evidence: https://forum.polygon.technology/t/security-releases-review-bor-v2-10-0-austin-hf-and-heimdall-v0-11-0-kyoto-hf/22138
- Avalanche, cycle 2. Known weaknesses around Helicon: the gas floor of ACP-194 and the worst-case balance bounds. Result: The floor charges a sender at least half of the gas limit and closes a queue flooding path. The bounds decide whether a transaction may be included. Both act on the fee payer of a transaction. The PoolManager never pays gas, and a revert inside a transaction still rolls back all PoolManager state, transient storage included. Evidence: https://docs.avax.network/docs/acps/194-continuous-execution
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 5. Lead L-209 and L-332: do the special addresses answer the PoolManager differently when it is an inner frame with another transaction origin? A 69 byte forwarding stub was placed at the PoolManager address by state override and called by 0x00000000000000000000000000000000c0ffee01. Sixteen shapes per target: empty calldata with 1 wei and with zero value, transfer of 0 and of 1, balanceOf(PoolManager) under STATICCALL, the ten IHooks selectors and unlockCallback. 55 targets on Polygon, 75 on BNB Smart Chain, 56 on Avalanche. Each shape was also sent as a top level call with from set to the PoolManager at the same block. Result: No difference on any of the three chains. The stub and the direct call gave the same success flag and the same return data for every shape and target. The only mismatches are artefacts: the PoolManager address itself holds the stub in the stub run. No target returns 32 bytes that start with a hook selector, so none passes the response test at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154. A 32 byte true comes back only from token contracts (the wrapped native tokens, and 0x1010 for amount zero). Success with empty data comes from accounts without code and from precompiles that return nothing for this input, which is the known case where take debits the caller and moves nothing (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). Value calls succeed at accounts without code, at several precompiles, at the wrapped native tokens and at contracts with a receive function such as the routers, the PositionManager, the EntryPoints and the burn and fee contracts. The caller of take is debited the full amount in each case (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Evidence: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, block 97807369; rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (Geth v1.8.2), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 135226007 and 135226327; rpc https://avalanche-c-chain-rpc.publicnode.com (avalanchego 1.15.3), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, block 101141646
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Lead L-261 and L-332: which entry points of the Jenner native code can an account without a role call, can any of them change another holder's balance, can transfer succeed without lowering the caller's balance, and does any CAS20 address report the native BNB balance? Read of cas20.go, cas20_token.go, cas20_admin.go, cas20_asset.go, cas20_stablecoin.go, cas20_permit.go, cas20_memo.go, cas20_factory.go, cas20_policy.go, cas20_activation.go, cas20_errors.go, cas20_storage.go and contracts_stateful.go on master, plus calls on Chapel. Result: An account without a role can call the views, approve, transfer, transferFrom, permit and the memo variants of a token, the read functions of the registries and, once the feature is activated, createCAS20, createPolicy and createCompositePolicy. transfer and transferFrom debit the named source by the amount and credit the recipient, and transferFrom needs an allowance of the source. mint, burn, seizeWithMemo, pause, updatePolicy, updateSupplyCap and the multiplier setters each need a role. The factory runs its init calls with elevated rights, and those calls act only on the storage of the token being created, whose address must hold no code. transfer returns success only after the debit, except for a zero amount and for a transfer to self. Every successful transfer returns a 32 byte true and never empty data. balanceOf reads the token ledger and returns 0 for an address that holds only BNB. No CAS20 file reads or writes a native balance or calls a contract, and every entry point reverts when value is attached. The millisecond timestamp precompile 0x70 ignores its input and returns one 32 byte word that is constant within a block. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20_token.go and the sibling files named in the check; rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Upcoming fork: what changes for the PoolManager on 2026-12-08 at the addresses that Jenner turns into native code, and can any pool, claim or fee already exist under those addresses? Compared mainnet answers before the fork with Chapel answers after it. Result: Before the fork the CAS20 range, the three singleton addresses, 0x2007 and 0x70 answer every call with success and empty data. A take that names one of them as currency succeeds, moves nothing and debits the caller (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). sync reverts for them, because the balanceOf call returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94), so no credit, no liquidity and no claim can exist under these ids today. After the fork the singleton addresses, 0x2007 and uncreated token addresses of variant 0 and 1 revert on every shape, so take and sync both revert. 0x70 answers balanceOf and transfer with the millisecond timestamp: sync succeeds, settle credits zero because the word is constant within a block (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and take reverts because the word is not 1. As a hook address 0x70 has the flags afterSwap, beforeDonate and afterDonate, and its answer fails the selector test at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154 before and after the fork. The fork therefore changes no balance and no claim of the deployed PoolManager. Evidence: rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (Geth v1.8.2), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, block 135226007; rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/BEPs/master/BEPs/BEP-706.md
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Lead L-241: does Jenner add a system call or a transaction type that runs user-chosen code with caller 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe and non-zero value, and does the probe of finding F-058 still return the same words?. Result: No. core/state_processor.go has the same three calls from the system address as before, each with zero value and a fixed target. Parlia sends its system messages from the block coinbase. The CAS20 code makes no call. ResolveLaneState for the payment lane runs before the block EVM is created and receives only the state database (the package paymentlanemeta that it calls was not read). The probe returned CALLVALUE 7 with no balance moved on Chapel at block 144,360,370, where Jenner is active, and on mainnet at block 135,226,408. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/state_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/consensus/parlia/parlia.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/payment_lane.go; rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Lead L-157: where does the opcode fusion feature of pull 3395 live, and does the deployed PoolManager give the same results with and without it?. Result: The feature no longer exists in the client. v1.8.0-alpha removed the superinstruction interpreter, the fused opcodes and their jump table entries (pull 3759), and v1.8.2 is mandatory before 2026-12-08. A differential test of 420 Quoter simulations through the deployed PoolManager at block 135,226,597 gave 409 identical answers on Geth v1.8.2, Geth v1.7.8 and reth-bsc, and the other 11 were rate limited on the v1.7.8 endpoint and identical on the other two. Whether the v1.7.8 endpoint runs with the optimisation switched on could not be confirmed, and the v1.7 source was not read. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/CHANGELOG.md; rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, https://bsc.blockrazor.xyz and https://bsc-rpc.publicnode.com at block 135226597
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Lead L-214 and L-124 for BNB Smart Chain: can a CAS20 transfer return true while the amount goes to another account or to a guard, and does any CAS20 address expose the native balance?. Result: No on both counts. move checks the sender policy and the receiver policy and reverts with PolicyForbids when either fails. On success it writes exactly two balance slots, the source and the named recipient. There is no escrow, no pending credit and no recovery account. Chapel confirmed the revert for a token with a sender policy and the exact credit for 12 tokens. No CAS20 code touches a BNB balance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20_token.go lines 239 to 269; rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23
- Polygon, cycle 5. Faces on Polygon: walk of sync, settle, take, mint, burn and protocol fee collection across the two EURe addresses and across address(0) and 0x1010, in every order, for an ordinary caller. Result: No order credits one payment twice or pays out more than was credited. sync holds one currency and one reserve figure at a time (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). settle credits only the rise of the synced currency's balance since that sync (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and a native settle is refused while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356). take debits the id it names before it transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). A take or a fee collection of the other face between sync and settle lowers the measured rise and costs the settling caller. mint and burn act on separate claim ids (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336). A standing surplus cannot be claimed, because sync always starts from the current balance. The hazards that remain are the issuer hazard recorded for EURe and the dead credit recorded for 0x1010. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-365; rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 97808115 to 97808450
- Polygon, cycle 5. Can an ordinary account move the PoolManager's EURe through the forwarding functions of the two EURe addresses?. Result: No. transfer_withCaller, transferFrom_withCaller and approve_withCaller revert at the V2 address when an ordinary account calls them. At the V1 address the same calls fall into a fallback that returns success with no data and changes no balance and no allowance. transferFrom reverts at both addresses for a spender without allowance, and the PoolManager never grants an allowance. setController reverts at both addresses for an ordinary caller. Evidence: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, block 97808450
- Polygon, Avalanche, cycle 5. Is any other balance of the PoolManager reachable under two currency ids? Full list of pooled currencies from all Initialize logs (7,456 on Polygon, 2,242 on Avalanche), balanceOf(PoolManager) for each, grouping by identical non-zero balance, a simulated transfer of one base unit for every member of every group, and a bit partition group test that moves half of the balance of 170 most pooled tokens per chain and reads all 170 balances. Result: Polygon: the EURe pair is the only shared balance, and 0x1010 is the only currency that equals the native balance. Avalanche: none. Two addresses that share a ledger one to one show equal balances for every holder, so the grouping covers all such pairs among currencies with a non-zero PoolManager balance. Faces in different units are covered only for the 170 most pooled tokens per chain, because the endpoints cap return data at 100,000 bytes. Evidence: rpc https://polygon.gateway.tenderly.co eth_getLogs; https://api.routescan.io/v2/network/mainnet/evm/43114/etherscan/api; rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 97808010 to 97808355; rpc https://avalanche-c-chain-rpc.publicnode.com (avalanchego 1.15.3), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 101142789 to 101143228
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Faces on BNB Smart Chain: sample of 1,364 currencies from the 2,985 pools initialized in blocks 134,978,682 to 135,228,681, with the same balance grouping, one unit transfers for 172 members of 41 groups, and the group test on the 170 most pooled tokens. Result: No shared balance and no address that reports the native BNB balance. One token balance rose when another token was moved, which is a reward style inflow and is recorded as a lead. The sample covers about 31 hours of pool creation. Older pools were not listed, because public endpoints do not serve older logs. - Avalanche, cycle 5. Lead L-159: do the PositionManager, Permit2, the Universal Routers or any hook on Avalanche hold two constant storage slots that differ only in bit 248?. Result: No. All PUSH32 constants were extracted from the runtime code of 11 periphery contracts (652 constants) and of 282 hooks with code plus one ERC-1967 implementation (4,766 constants), the hooks being every hook address named in the 5,779 Initialize logs. No contract holds two constants that are equal after the lowest bit of the first byte is cleared. Slots that a contract computes at run time by arithmetic on a constant are not covered by this test. Evidence: https://api.routescan.io/v2/network/mainnet/evm/43114/etherscan/api (Initialize logs); rpc https://avalanche-c-chain-rpc.publicnode.com (avalanchego 1.15.3), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, eth_getCode and eth_getStorageAt at the latest block
- Polygon, cycle 5. Upcoming fork on Polygon: does the dormant Hampi fork or any scheduled Bor fork change what the PoolManager bytecode computes?. Result: No. Hampi has no activation block and its single gate changes only whether SSTORE reads committed state before an out of gas exit. Gas charged, results and state roots stay the same according to the pull request and its tests. Bor master and develop define no fork after Uburu. A fork distributed privately, as Uburu was, could not be reviewed in advance. Evidence: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/pull/2361; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/params/config.go
- Avalanche, cycle 5. Upcoming fork on Avalanche: does Igloo or ACP-209 change what an ordinary account can make the PoolManager do in the next six months?. Result: Nothing is scheduled. IglooTime is unscheduled on Mainnet and Fuji, and its public scope is the move of L1 chains to the Continuous Execution engine. ACP-209 is Proposed without an implementation. If it ships as written, delegated accounts become possible as hooks (the case of finding F-004), and any account could deposit AVAX into the reserved balance of the PoolManager, which contract code cannot see or spend. Neither changes settle, which credits msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/master/upgrade/upgrade.go; https://github.com/avalanche-foundation/ACPs/blob/main/ACPs/209-eip7702-style-account-abstraction/README.md
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Upcoming fork: does the BEP-703 payment lane move balances, pay fees in tokens or change how PoolManager transactions are priced?. Result: No. The lane is one inequality on gas totals per block. It reserves 5 percent of the block gas limit by default, at most 10 percent, for bare BNB transfers to accounts without code and for transactions to contracts that governance lists. A PoolManager transaction is a general transaction and competes for the remaining 90 to 95 percent of an 80,000,000 gas block. The transaction cap of 16,777,216 gas is unchanged, and the largest Quoter simulation of this cycle used 11,518,424 gas. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/BEPs/master/BEPs/BEP-703.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/paymentlane/paymentlane.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Can a CAS20 balanceOf call that runs short of gas return zero, so that sync records a false zero reserve and settle credits the whole balance?. Result: No. A storage read that cannot be paid returns a zero word inside the native code and sets a sticky out of gas flag. finishCAS20Metered checks that flag before it returns data and ends the call with ErrOutOfGas, which the EVM reports as a failed call. The high level balanceOf call at src/types/Currency.sol:94 then reverts. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20_storage.go lines 124 to 146 and cas20_errors.go lines 55 to 63
- Polygon, cycle 5. Pools on Polygon whose currency has no code: can anything be deposited or credited under 0x455e53cbb86018ac2b8092fdcd39d8444affc3f6 (two pools) or 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead (one pool)?. Result: No. sync reverts for both addresses on the deployed PoolManager because balanceOf returns no data, so settle can never credit these ids, liquidity cannot be paid for, and no claim can be minted against a positive delta. A take of a non-zero amount would leave a debt that cannot be settled and the unlock reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Evidence: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call sync(address) on 0x67366782805870060151383f4bbff9dab53e5cd6 and eth_getCode, block 97808450
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 8. Exits: can an ordinary account make another user's liquidity removal or claim redemption impossible to include on these networks through gas caps, storage prices or the cost of tick crossings. Result: No. Removal runs Pool.modifyLiquidity, which has no loop and touches two ticks, at most two bitmap words, one position and the pool liquidity (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236). Its gas does not grow with the number of initialized ticks or positions. Under the Polygon storage prices of PIP-88 (cold read 5460, cold write surcharge 2940) the dozen cold slots of a removal add an estimated 40,000 gas to the 85,099 to 130,613 gas that the repository snapshots record for a removal (snapshots/PoolManagerTest.json:10-15). The caps are 16,777,216 gas on BNB Smart Chain, 33,554,432 on Polygon and the block limit of 80,000,000 on Avalanche. burn and take have no loop either (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 331-336). The swap loop is the only part of core whose gas an outsider can raise, and that is filed as a finding of this cycle with effect degrade. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/params/protocol_params.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/params/protocol_params.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/worstcase/state.go ; src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 8. Exits: special recipients. Can an outsider make the native payout of another user's take revert, or does any of the three chains refuse value transfers from the PoolManager to particular recipients. Result: No. The recipient of a take is chosen by the caller, and the native payout forwards all gas (src/types/Currency.sol:48). The earlier sweeps list the addresses that refuse value (system contracts that revert on empty calldata, the Polygon token contract 0x1010, the deprecated C-Chain precompiles), and a user reaches them only by naming them. The BNB Smart Chain client skips the value transfer only when the caller of the frame is the system address (core/vm/evm.go lines 291 to 347 at tag v1.8.2), which the PoolManager never is. The hard coded address filter of BNB Smart Chain applies to the sender and recipient of the top level transaction only, as cycle 1 recorded. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/evm.go ; src/types/Currency.sol:44-52
- Polygon, cycle 8. Known weakness and by design behaviour: the StateReceiver installed by Uburu lets any account replay a failed state sync. Can an ordinary account use the replay paths to make 0x1001 or FxChild call the PoolManager or its owner contract with data of its choice. Result: No. A replay must match the stored hash of receiver and data, or a leaf under the historic Merkle root, so the caller chooses only the time (StateReceiver.sol lines 85 to 133). The call is onStateReceive(uint256,bytes), which the PoolManager does not implement: an eth_call from 0x1001 to the PoolManager with that selector reverts with empty data. FxChild forwards to processMessageFromRoot on a receiver named in the record, and the PoolManager owner 0x8a1b966ac46f42275860f905dbc75efbfdc12374 reverts unless the caller is FxChild and the sender is the Ethereum timelock 0x1a9c8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be35bc. Any Ethereum account can send a record through FxRoot, and FxRoot writes that account as the sender. Of the 25 failed records pending since Uburu, 23 are for FxChild, and none has the timelock as sender or the owner contract as receiver. The 67 historic leaves that have not been replayed were not enumerated and are a lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/genesis-contracts/master/contracts/StateReceiver.sol ; rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call, rpc https://mainnet.gateway.tenderly.co eth_getLogs, 2026-11-23; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/polygon_statesync_since_uburu.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/polygon_owner_proxy_auth.json
- Polygon, cycle 8. Known weaknesses of Bor disclosed in 2026 that earlier cycles did not judge: the four issues of v2.5.9 (handshake panic, header panic, state sync pagination, truncated block number checks) and the BlockSTM items of v2.10.3. Result: None gives an ordinary account a lever on PoolManager funds. The two panics and the two BlockSTM items stop or slow nodes. The pagination gap made nodes reject each other's blocks. The block number issue let an authorised producer present a block number far above the parent's, which matters to contracts that read block.number. The PoolManager bytecode has no NUMBER, TIMESTAMP or BLOCKHASH opcode (assumption A10) and its accounting closes inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The v2.10.3 post states that execution results are unchanged by its fixes, and the serial and parallel processors must agree on every block. Evidence: https://forum.polygon.technology/t/bor-security-bug-fix-v2-5-9-review-post/21765 ; https://forum.polygon.technology/t/bor-security-bug-fix-review-v2-10-3/22379
- Polygon, cycle 8. Known weakness: the 2021 fault in transferWithSig of the native token contract 0x1010, which moved POL without a balance check. Is the function live, and could it move the PoolManager's native balance. Result: The function is disabled. A call reverts with the string Disabled feature. A signature transfer debits the recovered signer, and no signature recovers to a contract address, so the PoolManager balance could not be the source even if the function were live. The mirror of the native balance at 0x1010 stays as finding F-008 describes. Evidence: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call to 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 with selector 0x19d27d9c, 2026-11-23; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/special_probe.json
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Known weakness: the superinstruction interpreter of BNB Smart Chain v1.7.x let SSTORE run inside a STATICCALL frame (pull request 3582). Does any accounting step of the PoolManager rely on the write protection of STATICCALL. Result: No. The PoolManager makes one kind of static call, balanceOf on a currency, in sync and in _settle (src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/PoolManager.sol:285 and 359). A token that could write or re-enter during that call would gain nothing over calling the PoolManager before or after it: sync stores the currency and the returned balance after the call (src/PoolManager.sol:285-286), and _settle reads the stored reserves before the call, credits only the currency it read at line 350 and then clears the slot (lines 358-364). In both places the returned number is already chosen by the token. A token that is not written by the attacker does not re-enter. The pull request describes the outcome as wrong gas use and a bad block on nodes that ran the optimized interpreter, which was an opt-in flag. The changelog records that v1.8.0-alpha removed the interpreter, and v1.8.2 is mandatory before 2026-12-08. Evidence: https://github.com/bnb-chain/bsc/pull/3582 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/CHANGELOG.md ; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. The fork boundary of Jenner on 2026-12-08. Until then a transfer call to 0x70 or to a CAS20 address succeeds with empty data. Can an account create a debt, a credit, a claim or pool liquidity in such a currency before the fork that becomes a claim on real tokens after it. Result: No. Before the fork take of such a currency succeeds and only debits the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). A positive delta in it can come only from settle, which needs sync, and sync reverts because balanceOf returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94). mint adds a debt of the same size as the claim (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329). Pool operations move deltas between the caller, the hook and the pool and add to zero, so no unlock can close while any party owes the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Nothing denominated in the currency can therefore exist in storage when the fork arrives, except pools with zero liquidity. After the fork an uncreated CAS20 address reverts on every call, as cycle 5 saw on Chapel, and a created token is an issuer matter (F-007, F-076). Evidence: rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org eth_getCode and eth_call at block 135,334,992; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/special_probe.json ; https://www.bnbchain.org/en/blog/jenner-hardfork-changes-upgrade-guide
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Lead L-331: do PIT, ASS, CATE and GFH charge the PoolManager more than the amount when it transfers them. Result: No. Eight simulated transfers per token set (one thousandth and one third of the balance, to a fresh address and to 0xdead) at block 135,335,118 all returned a 32 byte true. For ASS, PIT and CATE the PoolManager balance fell by slightly less than the amount, because the fee is taken from what the recipient receives and part of it is reflected to holders, the PoolManager among them. For GFH it fell by exactly the amount. take debits the caller the requested amount (src/PoolManager.sol:294), so a payout leaves the PoolManager whole or a few thousand base units ahead. Evidence: rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (Geth v1.8.2) eth_call with Multicall3 code at the PoolManager address, 2026-11-23; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/l331_fee_tokens.json
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Lead L-160, reflection tokens: can a caller profit by putting its own transfer of a reflection token between sync and settle, so that the reflected fee on the PoolManager balance is credited to it. Result: No. settle credits the rise of the PoolManager balance since sync (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). A transfer of one third of the PoolManager's PIT balance (168,336,790 PIT) paid a fee of about 6,733,000 PIT and raised the PoolManager balance by 0.0113 PIT. For ASS the same test paid about 1,604,000 ASS and raised it by 0.0026 ASS. The caller pays the whole fee and can be credited only the PoolManager's share of it, which is about two parts in a billion. Reflection that accrued before the sync is already inside the stored reserves and is credited to nobody. - Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 8. Lead L-303, second half: is the transfer limit plugin of ViciCoin used by another pooled token on Polygon, and does it exist on the other two chains. Result: No. Every one of the 7,428 logs of the plugin 0xf58fed40fba1ab7aa7ffc160b863bedd998386a7 on Polygon names VCNT in an indexed topic, so the contract serves that one token. The plugin address and the VCNT address hold no code on BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche. Another issuer of the same framework would deploy its own plugin, which this check cannot see. - Avalanche, cycle 8. Open question of the cycle 6 and cycle 7 critics: does the C-Chain accept set code transactions, so that an account can carry a delegation and act as a hook or as a caller with code. Result: No. The code that decides block validity under Continuous Execution validates each transaction with an accept mask of legacy, access list and dynamic fee types (worstcase/state.go lines 181 to 193) and rejects a sender that holds code (lines 202 to 209). The CLZ opcode of Osaka is undefined on the public endpoint, which matches a rule set without the later Ethereum forks. Code at a hook address on the C-Chain can therefore change only through a contract's own upgrade path, as on Ethereum before EIP-7702 (assumption A7, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:337-339). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/worstcase/state.go ; rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc eth_call with data 0x60011e5f5260205ff3, 2026-11-23
- Avalanche, cycle 8. By design behaviour of Continuous Execution: consensus accepts a block before it is executed, includes a transaction when the sender can pay its worst case cost, and treats an execution error as fatal. Does any of this break the atomic settlement that unlock relies on, or let state reach the PoolManager outside a transaction. Result: No. Execution still applies transactions one by one with core.ApplyTransaction, in block order, each on the state left by the one before (saexec/execution.go lines 346 to 364), and cycle 2 showed that each call resets transient storage. A transaction that reverts is still included and charged, and all PoolManager state it wrote is rolled back with it. The fatal branch concerns a transaction that is invalid at execution time, which the worst case check exists to exclude. It would stop the chain for everyone and gives no account PoolManager funds. Whether an ordinary account can reach that branch is filed as a low lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/saexec/execution.go ; https://docs.avax.network/docs/nodes/architecture/execution/continuous-execution
- Avalanche, cycle 8. Can a cross-chain import write into the storage of the PoolManager account. The C-Chain keeps balances of other X-Chain assets inside the storage trie of the holder. Result: No. At tip an import whose inputs or outputs carry an asset other than AVAX is rejected (cchain/tx/import.go lines 112 to 129). Asset balances live under slot indexes with the lowest bit of the first byte set, and contract code can only reach slot indexes with that bit cleared (cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go lines 45 to 62 and 124 to 171). An AVAX import raises the native balance, which cycle 2 cleared. - BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Known weaknesses of the BNB Smart Chain clients in the Jenner release line that earlier cycles did not judge: the reth-bsc state root fault fixed in v0.1.4-hotfix, the per byte pricing of precompile 0x68, and the BEP-706 sample code that accepts an empty answer from 0x70. Result: None reaches PoolManager funds through an ordinary account. The state root fault decides which blocks a reth-bsc node accepts. The pricing change concerns a precompile that the PoolManager never calls and that reverts on its call shapes, as the earlier sweeps showed. The empty answer of 0x70 before activation affects contracts that read the timestamp from it. The PoolManager reaches 0x70 only when a caller names it as currency or hook: sync reverts on the empty answer before the fork and stores a timestamp that is constant inside a block after it, so settle credits zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). Evidence: https://github.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/releases ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/CHANGELOG.md ; https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/bnb-chain-sets-jenner-date-post-flags-timestamp-risk

- Polygon, cycle 9. Whether the optional switch dispatch interpreter of Bor v2.11.x, which a validator can enable with evm-switch-dispatch, computes a different result for any opcode the PoolManager uses. Result: No. The file was read in full. Every inlined opcode takes its operands in the jump table order and calls the same uint256 method, the stack checks are the same, JUMP and JUMPI check the jump destination before moving the program counter, and JUMPI tests the whole condition word. SAR with a shift of exactly 256 reaches SRsh, which returns zero for a non-negative value and all ones for a negative value, as specified. Constant gas of the inlined opcodes is charged before the next opcode that can have an effect, so the GAS opcode and every call see the same remaining gas. The setting is off by default. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/vm/interpreter_dispatch.go and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/internal/cli/server/config.go

Result: No. core/vm, the state code, the chain config, the protocol parameters and the parallel state processor are byte identical at the two tags. The release changes peering, fork ID handling and a sequence store producer path, and moves to Go 1.26.11. Evidence: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/releases/tag/v2.11.2 and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/vm/instructions.go

An ordinary account cannot be the beneficiary. - BNB Smart Chain, cycle 9. The BNB Smart Chain rule that code cannot run at the block coinbase address (geth v1.8.2 core/vm/interpreter.go lines 96 to 98, reth-bsc src/evm/api/mod.rs lines 235 to 270): can an ordinary account use it against the PoolManager. Result: No. The coinbase is the signing address of the validator that produced the block, so only a validator can choose it, and it has code only if the validator delegated its own key through EIP-7702. A hook or token at that address would fail in that validator's blocks, which hurts only pools that chose such a contract. A native take to an address without code is not affected, because the rule applies only when code runs. Recorded with actor operator. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/interpreter.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 9. Whether an ordinary account can place a contract at an address that becomes a CAS20 precompile at Jenner, so that the code of a hook or currency changes after pools are created (A7). Result: Not feasible. The prefix rule fixes 0xca52 and eight zero bytes and limits byte 10 to two values, about 81 fixed bits, so a CREATE2 search for such an address needs about 2^80 hashes. Before Jenner these addresses hold no code, so sync and settle of such a currency revert in balanceOf and no account can be credited in it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix/src/evm/precompiles/cas20/mod.rs and rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org eth_getCode, 2026-11-24
- Avalanche, cycle 9. What the PoolManager does when an ordinary caller names an Avalanche precompile address after Helicon (P1 and P2). Result: The three native asset addresses run DeprecatedContract and revert, warp rejects a call without a valid selector, and P256 at 0x100 returns empty data and moves nothing. A take to the native asset addresses therefore reverts, and a take naming 0x100 as currency succeeds with empty data and debits the caller the full amount, as for any address without code. No call moves value that the caller does not owe. Evidence: https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/graft/coreth/@v/v1.15.3.zip and rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc eth_call from the PoolManager address, 2026-11-24

- Polygon, cycle 12. Does the MULMOD memo of bor v2.12.0-beta give the stock result for every input, including FullMath's modulus 2^256-1, destination equal to modulus, and state carried between calls, frames and transactions of one EVM. Result: Yes as read. The memo compares all four limbs of the modulus before reuse and recomputes Reciprocal(z) on a miss (core/vm/mulmod_memo.go lines 55-66). MulModWithReciprocal and MulMod in uint256 v1.3.2 run the same umul and the same reduce4 call (uint256.go lines 688-748), reduce4 only reads the reciprocal (mod.go lines 334-381), and opMulmod aliases destination and modulus in the same way in both versions (instructions.go line 202 at v2.11.1 and v2.12.0-beta). Moduli with a zero top limb and a zero modulus take the stock call. Each parallel incarnation constructs its own EVM (core/parallel_state_processor.go lines 132 and 628), so the unsynchronised memo is not shared between goroutines. The ruint 1.21.0 fault class (OPCODES.md) does not apply: bor uses holiman/uint256. Result: No as read. Keys are string(data) over the whole input, so inputs of different length or content never share an entry; Load builds a non-retained string view, Store copies the input and stores the hash by value with LoadOrStore, and a full cache stops inserting rather than evicting (core/vm/shared_cache.go lines 162-241). The 64 byte legacy path is unchanged from v2.11.1, which cycle 11 cleared. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/shared_cache.go

Can the ecrecover result cache of bor v2.11.1 be poisoned through an eth_call or eth_simulateV1 that overrides the precompile at 0x01, a hole that v2.12.0-beta closes with precompilesOverridden. Result: Not on the import path of v2.11.1: the shared ecrecover, keccak and jump destination caches are created per block in newSharedBlockCaches and applied only to the import prefetcher and the parallel workers (core/blockchain.go lines 1268-1289); the RPC path creates no shared cache. Result: BSC adds a process-wide LRU of jump destination bitmaps keyed by code hash (core/vm/contract.go lines 27-30, used in isCode lines 99-112), which every EVM of the process shares, including the prefetch workers. Each EVM runs on one StateDB copy in one goroutine (core/state_prefetcher.go lines 71-121), and Call takes the code and its hash from that StateDB with no execution in between (evm.go lines 355-363 and resolveCode / resolveCodeHash at lines 700-724). The account's code hash is the hash of the stored code, so every bitmap is stored under the hash of the bytes it was computed from. Init code is analysed under the zero hash and never stored (evm.go line 631). Pooled Contract objects clear the cached analysis on reuse (contract_pool.go line 36). There is no separate code hash key for the analysis, so a jump table always belongs to the bytes it travels with. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-bytecode/revm-bytecode-10.0.0.crate

- Polygon, cycle 15. Do bor v2.11.2 and the unreleased develop branch change the interpreter, the integer library or state handling compared with the builds already tested?. Result: 17 core/vm and core/state files are byte-identical between v2.11.1 and v2.11.2. develop is identical to v2.12.0-beta in 14 core/vm files and in parallel_statedb.go, blockchain.go and worker.go. Every tag and branch pins holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. The opcode handlers call SDiv, SMod, Exp, AddMod and MulMod with the result aliasing the last operand (instructions.go lines 60, 74, 81, 196 and 202). The library writes the result only after the computation, so the aliasing is harmless. The only correctness fix in a recent release, v1.3.1's DivMod aliasing fix, is a function the interpreter does not call. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/vm/instructions.go
- Polygon, cycle 15. Lead L-750: the cache that --precompile-cache adds in bor v2.12.0-beta. What is its key, and can a STATICCALL from sync(X) get a cached result for a different input or a different precompile?. Result: The flag adds the extended keccak store, keyed by string(data) (shared_cache.go lines 160-245), and gives the builder and the serial importer the ecrecover cache. The ecrecover cache serves only address 0x01 with input of at most 128 bytes. Its key is the input right-padded to 128 bytes, which is the padding ecrecover applies anyway. It is skipped when the precompile set is overridden. Gas is charged from RequiredGas on a hit, and the stored and returned slices are clones (evm.go lines 53-116). No other precompile is cached. A sync(0x01) gets the same bytes as an uncached call, and balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) parses them the same way. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/evm.go
- Polygon, cycle 15. Can an ordinary account use Salvador, which gives five accounts code at block 98,688,600, against other users' funds in the PoolManager?. Result: No. The targets hold no ERC-6909 claims in the six largest currency ids and no PositionManager NFT. A pool that names one of them as hook or currency already fails on every flagged call while the address has no code, and afterwards it reverts. The same holds for a native take to such an address, which only fails the caller's own action (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). The sweeper moves only the native balance of its own address. Evidence: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/pull/2546
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 15. Does BSC master, the branch that ships Jenner, change opcodes, jump analysis, memory or state relative to v1.8.2? The develop interpreter differs only by the Pasteur gate on the coinbase rule. - Avalanche, cycle 15. Does the libevm pin of avalanchego master (a335c2ecf4df) or uint256 v1.2.4 change an opcode result for the PoolManager?. Result: Of 22 core/vm and core/state files compared between the two libevm commits, only the precompile environment file changes, and it drops the raw caller and self addresses. In uint256 v1.2.4, Mod, MulMod, AddMod and SMod compute into locals and assign z last (uint256.go lines 198-235, 590-760). The AddMod fast path subtracts m at most once, which is enough because x[3] <= m[3] implies x < 2m. The vectors above confirm this on the live node. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.2.4/uint256.go

- Polygon, cycle 17. Leads L-032 and L-161 on the releases after v2.11.1: does any change to BlockSTM, its serial fallback or the merge of results let transient storage pass from one transaction to the next. Result: No. The executor, state database, journal, transient storage and state transition files are byte identical in v2.11.1, v2.11.2 and v2.12.0-beta, and the parallel state processor differs only in one error message. Cycle 11's reading therefore holds for every Polygon build that is released or proposed: each incarnation starts from a fresh state copy, Prepare installs a new transient map, and transient storage is not in the multi-version write set that the merge copies. The PoolManager's lock, deltas and synced currency (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) cannot leak across transactions on any of these builds. Upcoming forks angle: assume every upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships (BSC Jenner on 2026-12-08, Polygon Salvador at block 98,688,600 and bor v2.12.0 with the MULMOD memo and the widened keccak cache, Avalanche Igloo if it is scheduled). - Polygon, cycle 21. Does the MULMOD reciprocal memo of the coming bor release change any mulmod result used by FullMath.mulDiv, mulDivRoundingUp or SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 48, 112; src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252)?. Result: No. The memo takes the memo path only for a modulus with a nonzero top limb, compares the full modulus by value before reuse, and calls MulModWithReciprocal, which in uint256 v1.3.2 runs the same reduce4 on the same product as MulMod with a freshly computed reciprocal. Moduli below 2^192, including 2^128 and 2^96 used through mulDiv, take the unchanged stock call. The memo is not in v2.11.1, which both endpoints run. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/core/vm/mulmod_memo.go and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.3.2/uint256.go lines 688-748

- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 24. Whether a public account can cause a reorganisation or profit from one against a PoolManager user, including replay of a settled or taken transaction in another order (lead L-1046). Result: A reorganisation needs block producers on all three networks: bor producers and Heimdall milestones, BSC validators with BEP-126 votes, Avalanche validators under Snowman. A re-included transaction keeps its signature and nonce and runs once. Its unlock is atomic (PoolManager.sol:104-114), so a take without a matching settle reverts whatever the order. A different order can change the price a swap gets, which is the ordinary ordering risk that slippage limits in routers handle. Only the owner or fee controller can change the protocol fee, and only a pool's own hook can change its dynamic fee, so a replay cannot pay more than the pool's state at that position gives. Evidence: https://github.com/bnb-chain/BEPs/blob/master/BEPs/BEP126.md

Storage and transient storage are revm's maps keyed by address and full U256 slot. The Hertz fix is a table of fixed historical mainnet transaction hashes whose slots are written before or after those transactions on import only (src/node/evm/patch/mod.rs:16-708, executor.rs:818-822, 931); it has no shared storage read path, and no patched address is the PoolManager. - Polygon, cycle 34. Transient storage lifetime and slot read order in bor v2.11.2 ParallelStateDB, the BlockSTM V2 worker state, read as source. Result: Each transaction gets a new transient store in Prepare (parallel_statedb.go:1277-1279) and a recycled worker clears it (line 272), so the unlock flag at src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25 and the deltas at src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39 cannot pass from one transaction to the next in a parallel block. Persistent reads take the worker's own write first, then the highest lower writer in the MVStore unless a later SuicidePath write wiped the account, then base state, and every answer is recorded for validation (lines 332-349, 597-620, 967-1034); validateOne re-executes a transaction whose read set went stale (v2_executor.go:629-660). A parallel result that differed from serial order would also give another state root than the serial importers, which is a fork and not a silent change of pool state. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/state/parallel_statedb.go, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/blockstm/v2_executor.go

## Ethereum mainnet reference and cross-chain deployment parity

- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether ERC-4337 bundles or EIP-7702 batches, which run several users' operations in one transaction, can leak an unlock flag, a delta or a stale sync from one operation into another and move funds. Result: unlock clears the flag before returning and reverts unless every delta is zero, so the flag and the deltas never outlive the unlock that created them. Only the synced currency and reserves can survive. A later operation's own sync overwrites them and any ERC-20 settle resets the currency, and a credit is only ever the balance increase since the most recent sync, so a stale sync cannot capture another user's payment. The remaining effects are reverts, recorded in the info finding. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288, 349-364; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/ERCs/master/ERCS/erc-4337.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the native asset has a second, ERC-20 face on mainnet, and whether an attacker-deployed token that mirrors ETH or another token's balance can be credited for funds it did not pay. Result: ETH has no enshrined ERC-20 form; the PoolManager's ETH balance (54,377.2) and WETH balance (576.35) are independent. A mirror token only earns a delta in its own currency id, because _settle credits the synced currency. msg.value is rejected while an ERC-20 is synced, so an ETH payment cannot be read as a balance increase of a mirror token. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-364; on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26470360 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether ETH forced into the PoolManager by SELFDESTRUCT, a beacon withdrawal or a fee recipient setting can be claimed or can break accounting. Result: Native credit is msg.value only and the contract balance is never read for native settlement. Forced ETH becomes an unclaimable surplus. No receive or fallback function appears in the contracts read under src; settle and settleFor are the only payable functions. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-283, 353-354; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-4895.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-6780.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether a token reachable at two addresses, such as USDT after deprecate() forwards the old address to a new contract, lets one payment be credited twice or lets one currency id drain the other's backing. Result: There is one sync slot. Each credit equals a real balance increase observed between one sync and the next settle with no other sync in between, and each take or fee collection sends at most the amount it debits. Summed over both currency ids, credits minus debits equals the real balance change, so the shared balance always covers both sets of claims. Collection of the alias while the other address is synced can only lower the settler's credit or revert. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, 349-364; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7?fields=sources,compilation
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the USDT transfer fee switch, if turned on, makes the PoolManager pay out more than it debits or credit more than it receives. Result: take debits the full amount and USDT removes exactly that amount from the sender, with the fee taken from what the recipient gets. settle credits the measured balance increase. The PoolManager stays whole; payers must send more to cover the fee. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 358-360; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7?fields=sources,compilation (lines 122 to 135, 425 to 434)
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the 16,777,216 gas cap per transaction (EIP-7825) or the 60,000,000 block gas limit can make liquidity removal or a necessary swap impossible to include. Result: modifyLiquidity touches two ticks, one position and the bitmap, so its cost is constant. Pool.swap stops at sqrtPriceLimitX96, so any swap can be split across transactions. By my estimate from EIP-2929 costs and the repository gas snapshots, one transaction still crosses several hundred initialized ticks or about 3,000 empty bitmap words. Crossing the full empty range of a pool with tick spacing 1 (6,932 words) no longer fits in one transaction but can be done in steps by anyone. I did not measure these numbers on chain. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238, 344-437; snapshots/TickBitmapTest.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7825.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether a precompile or system contract address used as a pool currency can produce a settle credit or a silent transfer. Result: I sent the balanceOf and transfer calldata that the PoolManager would send, from the PoolManager address, to all 18 precompiles and the five system contracts with eth_call at block 26470418. SHA256, RIPEMD160 and identity return the same constant for balanceOf on every call, so paid is zero, and their transfer return value is not 1, so take reverts. ECRECOVER and P256VERIFY return empty data: balanceOf fails decoding and transfer succeeds while moving nothing, which costs only the caller. The other precompiles fail and the system contracts revert on both calls. No delta can be created without paying. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:60-75, 90-96; src/PoolManager.sol:358-360; on-chain eth_call via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26470418
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether any mainnet system contract or protocol operation can move ETH or tokens out of the PoolManager or change its code. Result: The five system contracts only record roots, hashes and validator requests, and withdrawals only add ETH. Nothing at protocol level debits an arbitrary account or rewrites contract code. Evidence: on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26470360 (2026-11-22) (eth_config, eth_getCode); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-4895.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether every opcode the cancun build needs exists on mainnet at the expected cost, and whether core depends on block or transaction globals that later forks changed. Result: Mainnet is past Dencun (CLZ from Osaka executes), so PUSH0, MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE are available. The Pectra and Fusaka EIP lists contain no repricing of an opcode that core uses. A search of src outside src/test finds no use of tx.origin, block fields, blockhash, selfdestruct, create or delegatecall.
