- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether an EOA that delegates to the PoolManager's code through EIP-7702 can reach the real PoolManager's funds or pass as it. Result: Delegated code runs with the EOA's own storage and balance. initialize, modifyLiquidity, swap and donate revert there because address(this) differs from the immutable original. The other functions act only on the EOA's own state and tokens. The real contract's storage and balances are untouched. - Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether a currency or hook contract can lose its code on mainnet, and what take, sync and hook calls do at an address with no code. Result: After EIP-6780 a contract keeps its code unless it self-destructs in its creation transaction, so only EIP-7702 accounts can lose code later. A take of a codeless currency debits the caller and moves nothing, which harms only the caller. balanceOf on a codeless address returns no data and the Solidity decoder is expected to revert, so sync fails and no credit arises; I did not execute this. A codeless hook makes hook calls revert, covered in the EIP-7702 finding. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:60-75, 94; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-6780.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the math and bit libraries are numerically self-consistent as written: TickMath constants and both directions, BitMath lookup tables, FullMath.mulDiv, LiquidityMath.addDelta, SwapMath.getSqrtPriceTarget, BalanceDelta packing, tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick, and the four transient slot constants. Result: A Python model of the code as written matched exact integer arithmetic on 300,000 random mulDiv cases, all bit positions and 200,000 random words for BitMath, about 70,000 ticks and 60,000 prices for TickMath including both ends of the range, and 100,000 cases each for the helpers. The TickMath multipliers equal 2^128 divided by sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i) to within one unit. The slot constants equal keccak256 of their names minus one. This is a self-consistency check and uses no other copy of the code. Result: Mainnet has no protocol feature that reads a token balance for gas payment, staking or voting within a transaction; gas is paid in ETH only. take creates a negative delta that must be zero before unlock returns, so the tokens come back in the same transaction. - Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether msg.value can be counted twice in native settlement through batching inside the PoolManager. Result: The PoolManager has no multicall and performs no delegatecall, so each settle call sees its own msg.value once. settle and settleFor are the only payable functions. - Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the Glamsterdam changes scheduled so far alter how the existing bytecode executes: new opcodes, code size, ETH transfer logs and the state gas reservoir. Result: EIP-8024 keeps jump destination analysis unchanged and states that contracts which never execute the new opcode bytes are unaffected. EIP-7954 only raises size limits. EIP-7708 adds a log to value transfers. EIP-8037 forwards the state gas reservoir to child calls in full and leaves the 63/64 rule on ordinary gas; core forwards all gas to hooks and to native recipients and reverts as a whole if a callee burns it. EIP-8038 raises costs only, which is tracked as a lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8024.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7954.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7708.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8037.md; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134; src/types/Currency.sol:48
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether block ordering power, reorgs or finality delay on mainnet can split a settlement or let funds leave before payment is final. Result: Every delta must net to zero before unlock returns, inside one transaction, and a transaction is included or dropped as a whole. Core holds no cross-chain or delayed obligations. I did not fetch a source on finality time or reorg depth; the conclusion rests on the code alone. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Sweep of all 18 precompiles with the PoolManager as sender: empty calldata with zero value and with 1 ETH (P1), transfer(address,uint256) with zero and 1e18 (P2), balanceOf(PoolManager) (P3) and all ten IHooks selectors with well-formed arguments (P5). Follow-up on each target that did not revert. Result: No precompile yields a credit or an unpaid outflow. ECRECOVER and P256VERIFY return empty data: take succeeds and moves nothing while the caller is debited, and sync reverts because the Solidity decoder needs 32 bytes, so no credit can arise. SHA256, RIPEMD160 and IDENTITY return 32 bytes or more that depend only on the input, so the value read at sync equals the value read at settle and paid is zero; their answer to transfer is a digest or the echoed calldata, never the word 1, so take reverts. The other precompiles fail on the input lengths the PoolManager can produce. ETH sent to a precompile address with a native take stays there and the caller owes it. The sync results on the existing mainnet deployment (reverts for 0x01, 0x100 and an empty address, succeeds for 0x02, 0x03, 0x04) agree with this reading of the source; I used them as a behavioural reference and did not compare code. Same 15 call shapes against the beacon roots, history storage, deposit, withdrawal request and consolidation request contracts, and whether the PoolManager can be made to file a withdrawal or consolidation request. - Ethereum, cycle 2. Whether any special address on mainnet can serve as a hook that the PoolManager accepts, so that a hook call has a lasting side effect made with the PoolManager as sender. Result: A hook call is kept only if the return data is at least 32 bytes and starts with the called selector. Of all swept targets only the identity precompile does that, and 0x04 fails the address check because it sets the after-swap returns-delta bit without the after-swap bit. - Ethereum, cycle 2. Native payout (P1) to contracts that book incoming ETH to the sender: WETH9, Lido stETH, frxETHMinter, EntryPoint v0.6, v0.7 and v0.8, the OptimismPortal of OP Mainnet and Base, and the TokenJar. The call was made by the PoolManager address with an unrelated transaction origin. Does the caller end up owing less than what left, with or without a sync and settle around the payout?. Result: take debits the caller the full amount of currency address(0) before the transfer. With sync(WETH9) before and settle after, the caller is credited exactly the 1e18 WETH that the PoolManager received for 1 ETH, so the PoolManager converts 1:1 and both legs are booked. For stETH the credit is 1 wei less than the debit. In every case the value is booked to the PoolManager and the caller owes the full native amount. Without the sync bracket the received tokens are an unbooked surplus. - Ethereum, cycle 2. Faces on mainnet: can one balance be reached under two currency ids so that a payment is credited twice or one id drains the other. Checked ETH against WETH9, tokens with two entry points (the PoolManager holds 258.6 TUSD and 4,089 SNX), and a ledger credited by a value transfer (EntryPoint). Result: ETH and WETH9 are separate balances. There is one sync slot, each sync overwrites both transient values, and a credit is the measured rise since the latest sync, so one transfer in is credited once under one id. Each take sends at most what it debits under the id named. Over all ids that share a balance, credits minus debits equal the real change. A native payment cannot be counted under an ERC-20 id because settle rejects msg.value while an ERC-20 is synced, settle and settleFor are the only payable functions, and sync(address(0)) followed by a later sync re-reads the balance. I did not call the second entry point of TUSD or SNX on chain. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-307, 349-364; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32; on-chain eth_call via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26471525 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Opcode and call semantics the PoolManager relies on, read in the Osaka execution specification: transient storage lifetime and rollback, value transfer order, static context, return data after failed calls, gas forwarding and precompile dispatch. Result: Transient storage is created per transaction and rolled back with the frame, value moves before callee code runs and is undone on failure, a failed or underfunded call returns 0 with empty return data, and the callee receives at most 63/64 of the gas. The source handles each case by reverting: a failed native or token transfer reverts with a wrapped error, a failed hook call reverts, and a failed balanceOf reverts through the decoder. No path continues after a failed external call, so the gas rule can make an operation fail and cannot make it half succeed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/execution-specs/mainnet/src/ethereum/forks/osaka/vm/interpreter.py (lines 263 to 303); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/execution-specs/mainnet/src/ethereum/forks/osaka/fork.py (lines 622, 932); src/types/Currency.sol:48-53, 64-86; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Known weaknesses of mainnet execution clients, precompiles and system contracts from the last two years: could an ordinary account use any of them against funds in the PoolManager. Result: The incidents I found are liveness and consensus faults: the Reth state root stall of 2025-09-02, Nethermind nodes rejecting a canonical block at the Fusaka fork, and client fixes for MODEXP in Geth and P256VERIFY in Besu that the Fusaka retrospective lists. A node that stalls or rejects a block does not execute a different result for an included transaction, and settlement in core is atomic inside one transaction. The PoolManager calls a precompile only when a caller names one as currency, hook or recipient, and the sweep shows those calls give the caller nothing. I did not search vendor advisory databases one by one, and I did not find a published mainnet bug in TSTORE, TLOAD or CALL handling. Bridge contracts of the other networks on Ethereum as recipient of a native take or as currency or hook: the OptimismPortal of OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo and MegaETH, seven L1StandardBridge proxies and the OP L1CrossDomainMessenger, the Arbitrum Inbox, Bridge and gateway router, the Polygon RootChainManager, DepositManager and EtherPredicate, the Polygon zkEVM bridge, and the zkSync Era, Linea, Starknet and Scroll entry contracts. - Ethereum, cycle 8. Transaction types and execution contexts of Ethereum against unlock, sync, settle and take: types 0x0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x3 and 0x4, the system calls at block boundaries, withdrawals, and bundles inside one transaction. Who is msg.sender, what is msg.value and what does transient storage hold in each?. Result: Types 0x0, 0x1 and 0x2 differ in fee fields and access list only. Type 0x3 adds blob hashes that the PoolManager never reads and must name a recipient. Type 0x4 sets delegation designators before execution and then runs one ordinary top level call. In all five the sender is the signer, value is debited from the signer before the first frame, and the transaction has one transient map that is empty at the start. A delegated account can be the sender of unlock itself, and the walk with a designator placed by state override passed all four steps with tx.origin equal to msg.sender. A delegation that was set by a transaction which later reverted stays set, which changes code at an account and nothing inside the PoolManager. System calls use the system address as caller, a fixed target and their own transient map, and withdrawals credit balances without execution, as cycles 2 and 3 read in the specification. The census of 120 blocks found no sixth type. The remaining cross user effect is a sync left by an earlier call of the same transaction (F-071). Evidence: on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_getBlockByNumber for 120 blocks from 26,430,231 to 26,480,211; eth_call with state override); research/network-risk/cycles/008/ethereum-reference.work/raw_txtypes.json and walk7702.py; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114
- Ethereum, cycle 8. Critic gap of cycle 7: which Ethereum fork is scheduled, and does it add a transaction type with more than one frame? If the frame transaction of EIP-8141 were live, what would unlock, sync, settle and take see?. Result: Glamsterdam is next and has no mainnet date; its scheduled EIPs add no transaction type. EIP-8141 is scheduled for the fork after it and has no activation date on any network. Read against the draft text: frames are top level calls that run one after another, and transient storage is discarded between frames, so each frame meets a locked PoolManager with no synced currency, and the stale sync of F-071 cannot cross a frame. unlock opens and closes inside one frame (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Value enters only in SENDER frames, where it is debited from tx.sender as in a CALL. In DEFAULT frames msg.sender is 0xaa for every author, value is zero, and the only functions that act for 0xaa without an unlock are sync, initialize and the ERC-6909 transfer and approval functions. 0xaa is not a valid hook address, because it sets the after add liquidity returns delta bit without the after add liquidity bit (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:113-116), so updateDynamicLPFee cannot be reached with it. The draft may change before it ships, and I did not read a client implementation. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8141.md (lines 101 to 131 and 432 to 481); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8081.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7773.md
- Ethereum, cycle 8. The Hoodi activation of Glamsterdam was withdrawn because EIP-8037 breaks assumptions of deployed contracts. Does the source hold such an assumption: a fixed gas amount for a call, a gas check, or a path that must fit a gas figure?. Result: No. The three external call sites forward gas() (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), the unlock callback and balanceOf are plain high level calls, and a search of src outside src/test finds no gasleft and no numeric gas argument. Under the current text a new slot costs 97,920 state gas and a changed slot 10,000 gas, so opening a position at two fresh ticks, which writes between 5 and 11 new slots, costs between about 0.4 and 1.0 million gas more than today, and a tick crossing, which changes two fee growth slots, about 14,000 more. A swap can still be split by its price limit and a removal touches a fixed number of slots. A native take to an address that does not exist would cost 183,600 state gas more. These are costs for the caller and no path becomes unreachable. I did not measure the deployed contract under the new rules. Lead L-722 for geth: does the parallel executor driven by block-level access lists keep transient storage per transaction and the PoolManager's storage writes in transaction order?. Receipts and gas are gathered in block order (lines 239-266). - Ethereum, cycle 21. Lead L-820: reth's parallel executor for blocks with an access list. Does each transaction start with empty transient storage, and is the rebuilt access list checked against the header?. Result: Yes to both. A worker executes each transaction with execute_transaction_without_commit, which detaches the overlay through take_pending_state and calls clear_transaction_state, which clears transient_storage together with the journal, logs and warm sets (evm2 evm/tx.rs lines 240-249, evm/state/mod.rs lines 563-579); a nested transaction gets committed_copy with an empty transient map (lines 135-150). The canonical executor commits worker results in block order and builds the access list from that commit (reth bal/execute.rs lines 157-196), and validation.rs lines 113-131 reject the block when the rebuilt hash differs from the header's. So the unlock flag, deltas and synced currency in src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-26 and src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 cannot cross from one transaction to the next on this path. A builder that ships a false access list only gets its block rejected, which is an operator matter. - Ethereum, cycle 24. Lead L-1047: what an ordinary account can undo or reorder around another account's PoolManager transaction, using the entry points that need no unlock. Result: Ordering cannot move a credit. sync writes only transient slots of the current transaction (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:23-30, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), which EIP-1153 clears at the end of the transaction, so a sync in an inserted transaction is gone before the victim's starts. settle compares the balance with what the victim's own sync recorded inside its own transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so tokens sent to the PoolManager by another transaction before that sync are part of the recorded reserves and are credited to no one. ERC-6909 transfer and transferFrom move only the caller's claims or allowances given to it (src/ERC6909.sol:25-45). extsload and exttload are views. initialize only succeeds on a pool with no price (src/libraries/Pool.sol:101), so a front-run can choose the starting price of a pool nobody has created; modifyLiquidity takes no price bound (src/types/PoolOperation.sol:8-16), so a direct caller without a slippage check of its own would add at that price. That is the same on every network and is the job of the caller's router. Inside one block, a builder or searcher can sandwich swaps, which the swapper bounds with sqrtPriceLimitX96. Reorgs on mainnet are one block deep in the 2025 data (about 0.11 percent of slots) and blocks finalize about 18 minutes behind the head; a reorg drops or reorders whole transactions and cannot split one settlement. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-288; src/PoolManager.sol:349-364; https://ethresear.ch/t/post-pectra-effects-on-ethereum-reorg-rate-propagation-and-block-size/23018

The cache sits in each frame's CallContext and is reset when a frame starts (interpreter.go line 515). - Ethereum, cycle 31. The leading quotient digit test that Int256 1.15.0 added to Remainder512By256Bits and Remainder512By192Bits, the 4 limb remainder MULMOD reaches at SqrtPriceMath.sol:44-47. Result: Correct by argument and by test. The leading digit of the normalised division is zero exactly when floor(N / b^(uLen - 4)) < d; a top dividend limb below d3 gives that, and it also keeps the extra limb zero because d3 < 2^(64 - shift). The test is strict, unlike the <= of ruint 1.21.0. The transcription in scripts/neth_rem512.py, both arms, gave the exact remainder on 489,674 cases, 83,280 with the top limb at d3 - 1, d3 or d3 + 1, and without the test also on 39,130; the planted <= gave 586 mismatches, all in that edge shape. - Ethereum, cycle 31. Nethermind's fused PUSH2 with JUMP or JUMPI in untraced execution, against the unfused sequence, at 2.2.2 and 2.3.0-rc. Result: Same stack, gas, program counter and outcome as read. The fused path decodes the two byte destination big endian, charges 3, then 8 or 10, then 1 for the landed JUMPDEST, pops only the condition for JUMPI and tests all 32 bytes, validates the destination only when the jump is taken, and keeps the stack limit at 1,024 (MaxStackSize is 1,025 and the prelude rejects a head of 1,024 or more). Code is padded, so a truncated PUSH2 at the end reads zeros and is followed by STOP. Its only effect is that a trace runs the other path. Result: No. src never branches on gas: payouts and hook calls pass gas() (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), and under EIP-8037 the state gas reservoir passes whole to the child while gas() returns the execution gas left. modifyLiquidity writes a fixed set of slots (two ticks, up to two bitmap words, one position, the pool liquidity), about nine new slots for a fresh range, which costs about 0.9 million state gas outside the 16,777,216 execution cap and about 0.1 million execution gas for writes. A swap that crosses an initialized tick pays two STORAGE_WRITE of 10,000 instead of 2,800 for the fee growth outside words; by my estimate one transaction still crosses several hundred initialized ticks, and a longer swap can be split by price limit. A native take to a new account pays 183,600 state gas, which the caller's transaction pays. None of this moves value. ETH transfer logs (EIP-7708), the SELFDESTRUCT burn removal (EIP-8246) and the factory predeploy (EIP-7997) touch no PoolManager balance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8037.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8038.md (lines 43-53, 89-103); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7773.md (lines 20-41); src/libraries/Pool.sol:159-236; src/types/Currency.sol:44-80; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-136

Operands follow the PoolManager's shapes: moduli near 2^96 (MULMOD at FullMath.sol:48 and :112 for mulDiv by Q96, SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105, :250), 2^128 and its neighbours (Position.sol:94 and :96 by Q128), sqrt prices from 4295128739 to 1461446703485210103287273052203988822378723970342 as divisors (SqrtPriceMath.sol:47, :71, :208-209), up to 2^192 - 1, words shifted by 32 to 96 bits, plus hard cases built as q times d plus a small r with a divisor whose low limbs are near all ones. The rare branches ran: 65,504 KnuthStep add-back corrections, 508 saturated KnuthStep digits, 1,308 inline add-backs and 106,556 full multiply-subtract steps in Remainder512By192Bits, 364 and 494 add-backs in the two DivideBy192Bits digits, 374 second qhat corrections and 12,328 zero low limb fast paths in DivideBy128BitsX86Base, and 86,490 skips of the zero leading digit. Two branches were never reached: the CorrectStep after a saturated KnuthStep digit and the add-back after a saturated digit in Remainder512By192Bits; both need a quotient digit two too high, which Knuth's bound allows only for unnormalised remainders the callers do not build. Planted faults: dropping the KnuthStep add-back gave 36,362 mismatches, testing the zero digit skip with <= gave 22, dropping the inline add-back gave 396, and dropping the second correction in DivideBy128BitsX86Base hit the hardware divide fault (the precondition assert). Dropping the second correction in the first DivideBy192Bits digit and the saturated add-back were not caught, since the single add-back covers the first and the second is unreached. Nethermind 2.3.0 final is not tagged; release/2.3.0 pins Int256 1.15.0, the version transcribed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NethermindEth/int256/v1.15.0/src/Nethermind.Int256/UInt256.divmod.cs (sha256 4703d1a5, lines 325-443, 1807-1860, 2003-2210, 2297-2508, 2774-2952, 3499-3707, 3900-4166, 4552-4572) ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NethermindEth/int256/v1.15.0/src/Nethermind.Int256/UInt256.lookups.cs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NethermindEth/int256/v1.15.0/src/Nethermind.Int256/UInt256.cs (Sub, lines 1736-1744) ; research/network-risk/cycles/033/ethereum-reference.work/scripts/neth_four.py, out/neth-four.json, out/neth-four-plant1.json to plant6

- Ethereum, cycle 33. Lead L-1245, second part: does reth itself start a transaction while another one is running, the path that evm2 7c9f3b6d's suspended_frames and enclosing_refund now handle?. Result: evm2 e80df9c4 treats a transaction as nested only when Evm::running is set, for example one started from an inspector hook (evm/mod.rs lines 1399-1420). In reth main, prewarm calls transact_and_discard and transact_with_inspector on the worker's own EVM (prewarm.rs lines 374 and 415), and its only inspector, BalanceTracker, implements step, call, call_end and create and starts no transaction (reuse.rs lines 1022-1080). RPC eth_call, simulate, callMany and access list creation call transact or transact_with_inspector at the top level (rpc-eth-api helpers/call.rs lines 244, 290, 405, 515). No caller read starts a transaction inside a running one, so the new path is not reached on an Ethereum reth node for block validation or RPC. The payload builder crate (crates/ethereum/payload/src/lib.rs) contains no direct transact call; its executor path was not read. Do the new rules of EIP-8037 change what call(gas(), ...) at src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134 hands the callee, or let a sub-call fail while the PoolManager call succeeds?. Result: EIP-8037 has GAS return gas_left only and applies 63/64 to gas_left only, with the whole state gas reservoir passed to the child. Measured on Sepolia reth, a child sees 16,497,333 of 16,762,214, the same 63/64 ratio as today. Every failed sub-call in src/ reverts the PoolManager call (src/types/Currency.sol:51 and :82, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, the unlock callback at src/PoolManager.sol:110), and src/ never reads gasleft, so a smaller budget or a refill that raises gas_left can only make the caller's own transaction fail or succeed as a whole. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8037.md
- Ethereum, cycle 39. Geth's eth_call on Sepolia gives up to 49,984,998 or 59,984,998 execution gas, above the 2^24 that EIP-8037 allows a mined transaction, while reth caps it. Result: A simulation on a Geth node can succeed where the mined transaction runs out of gas. In src/ that failure reverts the whole unlock, so the cost falls on the sender's own transaction and fee; no other user's balance or claim changes. Evidence: https://rpc.sepolia.ethpandaops.io eth_call, 2026-11-28
- Ethereum, cycle 39. Upcoming forks within six months, assumed shipped: Glamsterdam with the 20 EIPs of EIP-7773, checked against the live Sepolia deployment of those rules. Result: Cycle 37's clearance stands and is now backed by execution under the real rules: every opcode vector and every PoolManager script gives the mainnet words on Sepolia, the differences are gas only, and higher state costs (about 110,000 gas for a new slot with an empty reservoir) only raise what a swap, a position or a claim mint costs the caller. Funds already in the PoolManager are untouched by the fork, and the day after an ordinary account gains no path to them. Evidence: https://ethereum-sepolia-rpc.publicnode.com eth_config, 2026-11-28

## High-throughput chains with modified gas models

- Monad, cycle 1. A1: whether an unlock flag, a currency delta or a synced currency can survive from one Monad transaction into another, through optimistic parallel execution, a retried transaction, or a system transaction. Result: The client builds a new State for every execution attempt of every transaction, and transient storage is a field of the per-account state inside it. A retry discards the first State. System transactions get their own State and only run the staking syscall. The lock, delta, counter and reserve slots at src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32 and src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36 therefore start at zero in each transaction. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/ethereum/execute_transaction.cpp lines 454 and 480; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/ethereum/state3/account_state.hpp line 70; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/execute_system_transaction.cpp
- Monad, cycle 1. A3: whether Monad's reserve balance rule can block a native payout from the PoolManager, or revert a transaction because the PoolManager's MON balance fell below 10 MON. Result: The check skips every account whose code is not empty and not an EIP-7702 delegation ('Skip if not EOA'). The PoolManager has 24009 bytes of ordinary code, so its balance is never tested. A recipient's balance only rises in take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), which cannot count as a dip. The rule can still revert a user's own transaction when the user pays MON into settle (src/PoolManager.sol:300-302) from an account that ends below its threshold. That is a failed transaction for that user and moves no pool funds. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/reserve_balance.cpp lines 81 to 98 and 191 to 210; https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/reserve-balance.md
- Monad, cycle 1. A3: whether MON has an ERC-20 face, so that a pool on address(0) and a pool on a token could draw on one balance. Result: No. WMON is a 3249 byte contract with no proxy slot, and its totalSupply equals the MON it holds. balanceOf(PoolManager) on WMON is 927,086 while the PoolManager's native balance is 216,079,353. The staking and reserve precompiles revert on balanceOf and transfer. Native settlement uses msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354) and token settlement uses a balance difference (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and no Monad contract found here links the two. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22
- Monad, cycle 1. A4: whether a Monad precompile can serve as a currency whose balanceOf or transfer gives credit without payment, or as a hook that the PoolManager calls with effect. Result: The staking precompile (0x1000) and the reserve balance precompile (0x1001) reject STATICCALL, so sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) reverts at balanceOf for either address. Under CALL they revert on the transfer selector, so take reverts at src/types/Currency.sol:82-86. The staking precompile also reverts on afterInitialize and on empty calldata with value, so it cannot be a hook and cannot receive a native take. P256 at 0x0100 returns empty data to balanceOf, which fails ABI decoding. Hook calls carry zero value (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and a fixed selector, and the PoolManager has no stake or delegation that a staking call from it could move. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/monad_precompiles.cpp lines 43 to 49
- Monad, cycle 1. A10 and A3: whether the higher cold access costs (10100 per account, 8100 per storage page) break a payout or a hook call that relies on a fixed gas amount. Result: The PoolManager passes gas() on the native transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:48), on the ERC-20 transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73) and on hook calls (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). It never uses the 2300 stipend or a hard-coded gas value. Contracts around it that do are outside the PoolManager. Evidence: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/opcode-pricing.md
- Monad, cycle 1. A9: whether the 30 million per-transaction gas cap together with MIP-8 storage pricing can make a swap or a liquidity removal impossible to include. Result: A tick crossing reads one bitmap word and updates one tick record. Under MIP-8 that is one page load (8000), one page write (2800), small base charges and at most two new slots at 17000 each, so tens of thousands of gas per tick and several hundred ticks per transaction in the worst case. A swap stops at the caller's price limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344) and can continue in the next transaction. modifyLiquidity touches two ticks and one position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), which is constant work. The per-tick figure is computed from the documented schedule and was not measured on chain. Evidence: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/opcode-pricing.md; https://docs.monad.xyz/ai/current-facts.md
- Monad, cycle 1. Whether charging gas on the gas limit, or the reserve balance precompile, gives a hook or token a way to change PoolManager accounting. Result: Both act on the transaction sender's MON balance or report a read-only flag. Neither changes a token balance at the PoolManager, a delta or a storage slot. The deltas must still net to zero at src/PoolManager.sol:112. Evidence: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/gas-pricing.md; https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/precompiles.md
- Monad, MegaETH, cycle 1. A12: whether anyone can call the PoolManager as the zero address, which is the protocol fee controller on both networks, and what that caller could take. Result: No transaction type documented for either chain produces msg.sender zero. Monad system transactions come from 0x6f49a8F621353f12378d0046E7d7e4b9B249DC9e and must target the staking address. MegaETH system transactions come from the registry's system address and may only call the Oracle, pre-block calls come from 0xff...fe to fixed contracts, and a deposit carries its L1 sender. With no controller, setProtocolFee (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-41) cannot run, so protocol fees stay zero, and protocolFeesAccrued reads zero for the currencies checked. collectProtocolFees subtracts with overflow checks at src/ProtocolFees.sol:55, so a caller could not withdraw more than the accrued amount in any case. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/validate_system_transaction.cpp lines 53 to 65; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/system-contracts/system-tx.md; rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22
- MegaETH, cycle 1. A1: whether MegaETH has an execution context with its own transient storage that shares persistent state with a running PoolManager call. A second context would let a stale sync in one context be paid by a transfer made in the other. Result: The only nested context is the KeylessDeploy sandbox. It runs a separate EVM with its own journal over the parent state, and the node starts it only when the KeylessDeploy call is the top-level call of the transaction. A contract that calls it mid-transaction reaches bytecode that reverts with NotIntercepted. The outer transaction therefore has no PoolManager activity before or after the sandbox, and the sandbox itself is one ordinary context. Mini-blocks and EVM blocks do not split a transaction, and detention and resource counters reset per transaction. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/system-contracts/keyless-deploy.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/sandbox/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/sandbox/execution.rs
- MegaETH, cycle 1. A3 and A8: whether an OP Stack deposit can raise the PoolManager's native balance in a way that counts as payment, or let an L1 actor call as the PoolManager or as its owner. Result: A deposit mints ETH to its from account, never to the target. The PoolManager accepts value only in settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307), both of which require an unlocked manager, and it has no receive or fallback function. Native settlement credits msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), so ETH that reaches the balance another way, for example through SELFDESTRUCT, is credited to nobody. A contract sender on L1 is aliased by a fixed offset, and an externally owned sender keeps its address, so reaching the PoolManager address or the receiver address as sender needs control of that externally owned account or an L1 contract at the address minus the offset. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/deposits.html
- MegaETH, cycle 1. A3: whether ETH on MegaETH has an ERC-20 face, through the WETH predeploy or the LegacyERC20ETH address. Result: WETH at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 has ordinary code, empty proxy slots and totalSupply equal to the ETH it holds. Its balanceOf(PoolManager) is 0.0058 while the PoolManager's native balance is 2.2648 ETH. 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000 has no code. Evidence: rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22
- MegaETH, cycle 1. A4 and A7: whether a MegaETH system contract or OP Stack predeploy can be used as a hook, or made to act on a call the PoolManager issues. Result: The six system contract addresses end in 1 to 6, and each of those bit patterns fails isValidHookAddress (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:111-120). The calls the PoolManager can be made to issue are limited to hook selectors with zero value (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), transfer(to, amount) on a currency (src/types/Currency.sol:60-73), balanceOf(self) (src/types/Currency.sol:94), unlockCallback on the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:110) and a native transfer with empty calldata (src/types/Currency.sol:48). Each of the last two fund-moving calls creates a negative delta that the caller must repay before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112), so sending pool ETH to a predeploy such as L2ToL1MessagePasser costs the caller the same amount. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/system-contracts/overview.md; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22
- MegaETH, cycle 1. A7 and A9: whether the 98/100 forwarding rule, the per-frame resource budgets, the 200 million compute gas cap or the cap of 1,000 new state entries per transaction can trap funds in the PoolManager. Result: The PoolManager treats a failed hook or token call as a revert (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, src/types/Currency.sol:82-86), so a frame that runs out of any budget cannot leave partial state. A swap that crosses ticks for the first time writes up to two new slots per tick in crossTick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-612), so one transaction can cross a few hundred fresh ticks before the state growth cap. It can stop at a price limit and continue later (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344). Removing liquidity touches two ticks and one position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238). The per-block cap of the same size is left as a lead. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/gas-forwarding.md
- MegaETH, cycle 1. A7: whether code at a hook or token address on MegaETH can disappear after pool creation through SELFDESTRUCT. Result: SELFDESTRUCT follows EIP-6780 since Rex2 and was disabled before that. A contract loses code only in the transaction that created it. EIP-7702 delegation works as on Ethereum Prague and is the same risk class as an upgradeable hook. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/selfdestruct.md
- MegaETH, cycle 1. A9: whether the SALT bucket multiplier lets an attacker raise storage gas until a liquidity removal or a take cannot be paid for. Result: Storage gas applies to zero to nonzero writes and to account creation, at 20,000 or 25,000 times (multiplier minus 1). A removal writes at most a few such slots (position fee growth fields) and a take to a new address creates one account. The gas limit is 10,000,000,000 and the base fee read on chain is 0.001 gwei, so even a multiplier in the thousands leaves the exit affordable. How an attacker would grow a chosen bucket was not analysed, because the bound already clears the freeze question. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/overview-3/gas-model.md; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, queries at blocks 32548426 to 32549054 on 2026-11-22
- Monad, MegaETH, cycle 1. Whether a protocol address with hook flag bits and no hook interface (Monad 0x0100, OP Stack predeploys such as 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010) adds a hazard beyond what any address without code already gives. Result: No. For such an address the hook call either reverts or returns fewer than 32 bytes, and the PoolManager reverts at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 or src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154. That is the same result as a flagged address with no code on any chain. A pool created with such a hook address can lock the operations whose flags are set. The hook address is part of the pool identity, so a liquidity provider can read it before depositing. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, queries at blocks 124417992 to 124420045 on 2026-11-22
- Monad, cycle 2. Sweep of every Monad precompile and system address (0x01 to 0x11, 0x0100, 0x1000, 0x1001, the EIP-2935, EIP-4788, EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 addresses, SYSTEM_SENDER, 0xff...fe, the MIP-11 fee account and WMON) with calls from the PoolManager address: empty calldata with zero and nonzero value, transfer with amounts 0, 1 and 1e18, balanceOf(PoolManager), the ten IHooks selectors and unlockCallback. Result: No address gives credit without payment and none moves PoolManager value on a transfer call except WMON, which is an ordinary wrapper. 0x01 and 0x0100 return success with empty data, so a take of those ids debits the caller and moves nothing (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74), and sync reverts on the empty answer. 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 answer balanceOf with a constant, so settle after sync credits zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and they fail the transfer test because the first word is not 1. 0x1000 and 0x1001 revert on every shape and fail under STATICCALL. Addresses without code behave as on Ethereum. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance and eth_getStorageAt at blocks 124455000 to 124466634 on 2026-11-22
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Sweep of 0x01 to 0x11, 0x0100, all 256 addresses 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000000 to 00ff, 0x6342000000000000000000000000000000000001 to 0007, the EIP-2935 and EIP-4788 contracts, the EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 addresses, LegacyERC20ETH, the L1 attributes depositor, the system address and 0xff...fe with the same call shapes from the PoolManager address. Result: No address gives credit without payment. Only WETH returns success on transfer with a true word, and it is an ordinary wrapper. Seven predeploys accept a native payout (L2ToL1MessagePasser, four fee vaults, WETH and L1BlockNumber), and in each case the caller of take is debited the full amount at src/PoolManager.sol:294 before the transfer. The six MegaETH system contracts revert on all shapes, with NotIntercepted (0x1894f076) for MegaAccessControl and MegaLimitControl. The precompiles behave as on Ethereum. Evidence: rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager and with state overrides, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas and eth_getBlockByNumber at blocks 32558000 to 32563302 on 2026-11-22
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Whether the L1BlockNumber predeploy at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000013, which answers balanceOf(PoolManager) with a number that rises over time, can serve as a currency that yields credit. Result: No. The answer equals L1Block.number(), which changes only through the L1 attributes transaction at the start of a block. Inside one transaction sync and settle read the same value and the credit is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). Transient storage does not survive the transaction, so a sync from an earlier block cannot be used. A transfer call returns the same word, which is not 1, so take reverts at src/types/Currency.sol:68 and 82-86. Its low bits are 0x13, which isValidHookAddress rejects because bit 1 is set without bit 10 (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:113-116). Evidence: rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager and with state overrides, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas and eth_getBlockByNumber at blocks 32558000 to 32563302 on 2026-11-22
- MegaETH, cycle 2. What a native payout from the PoolManager does at each predeploy that accepts it, and whether the caller owes the full value: take(address(0), predeploy, amount) for L2ToL1MessagePasser, the four fee vaults, WETH, L1BlockNumber and L2StandardBridge. Result: The caller owes the full amount in every case, because take records the debit before the transfer and unlock reverts unless it is settled (src/PoolManager.sol:112, 294-295). L2ToL1MessagePasser keeps the ETH and registers a withdrawal whose sender and target are the PoolManager address, so the value is lost to the caller. The fee vaults and L1BlockNumber keep the ETH. WETH credits the PoolManager with the same amount of WETH. L2StandardBridge rejects the call when the PoolManager is called by another account. The op-stack-eth unit recorded the same self-inflicted loss as a low finding in this cycle, and chain 4326 can be added to it. Evidence: rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager and with state overrides, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas and eth_getBlockByNumber at blocks 32558000 to 32563302 on 2026-11-22
- Monad, MegaETH, cycle 2. Faces of the native asset through the wrapper: sync(wrapper), take(address(0), wrapper, X) so that the PoolManager itself deposits X into WMON or WETH, settle, then take, mint, burn and native settle in every order. Result: The sequence nets to zero. The native payout debits the caller X of currency address(0) and lowers the native balance by X. The wrapper credits the PoolManager with X, and settle credits the caller X of the wrapper id, which is the measured rise since sync. The caller then holds a debt of X native and a credit of X wrapped, and unlock requires both to be closed (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Closing them returns X native to the PoolManager or removes X wrapped from it. Without the earlier sync the wrapped tokens stay with the PoolManager as unowned surplus and the caller still owes X. mint and burn only move the same deltas into claims (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336). The one to one credit was confirmed on both chains with a probe of 0.001 native units. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance and eth_getStorageAt at blocks 124455000 to 124466634 on 2026-11-22 and rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager and with state overrides, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas and eth_getBlockByNumber at blocks 32558000 to 32563302 on 2026-11-22
- Monad, MegaETH, cycle 2. Whether any address on either chain exposes the PoolManager's native balance, or the balance of a token it holds, under a second currency id, and whether two ids on one balance could be credited twice. Result: No second face was found. MON and ETH have no ERC-20 interface among the precompiles and predeploys swept, LegacyERC20ETH has no code on MegaETH, and no listed Monad token mirrors the native balance. For the general case the code keeps one synced currency in one transient slot (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36), settle credits only the rise of that one currency or msg.value and rejects msg.value while an ERC-20 is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:353-361), and take debits exactly the amount it sends (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). Each credit therefore needs its own payment even if two ids shared one balance. Tokens outside the lists checked were not enumerated on Monad. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance and eth_getStorageAt at blocks 124455000 to 124466634 on 2026-11-22 and rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager and with state overrides, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas and eth_getBlockByNumber at blocks 32558000 to 32563302 on 2026-11-22
- Monad, cycle 2. Opcode differential from the Monad client source for the patterns the PoolManager relies on: CALL with value, gas forwarding, calls to addresses without code, return data, STATICCALL, TSTORE and TLOAD with rollback, and precompile dispatch. Result: No departure from Ethereum was found. call_impl applies the 63/64 rule, the 2300 stipend and the depth limit and reports success only for status Success. pre_call moves value for CALL and CALLCODE inside a pushed state version, and post_call rejects that version on any failure, which restores balances, storage and transient storage. Precompile dispatch happens after pre_call, so a reverted precompile call returns the value. The Monad precompiles return Rejected for any call kind other than CALL, which the caller sees as a failed call. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/vm/runtime/call.cpp
- Monad, cycle 2. Whether the 8 MB memory cap per transaction (MIP-3) can break a PoolManager path that copies return data, or freeze a withdrawal. Result: No. The PoolManager copies hook return data and revert data in full (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:140-149, src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:83-119) and copies 32 bytes after a token transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73). A callee that returns more than the remaining memory makes the PoolManager frame halt, which reverts the call. Only a hook or token chosen for the pool can do this, and that case is F-004. A removal in a pool without such a hook uses a few hundred bytes of memory. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/monad-crypto/MIPs/main/MIPs/MIP-3.md
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Opcode differential from the mega-evm source: TSTORE, TLOAD, CALLVALUE, RETURNDATASIZE, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, PUSH0, CALL with value, the 98/100 forwarding rule, per-frame resource budgets and the storage call stipend. Result: The opcode bodies are the revm handlers with accounting wrappers, so results are those of Ethereum Prague. The changed rules are fail-closed for the PoolManager. A child that receives less gas or exceeds its resource share reverts, and the PoolManager reverts on a failed native transfer, token transfer, hook call or unlock callback (src/types/Currency.sol:51-53 and 82-86, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137). No path treats a failed call as success. The extra 23,000 gas stipend on value calls cannot pay computation, and the PoolManager forwards all gas anyway. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/evm/instructions.rs
- MegaETH, cycle 2. A1 from the node source: does transient storage end with the transaction, including after an error or a panic, and does the KeylessDeploy sandbox share it. Result: Yes for the transaction boundary and no for the sandbox. Every transaction ends with the journal finalize step that clears transient storage, and the panic recovery path calls the same step. The sandbox database reads accounts and storage from the parent journal state and has its own journal. Together with the cycle 1 reading of the Monad client this answers the open question on transient storage for chains 143 and 4326. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/evm/mod.rs
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Whether an attacker can inflate the SALT bucket that holds a victim's storage slot until a zero to nonzero write there becomes unaffordable, given that the bucket index comes from a fixed-seed hash. Result: Not on the normal path. A bucket doubles when it is more than 80 percent full, so reaching multiplier 2^k needs about 205 times 2^k entries in that bucket, each paying 20,000 times (multiplier minus 1) storage gas at the multiplier in force. The total is about 2.7 million times 4^k gas. Multiplier 1,024 costs the attacker about 2.8 ETH at the current base fee and adds 20.5 million gas, about 0.00002 ETH, to one write by the victim. A write that exceeds the 10 billion gas transaction limit needs a multiplier near 500,000 and about 740,000 ETH. A removal mostly clears slots or rewrites nonzero slots, and the recipient of a payout can choose an address that already holds the token. The figures are computed from the documented rule, and the value of NUM_KV_BUCKETS was not read. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/dual-gas-model.md
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Whether a call that the PoolManager issues can match a MegaETH call interceptor (Oracle sendHint, KeylessDeploy, MegaAccessControl, MegaLimitControl) and produce a synthetic success. Result: No. Each interceptor requires the target address and a specific four-byte selector. The PoolManager can address a system contract only as a currency or as a hook, with transfer, balanceOf, an IHooks selector or empty calldata. None of these matches, the call falls through to the contract code, and the code reverts on all of them. The hook route is closed earlier, because the addresses end in 1 to 6 and fail isValidHookAddress (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:111-120). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/system/intercept.rs
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Whether gas detention or disableVolatileDataAccess can be imposed on another user's PoolManager transaction. Result: No. Detention state is reset at the start of each transaction and applies to the transaction that made the volatile read. The access control switch covers the caller's frame and its descendants. A third party is in neither position for a victim's transaction unless the victim's pool uses that party's hook or token, which is F-018. Since REX4 the cap is relative, so a transaction can always spend 20 million compute gas after the read. Evidence: https://github.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/blob/main/docs/spec/evm/gas-detention.md
- Monad, cycle 2. Known weakness: the Spearbit finding that DELEGATECALL to the staking precompile credited stake without moving MON, and its STATICCALL variant. Can an ordinary account use the precompile against PoolManager funds today. Result: No. The fix rejects every message whose kind is not CALL or whose flags are nonzero before dispatch, and the STATICCALL probe from the PoolManager address fails. The PoolManager never issues DELEGATECALL (no use in src outside tests) and cannot send a staking selector. The precompile takes funds only from msg.value of its caller. Evidence: https://cantina.xyz/portfolio/d90b081f-fb8c-4ca7-8e68-6a9219288ae1
- Monad, cycle 2. Known weaknesses in the reserve balance rule: the Code4rena finding on EIP-7702 delegation status that let a sender stall block proposals for free, the testnet crash of 2025-09-27 from relaxed balance merging, and the three bugs described by Category Labs. Can any of them be used against funds in the PoolManager. Result: No path was found. All of them concern whether a sender can pay its fee and whether consensus and execution agree on that. Their effect is a stalled or halted chain, which delays every user alike and moves no balance. The execution check skips accounts whose final code is contract code, so the PoolManager is never the account under test. A user who adds MON and ends below the reserve can have the deposit reverted when the emptying exception does not apply, and a payout only raises the recipient's balance. Evidence: https://code4rena.com/reports/2025-09-monad and https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-09-monad/blob/3d1f9a1d/README.md and https://www.category.xyz/blogs/finding-bugs-that-frontier-models-miss
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Known weaknesses: the BlockSec findings on MegaEVM (unbounded TSTORE, cheap KZG, KZG gas cost crash, costly opcode loops) and the REX4 audit fixes. Can an ordinary account use them against funds in the PoolManager. Result: No path was found. Each is a way to load or crash the node or to escape a resource limit. The PoolManager writes transient storage at fixed slots and at one slot per account and currency (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41), which a caller can multiply only at its own gas cost, and the effect is on node memory. Three of the four BlockSec findings are marked confirmed without a stated fix, so node availability under these loads stays an operator matter. Only the report index was read. Evidence: https://blocksec.com/audit-report/audit-report-megaeth--megaevm--stateless-validator---salt
- Monad, MegaETH, cycle 2. Which special addresses pass isValidHookAddress, and what a pool created with one of them as hook can do. Result: Monad has three (0x10, 0x0100, 0x1000) and MegaETH has 39 among the swept addresses. 0x1000 on Monad, the EIP-4788 contract and 0xff...fe on MegaETH carry an initialize flag and fail the hook call, so no pool can be created with them. The others let a pool be created and then block only the flagged action: donate, swap, or for 0x0100 every call with liquidityDelta of zero or less. A provider would have to choose such a pool. The 0x0100 case is the one cycle 1 recorded, and it also exists on any chain with the P256 precompile. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.monad.xyz, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance and eth_getStorageAt at blocks 124455000 to 124466634 on 2026-11-22 and rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, eth_call with from set to the PoolManager and with state overrides, eth_getCode, eth_getBalance, eth_estimateGas and eth_getBlockByNumber at blocks 32558000 to 32563302 on 2026-11-22
- MegaETH, cycle 2. Aave aTokens and other yield tokens at the MegaETH PoolManager: can growth of the balance between sync and settle be collected by an ordinary account. Result: The eight aToken balances are below one dollar each. An aToken balance depends on the stored index and the block timestamp, both fixed inside one transaction unless the reserve is touched, so sync and settle in one transaction see the same value in the usual case. Growth across blocks stays with the PoolManager as surplus that no pool is owed. The arbitrum-family unit recorded this class for Arbitrum One in this cycle. The claim about the index was not tested on chain here. Evidence: https://megaeth.blockscout.com/api/v2/addresses/0xacb7e78fa05d562e0a5d3089ec896d57d057d38e/token-balances

Critic gap of cycle 2: does the compiled execution path of the Monad client treat TSTORE and TLOAD like the interpreter, so that the lock, the deltas and the synced reserves (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) behave the same whichever path runs the PoolManager?. - MegaETH, cycle 4. Lead L-171: are L1 deposits placed ahead of sequencer transactions, and can a deposit be skipped because the block's state growth counter has reached 1,000 while deposits remain?. Result: Deposits come first. In 25 of 25 sampled deposit blocks the user deposit is at index 1, after the L1 attributes transaction and before every system and sequencer transaction, so the counter is near zero when deposits run. The OP Stack derivation rule places the user deposits of an L1 block in the first L2 block of its epoch. The L1 portal sells at most 20,000,000 gas of deposits per L1 block, and cycle 2 measured 20,333,678 gas for 900 new slots, so the deposits of one L1 block cannot create 1,000 entries. The limiter also applies its test before a transaction and admits the one that reaches the limit. A deposit can fail on its own transaction limits and is then included as failed with its mint kept. Evidence: https://megaeth.blockscout.com/api/v2/optimism/deposits, rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc (eth_call with state overrides, eth_getLogs, eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_getBlockReceipts, eth_createAccessList, debug_traceTransaction) at blocks 32,206,276 to 32,609,052 on 2026-11-23, https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/derivation.html, rpc https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com resourceConfig() and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/block/limit.rs lines 765 to 893

- MegaETH, cycle 7. Inherited caller on MegaETH. From a frame that the PoolManager called, do the natively implemented behaviours (Oracle sendHint, KeylessDeploy, MegaAccessControl, MegaLimitControl) act on the PoolManager when reached by DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE or STATICCALL, and does a switch set by a callee outlive the callee?. Result: No. The interceptors test the target address, which under DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE is the calling account, so those kinds run the contract's Solidity code and revert with NotIntercepted for MegaAccessControl and MegaLimitControl. KeylessDeploy reverts with NotIntercepted under every kind from an inner frame. CALL and STATICCALL of disableVolatileDataAccess take effect for the calling frame and its descendants, and after that frame returned the frame at the PoolManager address read isVolatileDataAccessDisabled false and a TIMESTAMP read succeeded. The effect stays inside the frame that asked for it, which is the hook and token case of F-018. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.3/crates/mega-evm/src/system/intercept.rs lines 295 to 510 and rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc (eth_call with state overrides, eth_getLogs, eth_getTransactionReceipt, eth_getBlockByNumber) at blocks 32,657,833 to 32,660,113 on 2026-11-23, raw/mega_sys.txt

Result: No address gives credit without payment or acts on the inherited caller. The outcomes for the shapes the PoolManager can issue match the cycle 2 sweep: WETH and Wrapped Native are wrappers, the four fee vaults, L2ToL1MessagePasser and L1BlockNumber accept a native payout that the caller of take owes in full, the two EntryPoints book a payout as a deposit of the PoolManager that it can never withdraw, and the six system contracts revert. - Monad, cycle 13. Correction and extension of the cycle 12 clearance that the only emitter change from v0.16.5 to v0.16.7 is the constant-by-variable shift. Four more compiled-path changes exist. (1) touch_memory, used by every compiled MLOAD and MSTORE with a non-literal offset, skips the bounds and expansion check when the same stack element already passed it for at least the same size. Result: Safe as read. The size is recorded on the StackElem object (virtual_stack.hpp lines 216-227 and 279). Every StackElem is constructed fresh by placement new with touched_memory_size_ zero (rc_ptr.hpp line 64, virtual_stack.cpp lines 90-94 and 346-361), and every operation that produces a new value returns a new element: release_general_reg, release_avx_reg and alloc_or_release_* move the register into a new_stack_elem (virtual_stack.cpp lines 821-856, emitter.cpp lines 1161-1233); operations that return an input unchanged (x - 0, x & ~0, shift by 0) return the same value. A cached element therefore always holds the value that was checked, memory never shrinks within a frame, and the data pointer is reloaded from the context on each access, so a reallocation by expansion is followed. Literal offsets, such as mload(0) in src/types/Currency.sol:68, are never cached. The cached path is taken for example by mstore(fmp, 0) at src/types/Currency.sol:77 after mstore(fmp, selector) at line 60. - Monad, cycle 13. (2) Monad v0.16.7 write_to_final_stack_offsets, which writes the virtual stack back at the end of every compiled basic block: dependency counts moved from an unordered_map keyed by heap address to an array indexed by each element's lowest stack index, elements are visited in stack index order, and stack words that were stored from general registers are loaded word by word into an AVX register (mov_words_to_ymm). Result: The algorithm is the same topological write with cycle breaking; only the order in which dependency-free elements are taken changes, and the result does not depend on that order. blockexit.py models the code as written on 200,000 random block-exit states (elements in any mix of stack slot, general register, AVX register and literal, one to three stack indices each): both the stack index order and a shuffled order standing for v0.16.5 leave every final stack index with its element's value, and a planted fault that ignores dependencies is caught in 9,479 of 20,000 cases. mov_words_to_ymm puts word 0 and 1 in the low half and 2 and 3 in the high half, matching the little endian slot layout of stack_offset_to_mem256 (emitter.cpp lines 109-116). The scratch register it uses is free at allocation and distinct from the init register and from every element register. The array index stays in range under the invariant v0.16.5 already needed (an element at a slot in [min_delta, top] has its lowest index there). Every JUMP and JUMPI of the PoolManager, among them the TickBitmap and BitMath branches, passes through this code. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 1384-1690 ; research/network-risk/cycles/013/high-throughput.work/blockexit.py ; research/network-risk/cycles/013/high-throughput.work/blockexit-planted.json
- Monad, cycle 13. (3) Monad v0.16.7 block_prologue stack bound check, changed from 'min_delta < -1024 or max_delta > 1024' to 'max_delta - min_delta > 1024' before the two runtime checks, and (4) MSTORE8 of a value held in a stack slot and the branchless CLZ. Result: With min_delta at most 0 and max_delta at least 0, every block the new static test rejects is one whose two runtime checks (size at least -min_delta and size at most 1024 - max_delta) no stack size passes, and the old static test is implied by the new one, so both versions fail exactly the same stack sizes and an exceptional halt consumes all gas either way. MSTORE8 now reads four bytes of the little endian slot and stores the low byte, the same byte as before. The PoolManager bytecode has no MSTORE8 (0x53) and no CLZ (0x1e) by linear disassembly of build/PoolManager.json. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 1325-1365 and 3395-3412 ; research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json
- Monad, cycle 13. Whether code compiled by the 0.16.7 emitter on the RPC fleet could compute PoolManager state that differs from the validators, who are listed on v0.16.5, without anyone noticing. Block execution with a cold cache calls cached_compile_and_execute_raw, compiling synchronously on the first call; with a warm cache it interprets and starts asynchronous compilation once interpretation of the code hash has used max_code_size(10,240, size) gas. - Monad, cycle 16. Monad main, EIP-8024 and SLOTNUM: can the new opcodes or their immediates change the jump destination map or the execution of the deployed PoolManager?. Result: No. The opcodes are gated on Amsterdam, which only MONAD_NEXT selects, and mainnet's revision function ends at MONAD_TEN. The interpreter's jump analysis has no EIP-8024 case, because an allowed immediate is never 0x5b or a PUSH. The compiler consumes an immediate only when it is allowed and otherwise ends the block as invalid, so 0x5b after 0xe6 to 0xe8 stays a JUMPDEST. A linear scan of the 24,009 byte runtime finds no 0x4b, 0xe6, 0xe7 or 0xe8 outside push data, so no PoolManager instruction changes meaning. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/vm/compiler/ir/basic_blocks.hpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/vm/interpreter/intercode.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/chain/monad_mainnet.cpp lines 33-51 ; research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json

Monad main, generic 256 bit division and modular arithmetic that DIV, MOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD call (udivrem, addmod, mulmod), read against v0.16.7 for the paths FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and 48) and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp use. Result: Equivalent as read. udivrem now forms the remainder from the n significant divisor words. After Knuth division the normalised remainder is below the normalised divisor, so the words at n and above are zero, and v0.16.7 read the same zeros. The short path zero fills the remainder and copies min(M, N) words, which also removes an over-read when M is less than N. addmod's fast path returns the same value through one variable. mulmod's wide_mul is truncating_mul of width M+N. - Monad, cycle 21. Monad PR #2667 (v0.16.6), which checks memory bounds once per offset stack element in compiled code. Can a compiled MLOAD or MSTORE skip an expansion it needs?. Result: No. touch_memory serves only accesses of at most 32 bytes (MLOAD, MSTORE, MSTORE8) and skips the check only when the same immutable stack element has already been checked for at least as many bytes. That earlier check runs before it in the same straight-line block, or in a fall-through block that is not a jump destination (emitter.cpp jumpi, lines 3516 to 3536 on main). Memory never shrinks within a frame, and a failed check leaves the frame. The path exists only in v0.16.6 and later, which validators do not run, and simulated calls use the interpreter. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp
- Monad, cycle 21. Monad MONAD_NINE memory cap (8 MB per transaction, counted over the current frame and its parents), measured on the live interpreter. Can an ordinary account use it to make a PoolManager call of another user fail, or to make the PoolManager continue after a failed sub-call?. Result: The cap holds at its exact edge: a write ending at byte 8,388,608 succeeds and one ending at 8,388,640 fails as out of gas. Only frames of the same transaction count, so an outside account can reach a victim's PoolManager call only through a hook or token in the victim's pool (pool-creator). Every PoolManager sub-call treats failure as a revert of the whole call: hook calls at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-135, payouts at src/types/Currency.sol:44-80, and the revert wrapper at src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:84-112. No path continues past a frame that the cap stopped. A hook that returns several MB makes its own pool's calls fail through the copy at Hooks.sol:140-149, which is a pool-creator hazard already covered by F-004. Evidence: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/opcode-pricing and eth_call on https://rpc.monad.xyz with initcode 0x6001627fffe05200 (result 0x) and 0x600162800000520000 (out of gas)
- Monad, cycle 21. Lead L-933: can a transaction from Monad SYSTEM_SENDER, whose key system_sender.hpp calls known, reach the staking reward, snapshot or epoch change functions?. Result: No such path was found. The three syscalls are dispatched only in ExecuteSystemTransaction::execute_staking_syscall (execute_system_transaction.cpp lines 209 to 233). - Monad, cycle 25. shift_literal_by_non_literal in the v0.16.6 and v0.16.7 emitter, used by the tick bitmap masks shl(and(tick,0xff),1) and 1 << bitPos (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:73, :110), read again line by line. Result: For SHL, the 96-byte table holds 7 as the bit mask, 32 zero bytes, then the value. The window load at value minus k bytes and the carry load one byte lower are shifted per 64-bit lane by b bits, and the carry is moved right by 8. With the count clamped to 256, this gives bit i of lane j equal to bit 64j+i-8k-b of the value for every count from 0 to 256. SHR and SAR use value, fill, fill words, the mask at offset 80, and the mirror image of this rule. The fill is all ones for a negative literal under SAR. The highest byte any load reaches is the first byte of the third word, which holds fill. Cycle 16 ran 46 micro programs per shape and a planted fault on this path. The reading agrees with them. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp
- Monad, cycle 25. The once-per-element memory bound check of v0.16.6 (emitter.cpp lines 6301-6313 at v0.16.7). Result: The check is skipped only when the same stack element, holding the same offset, already passed a check for at least the same read size in the same compiled block. Memory never shrinks within a frame, and a failed first check leaves the frame. So the skip never admits an access the full check would refuse, and it never omits an expansion charge, which is zero for memory already allocated. Cycle 23 ran the PoolManager natively at v0.16.7 with this code and found no difference from the interpreter. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp

The mulmod that runtime/math.hpp calls is the division-based one (uint256.hpp lines 955-962 on main), and math.hpp changed only in an include and a revision constant. The udivrem change on main (the remainder is taken from the n significant words, and the rest is zero) gives the same words as v0.16.7, because Knuth division leaves the higher words of the normalised numerator zero. Result: The PoolManager's outgoing calldata always starts with a selector held as a constant in its bytecode (transfer at Currency.sol:60, balanceOf at Currency.sol:94, the IHooks selectors in Hooks.sol) or is empty for a native take (Currency.sol:48). Evidence: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/megaeth-labs/mega-evm@1.7.4/crates/mega-evm/src/system/intercept.rs and build/PoolManager.json (byte scan)
- MegaETH, cycle 29. Rex4 per-call-frame budgets: a frame that exceeds its local data size, KV update, compute gas or state growth budget (98/100 of the parent's remaining) reverts with MegaLimitExceeded while the parent continues. Result: The PoolManager never continues after a failed sub-call. A failed native take reverts through Currency.sol:51-53, a failed or malformed transfer through Currency.sol:82-86, a failed hook call through Hooks.sol:134-137, and balanceOf is a high-level call that reverts (Currency.sol:94). A frame-local exceed below the PoolManager therefore reverts the whole unlock and leaves no delta or payout behind, and an exceed in the PoolManager frame itself reverts unlock for the caller alone. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/network-upgrades/rex4.md and src/types/Currency.sol:44-87
- MegaETH, cycle 29. Rex4 storage gas stipend of 23,000 gas added to every internal CALL with value, burned on return. Result: It changes only the gas a native take recipient can spend on storage gas and the gas the transaction pays. The value sent, the debit to the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and the success test of Currency.sol:48-53 are unchanged. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/network-upgrades/rex4.md
- MegaETH, cycle 29. Past fault: before Rex1 a compute gas limit lowered by one transaction's volatile data access persisted into later transactions of the same block, so any account could make unrelated transactions fail with ComputeGasLimitExceeded. Result: Rex1 activated on mainnet at 1766282400 (2025-12-21). The PoolManager has no code before block 7,009,653, whose timestamp is 1769806664 (2026-01-30), so no PoolManager transaction ever ran under the leak. In mega-evm v1.7.4 the tracker resets the detained limit to the transaction limit at every transaction start when REX1 is enabled (limit/compute_gas.rs:204-209, limit/limit.rs:170-173). Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/network-upgrades/rex1.md, https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/megaeth-labs/mega-evm@1.7.4/crates/mega-evm/src/limit/compute_gas.rs and https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc (eth_getCode bisection, eth_getBlockByNumber 0x6af575)

- Monad, cycle 31. Lead L-1137: how the compiler's basic block parser on the main branch treats the byte after 0xE6 to 0xE8 when EIP-8024 is active, compared with the interpreter's jump destination scan, and whether any PoolManager jump target is affected. Result: decode_eip8024 consumes the immediate only when it is allowed, and allowed immediates exclude 0x5B and 0x60 to 0x7F (evm/opcodes.hpp:630-646), so consuming one can neither hide a JUMPDEST nor shift the alignment of push data. A disallowed immediate ends the block and is parsed again as an instruction, so a 0x5B there stays a jump destination, which matches the interpreter's unchanged scan (interpreter/intercode.cpp:59-79). PUSH data is still skipped by num_args (basic_blocks.hpp:437-447). The PoolManager on 143 and 4326 has no 0xE6 to 0xE8 byte outside push data, and its 610 JUMPDEST bytes outside push data are the same under either reading. Result: A frame stopped by a per-frame budget always ends with success 0. State growth: success 0, 68 bytes, MegaLimitExceeded(kind 3, limit 980). Compute gas: success 0, 68 bytes, MegaLimitExceeded(kind 2, limit 58,776,852). With 50,000,000 gas the compute and log children ran out of ordinary gas first: success 0, no data. Only the child that stops returned success 1 with no data. A transaction-level exceed halts the whole transaction as out of gas. Currency.transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74) therefore never sees a budget stop as a transfer that returned nothing, and take reverts through CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86). - Monad, cycle 35. What a wrong word from Monad block 0xde6 (the delta TLOAD of clear) could let an account do. Result: clear reads the delta only to compare it with the caller's amount and revert on a difference (src/PoolManager.sol:311-314). The debit it then books is minus the caller's own amount, which toInt128 keeps at or above zero (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-58), through applyDelta, which reads the slot again in its own blocks (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:28-40), and the nonzero count follows applyDelta's values (src/PoolManager.sol:368-377). A wrong read can make clear revert or let it lower the caller's own credit or raise its own debt; it cannot lower a debt or create a credit. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:310-319

- Monad, cycle 37. Upcoming Monad forks: every proposal on the MIP index that earlier cycles did not record (MIP-14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24), assuming each ships. Result: None gives an ordinary account a way to pool funds. SETCODEFROM (MIP-19) and CREATEBIG (MIP-21) need their opcode bytes in executable code, and the PoolManager has none, so its code stays what it is; a token or hook that adopts code is the pool-creator hazard already recorded under A7. MIP-20 changes gas only, and every PoolManager call forwards all gas (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). MIP-23 applies the reserve check to accounts without regular code, and the PoolManager neither sets a reserve nor is checked. MIP-24's precompile at 0x1002 cannot read the 68-byte transfer or 36-byte balanceOf calldata as a valid signature, so take or sync on it can only fail or move nothing for the caller's own currency id. Evidence: https://mips.monad.xyz/
