- Monad, cycle 39. Lead L-1340: can block 0xde6 of the compiled PoolManager (the delta read of clear) run its out-of-line CALLDATALOAD path, which serves calldata shorter than offset 0x24 plus 32 bytes, that is shorter than 68 bytes, including calldata of exactly 4, 35 and 36 bytes?. Result: No. In the deployed bytecode (24,009 bytes, sha256 288b97729c9e4f34..., equal to eth_getCode on rpc.monad.xyz on 2026-11-28) the selector 0x80f0b44c jumps to 0xd87, which reverts at 0xdb6 to 0x330 when calldatasize minus 4 is less than 64 (signed). It then calls the address check at 0x2d3f, returns to 0xdbe, checks the unlock flag, and falls through to 0xde6. 0xde6 is not a JUMPDEST and the only PUSH2 of 0x0dbe in the code is at 0xdb7, so every entry to 0xde6 has calldata of at least 68 bytes and CALLDATALOAD(0x24) never takes the short path. Live eth_call of clear with 35, 36 and 67 bytes reverts with empty data on both networks (and with 4 bytes on MegaETH), and with 68 bytes reverts with ManagerLocked 0x54e3ca0d, so the decoder check runs before the lock check. The amount compared at src/PoolManager.sol:314 is always read from calldata in bounds. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:310-319; research/network-risk/cycles/023/high-throughput.work/pm143.bin offsets 0xd87-0xe13; research/network-risk/cycles/039/high-throughput.work/out/clear-shortcd.txt
- MegaETH, cycle 39. Lead L-1334: is there a public method on mainnet.megaeth.com whose answer comes from the sequencer's JIT rather than a replica, other than transaction submission?. Result: No. The RPC reference fetched on 2026-11-28 lists eth_call, eth_callMany, eth_createAccessList and eth_estimateGas as routed to the compute pool, and debug_traceCall, eth_callAfter and trace_call as unavailable. rpc_modules, realtime_call, mega_call, eth_callBundle, eth_simulateV1 and debug_traceCall return -32601 on the endpoint. Only eth_sendRawTransactionSync and realtime_sendRawTransaction return the sequencer's result, and they need a real transaction. The F-166 vectors therefore cannot be run against the producer through a read-only call. This repeats the cycle 19 result with today's page. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/rpc/reference; research/network-risk/cycles/039/high-throughput.work/out/l1334-methods.txt

## HyperEVM

- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Do PUSH0, MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE and SELFBALANCE exist and behave as the bytecode expects (A10)?. Result: Yes. A read-only creation style eth_call that stores 0x2a with TSTORE, loads it with TLOAD, copies it with MCOPY and reads SELFBALANCE returned 0x2a in both words. The docs state Cancun without blobs and the replay client uses SpecId::CANCUN. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call init code 0x602a5f5d5f5c5f5260205f60205e475060405ff3; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Is EIP-7702 active, which would let code at a hook address change after pool creation (A7)?. Result: No sign of Prague. The BLS12-381 precompile address 0x0b and the P256 address 0x0100 return empty data, block headers have no requestsHash, the docs state Cancun, and the replay client passes no authorization list. A hook address that has code keeps it under the Cancun SELFDESTRUCT rule. This needs a re-check when HyperEVM announces a fork. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call to 0x0b and 0x0100; eth_getBlockByNumber latest; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Does transient storage (unlock flag, deltas, synced currency and reserves) leak between a system transaction and a user transaction, or between two user transactions in one block (A1)?. Result: No. The replay client builds a new EVM and calls transact once per system transaction and once per signed transaction, and commits state after each (run.rs lines 155 to 168 and 216 to 258). It asserts that its receipts equal the receipts recorded by the production node, so the production node gives the same per transaction lifetime. src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38 and src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:12-34 therefore see Ethereum's behaviour. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Can a HyperCore to HyperEVM credit raise the PoolManager token balance between sync and settle and be claimed by the settler (A2, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365)?. Result: No. A credit is a separate system transaction that runs before the user transactions of the block, and the recipient is the HyperCore sender's own address. sync and settle of one payment run inside one user transaction. A credit that lands earlier is already inside the reserves that sync records. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Can any party make a system transaction call the PoolManager, or reach it with msg.sender equal to the owner or to the zero address fee controller (A8, A12)?. Result: No path found. Observed and documented system transactions target the linked contract of a token or the HyperCore sender's own address, and their senders are 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, a 0x20 system address, or the two AQAv2 addresses. The PoolManager would become a target only if a token were linked to it, which needs a finalize action from the owner in storage slot 0. No sender is the zero address. With the controller at zero, setProtocolFee and collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-57) are unreachable and no protocol fee can accrue. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber over 120 blocks ending 51,941,801; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Does the native asset have an ERC-20 face, so that pools on address(0) and pools on a token address draw on one balance (A3)?. Result: No. HYPE links to the native balance and has no linked EVM contract. WHYPE is a wrapper whose totalSupply equals its own native balance. A native payment is msg.value and a native payout is a value call (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354, src/types/Currency.sol:48), in the same 18 decimal unit as address(this).balance. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call totalSupply() and eth_getBalance on 0x5555555555555555555555555555555555555555
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Do the 3,000,000 gas fast blocks or the 30,000,000 gas slow blocks freeze liquidity removal or swaps (A9)?. Result: No freeze found. modifyLiquidity updates two ticks, the bitmap and one position with no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), which fits a fast block. A swap that would cross more ticks than one transaction can pay for can be cut with sqrtPriceLimitX96 and continued in the next transaction, because the loop stops at the limit and stores the reached price (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-439). A sender that needs more than 3,000,000 gas can opt in to slow blocks with the HyperCore action evmUserModify. That costs latency and does not block funds. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/dual-block-architecture; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getBlockByNumber for 75 blocks ending 51,942,345
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Can anyone make the PoolManager send a HyperCore action through CoreWriter, for example add API wallet or spot send, and so control what the PoolManager address holds on HyperCore?. Result: No. CoreWriter's code dispatches only selector 0x17938e13. The PoolManager can call an arbitrary address only with transfer(address,uint256) calldata, balanceOf(address) calldata, hook selectors, or empty calldata with value (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 60-75, 94 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-155), and it calls unlockCallback only on msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:110). None of these matches sendRawAction. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getCode 0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interacting-with-hypercore
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Can the HYPE bridge address or CoreWriter be used as a hook address so that the PoolManager calls them inside a pool action?. Result: No. The low 14 bits of 0x2222 and 0x3333 both set AFTER_ADD_LIQUIDITY_RETURNS_DELTA (bit 1) without AFTER_ADD_LIQUIDITY (bit 10), so isValidHookAddress returns false and initialize reverts (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127, src/PoolManager.sol:126). Both contracts also revert on hook selectors. Evidence: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getCode on both addresses
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Can a read precompile used as a currency address create credit, since 0x0809 answers balanceOf with a number that grows over time (A2, A4)?. Result: No effect on other currencies. Inside one transaction the precompile value is fixed, so settle computes a paid amount of zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). take of that currency always reverts, because the precompile returns 32 bytes that are not 1 and Currency.transfer treats that as failure (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 and 82-86). Deltas, reserves and claims are tracked per currency address (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41), so a currency with odd balance behaviour cannot draw on the balance of a real token. The other precompiles tested fail on balanceOf calldata, so sync reverts. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call to 0x0809 and neighbours with balanceOf and transfer calldata; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/precompile.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Does holding a pool token for part of one transaction have value on HyperEVM, given that take lends everything for free inside unlock (A5)?. Result: No use found. Gas is paid only in HYPE by the transaction sender. Read precompiles report HyperCore state fixed when the EVM block is built and do not read EVM balances. Bridging a borrowed balance to HyperCore removes it from the EVM, so the borrower cannot settle, unlock reverts on the unsettled delta (src/PoolManager.sol:112) and the bridge log is discarded with the revert. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interacting-with-hypercore; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interaction-timings; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. What happens if a HyperCore spot token is linked to the PoolManager address as its EVM contract?. Result: Nothing that touches pool funds, in the documented linking behaviour. HyperCore to EVM transfers would call transfer(address,uint256) on the PoolManager, which has no such function and no fallback (the ERC-6909 transfer takes three arguments, src/ERC6909.sol:25), so the call reverts. EVM to HyperCore credits need an ERC-20 Transfer log from the linked contract. The PoolManager emits only the five field ERC-6909 Transfer event (src/interfaces/external/IERC6909Claims.sol:14) and its deployed bytecode does not contain the ERC-20 Transfer topic 0xddf252ad. Linking also needs a finalize action from the owner stored in slot 0. The interaction with AQAv2 sender rules is left as a lead. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getCode and eth_getStorageAt on the PoolManager
- HyperEVM, cycle 1. Can a reorg or equivocation undo a settlement after funds have left the PoolManager (A14)?. Result: Not under the stated consensus rules. HyperEVM blocks are part of HyperBFT execution, honest nodes agree on the ordered list of committed rounds, and a quorum is more than two thirds of stake. Settlement in core is atomic inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so there is no state that spans blocks. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/staking; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Sweep of the standard precompile range 0x01 to 0x20 and 0x0100 with the PoolManager as caller, using empty calldata, transfer(address,uint256) with a nonzero amount and balanceOf(PoolManager): does any address act as a currency or recipient in a way Ethereum's does not (P1, P2, P3)?. Result: No. 0x01 returns nothing, 0x02 and 0x03 return a 32 byte hash, 0x04 returns its input, 0x05, 0x06, 0x07 and 0x09 fail on the transfer and balanceOf shapes, and 0x08 and 0x0a fail on them as well when given enough gas (0x08 answers empty calldata with a 32 byte 1, as on Ethereum, which no PoolManager call shape for a currency can produce). 0x0b to 0x20 and 0x0100 answer like accounts without code. This is Ethereum's Cancun behaviour. None of these addresses returns a 32 byte 1 or empty data for the transfer shape while holding a balance, so take either reverts or moves nothing and still debits the caller (src/types/Currency.sol:64-86). 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 answer balanceOf with a constant, so settle computes zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). Only the gas price of seven of them differs, see the MRB finding. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call from 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F to each address with three call shapes, latest, 2026-11-22
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Sweep of 0x0700 to 0x09ff and 0x1000 to 0x1010 with the same three call shapes: which addresses are read precompiles today and can any of them serve as currency, recipient or hook?. Result: Read precompiles occupy 0x0800 to 0x0814. Twenty of them fail on every PoolManager call shape, including all ten IHooks selectors on 0x0800 and 0x0810, the only two whose low 14 bits pass Hooks.isValidHookAddress. A failed call burns the gas forwarded and the PoolManager reverts (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-137, src/types/Currency.sol:82-86, and the balanceOf call at Currency.sol:94). A pool created with 0x0800 or 0x0810 as hook can be initialized, since neither has an initialize flag, and can never receive liquidity, because beforeAddLiquidity fails. Nobody else's funds are involved. All other addresses in the ranges answer like accounts without code. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call from 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F, three shapes for 785 addresses and fifteen shapes for 0x0800, 0x0809 and 0x0810
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Can 0x0809, which answers every call with the L1 block number, give a credit when used as currency, given that the number grows by about 20 per second (A2, A4)?. Result: No. Two calls to 0x0809 inside one execution returned the same value (0x495c881c and 0x495c881c), while separate executions about a second apart returned 0x495c8830 and 0x495c8846. sync and settle run in one transaction because the synced currency is transient (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-38), so paid is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). take under this id reverts, because the 32 byte answer is not 1 (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). This confirms the cycle 1 clearance with a measurement inside one execution. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call creation probe 0x60205f5f5f6108095afa50602060205f5f6108095afa5060405ff3, three runs
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Do the HYPE bridge 0x2222...2222, CoreWriter 0x3333...3333, the CoreDepositWallet, a token system address and the system interest address accept any PoolManager call shape other than the native payout already recorded in F-021?. Result: No. The bridge accepts empty calldata with or without value and reverts on transfer, balanceOf and all ten hook selectors. CoreWriter reverts on all fifteen shapes. The CoreDepositWallet reverts on all fifteen, and its transfer function names the reason: Caller is not the system address. 0x2000000000000000000000000000000000000077 and 0x5000000000000000000000000000000000000000 have no code, so a take to them is an ordinary transfer by the PoolManager that the caller pays for, and a take that names them as currency moves nothing and debits the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call from 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F with fifteen shapes per address, latest
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Which special addresses pass the hook address check, and can the PoolManager be made to call them inside a pool action with an accepted answer (P5)?. Result: Four pass Hooks.isValidHookAddress (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127): WHYPE, EntryPoint v0.6, 0x0800 and 0x0810. WHYPE has the afterInitialize flag and its fallback returns no data, so callHook reverts with InvalidHookResponse and initialize reverts (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154, src/PoolManager.sol:141). EntryPoint v0.6 has the beforeInitialize flag and reverts on the selector, so initialize reverts. The two precompiles are covered above. Every other special address fails the flag check. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call with the IHooks selectors from 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F; flag bits computed from the addresses against src/libraries/Hooks.sol:29-47
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Can a native payout to WHYPE, whose fallback wraps the value for the sender, leave the PoolManager owing native HYPE that it no longer holds, or give the caller a WHYPE credit it did not pay for?. Result: No. take(address(0), WHYPE, x) debits the caller x of the native id before the call (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295) and WHYPE credits the PoolManager x WHYPE. If the caller had synced WHYPE first, settle credits it x under the WHYPE id (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364). The caller then holds a debit of x native and a credit of x WHYPE and must clear both before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Whichever way it clears them, the native balance and the native amounts owed fall together and the WHYPE balance and amounts owed rise together. This is an in place wrap paid by the caller. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call from 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F to 0x5555555555555555555555555555555555555555 with empty calldata and value; WHYPE runtime code in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs lines 47 to 53
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. stHYPE and wstHYPE: can one deposit be credited under both currency ids, can an ordinary account raise the stHYPE balance of the PoolManager inside its own sync window, and does rounding between the two units pay out more than a dust amount?. Result: No to all three. The synced currency is one transient slot, so only one measuring window is open at a time and a second sync replaces the first (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). Each window credits the rise of one balanceOf (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and both balances rise only when shares arrive: the stHYPE rate depends on block.timestamp alone between rebases (stHYPE.sol lines 495 to 513), mint and burn keep the rate (lines 244 to 256), and rebase is role gated. Every take is debited in full under the id it names (src/PoolManager.sol:294). The sum of credits therefore never exceeds the shares paid in. Rounding: an stHYPE transfer moves floor(amount times shares per unit) of 24 decimal shares and wstHYPE moves multiples of 1e6 shares, so one settle can be off by at most one base unit of either token, far below the gas cost of the call. The effects that remain need the issuer and are in the stHYPE finding. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/999/0xe71caf5c1fe56d8897c7b604295d23968049e057?fields=sources; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/999/0x104324863cfb2220756c60384efa9bb67a57aaf7?fields=sources; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call rebase() from an unprivileged address
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Recheck of assumption A3 on 2026-11-22: does native HYPE now have an ERC-20 face or a linked EVM contract, and is any HyperCore token linked to the PoolManager, to WHYPE or to a system address?. Result: No. spotMeta returns evmContract null for HYPE (index 150). Of 194 linked tokens no two share an address and none points at the PoolManager, WHYPE, the bridge, CoreWriter or a 0x20 address. WHYPE remains a plain wrapper whose code has no path that reads another account's native balance. Evidence: https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info spotMeta, 519 tokens
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Assumption A1 for system transactions, including the AQAv2 ones whose sender is the CoreDepositWallet or the treasury address: can an unlock flag, a delta or a stale sync written in one transaction be read by the next transaction of the block?. Result: No, on the evidence of the maintained archive client. It runs every system and signed transaction through one transact call (src/node/evm/executor.rs lines 192 to 213), and the revm fork it pins clears transient storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize and restores it on checkpoint revert (journal/inner.rs lines 97 to 180 and 461 to 476). The client recovers any 20 byte sender from the s value, so the AQAv2 senders are covered, and it rejects a block whose gas used, receipts root or logs bloom differs from the header written by the validator node (src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs lines 27 to 45). Lock, CurrencyDelta, CurrencyReserves and NonzeroDeltaCount (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41, CurrencyReserves.sol:21-38, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:12-34) therefore start each transaction at zero. This closes the gap the critic named for the replay client. The limit of the evidence: a header comparison shows a difference only if some past transaction depended on leaked transient state, and the validator binary itself is closed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/evm/executor.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/revm/fdf9b16bdd4388a680c97440c6e7f085647ece01/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Can system transactions crowd signed transactions out of a block and so delay a liquidity removal, given that an ordinary account can trigger them through HyperCore transfers?. Result: No. The archive client adds gas to the block total only for transactions that are not system transactions (src/node/evm/executor.rs lines 225 to 227) and checks each signed transaction against the remaining block gas without them (lines 196 to 206). A removal needs no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238) and fits a fast block. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/evm/executor.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Does the PoolManager address have a HyperCore account, a HyperCore balance or the big block flag, and can a third party set any of these in a way that changes how the PoolManager behaves on the EVM?. Result: No account exists: spotClearinghouseState returns no balances, userRole returns missing and preTransferCheck returns userExists false. A third party can create the account and fund it by sending HyperCore assets to the address, which changes nothing on the EVM. The big block flag and every HyperCore action need a signature of the account or a CoreWriter call by it, and the PoolManager can make neither (cycle 1 clearance on CoreWriter, rechecked: CoreWriter reverts on every PoolManager call shape). Evidence: https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info spotClearinghouseState, userRole, preTransferCheck for 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Opcode differential for the opcodes and call patterns the PoolManager relies on: do TSTORE, TLOAD, SSTORE, SLOAD, MCOPY, KECCAK256, LOG, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, SELFBALANCE, CALL with and without value, STATICCALL, RETURNDATASIZE, PUSH0 and CREATE cost what they cost on Ethereum, and does the client change any of them?. Result: They cost the same in 23 measured snippets, to the unit of gas. The archive client uses revm's mainnet instruction table and replaces only BLOCKHASH for blocks below 243,538 (src/evm/api/mod.rs lines 33 to 43). Core does not use BLOCKHASH. The measured differences are confined to seven precompiles that core never calls. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm and https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call creation probes bracketed by GAS; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/evm/api/mod.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 2. Did the November 2026 hard fork move HyperEVM past Cancun or enable EIP-7702, which would let code at a hook address change (A7)?. Result: No. The fork is a precompile repricing. Both spec ids of the archive client map to revm's CANCUN (src/evm/spec.rs line 17), the Prague precompile addresses 0x0b to 0x11 and 0x0100 still answer like empty accounts, and the HyperEVM docs page still states Cancun without blobs. - HyperEVM, cycle 2. Does any file under src outside src/test read the chain id, block fields, the transaction origin, the gas price or external code, or contain a hardcoded address, so that the code could behave differently on HyperEVM than elsewhere?. Result: No. A search of src outside src/test for chainid, block., blockhash, timestamp, coinbase, basefee, prevrandao, gasprice, origin, selfbalance, extcode, create, selfdestruct, delegatecall and for 20 byte literals finds only the delegatecall guard (src/NoDelegateCall.sol:19-25) and address masks. The raw external calls are the native payout and the ERC-20 transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73) and the hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134); the high level calls are unlockCallback (src/PoolManager.sol:110) and balanceOf (src/types/Currency.sol:94 and 102). - HyperEVM, cycle 2. Can an EntryPoint address used as currency draw on any balance that belongs to other users, since both EntryPoints answer balanceOf(PoolManager) and accept native value from the PoolManager?. Result: No. The EntryPoint deposit of the PoolManager rises only when native value is sent for it. If the PoolManager sends it through take, the caller is debited the native amount (src/PoolManager.sol:294). A credit under the EntryPoint id can be minted as a claim and can never be paid out, because transfer(address,uint256) reverts on both EntryPoints (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86). Deltas and claims are separate per currency address (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-16), so this id cannot reach HYPE, WHYPE or USDC held for pools. - HyperEVM, cycle 4. Critic gap from cycles 2 and 3: do the special addresses answer the PoolManager differently when it is an inner frame with another transaction origin? Sixteen call shapes (P1 with value 1 wei and with zero value, P2 transfer of 0 and of 1, P3 balanceOf under STATICCALL, the ten IHooks selectors of P5 and unlockCallback of P7) against 45 targets: precompiles 0x05 to 0x0a, read precompiles 0x0800 to 0x0814, the HYPE bridge address, CoreWriter, WHYPE, the CoreDepositWallet, USDC, the AQAv2 treasury address, the USDC system address, the system interest address, three EntryPoints, Multicall3, Permit2, the deterministic deployer, CreateX, the PoolManager owner, PositionManager and the zero address. Result: No difference. Every shape gave the same success flag and return data from a top level call sent as the PoolManager and from a forwarding stub placed at the PoolManager address by state override and called by another account. 0x0809 answers every shape with the L1 block number, and the direct call and the stub call returned the same number whenever both ran against the same block. Cycle 2 measured that the number is fixed inside one execution, so it gives no credit as a currency (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360) and fails as a token because the answer is not 1 (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). The other twenty read precompiles fail every shape in both frames. CoreWriter and the CoreDepositWallet revert on every shape. The bridge address accepts only empty calldata. WHYPE accepts every selector through its fallback and returns no data, so a hook call to it fails the length test (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154). This closes lead L-209 for HyperEVM. - HyperEVM, cycle 4. Which system transactions can an ordinary HyperCore account cause, which need a validator vote, and can any of them reach the PoolManager or carry it as sender (assumptions A2 and A8, the question the cycle 2 critic left with F-020 and F-044)?. Result: An ordinary account can cause three kinds: a HYPE credit from the bridge address to an EVM account, a transfer call on a linked contract from that token's system address, and a coreReceiveWithData call on a linked contract. The targets are the recipient account or the token's linked contract and the sender is a system address. The PoolManager is no linked contract and cannot become one without its owner, and a plain HYPE credit to it reverts. The fourth kind, transfers sent in the name of the AQAv2 linked contract and treasury address, follows user flows in size and names only the two addresses fixed at activation, which needs a validator vote. In 1,927 system transactions none targeted the PoolManager, none had it as sender and none came from the zero address, which is the protocol fee controller here (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48). Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com eth_getBlockByNumber census of 4,725 blocks; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers.md
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. The protocol fee controller is the zero address. If some transaction ever ran with msg.sender zero, could collectProtocolFees pay out pool funds?. Result: No. collectProtocolFees subtracts the amount from protocolFeesAccrued with a checked subtraction before the transfer (src/ProtocolFees.sol:54-56). That counter grows only by the protocol share of swap fees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:66-70, src/PoolManager.sol:238), and no protocol fee can be set while the controller is zero (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-41). On chain the counter is 0 for native HYPE, WHYPE, USDC and Wrapped USDC. A call with amount zero transfers nothing. Evidence: src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call protocolFeesAccrued(address) and eth_getStorageAt slot 2
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Work item 1, exits: can an ordinary account make another user's liquidity removal or claim redemption impossible to include or always revert on HyperEVM through gas caps, storage pricing, mempool rules or the big block flag?. Result: No. Removal has no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238) and two mined removals used about 60,500 gas each in the modifyLiquidity frame against a 3,000,000 gas small block. burn and take have no loop either (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 332-336). The mempool rule of 8 pending nonces and the one day pruning apply to the sender's own account. The big block flag is set by a HyperCore action of the account itself. System transactions do not use block gas. Filling small blocks costs base fee that is burned and rises with each full block. What an attacker can make expensive is a swap, which is recorded in the finding that extends F-039. A pool's own hook can still block removal, which is F-004. Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com debug_traceTransaction; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/dual-block-architecture.md
- HyperEVM, Elysium, cycle 4. Lead L-219: an Elysium account sends a child chain message whose target on HyperEVM is the HYPE bridge address, a token system address or CoreWriter. Is a HyperCore balance credited to the Elysium Bridge contract, can a later message spend it, and can this move the HYPE that backs Elysium?. Result: The credit goes to the Bridge contract's own HyperCore account and any later message can spend it, and neither step reaches the backing. In a simulated executeCall from the allowed outbox the Bridge sent 1 HYPE to the bridge address, which emitted Received with the Bridge as user, and a call to CoreWriter logged an action with the Bridge as user. The Bridge sends only the value of the message it executes, and that value was burned on Elysium when the message was created, so its 297,189 HYPE cannot leave without an equal burn. HYPE routed this way lands in a HyperCore account that every Elysium account can command through CoreWriter, so the sender of such a message can lose it to whoever sends the next message. No Received log and no CoreWriter log names the Bridge since its deployment, and the Bridge has no HyperCore account. Token escrow sits in the gateway 0xd97B30dE0bA0C2eAeE942afce77530e06c5F122c, which a Bridge call cannot command without the counterpart gateway as child chain sender. I did not read the gateway code in this cycle and take that from the standard Arbitrum design. Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com debug_traceCall executeCall(address,uint256,bytes) on 0x503D572157113fAaaD4DbeD2647Bb10b949216B6 with from 0xec6b106dfa14428fe5eec2a4065a7be599f02728; eth_getLogs from block 48,956,737; https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info preTransferCheck
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Can an ordinary account link a HyperCore spot token to the PoolManager, so that HyperCore sends system transactions to it or reads its logs as token movements?. Result: No. HyperCore accepts a link when the finalizer deployed the contract with CREATE at a stated nonce, or is stored in the contract's slot 0, or in the slot keccak256("HyperCore deployer"). The PoolManager was created with CREATE2 by the deterministic deployer, a contract that cannot send actions. Slot 0 holds the owner. The custom slot is zero and no function writes a caller chosen slot: persistent writes go to mappings and pool state (src/ERC6909.sol:25-88, src/ProtocolFees.sol:29-70, src/libraries/Pool.sol). Only the owner contract could finalize a link, which is a governance act. A linked PoolManager would still revert on transfer(address,uint256) and coreReceiveWithData, which it does not implement, and it emits no ERC-20 Transfer log. Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com debug_traceTransaction 0x886b45bc662d93a4b74935513eb8dc8c1179c4a6c70056f4b4ba5b251c58e4c5; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getStorageAt; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers.md
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Cycle 3 critic question applied to HyperEVM: what can an ordinary account make the PoolManager say to the hooks that serve most pools, given that initialize accepts any pool definition that names the hook (src/PoolManager.sol:117-142)?. Result: Little. The hook 0x6227f0128935079abc6993f1166dc5d716032aec (109 pools) and its siblings 0x50c42fd2b1c73a4416535068b9a3a4c5732aeaec and 0xf201641ea2985f079791c6a28c0d3ebfdebdeaec revert in beforeInitialize with error 0x0f2e5b6c when an ordinary account initializes a pool with unknown currencies, and so do five further hooks with the beforeInitialize flag. EquoHook (0x746301d1924933a5454f30a2828f2b3f63cc80cc and 0x176447020847b5ccea98a46e303808d3de22c0cc, 17 pools, verified) has no initialize flag. Its swap callbacks return at once for a pool id that its factory did not register (EquoHook.sol lines 646 to 648 and 667 to 669) and registerPool is limited to the factory (line 300), so a pool created by a stranger gets no fee logic and touches no stored state. One unverified hook is left as a lead. I tested one unknown currency pair per hook, so a hook that accepts some other pair from a stranger is not excluded. Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com debug_traceCall of PoolManager.initialize from an ordinary account; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/999/0x746301d1924933a5454f30a2828f2b3f63cc80cc?fields=sources

- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Work item 2, known weaknesses of read precompiles and CoreWriter: audits of AlphaHYPE, dHEDGE and Ventuals and the Papertrade incident of 2026-10-10 show that read precompiles return HyperCore state fixed when the EVM block is built, that CoreWriter actions land after the block, and that the best bid and offer precompile 0x080e can be moved for one block. Does any of this reach funds in the PoolManager?. Result: Not through core. Core calls no precompile and CoreWriter rejects every call shape the PoolManager can produce. A value fixed for the whole block cannot rise between sync and settle of one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365). The hazard is for a hook or token that prices or reports balances from a precompile: its numbers lag by one block and its price input can be pushed by a trade on the HyperCore book. That belongs to the author of the hook or token. None of the 307 ERC-20 pool currencies shows a balance change without a Transfer log. Evidence: https://alphaticks.io/041_CODESPECT_AlphaHYPE.pdf, https://papertraderesearch.xyz/, https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interacting-with-hypercore.md

The team stated that the April event was limited to the block explorer. Stale or shifted eth_call results mislead software that quotes off chain and core reads no block field. The token theft was a HyperCore deployer account moving its own supply, which is the issuer class already recorded in F-019. - HyperEVM, cycle 4. Assumption A1 once more, given the cycle 2 and 3 critic notes: is there new evidence about transient storage on the validator node, and how far does the archive client's block check reach?. Result: Nothing contradicts the earlier clearance and its limit is now stated more exactly. The archive client executes every transaction, system or signed, through one transact call (executor.rs lines 192 to 213) and compares gas used, receipts root and logs bloom with the header for the signed transactions. Receipts of system transactions are filtered out of that comparison (reth_copy.rs lines 41 to 47). A stale synced currency left by one transaction would change the outcome of a later native settle in the same block (src/PoolManager.sol:349-356), and such a difference in a signed transaction would break the replay. Both clients reproduce the chain to its head, which the archive endpoints I used show. The validator node itself remains unread. The answering hl-node build therefore does not carry the 1.21.0 mul_mod fault or a fault in the rewritten division paths at these shapes. - HyperEVM, cycle 17. RUSTSEC-2025-0137 (unsound reciprocal_mg10 in ruint before 1.17.0), which affects both public replay clients (hyper-evm-sync ruint 1.15.0, nanoreth f0cad31 ruint 1.16.0): can any EVM division reach reciprocal_mg10 with a divisor whose top bit is clear?. Result: No. In ruint 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 every division goes through div_inlined (src/algorithms/div/mod.rs lines 47-104 of 1.16.0), which trims zero limbs and sends one and two limb divisors to div_nx1 and div_nx2. Both shift the divisor by its leading zeros before calling reciprocal or reciprocal_2 (src/algorithms/div/small.rs lines 69-75 and 138-144), and the normalized variants are only called when the shift is zero (lines 33-39, 109-114). The precondition d >= 2^63 that the advisory says is only debug-checked therefore always holds. DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD of the PoolManager (22, 3, 4, 3, 1 and 13 instances in the build) cannot reach the unsound input. Evidence: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0137; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/v1.16.0/src/algorithms/div/small.rs and mod.rs (saved research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/src/)
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. RUSTSEC-2026-0220 (ruint before 1.20.0 truncates wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr amounts modulo 2^32 and reports wrong overflow flags), which affects both public replay clients: can SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE or SIGNEXTEND give a wrong word?. Result: No. revm-interpreter 15.2.0 (hyper-evm-sync) converts the shift with as_usize_saturated and shifts only when the amount is below 256 (src/instructions/bitwise.rs lines 87-92, 100-105, 114-121), BYTE only indexes below 32 (lines 73-79), and SIGNEXTEND only acts below 31 (arithmetic.rs lines 93-99), so a shift of 2^32 or more never reaches ruint. The overflow flag is not used by these handlers. The battery and the cycle 14 high limb set pass on both endpoints. TickMath (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:63, 111, 142-145) and BalanceDelta's SAR therefore keep their results. Evidence: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0220; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-15.2.0.crate (research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/dl/)

The memory size wrap that the new nanoreth Cargo.toml comment names (memory can grow until the size computation in a nested frame wraps unless memory_limit is set), and the revm 43.0.0 fix that returns MemoryOOG when a resize fails. Result: No effect on blocks or on the PoolManager. resize_memory in revm-interpreter 43.0.2 charges the quadratic memory cost before resizing (src/interpreter/shared_memory.rs lines 565-605), and on HyperEVM a transaction holds at most 30,000,000 gas, which pays for about 123,000 words (about 4 MB) across all frames, far from a usize wrap. The comment itself says no block can pay for 4 GiB. The PoolManager's own memory use is bounded by its calldata and return data. The official node returned out of gas during memory expansion for MSTORE at 2^32 and 2^64-1 and invalid operand for 2^64, as specified. - HyperEVM, cycle 17. Halt behaviour at the edges on the three endpoints: 0xFE, an undefined opcode, jumps to a non JUMPDEST, into push data and onto a 0x5b inside push data, stack underflow and overflow, huge memory offsets for MSTORE, MLOAD and KECCAK256, zero length CALLDATACOPY and MCOPY at offset 2^256-1, RETURNDATACOPY past the end, and an endless loop. Result: All three return the same halt for each program and the result Ethereum specifies: invalid jumps fail, zero length copies at huge offsets succeed without expansion, RETURNDATACOPY out of range fails with OutOfOffset. Jump destination analysis therefore treats push data as Ethereum does, which is what every Solidity dispatch and internal jump of the PoolManager relies on. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/probe_err.py, out/probe_err.json

- HyperEVM, cycle 22. ruint 1.20.1 changelog entry #634 (shifts by primitive integers without truncating large amounts) on the opcode path. Result: revm-interpreter 43.0.2 saturates the shift operand to usize and only shifts when it is below 256; at 256 or more SHL and SHR return 0 and SAR returns 0 or all ones by the sign bit (bitwise.rs lines 120-158). The u256 fast paths of wrapping_shl, wrapping_shr and arithmetic_shr were transcribed and agree with exact shifts on all tested amounts. BYTE saturates its index and returns 0 from 32 up (lines 107-117). TickBitmap, BitMath and the Slot0 and BalanceDelta packing (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol, src/libraries/BitMath.sol) therefore see the specified results. Evidence: cycles/017/hyperevm.work/dl/x-revm-interpreter-43.0.2 src/instructions/bitwise.rs lines 107-158; cycles/017/hyperevm.work/dl/x-ruint-1.20.1 src/bits.rs lines 17-19, 414-540, 554-660, 852-925; research/network-risk/cycles/022/hyperevm.work/out/ruint_shift_model.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 22. revm 43 transient storage semantics, which nb-20261125-2 runs for every signed and system transaction. Result: JournalInner.commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize each clear transient storage (journal/inner.rs lines 141-170, 174-200, 207-250); tstore records the previous value only when it changes and a revert reinserts or removes it (inner.rs lines 1060-1106; revm-context-interface entry.rs lines 454-469). The crates match the checksums in the nb-20261125-2 Cargo.lock. The unlock flag, deltas and synced reserves of src/libraries/Lock.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol and CurrencyReserves.sol cannot carry from one transaction to the next on this client. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-context/revm-context-43.0.3.crate and revm-context-interface-43.0.2.crate (sha256 9b06efea... and 3068385c..., equal to the Cargo.lock entries), saved in research/network-risk/cycles/022/hyperevm.work/dl
- HyperEVM, cycle 22. revm memory_limit, now enabled in nanoreth, against the memory the PoolManager uses. Result: The limit defaults to 2^32 - 1 bytes (revm-context cfg.rs lines 75-78 and 354-357). Expanding memory that far costs on the order of 10^13 gas, far above any call cap, so no PoolManager call can reach it and no result changes. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/022/hyperevm.work/dl/x-revm-context-43.0.3 src/cfg.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/Cargo.toml lines 74-79
- HyperEVM, cycle 22. disable_eip3607 for all transactions in nanoreth replay. Result: It lets a replayed signed transaction come from an address with code, but the sender still comes from ECDSA recovery for every transaction with nonzero gas price (transaction.rs lines 77-95). No one holds a key for the PoolManager address and HyperEVM has no EIP-7702 (Cancun only, probe below), so it does not let anyone act as the PoolManager. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/src/node/evm/config.rs lines 356-358 and src/node/primitives/transaction.rs lines 77-95

Pools without such a hook are unaffected. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/src/node/evm/executor.rs lines 101-145

- HyperEVM, cycle 26. Can the Osaka MODEXP at 0x05, or a precompile wrapped by the MRB repricing, act for the PoolManager as currency, recipient or token in a way that books value? Sweep of 0x01 to 0x13 and 0x100 with the P1, P2 and P3 call shapes from the PoolManager address, and PoolManager.sync on five of them. Result: Currency.transfer counts a call as successful only with empty return data or a first word equal to 1 (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 return a hash or an echo of the calldata, never 1; 0x05 to 0x0a fail on the transfer shape; 0x0b to 0x13 and 0x100 have no code and return empty, the known codeless case where a take moves nothing and the caller is still debited (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Every balanceOf answer depends only on the calldata, so sync and settle of such a currency in one transaction give paid = 0 (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). A native take to 0x05 with empty calldata succeeds and strands the value, which the caller pays for, as in F-021. The MRB wrapper changes only gas used (factory.rs run_mrb_precompile), so the only effect on src/ is the hook gas budget already in F-045. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/026/hyperevm.work/out/pcsweep-official.json, out/sync-precompiles-official.txt; cycles/022/hyperevm.work/src/nb2/src_node_evm_factory.rs lines 150-220
- HyperEVM, cycle 26. Does the HyperEVM block design (two mempools and block types, priority-fee ordering, burned priority fees, 8 nonce window, one day pruning) let an ordinary account change what the PoolManager computes for another user or leave another user's deltas open?. Result: No. Every PoolManager action needs the unlock flag set by unlock in the same transaction, and unlock reverts unless the caller's deltas net to zero when the callback returns (src/PoolManager.sol:103-113). The order of transactions in a block or between small and big blocks therefore changes only the pool price that later swaps see, which is ordinary price risk bounded by the swapper's own price limit, as on Ethereum. A user whose exit does not fit a small block can set the big block flag; exits measured in cycle 20 fit 3,000,000 gas. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/dual-block-architecture.md; research/network-risk/cycles/026/hyperevm.work/out/order-official.json; src/PoolManager.sol:103-113

- HyperEVM, cycle 28. L-1143: the borrows of the unchecked subtractions in getFeeGrowthInside (src/libraries/Pool.sol:498-509) and of the fee growth difference in Position.update (src/libraries/Position.sol:91-96), which no mined HyperEVM frame and no reference case had used. Script 1 initialises an upper tick above the price, crosses it downward after fees accrue and adds a position whose lower tick is new, so lower minus upper borrows (line 499-500). Script 3 moves the price into the first position's range, pokes and removes it (line 505-508). - HyperEVM, cycle 28. Upcoming forks over the next six months: announced or staged HyperEVM upgrades, and what an ordinary account could do on the day after a move to Prague or Osaka rules. Result: None is announced. The announcements channel up to 20 November 2026 names only HyperCore changes (HIP-3 deployer options, portfolio margin) and a reminder to update nanoreth. The HyperEVM page still states Cancun without blobs. The testnet runs no CLZ, no type 4 transactions and no 0x0b or 0x100 precompile. If Prague or Osaka shipped, src/ would compute nothing differently: no core contract reads tx.origin, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODEHASH, the block number, timestamp or blob fields, or gasleft (search of src/ outside src/test). The EIP-7825 cap of 16,777,216 gas per transaction lies above the 976,067 gas of the largest measured exit and above the 3,000,000 gas small block cap that already binds. - HyperEVM, cycle 32. Jump destination analysis on the official node, both replicas and testnet: jumps into PUSH data, into the data of a PUSH truncated at the end of the code, past the code, to offset 0 holding a PUSH, and to valid JUMPDEST offsets with bits set at 2^16, 2^32, 2^64, 2^128 or 2^255. Result: Every invalid destination halts the frame and every valid one is taken, as the specification and the Ethereum control node require, so no destination is truncated to a low limb and no push data is treated as code. Every branch in src/ goes through JUMP or JUMPI, including the signed remainder branch of TickBitmap.flipTick (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol) and the overflow branches of FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/032/hyperevm.work/out/edges32.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 32. RETURNDATACOPY bounds after empty and 32 byte return data, including offset beyond the size with length 0 and offset plus length overflowing. Result: In bounds copies succeed and every out of bounds copy halts the frame on all four HyperEVM endpoints and on Ethereum. The PoolManager copies exactly returndatasize() from offset 0 when it wraps a failed transfer or hook call (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:91-117), which is always in bounds. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/032/hyperevm.work/out/edges32.json and src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:83-119

- HyperEVM, cycle 36. Can an ordinary account link a HyperCore spot token to the PoolManager address, so that HyperCore credits or debits through it?. Result: No. Finalizing a link to a contract deployed by a contract needs a signature from the address held in the contract's first storage slot or in slot keccak256("HyperCore deployer"). The PoolManager's slot 0 holds its owner. No mapping slot of the PoolManager can equal a fixed hash without a preimage. The PoolManager also exposes no ERC-20 transfer(address,uint256) and no fallback, and its ERC-6909 Transfer event has a different topic from the ERC-20 Transfer that HyperCore reads. - HyperEVM, cycle 38. L-1333: the wide fee mulDiv at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:64-65 (PoolManager pc 22445/22513) run by eth_call through the deployed PoolManager 0x12D4...6B1F against three existing hookless pools (ids 0x10286777..., native and 0x44d6...; 0x3c4a8680..., WHYPE and 0x887c...; 0x4bf2e188..., 0xd4a2... and 0xfc91...), both directions, exact input of -2^236, -2^240, -2^250 and -(2^255-1), price limit two to three ticks away. A driver placed by state override unlocks, reads slot0 and liquidity, swaps, reads them again with the driver's two deltas, and reverts, so nothing settles. Result: All 24 calls return the same bytes on the official node and on both replicas. For each pool and direction the swap delta is the same for all four amounts, and the three amounts at or above 2^240 have a product (1e6 - fee) times amount of 2^256 or more, so the wide path ran. The swaps consume only what the limit allows: for example 0.0665 native HYPE in for 245,609 units of 0x44d6 in pool 0x10286777, and 0.0103 WHYPE in pool 0x3c4a8680. In 20 of the 24 cases the swap stayed in one step and the delta equals v4math.compute_swap_step to the unit; the other 4 (pool 0x10286777, one for zero, all four amounts) crossed out of the liquidity range, end with liquidity 0 at the limit, and agree across endpoints. The code bounds what a wrong word there could do: amountRemainingLessFee is only compared with amountIn at SwapMath.sol:69 and then discarded; if a wrong word fell below amountIn, the step would take the exhaust branch, consume the whole remaining amount as amountIn plus fee (SwapMath.sol:76-82, Pool.sol:377-380), and the final cast of amountSpecified minus amountSpecifiedRemaining, at least 2^236 in size, to int128 would revert (src/libraries/Pool.sol:452-460, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:40-43). A wrong word can therefore change no settled amount. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/038/hyperevm.work/out/l1333.json (eth_call on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, https://rpc.purroofgroup.com and https://rpc.hyperlend.finance/archive, 2026-11-28); src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:64-84
