## OP Stack chains with ETH gas

- Optimism, Zora, cycle 1. Whether LegacyERC20ETH at 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000, whose balanceOf mirrors the native ETH balance, lets a caller get credit twice for one ETH payment or take ETH under a second currency id (assumption A3). Result: No loss path. sync(LegacyERC20ETH) succeeds and records the PoolManager's ETH balance. While that currency is synced, any settle with msg.value above zero reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356), so a native payment can never be counted both as msg.value and as a balance increase. The only way to raise the balance in that window is to force ETH in without a call, and settle then credits exactly that amount under the legacy currency id. That credit cannot leave: take calls transfer on the legacy contract (src/types/Currency.sol:73), which reverts with 'transfer is disabled' when called from the PoolManager address. The forced ETH stays in the PoolManager as surplus that no delta refers to. A caller can only lose their own ETH this way. The contract source could not be fetched, so the behaviour is taken from the predeploy spec and from eth_call. Evidence: https://mainnet.optimism.io
- Base, Unichain, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether the native asset has an ERC-20 face on the chains where the predeploy spec lists LegacyERC20ETH. Result: eth_getCode at 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000 returns empty code on all five chains, and L1Block.isCustomGasToken() is false. sync on an address without code reverts because the balanceOf call returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94), so the address cannot be synced. Evidence: https://mainnet.base.org/
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether the WETH predeploy is upgradeable or shares a balance with native ETH. Result: The EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots of 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 are zero on all seven chains and the predeploy spec lists WETH9 as not proxied. The PoolManager's WETH balance and its native balance are separate numbers on every chain (for example 4,352 WETH and 6,502 ETH on Base). Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/predeploys.html
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether transient storage can survive from one user's transaction into another's (assumption A1): deposits, the L1 attributes transaction, Flashblocks. Result: The deposit spec processes each deposit as its own transaction in the manner of an EIP-1559 transaction and lists no change to transient storage. Flashblocks group whole transactions. exttload of the synced currency slot and the unlock slot returns zero on all seven chains. unlock re-locks before it returns and reverts if any delta is open (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so the only value that can outlive a call inside one transaction is a stale sync. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/deposits.html
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether the ETH mint of a deposit transaction, the L1 data fee, the operator fee or fee vault credits can change the PoolManager's balance outside a call (assumption A2 and A3). Result: The mint credits the deposit's from address only. Fees are debited from the transaction sender and credited to vault predeploys. The PoolManager is never a sender. A deposit that sends value to the PoolManager must call settle or settleFor, the only payable functions (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307), and otherwise reverts while the mint stays with the depositor. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/deposits.html
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether address aliasing lets someone act as the PoolManager, as the zero address controller, or as the owner (assumption A8). Result: An L1 contract's L2 sender is its address plus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111. To appear as the zero address a contract would have to sit at 0xeeeeffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeeef on L1, and to appear as the Unichain PoolManager at 0x0e873fffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeef3. Both would need a chosen 160 bit address. EOAs and EIP-7702 delegated accounts are not aliased, so they act only as themselves. The owner alias on Unichain and Ink is reachable only by the L1 timelock. Evidence: https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/protocol/differences
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether the 16,777,216 gas cap per transaction (EIP-7825) or the block gas limit can make withdrawals impossible (assumption A9). Result: modifyLiquidity updates two ticks and the bitmap with no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), take is one transfer, and a swap stops at the caller's price limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a large swap can be split. Block gas limits read from chain are between 30 and 60 million. Deposits are exempt from the cap and bounded at 20 million gas per L1 block. World Chain is left out because its cap was not confirmed. The Base figure comes from https://docs.base.org/specifications/transactions/throughput-and-limits. Evidence: https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/features/osaka-on-l2
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether the opcodes the PoolManager needs exist and whether OP Stack opcode differences reach core (assumption A10). Result: The deployed PoolManager answers owner() and exttload by eth_call on all seven chains, and the CLZ probe shows the Osaka rule set. The documented differences concern COINBASE, PREVRANDAO, ORIGIN and CALLER. A grep of src/ outside src/test finds no use of block fields, tx.origin, blockhash or selfdestruct. Evidence: https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/protocol/differences
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether interop contracts (SuperchainTokenBridge, SuperchainETHBridge, ETHLiquidity, CrossL2Inbox, L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger) can mint, burn or move balances today. Result: The five predeploy slots hold proxy code whose EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero on all seven chains. The Lagoon spec that defines these contracts is listed as in development with no mainnet date. Evidence: https://mainnet.unichain.org
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether a pool can name a predeploy or precompile as its hook and make the PoolManager call it with harmful effect (assumption A7). Result: Hook calls carry zero value (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and the call is accepted only if the callee returns at least 32 bytes that start with the hook selector (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). A contract that does not implement the exact hook function makes the whole call revert, so no side effect survives. WETH at 0x…0006 and the registries at 0x8453…0001 and 0x8453…0002 also fail isValidHookAddress because their low bits set a returns-delta flag without the matching action flag (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127). Evidence: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-155
- Base, cycle 1. Whether a B20 Asset stock split or reverse split changes balanceOf(PoolManager) without a transfer (assumption A2). Result: The UI multiplier changes only the derived views balanceOfUI, scaledBalanceOf and totalSupplyUI. The docs state that balanceOf, transfer amounts, totalSupply and allowances stay raw. The PoolManager reads balanceOf only (src/types/Currency.sol:94). Evidence: https://docs.base.org/specifications/b20/concepts/multipliers
- Base, cycle 1. Whether a B20 shaped address that has not been created behaves like an address without code, where a transfer call succeeds and moves nothing (assumption A4). Result: eth_call balanceOf and transfer (from the PoolManager) on the uninitialised address 0xb200000000000000000001000000000000000001 both revert, so take and sync on such a currency revert. An attacker who creates the token later in the same transaction controls only their own token. Evidence: https://mainnet.base.org/
- Base, cycle 1. Whether the move to 200 ms blocks and the BaseTime deposit in Denim affects core. Result: block.number now advances ten times faster and block.timestamp is unchanged. No file under src/ outside src/test reads either value, and the BaseTime deposit calls only its own predeploy at 0x4200…0030. Evidence: https://docs.base.org/upgrades/denim/200ms-blocks
- Worldchain, cycle 1. Whether one UserOp in a PBH or ERC-4337 bundle can leave transient state that takes funds from a later UserOp in the same transaction (assumption A1). Result: sync has no lock check (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), so an earlier UserOp can leave a synced ERC-20 currency. A later native settle with msg.value then reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356) unless the router calls sync(address(0)) first, which the comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 advises. A later ERC-20 payment starts with its own sync and overwrites the stale value. The stale reserves can only make a later settle revert or credit a real balance increase to whoever calls settle next, and a router that follows sync, transfer, settle never leaves such an increase unclaimed. The outcome is a reverted UserOp, with no transfer of funds. Evidence: https://worldcoin.github.io/world-chain/pbh/txs.html
- Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether anyone can use the protocol fee functions while protocolFeeController is the zero address (assumption A12). Result: setProtocolFee and collectProtocolFees require msg.sender to equal the controller (src/ProtocolFees.sol:36 and 48). No user transaction or aliased deposit can have the zero address as sender, and protocolFeesAccrued(native) is 0 on all five chains. Evidence: https://rpc-gel.inkonchain.com
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 1. Whether the deployed PoolManager is behind a proxy that an admin could repoint. Result: The EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots of the PoolManager are zero on all seven chains, including the Unichain instance at 0x1f98400000000000000000000000000000000004, and the code length is 24,009 or 24,050 bytes, far above a proxy stub. Evidence: https://mainnet.unichain.org
- Unichain, cycle 1. Whether Flashblocks, TEE block building or revert protection on Unichain change how core settles. Result: Flashblocks are preconfirmations of whole transactions and do not change consensus. Revert protection drops transactions that would revert before inclusion. Core settles inside one transaction and has no dependence on ordering or block time. Evidence: https://developers.uniswap.org/llms.mdx/docs/unichain/
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 2. Cycle 1 lead: does the execution client source reset transient storage at the start of every transaction, including user deposits, failed deposits and rejected transactions (assumption A1). Result: Yes for every client build the chains report. revm's JournalInner clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize, and checkpoint_revert restores transient entries. op-revm (commit 72fcf947 for Unichain, Ink and Soneium, commit 7220729 for World Chain, tag op-reth/v2.8.0 for Zora) and the Base handler (v1.5.6) end a successful or reverted transaction with commit_tx, treat a failed or halted deposit by reverting to the first checkpoint and then calling commit_tx, and call discard_tx for every other error. An unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency cannot reach the next transaction. OP Mainnet's endpoint does not report its commit, so for that chain this rests on the shared op-reth code line. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs
- Base, cycle 2. Whether a contract that the PoolManager calls (an unlock callback, a hook or a native payout recipient) can DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE a B20 token precompile and act on the token with the PoolManager as msg.sender. Result: No. The wrapper around every Base stateful precompile returns DelegateCallNotAllowed unless the call is a direct call. On chain, with the PoolManager as outer caller and a stub that forwards by DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE to OUSD, balanceOf and transfer revert with 0x0d89438e. With a plain CALL the token sees the stub as sender and the transfer fails for lack of balance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/macros.rs
- Base, cycle 2. Whether a B20 transfer made by a take survives when the surrounding call frame reverts, which would let a caller keep tokens while the PoolManager's delta is rolled back. Result: No. The precompile writes balances with EvmInternals.sstore into the revm journal, and revm commits the frame checkpoint only when the precompile result is ok and reverts it otherwise. Journal entries of an inner frame are undone when any outer frame reverts, the same as contract storage. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/handler/src/frame.rs
- Base, cycle 2. Whether anyone other than the token issuer can move the PoolManager's B20 balance: allowance, permit, factory privilege, or the shared Policy Registry. Result: No path found. transferFrom needs an allowance that only approve by the owner or a permit signed by the owner can set, and permit accepts an ECDSA signature only. The factory's privileged calls run only against a token created in the same call, guarded by TokenAlreadyExists. updatePolicy reverts with PolicyNotFound for an id that does not exist, so a token cannot point at a policy id that a stranger could later create and administer. Seize and burnBlocked need issuer roles and are covered by the cycle 1 issuer finding. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_stablecoin/logic/v3.rs
- Base, cycle 2. Whether the Base operated Activation Registry can freeze B20 tokens that the PoolManager already holds. Result: No. Activation is checked when the factory creates a token and when the Policy Registry is written. The token dispatcher checks only that the token address has code and then routes the call. Turning a feature off stops new tokens and stops list updates. It does not stop transfer or balanceOf on existing tokens. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/policy/dispatch.rs
- Base, cycle 2. Whether a currency id inside the B20 address prefix that has no token behind it (a variant byte that Base has not defined, or a valid variant that was never created) can collect credit that later becomes a claim on a real token (assumption A4). Result: No. For an undefined variant the address is a plain account without code: take succeeds and records a debt (src/types/Currency.sol:60-75), and sync reverts because balanceOf returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94). For an uncreated token every call reverts. A positive delta in such an id can come only from settle, which needs sync, or from a pool that already holds the id, which needs an earlier payment. No credit can exist before the token does. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_factory/variant.rs
- Base, cycle 2. Sweep of the Base only system addresses with msg.sender set to the PoolManager: B20 factory, Activation Registry, Policy Registry, NonceManager, TxContext, BaseTime, for empty calldata with and without value, transfer with zero and nonzero amount, balanceOf and the ten hook selectors. Result: All six revert on every shape. A take, a sync or a hook call that names one of them reverts as a whole, so nothing they do can persist. OUSD and AMDC, two live B20 tokens, answer transfer of zero with true and balanceOf with the PoolManager balance, and revert on empty calldata, on value and on the hook selectors. Evidence: https://mainnet.base.org/
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 2. Sweep of 38 predeploy slots, 20 precompile addresses and 26 preinstalled or reserved addresses with msg.sender set to the PoolManager and a separate tx.origin, for the call shapes P1, P2, P3 and P5: does any target accept a token style call and move value that the caller does not owe. Result: No. For P2 (transfer) the only targets that return true or empty data are real ERC-20 tokens (WETH, the governance token), addresses without code, the Safe singletons, ecrecover and P256VERIFY. The last four move nothing and the caller is still debited. For P1 (value with empty calldata) the caller is debited the full amount whatever the recipient does with it (src/PoolManager.sol:294). For P3 the targets that return 32 bytes are WETH, the governance token, LegacyERC20ETH on OP Mainnet and Zora, L1BlockNumber, the EntryPoints, sha256, ripemd160 and identity. L1BlockNumber and the three precompiles return a value that cannot change inside a transaction, so settle credits zero. The EntryPoint case is in the finding of this cycle. Evidence: https://mainnet.optimism.io
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 2. Faces of the native asset, wrapped native: walk sync, take, settle, mint and burn across address(0) and the WETH predeploy in both orders, including a native take whose recipient is WETH. Result: Value is conserved in every order. A native take to WETH debits the caller amount in currency address(0) and mints the same amount of WETH to the PoolManager. If WETH was synced before, settle credits the caller that amount of WETH. The caller then holds a native debt and an equal WETH credit, takes the WETH, unwraps it and pays the native debt. If WETH was not synced the minted WETH stays in the PoolManager as surplus that no one can claim, and the caller still owes the ETH. A native settle while WETH is synced reverts at src/PoolManager.sol:356. Mint and burn of claims under either id need a matching credit or burn of the same id (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/universal/WETH98.sol
- Optimism, cycle 2. Faces, tokens with more than one entry point: SNX on OP Mainnet is reachable at the proxy 0x8700dAec35aF8Ff88c16BdF0418774CB3D7599B4 and at its target 0x3f2a1f997ef089798d19473d96be484aeb3e4ecf, and the PoolManager holds 30,337 SNX. Walk sync, settle, take, mint and burn across the two ids in every order. Result: No gain in any order. The target is read only for the PoolManager: balanceOf works and transfer reverts with 'Only the proxy can call', so take under the target id always reverts and no debt in that id can be created by take. sync(target), an SNX transfer to the PoolManager and settle credit the payer under the target id for tokens it really paid. That credit can be cleared or minted as a claim and can never be paid out. The single synced currency slot is overwritten by the next sync and reset by settle (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32, src/PoolManager.sol:361), so one transfer is never credited under both ids. A real pair of working entry points would also conserve value, because each credit needs its own balance increase between a sync and a settle and each take moves the same number of units that it debits. Evidence: https://mainnet.optimism.io
- Optimism, Zora, cycle 2. Faces, native asset with the read only LegacyERC20ETH view: orders not listed in cycle 1, namely a native take before sync(LegacyERC20ETH), and inflows that the PoolManager itself can be made to cause. Result: No gain. If the caller takes ETH first, then syncs the legacy id, forces the ETH back with SELFDESTRUCT and settles, it holds a native debt and an equal legacy credit. The legacy credit cannot leave, so the caller pays the native debt a second time. No call shape that the PoolManager can be made to send brings ETH back into it, and the PoolManager has no receive function. collectProtocolFees only lowers the balance, which makes settle revert at src/PoolManager.sol:360. Evidence: https://mainnet.optimism.io
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 2. Whether any predeploy or precompile address can serve as a hook that returns a valid response, or that leaves a side effect after a hook call. Result: No. Of the special addresses, these have a valid flag combination under src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-126: 0x10, the BLS map to G1 precompile (afterDonate), 0x0100 P256VERIFY (afterRemoveLiquidity), L2StandardBridge 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010 (afterDonate), SchemaRegistry 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000020 (beforeDonate) and slot 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000030 (both donate hooks). None returns 32 bytes that start with the hook selector, so the call reverts with InvalidHookResponse or HookCallFailed (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, 152-154) and the whole operation reverts. The identity precompile would echo the selector, and its address 0x04 fails the flag check. A pool created with P256VERIFY as hook accepts liquidity and reverts on every removal. That needs LPs to pick such a pool. The Base precompile page states that P256VERIFY pricing follows EIP-7951 for equivalence with L1, so Ethereum has the same address. The case falls under the cycle 1 hook finding. Evidence: https://mainnet.optimism.io
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 2. Whether an L1 account can act on L2 as the PoolManager, or whether code can appear at the PoolManager's address on Ethereum and use the withdrawal path. Result: No. eth_getCode on Ethereum returns empty code at all seven PoolManager addresses and their nonce is 0. A deposit from an L1 contract carries the aliased sender, and an unaliased sender needs a signature made for that address. A withdrawal that the PoolManager is made to start through L2ToL1MessagePasser carries empty data and the PoolManager's own address as target, so it gives no authority on L1. Evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com
- Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 2. Known weakness: the reth trie iterator bug fixed in November 2026 (pull request 28264). The reth v2.10.0 notes list the fix with high update priority, and the Base v1.5.3 notes say it prevents a state root mismatch. Secondary reports say a crafted transaction could trigger it and stall unpatched nodes. Do the builds these chains report contain the fix. Result: Yes. The corrected comparison (walker position equal to the seek prefix) is present at base/reth tag base-v2.5.2.11 (Base v1.5.6), at ethereum-optimism/reth tag op-v2.7.0-0 (op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1 on Unichain, Ink and Soneium) and at tag op-v2.6.0-2 (World Chain v2.8.2 and conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 on Zora). Upstream reth v2.9.0 and v2.5.1 still have the old comparison. The bug is a liveness and proof correctness issue and gives no way to move PoolManager funds. OP Mainnet is left out because its endpoint does not report a commit. Evidence: https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28264
- Worldchain, cycle 2. Cycle 1 lead: which upgrade activated the Osaka opcodes on World Chain and whether the EIP-7825 gas cap applies there. Result: Karst. op-reth v2.4.3 added the World Chain mainnet Karst time 1789992000 (21 September 2026). World Chain v2.8.2 pins an op-revm commit in which Karst maps to the Osaka instruction set. The gas cap clearance that cycle 1 gave for the other six chains therefore applies to World Chain as well: liquidity removal has no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238) and a swap stops at the caller's price limit. Evidence: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/releases/tag/op-reth/v2.4.3
- Base, cycle 2. Cycle 1 lead on Base Transactions (type 0x79, planned for Everest): is transient storage cleared between call phases and can a failed phase leave state behind. Result: Read from source at v1.5.6. A reverting phase is undone with checkpoint_revert, which also restores transient storage, and later phases are skipped. Committed phases share transient storage with later phases. All calls in the transaction have the same msg.sender, and unlock re-locks and requires zero open deltas before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so the only PoolManager state that can pass from one phase to the next is a synced currency set by the same sender. Everest has no activation date, and this must be read again at the release that activates it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/evm/src/eip8130.rs
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 2. Whether the transient slot constants in src/ are the values their comments state, so that the lock flag, the delta counter, the synced currency and the synced reserves cannot collide with each other or with a delta slot. Result: They are. keccak256('Unlocked') - 1, keccak256('NonzeroDeltaCount') - 1, keccak256('ReservesOf') - 1 and keccak256('Currency') - 1 were recomputed and equal the constants at src/libraries/Lock.sol:8, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10 and src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13. Delta slots are keccak256 of a 64 byte preimage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-16). Evidence: src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 5. Lead L-333. Which addresses from 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000000 to 0x42000000000000000000000000000000000000ff hold an implementation today, and what each returns to sixteen call shapes with the PoolManager as msg.sender: empty calldata with 0 and with 1 wei, transfer(address,uint256) with amount 0 and 1, balanceOf(PoolManager), the ten IHooks selectors with zeroed arguments, and unlockCallback(bytes). The PoolManager code was replaced by a 36 byte forwarding stub through a state override and the call came from a separate account. Result: On all seven chains the same targets do not revert: WETH 0x06 (accepts every shape, returns true for transfer and a balance for balanceOf, empty data otherwise), the four fee vaults 0x11, 0x19, 0x1a and 0x1b and L2ToL1MessagePasser 0x16 (empty calldata with and without value only), L1BlockNumber 0x13 (returns the 32 byte L1 block number for every shape), and the governance token 0x42 where it has code. Every other implemented predeploy reverts on all sixteen shapes: 0x00, 0x02, 0x07, 0x0f, 0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x15, 0x17, 0x18, 0x20, 0x21, 0x2c, 0x2d and BaseTime 0x30 on Base. Against src/: a transfer through L1BlockNumber fails the check at src/types/Currency.sol:68 because the returned word is the block number and never 1, sync on it stores a number that does not change inside a transaction so settle credits 0 (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and as a hook its 32 byte answer does not start with the hook selector (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). The fee vaults and the message passer accept a native payout while the caller stays debited (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295), which is the case of F-048. What a vault does with the ETH afterwards was not read, and the PoolManager has no call shape that could take it back. No interop predeploy (0x22 to 0x28, 0x30) has an implementation on any of the seven chains, so SuperchainETHBridge and ETHLiquidity cannot be called today: a value call or a transfer call from the PoolManager reverts in the proxy and changes no balance anywhere. Evidence: eth_call with state override and eth_getStorageAt of the EIP-1967 implementation slot on https://mainnet.optimism.io, https://mainnet.base.org/, https://mainnet.unichain.org, https://rpc.zora.energy/, https://worldchain-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/public, https://rpc-gel.inkonchain.com and https://rpc.soneium.org on 23 November 2026
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 5. Whether any address from 0x4200..0100 to 0x4200..07ff holds an implemented predeploy that earlier sweeps of 0x00 to 0x2f missed. Result: No. A loop contract placed by state override called each of the 2,048 addresses of the namespace with empty calldata and recorded success, code presence and return data length. Outside 0x00 to 0xff every address on every chain reverted with the 132 byte error of a proxy without implementation. Inside 0x00 to 0xff the implementation slot was read directly. The only chain specific slots are 0x30 on Base (BaseTime), 0x2c and 0x2d (absent on Base), and 0x42 (token code on OP Mainnet, Zora, World Chain, Ink and Soneium, an empty proxy on Base, no code on Unichain). The loop test above 0xff rests on the revert length, so an implemented predeploy that reverts with exactly 132 bytes on empty calldata would look empty. Evidence: eth_call with state override on the seven RPC endpoints of state/networks.json on 23 November 2026
- Optimism, Unichain, cycle 5. Upcoming fork, Lagoon on OP Mainnet and Unichain (target 11 January 2027). What the interop predeploys will answer when the PoolManager is made to call them through take, sync or a hook call, judged from their source because they are not deployed yet. Result: ETHLiquidity has burn() (payable, bridge only), mint(uint256) (bridge only), fund() (payable, any caller, reverts on zero value) and setPaused, and no receive or fallback. SuperchainETHBridge has sendETH(address,uint256), relayETH and refundETH and no receive or fallback. SuperchainTokenBridge has sendERC20 and relayERC20. None of the three has the selector of transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address), an IHooks function or unlockCallback, and a Solidity contract without fallback reverts on an unknown selector and on empty calldata. The PoolManager can only send those shapes (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 60-73, 94, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/PoolManager.sol:110), so every call from it to these three contracts would revert. This was read from the develop branch and from op-contracts v4.0.0, which may differ from the bytecode that the fork installs. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L2/ETHLiquidity.sol
- Optimism, Unichain, cycle 5. Upcoming fork, Lagoon. SuperchainETHBridge.relayETH and refundETH deliver ETH with a constructor that self-destructs, so ETH can reach the PoolManager without a call and without msg.value. Does an ordinary account gain a credit it did not pay for. Result: No. Native credit is msg.value of a settle call and nothing else (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), so ETH that arrives by self-destruct gives no native credit to anyone and stays as surplus. An ERC-20 credit is the rise of balanceOf between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and on Unichain no ERC-20 address reports the native balance. The ETH is burned on the other chain by the account that called sendETH, so the sender pays the full amount that arrives. An attacker cannot make a third party's relay land at the PoolManager, because the recipient is fixed by the sender of the message. Forced ETH was already possible on every chain through SELFDESTRUCT, so the fork adds a second route and no new effect. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L2/SuperchainETHBridge.sol
- Optimism, Zora, cycle 5. Faces of the native asset: LegacyERC20ETH. Walk sync, settle, take, mint and burn across address(0) and the legacy id in every order, including the forced ETH route that Lagoon adds on OP Mainnet, public protocol fee collection on OP Mainnet, and zero amounts. Result: No order gives a gain. 1. sync(legacy) then settle with value reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356). 2. sync(legacy), then ETH forced in (SELFDESTRUCT today, relayETH after Lagoon), then settle with no value: the settler is credited the forced amount under the legacy id. That credit can be minted as a claim, burned back or cleared (src/PoolManager.sol:310-336) and can never leave, because take calls transfer on the legacy contract and it reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:73, 82-86). The forced ETH stays in the PoolManager as surplus. 3. take of native amount a, then sync(legacy), then a forced back in, then settle: native debt a and legacy credit a. The native debt must still be paid with msg.value. 4. sync(legacy), then anything that lowers the native balance (a native take, or a native fee collection through the fee controller, which the check at src/ProtocolFees.sol:49 does not block for address(0)), then settle: the checked subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 reverts. 5. sync(legacy), sync(address(0)), settle with value v: the second sync resets the currency slot (src/PoolManager.sol:283), the credit is v in native, and a later sync(legacy) reads the balance that already includes v. 6. sync(legacy) and settle with no inflow: paid is 0, _accountDelta returns early (src/PoolManager.sol:369) and the slot is reset. 7. take(legacy, to, 0) reverts as well, since transfer of 0 reverts on chain. One inflow is credited once under one id, and only the native id can be paid out. On chain at block 159909409 the legacy contract returned the native balance for balanceOf(PoolManager) on both chains and reverted on the other fifteen shapes. Evidence: eth_call with state override on https://mainnet.optimism.io and https://rpc.zora.energy/ on 23 November 2026

- Optimism, Unichain, cycle 5. Lead L-091, first half. Do the sequencer defined gas refunds of Lagoon credit only the transaction sender, and can the credit reach the PoolManager or show up as a balance rise between a sync and a settle. Result: The specification credits tx.from with refund times effective gas price plus the operator fee difference, and debits the block beneficiary, the base fee vault and the operator fee vault. It applies the settlement after the EVM frame of the transaction has finished. The PoolManager has code and no delegation, so it cannot be tx.from of a signed transaction, and a deposit gets no refund. Because the credit is applied after execution, no sync and settle of that transaction can see it, including through the legacy ETH view on OP Mainnet. The specification is marked as not final. - Worldchain, cycle 5. Lead L-192. Does the parallel validation path for flashblocks in the World Chain node run each transaction on its own journal, and what happens when a result disagrees with the access list. Result: Yes. At the deployed tag v2.8.2, execute_workers runs a rayon parallel map in which every (index, transaction) pair builds a new revm State, sets the block access list index, creates a new EVM instance with create_evm and executes that one transaction without commit. Transient storage is part of the journal of an EVM instance, so each transaction starts with an empty transient map and no worker shares one with another. The outputs are sorted by index and committed in order into a canonical executor that rebuilds the access list. If the access list hash, the receipts root, the state root or the block hash differs from the sequencer's, the function returns an error and the flashblock is rejected. This path validates flashblocks on nodes that follow the sequencer. The sequential strategy in the same file runs on one State through the OP executor that cycle 2 read. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worldcoin/world-chain/v2.8.2/crates/validator/src/execution_strategy.rs

- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 7. Exits, tick crossing cost. Can an ordinary account place dust positions so that another user's swap can never be included under the gas cap, or so that a liquidity removal fails. Result: It can raise the cost of a swap and cannot block it. Each loop pass ends at the nearer of the next initialized tick and the caller's price limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-420), so a swap that would cross more ticks than fit under 16,777,216 gas is done in several transactions with a price limit each. A crossing reads the tick and writes two fee growth words (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-612), which by the gas schedule is at most about 50,000 gas when both words are written for the first time, so one transaction still crosses several hundred initialized ticks. The party that initializes a tick pays more gas for it than a swapper pays to cross it. modifyLiquidity touches the two ticks of the position and no others (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), so dust on other ticks does not change the cost of a removal. On Unichain a full sweep is at 61 percent of the cap today, so added dust ticks would force a full sweep of that pool into two transactions. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238 and 344-420; Quoter measurements in raw/quoter_gas.json of this unit's work directory

Is the forced path through L1 deposits still open for a position owner after Karst and Azul, and can an ordinary account close it. Result: The path is open and its cost can be raised only by buying deposit gas on L1. Deposits are exempt from the 16,777,216 gas cap and are limited to 20,000,000 gas per L1 block, and a block that omits them is invalid. On Base nodes derive the missing blocks themselves after a sequencing window of 3,600 L1 blocks. A removal through the deployed PositionManager needs a few hundred thousand gas. An account that fills the deposit gas market pays L1 fees for every block it fills. This matters only when the sequencer already censors, which needs the operator. - Base, cycle 7. Lead L-484, part one: every code path of the B20 stablecoin and asset logic v3, the factory and the policy registry at v1.5.6 that writes a balance or an allowance, and who may call it. Result: Balances are written in move_balance, burn_inner and mint. move_balance is reached from transfer with the caller as source, from transferFrom after the allowance of the source for the caller is checked, and from seizeWithMemo after the Seize role check. burn_inner needs the Burn role on the caller's own balance or the BurnBlocked role on a blocked account. mint needs the Mint role. Allowances are written by approve for the caller and by permit for the recovered signer, which must equal the owner. The asset variant adds batchMint (Mint role) and announce, which needs the operator role and then routes its inner calls with the same caller and the same privilege flag. The privilege flag that skips policy and role checks is true only inside the factory's creation of a token, and the factory builds the token object from the address it has just computed and checked to hold no code, so the flag cannot reach an existing token. The credited account is the named recipient: the recipient strategy returns the given address or an error for zero and for the token itself. A caller without a role can therefore change another holder's balance only by paying into it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_stablecoin/logic/v3.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_stablecoin/dispatch.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_asset/dispatch.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_factory/logic/v1.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/common/ops/credit_recipient.rs

- Base, cycle 7. Known weakness: the Base block production halts of 25 and 26 June 2026, caused by journal state kept after a rejected transaction. Could an ordinary account use that fault, or one like it, to carry the unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency of the PoolManager into another transaction (assumption A1). Result: No funds path. The state that leaked was the warm set of a transaction that failed validation, before any code ran, so it held no transient writes of the PoolManager. A block built on a contaminated journal is rejected by every node that executes it from a clean journal, which is what halted the chain, so a leaked value cannot become canonical state. The fault let whoever sent the rejected transaction stop block production for about two hours, which delays exits and takes nothing. At v1.5.6 catch_error calls discard_tx for every error that is not a failed deposit, and a failed deposit reverts to the first checkpoint and commits. Evidence: https://www.base.org/blog/postmortem-june-25th-block-production-outage.md ; https://github.com/base/base/pull/3806 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 7. Known weakness: op-reth and kona accepted deposit transactions written as a bare RLP body without the 0x7E type byte (fixed by optimism pull request 22778, released in op-reth v2.4.3). Could an ordinary account use it to run a call with a sender or a value that nobody authorised. Result: No for an ordinary account. The pull request describes a bypass of the leading-byte gates of derivation, which read batches. Batches are written by the batcher of the chain, so the party that could have placed an unsigned deposit, with a chosen sender and a mint, is the operator. Unichain, Ink and Soneium report op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1, which is later than v2.4.3. Zora reports conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, which is later by number only, since the Conduit build has its own numbering. The page lists four referencing pull requests numbered 4970 to 4973 with the title fix(consensus): reject non-canonical transaction encodings and does not name their repository, so the state of the Base client is not confirmed. I did not confirm the fix in the build of the OP Mainnet sequencer, which reports no version, or in the op-reth revision that World Chain v2.8.2 pins, and I did not read the decoder itself. Evidence: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22778 ; web3_clientVersion on the seven rpc URLs of state/networks.json on 2026-11-23
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 7. Known weakness: the reth trie iterator fault of November 2026 (wrong incremental state roots, stalls, wrong eth_getProof answers). Does it reach balances or pool state of the PoolManager. Result: No. The fault is in the computation of the state root and of proofs, and execution of calls is not affected. A node with a wrong root stalls or disagrees with the others. The exposed parties are bridges and services that trust eth_getProof. Base v1.5.6 and op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1 are later than the fixed releases v1.5.3 and v2.8.1. The Zora build (conduit-op-reth v2.5.1), the World Chain build (v2.8.2 of its own numbering) and the OP Mainnet build could not be matched to a fixed release. Evidence: https://www.0xcert.com/advisory/0xCERT-2026-0317
- Base, cycle 7. Known weaknesses: the four Cantina reviews of the Base precompiles (Beryl B20, Beryl precompile storage, Cobalt B20, Denim B20 v3). For each finding that touches calls the PoolManager makes or receives: could an ordinary account use it against the PoolManager balance. Result: None could. The high findings are an abort of execution on oversized pairing input and a changed access order in a frozen logic version, both consensus faults and both fixed. Storage writes of native precompiles skipped the 2,300 gas stipend check of EIP-2200. The PoolManager forwards all gas on every call it makes (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and holds no guard that relies on the stipend, so this changes nothing for it. Value sent to nonpayable factory and activation registry selectors was stranded and is now rejected, which the sweep of this cycle confirms. permit accepted high-s signatures, which still need the owner's own signature. Calls to B20 shaped addresses without a token revert before any token logic, which the auditors and the sweep both state. Unknown block list ids authorize every account and unknown allow list ids authorize none, and updatePolicy refuses an id that does not exist. The remaining items concern gas metering, refunds, metrics, string storage and test coverage. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/main/audits/beryl/beryl-b20.pdf ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/main/audits/beryl/beryl-precompiles-storage.pdf ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/main/audits/cobalt/cobalt-b20.pdf ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/main/audits/denim/denim-b20-v3.pdf
- Base, cycle 7. Known weaknesses: the Immunefi audit competition for the Azul upgrade of Base (April and May 2026) and the Cantina review of 200 ms blocks. Result: The published critical and high reports are unbounded snappy decompression in the gossip layer, engine and batcher stalls, a consensus split in cached flashblock execution, and wrong precompile rules in the ZK proof executor that would let a proof attest to an invalid L2 state root. The first three groups stop or split nodes. The last group concerns what the L1 proof contracts accept and so the funds in the L1 bridge. None gives an account on L2 a way to change a PoolManager balance, a delta or a claim. The 200 ms block review has three low findings about stale lookups after a reorg and proof history. Evidence: https://reports.immunefi.com/base ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/main/audits/denim/denim-200ms-blocks.pdf

- Worldchain, cycle 7. Exits, token transfer cost against the gas cap. MUPPETS on World Chain loops over all holders on every transfer. Can an ordinary account make a take of it impossible, and does a pool depend on it. Result: An ordinary account can make the token untransferable, and no pool depends on it. The verified source runs distributeDividends on every transfer, with two loops over the holder array and a balance write per holder. With 347 holders a transfer from the PoolManager cost 4,553,179 gas in a simulation, and each of six added holders raised the cost by 14,143 gas. At about 1,210 holders a transfer needs more than 16,777,216 gas and can no longer be included, although the block limit is 280,000,000. Adding the missing 864 holders takes one dust transfer each, about 9.2 billion gas in total, which is about 0.005 ETH at the base fee of 511,203 wei before the L1 data fee. The PoolManager holds 101.39 MUPPETS, and the explorer log search returns no Initialize log with the token as currency0 or currency1 (the same search returns 386 logs for USDC), so the balance is a stray transfer and no position is at stake. - Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 12. fixed-cache 0.1.11 (published 2026-10-19): does its change to the lock protocol alter what the keccak cache returns, and does any client of the seven chains pin it. Result: No client pins it: op-reth v2.8.2, v2.9.0, v2.10.0-rc.1 and develop, Base main, World Chain main, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 and reth main all pin 0.1.10. The release adds an opt-in seqlock read path (LOCK_FREE_READS, default DISABLED, unsafe to enable), a version counter in the top 8 bits of the bucket tag, and makes try_lock_ret compare tags without those bits. In the default path a tag match is still followed by key.equivalent, and alloy-primitives 1.7.3 compares the full input slice (keccak_cache.rs Key::eq), so fewer tag bits only add key comparisons. alloy-primitives 1.7.3 sets only STATS and EPOCHS in its CacheConfig, so a client that moved to 0.1.11 would run the locked path. Also Key holds MaybeUninit bytes, which the lock-free path forbids, so turning it on in alloy would be unsound and needs a reread. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/fixed-cache/fixed-cache-0.1.11.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/fixed-cache/fixed-cache-0.1.10.crate; https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/fixed-cache/versions

- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 12. Which block producing code could run a different EVM path than the public endpoint: external builders behind rollup-boost, and the fault proof programs. Result: A builder block is validated with engine_newPayload on the sequencer's own execution client before use and replaced by the local block if invalid, and every node re-executes it, so a builder that computed differently produces a rejected block and no state. The kona proof program had three derivation faults fixed by 26 March 2026, at a time when it was only the fallback proof system. Fault proofs govern L1 withdrawals, not the PoolManager balance, and acting on a fault needs the proposer or batcher, actor operator. Evidence: https://rollup-boost.flashbots.net/architecture/sidecar.html; https://gov.optimism.io/t/vulnerability-in-kona-fallback-proof-system/10650
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 12. Known weaknesses of the last two years not settled in cycle 10: the reth and op-reth state root fault of 5 November 2026 (fixed in op-reth v2.8.1 and Base node-reth v1.5.3), the kona fallback proof faults, the ruint advisories. Result: The state root fault lets a crafted transaction make the legacy state root code, which OP Stack block builders used, return a wrong root, so nodes disagree on the block and processing stalls. It does not change an opcode result or a storage value the PoolManager reads, the report states that L2 withdrawals were unaffected, and the endpoints run op-reth v2.8.1 or later and Base v1.5.6. An ordinary account could at most delay blocks, which takes no funds. The other items are answered above. None gives an ordinary account a path to PoolManager funds. Evidence: https://cryptoslate.com/ethereum-software-bug-triggers-emergency-fixes-across-major-layer-2-networks/; https://gov.optimism.io/t/vulnerability-in-kona-fallback-proof-system/10650

- Optimism, Base, Zora, Worldchain, cycle 16. F-133 and lead L-778: which code path puts a storage word of an address without code into the reth execution cache before a block destroys and recreates that address, on op-reth v2.8.1 and v2.8.2 (ethereum-optimism/reth op-v2.6.0-2), conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, world-chain v2.8.2 and base v1.5.6 (base/reth 9e380dd). Result: None on the default paths. Since Cancun an account is destroyed only in the transaction that created it, so a destroyed account whose original info has no code was created in that block. A storage read of such an address goes to the cache only through State::storage when the account status leaves storage unknown, and revm 42.0.0 returns zero without a read for LoadedNotExisting, InMemoryChange and the Destroyed states (states/account_status.rs lines 58-67, states/state.rs lines 270-300) and for an account created in the transaction (revm-context-interface account.rs lines 172-211). Access list entries only mark slots warm. The only reth path that reads storage slots outside execution is the block access list prewarm (prewarm.rs lines 342-431), which mod.rs lines 359-368 select only when the payload carries a block access list, and OP Stack and Base blocks carry none. The cache entries that the old branch fails to update therefore never exist, the next read misses and goes to the state overlay, and followers cannot be stalled this way. No path reaches the PoolManager in any case: it has code and no SELFDESTRUCT or CREATE (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364 read balances of contracts that already have code). A block access list fork would need a new node release, and base main (base/reth 2b20e42) and op-reth develop (op-v2.7.0-2) already write the recreated account's storage. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/reth/9e380dd9b22f95649fb1b5e84c85449ef03f5dca/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs (lines 1265-1310); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/reth/9e380dd9b22f95649fb1b5e84c85449ef03f5dca/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/prewarm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/reth/9e380dd9b22f95649fb1b5e84c85449ef03f5dca/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/mod.rs; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-database/revm-database-42.0.0.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-context-interface/revm-context-interface-42.0.0.crate; https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28148

- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 22. Which block producers run a code path other than the public endpoint: external builders behind rollup-boost (op-rbuilder and World Chain's PBH builder). Result: A builder's block reaches the chain only after the sequencer's own execution client and every follower execute it again; rollup-boost validates the builder payload with engine_newPayload on the local client and falls back to the local block, and the canonical chain is derived from L1 batches that verifiers re-execute. A builder that computed a pool result differently would produce a block that the clients answering these RPCs reject. The validation call in rollup-boost's server.rs discards the returned status and acts only on a transport error (lines 277-281 of the published source), so an invalid builder block surfaces at op-node's own newPayload instead; that is liveness at operator level and moves no funds. The rollup-boost text was read through search highlights of the published pages. Evidence: https://github.com/flashbots/rollup-boost/blob/main/docs/rollup-boost-ha.md; https://rollup-boost.flashbots.net/operators/production.html; https://docs.rs/rollup-boost/latest/src/rollup_boost/server.rs.html; https://worldcoin.github.io/world-chain/pbh/architecture.html

Result: Both are 64 bit targets. kona-client is built for mips64-unknown-none with target-pointer-width 64 and the corrected target-c-int-width 32 at tag kona-client/v1.9.0 (the c-int-width 64 error of the old builder image, which made str comparisons fail, is fixed in that file). - Base, cycle 22. Base Transactions phase loop in the first tagged release that carries it (v1.6.0-rc.1, eip8130.rs execute_calls): can a failed phase keep TSTORE writes while its storage writes and transfers are undone (lead L-891). Result: No. Each phase takes a journal checkpoint before its first call (eip8130.rs:1394), a failed or policy-blocked call marks the phase reverted, checkpoint_revert undoes it and every later phase is skipped (lines 1458-1474), and a completed phase is merged with checkpoint_commit (line 1483). In revm-context 43.0.3, which rc.1 pins, checkpoint_revert drains the journal and reverts every entry with the transient map passed in (src/journal/inner.rs:622-640), and a TransientStorageChange entry restores the old value (revm-context-interface 43.0.2 src/journaled_state/entry.rs:454-468), so a sync recorded at src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 inside a failed phase is rolled back with it. - Optimism, Unichain, cycle 24. Lagoon interop: can a relayed message make the PoolManager act for someone else, and can a forced-inclusion deposit execute a message or see transient storage of a sequenced transaction. Result: L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.relayMessage calls any target except two messengers with msg.sender equal to the messenger, so a message to the PoolManager can only call unlock, which calls unlockCallback on the messenger and reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:104-110), or functions that need no lock and act on the messenger's own claims. CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage reverts for deposits. Deposits run first in a block, each in its own transaction, and op-revm clears transient storage at commit. Lead L-1048: which blocks can be reorganised after public RPC served them, and can an ordinary account trigger it, for example with a forced-inclusion deposit. Result: Only blocks between the safe and unsafe head (13 seconds on Base to 3,302 seconds on Zora at the time of the query), and only through sequencer equivocation, a batch missing the sequencing window or an L1 reorg. A deposit is placed by derivation at the start of an L2 block whose L1 origin includes it and does not invalidate earlier sequenced blocks; after Lagoon deposits cannot execute interop messages. In the one halt of the year found (Base, June 2026), validators never accepted the bad block, so nothing served was removed. - Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 29. Precompile result cache that reth puts in front of block execution and prewarming (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs in ethereum-optimism/reth op-v2.7.0-2 and base/reth base-v2.5.2.11): key, hit rule, and which precompiles it wraps. Result: One cache per precompile address, keyed by the full input bytes and filtered by spec id; a hit is served only when the call has at least the gas the cached run used, and only successful outputs are stored. map_cacheable_precompiles wraps only precompiles whose supports_caching is true (alloy-evm 0.39.0 precompiles.rs:84-90), which excludes Identity and every precompile built with new_stateful. The OP Stack precompiles are pure, and every stateful Base precompile is built with new_stateful by the base_precompile macro, B20 tokens being resolved by a lookup the cache never wraps. The PoolManager itself calls no precompile (src/ has calls only at src/types/Currency.sol:48, 73 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/op-v2.7.0-2/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs (lines 70-72, 184-226); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/reth/base-v2.5.2.11/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs; https://static.crates.io/crates/alloy-evm/alloy-evm-0.39.0.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/macros.rs

- Optimism, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 33. Lagoon Sequencer Defined Metering: does the out-of-EVM ETH movement of the post-exec refund reach the PoolManager's balance or a settlement decision. Result: The refund credits the sender of the rebated transaction and debits the fee recipients; the post-exec transaction is not executed as code and is not user-submittable. The PoolManager is a contract and is never a transaction sender or fee recipient. Native settlement counts msg.value, not the balance (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365), and an ERC-20 settle compares balanceOf before and after inside the same transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-286, 357-359), so a credit to an EOA after execution changes no delta. Refunds never exceed measured gas, and GAS inside execution is unchanged. Evidence: https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/features/sdm; https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/lagoon/overview.html

Funds already in the PoolManager are untouched by the fork. Everest has no date on Base and is outside the window as published; World Chain and Zora have no scheduled fork. - Optimism, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 39. Lagoon metering settlement as implemented in alloy-op-evm block/mod.rs at op-reth v2.11.0-rc.1, and the refund policy that ships with it.
