- Optimism, Zora, cycle 39. A deposit with value addressed to the PoolManager itself. Result: The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function and its only payable functions are settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300, 305), both behind onlyWhenUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99). A deposit with value that calls it directly reverts and its mint stays at the deposit's from address. A deposit that calls an attacker's contract can only do what an ordinary transaction does. The saturating mint of v2.11.0-rc.1 changes nothing below a balance of 2^256 minus the mint. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:96-99; src/PoolManager.sol:300-307; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.11.0-rc.1/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs

## Stablecoin-native L1s

- Arc, cycle 1. Can one payment be credited twice through the two faces of USDC (address(0) by msg.value and 0x3600 by balance difference)?. Result: No. A native credit needs settle with msg.value while the synced currency slot is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). An ERC-20 credit needs the slot to hold 0x3600 from before the payment, and in that state settle reverts on any msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:356). The reserves slot is written only together with the currency slot (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so a stale reserve cannot be paired with a fresh sync. settle and settleFor are the only payable functions and the contract has no receive or fallback. Every inflow is credited to exactly one currency and every take debits the currency it pays from, so the two faces stay jointly solvent. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/PoolManager.sol:349-364, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32; https://docs.arc.io/arc/concepts/stablecoin-native-model.md
- Arc, cycle 1. Can the 12 digit truncation of USDC.balanceOf be used to take funds? Native value can be forced into the PoolManager with SELFDESTRUCT while 0x3600 is synced. Result: The over-credit is bounded by one ERC-20 unit, 10^12 wei or 0.000001 USDC, per sync and settle pair, because paid is floor(after/10^12) minus floor(before/10^12). The minimum base fee is 20 gwei, so even 30,000 gas costs 6 x 10^14 wei, 600 times the largest possible gain. The dust taken comes from native-denominated claims and can leave them short by less than 0.000001 USDC per event. The PoolManager native balance had a remainder of 970996181983 wei at block 32,554,675, so such dust exists. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:358-360; https://docs.arc.io/arc/concepts/stablecoin-native-model.md; https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/gas-and-fees.md; eth_getBalance via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io
- Arc, cycle 1. collect on the Arc fee adapter is callable by anyone, and collectProtocolFees has no lock check. Can a fee withdrawal in the middle of an unlock profit the caller, given that a native fee transfer changes USDC.balanceOf while 0x3600 is synced?. Result: No profit path found. The guard at src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-52 blocks only the case where the collected currency is nonzero and equals the synced currency, so a native collection can run while 0x3600 is synced. That transfer lowers the PoolManager balance, which reduces the settler's own credit or makes src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert. The recipient is the fixed TOKEN_JAR, a native send to the PoolManager itself would revert for lack of a receive function, and protocolFeesAccrued is reduced with checked arithmetic at src/ProtocolFees.sol:55. Evidence: src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57; eth_call of collect from 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io
- Arc, cycle 1. Can CallFrom, Memo or Multicall3From make the PoolManager see a msg.sender that did not authorise the call?. Result: No. CallFrom accepts calls only from Memo and Multicall3From, and the EVM reverts unless the substituted sender is the calling helper or tx.origin. The only identity that can be preserved is the EOA that signed the transaction, which could call the PoolManager directly. unlock from a codeless EOA reverts when the empty callback return is decoded (src/PoolManager.sol:110). eth_call from the PoolManager address to CallFrom returns 'unauthorized caller'. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/call_from.rs; https://docs.arc.io/arc/concepts/transaction-memos.md
- Arc, cycle 1. Does any Arc precompile or system contract act as a third face of USDC, or do anything when the PoolManager calls it with transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address) or a hook selector? take lets any caller make the PoolManager call transfer on an arbitrary address (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and initialize lets any address with flag bits be called as a hook. Result: No. eth_call from the PoolManager address with transfer, balanceOf and all ten IHooks selectors reverts on 0x1800..00 to ..04, Memo and Multicall3From ('Invalid selector', 'unauthorized caller' or a bare revert). Native Coin Authority exposes transfer(address,address,uint256), a different selector, and accepts only the USDC token as caller. A hook call must also return its own selector or the PoolManager reverts (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 and 151-153). The system log emitter 0xffff...fffe has no code, so it behaves like any codeless address. Evidence: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io at block 32,554,675; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/native_coin_authority.rs
- Arc, cycle 1. Do Arc's opcode differences (PREVRANDAO 0, blob opcodes, absent beacon roots, non-increasing timestamps) reach the PoolManager?. Result: No. A search of src/ finds no use of block fields, tx.origin, gasleft, code size checks, SELFDESTRUCT or delegatecall in the non-test contracts. Core has no dependence on block time or randomness. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol, src/ProtocolFees.sol, src/types/Currency.sol, src/libraries/*.sol (grep); https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/evm-differences.md
- Arc, cycle 1. Arc reverts value transfers to the zero address, to self-destructed accounts and to blocklisted recipients. Can a third party use these rules to block someone else's withdrawal?. Result: No. The recipient of take is chosen by the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:291) and the recipient of collectProtocolFees by the controller (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44). Core never pushes native value to an address a third party controls. A caller who names a bad recipient reverts only their own transaction. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57; https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/evm-differences.md
- Arc, cycle 1. Does Multicall3From change the lifetime of transient storage or let a stale sync reach another user?. Result: No. The subcalls run inside one ordinary transaction from one signing EOA, so transient storage is shared only among that sender's own calls and is discarded at the end of the transaction as on Ethereum. Evidence: https://docs.arc.io/arc/concepts/batched-transactions.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/call_from.rs
- Arc, cycle 1. Can a reorganisation undo a settlement after funds left the PoolManager (A14)?. Result: No. Arc finalises each block with more than two thirds of a permissioned validator set and documents no reorganisation risk. Evidence: https://docs.arc.io/arc/concepts/deterministic-finality.md
- Tempo, cycle 1. Tempo has no native asset. Can address(0) pools, settle with value, or native take create or move value?. Result: No. CALLVALUE is always 0 and the client rejects transactions with value, so the native branch of settle always credits 0 (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354, 364 and 369). No positive address(0) delta can come from a payment. The native branch of take needs a value transfer from an account whose balance is 0. sync and settle never read the native balance (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283). address(0) pools can be created and are inert. Evidence: https://tempo.com/developers/docs/quickstart/evm-compatibility.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/crates/evm/src/handler.rs; eth_call with value via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz returns 'value transfer not allowed'
- Tempo, cycle 1. Does any Tempo precompile respond when the PoolManager calls it with transfer(address,uint256), balanceOf(address) or a hook selector?. Result: Only real TIP-20 tokens accept transfer. eth_call from the PoolManager address reverts with UnknownFunctionSelector on TIP20Factory, FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP403Registry, ReceivePolicyGuard, SignatureVerifier, AddressRegistry, TIP20ChannelReserve, NonceManager, AccountKeychain, both ValidatorConfig contracts, CurrentCommittee, StorageCredits, ZoneFactory and ZoneVerifier, and with a bare revert on the ZonePortal implementation and ZoneMessenger. All ten IHooks selectors revert on pathUSD, OUSD and the nine precompiles I tested. A hook call must return its own selector (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 and 151-153). Evidence: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz at block 50,260,093; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/crates/contracts/src/precompiles/mod.rs
- Tempo, cycle 1. StorageCredits.balanceOf(PoolManager) returns a number that rises when the PoolManager clears storage. Can sync and settle on currency 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 turn that into funds?. Result: No. sync and settle can create a positive delta in a currency whose address is the precompile, because the credit count rises between the two reads when slots are cleared. That delta can only be cleared or minted as an ERC-6909 claim for the same id. take reverts because the precompile has no transfer function, and no real asset is accounted under that address. It would matter only to someone who provided real tokens to a pool against that address. Evidence: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz (balanceOf returns 15, transfer reverts with UnknownFunctionSelector); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/tips/tip-1060.md; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-364
- Tempo, cycle 1. A call to a codeless address succeeds and take would move nothing (A4). Does the TIP-20 address space make this worse, since token addresses are deterministic and can be named before the token exists?. Result: No. An address under the TIP-20 prefix with no token reverts with Uninitialized for both transfer and balanceOf, which is stricter than Ethereum. Token creation reverts if the address is occupied and tokens cannot be removed, so code at a token address does not change after creation. Evidence: eth_call to 0x20c00000000000000000000000000000deadbeef via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/tip20/spec.md
- Tempo, cycle 1. Type 0x76 batches share transient storage across calls. Can an unlock flag, a delta or a stale sync leak to another party (A1)?. Result: No. Every call in a batch has the same sender as caller and the batch is one transaction with one rollback checkpoint, so only the sender's own calls share state. unlock sets and clears its flag inside one call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The storage credits specification states that transient state resets every transaction under EIP-1153 semantics. I confirmed the batch loop in the client source and did not read the interpreter code that clears transient storage at the end of a transaction. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/crates/evm/src/handler.rs (execute_batch); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/tips/tip-1060.md
- Tempo, cycle 1. Fee pre-collection, fee refunds, public fee distribution and guard claims move TIP-20 balances outside ordinary transfers. Can any of them change the PoolManager balance with funds that belong to someone else (A2)?. Result: No path found. The fee payer is the sender or a sponsor that signed, and the PoolManager cannot sign. The refund returns to the fee payer. distributeFees pays a validator's registered recipient, and a guard claim pays a destination chosen by the receipt's recovery authority, so both move the actor's own funds. Outflows from the PoolManager need an allowance or a permit signature it cannot produce, or an issuer role (see the issuer finding). TIP-20 rewards were removed in T8. Evidence: https://tempo.xyz/developers/docs/protocol/fees/spec-fee.md; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/tip20/spec.md; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/guide/node/network-upgrades.md
- Tempo, cycle 1. Can a receive policy or a virtual address redirect payments that users send to the PoolManager, so that settle credits nothing?. Result: No. A receive policy is set by the account itself and receivePolicy(PoolManager) is unset. The PoolManager has no code path that calls the registry. A virtual address needs ten 0xfd bytes in the middle of the address, which the PoolManager address does not have. Evidence: eth_call receivePolicy(0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029) via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/tip403/spec.md; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/tip20/virtual-addresses.md
- Tempo, cycle 1. Do 250,000 gas per new slot, the 30M transaction cap and the 30M general gas budget per block make swaps or liquidity removal impossible to include (A9)?. Result: No freeze found. Removing liquidity touches two ticks and one position and clears slots. A swap pays up to two fresh slots per tick crossed for the first time (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-611), about 500,000 gas, so roughly 55 first-time crossings fit in one transaction, and a larger move can be split with sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344). Filling the general budget costs an attacker about 0.018 USD per block at the base fee, which raises the tip others must pay and does not stop them. I did not measure gas on chain. Evidence: https://tempo.com/developers/docs/quickstart/evm-compatibility.md; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/tips/tip-1010.md; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/blockspace/payment-lane-specification.md; src/libraries/Pool.sol:344 and 602-611
- Tempo, cycle 1. Can a reorganisation undo a settlement after funds left the PoolManager (A14)?. Result: No. Simplex BFT gives deterministic finality and a finalized block cannot be reverted. Evidence: https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/blockspace/consensus.md
- Tempo, Arc, cycle 1. Can code at a hook address change after pool creation in a way Ethereum does not allow (A7)?. Result: No new way found. Both chains target Osaka with EIP-6780 SELFDESTRUCT and EIP-7702, the same as Ethereum. A hook at a delegated EOA can change behaviour by re-delegating, which is equally possible on Ethereum and is a trust decision for LPs of that pool. Tempo's T14 configurable accounts apply to accounts without contract code. Evidence: https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/evm-differences.md; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/quickstart/evm-compatibility.md; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/upgrades/t14.md
- Arc, cycle 2. Where does the Arc client discard transient storage between two transactions of a block, and can an unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency of the PoolManager survive into the next transaction (A1)? The earlier cycle had only an RPC probe. Result: No. ArcEvm::transact_one and transact_system_call run the Arc handler, which overrides pre_execution, reward_beneficiary and validate_initial_tx_gas and leaves the rest to revm. revm-handler 18.1.0 calls journal.commit_tx in execution_result and journal.discard_tx in catch_error, and revm-context 16.0.1 clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize. The block executor calls evm.transact for each transaction and commits the returned state. I read the main branch. The RPC reports arc/v1, so the release that mainnet runs is unconfirmed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/executor.rs; https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/revm-context/16.0.1/download (src/journal/inner.rs); https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/revm-handler/18.1.0/download (src/handler.rs)
- Arc, cycle 2. Does the USDC implementation at 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6, the only code that may call Native Coin Authority, let any role other than the proxy admin move or burn the native balance of an arbitrary account such as the PoolManager?. Result: No. transfer moves only msg.sender's balance. transferFrom needs an allowance, and the PoolManager makes no approve call (its outbound selectors are transfer, balanceOf, unlockCallback and the hook selectors, src/types/Currency.sol:60-73 and 94, src/PoolManager.sol:110, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-134). permit and the EIP-3009 functions need an ECDSA signature of the owner or a 32 byte ERC-1271 magic value from the owner's code, and the PoolManager has no isValidSignature function and no fallback. burn destroys only the calling minter's balance. rescueERC20 moves tokens held by the token contract itself. A seizure needs an implementation upgrade by the proxy admin. The scaling by 10^12 uses SafeMath and cannot wrap for amounts below 2^127. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/5042/0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6?fields=sources,abi,compilation; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/native_coin_authority.rs
- Arc, cycle 2. Sweep of Arc special addresses with from set to the PoolManager: empty calldata with and without value, transfer(address,uint256) with 0 and 1, balanceOf(PoolManager), the ten IHooks selectors and unlockCallback. Targets: precompiles 0x01 to 0x13 and 0x100, 0x1800...00 to ...07, the four system proxies at 0x3600...01 to ...04, the USDC proxy and implementation, the log emitter, EIP-2935, EIP-4788, EIP-7002 and EIP-7251 addresses, Memo, Multicall3From, Multicall3, Permit2, the CREATE2 factory, three EntryPoints, EURC, cirBTC, WETH, USYC and its two helpers, six CCTP contracts, both Gateway contracts, FxEscrow, the fee jar, the fee adapter, the owner contract, the Wormhole core and the Uniswap periphery. Result: No target returns a hook selector with 32 bytes that start with that selector, so none passes as a hook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:151-153). The identity precompile echoes the calldata, and its address 0x04 carries only flag bit 2 without bit 6, which initialize rejects (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:112). transfer returns true only on USDC, EURC, cirBTC and WETH. Codeless addresses and 0x01 and 0x100 return success with empty data, which makes take a debit without a payment. balanceOf returns a constant on 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04, so sync and settle on them credit zero, and reverts or returns empty data on the other precompiles, so sync reverts. The Arc precompiles at 0x1800...00 to ...07 and the four system proxies revert on every shape. The follow-ups on the EntryPoints and the USDC implementation are recorded as findings. Evidence: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io at blocks 32,582,357 to 32,584,426
- Arc, cycle 2. Walk of sync, settle, take, mint and burn across three ids over one balance on Arc: address(0), the USDC proxy 0x3600 and the USDC implementation 0xc6ad..., in every order, with the deployed contract probed for value-bearing calls. Result: No double credit and no undebited payout. A native credit needs the sync slot to be zero and equals msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). With either ERC-20 id synced, settle with value reverts (line 356). sync writes currency and reserves together and sync(address(0)) clears only the currency (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32), so a stale reserve is never paired with a later currency. take debits the id it pays from before the transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). take of 0x3600 to the PoolManager itself moves nothing and still debits. On chain the deployed PoolManager rejects value on empty calldata, on sync and on unlock, returns ManagerLocked (0x54e3ca0d) for settle and settleFor outside an unlock, and accepts sync(0x3600) while locked. The implementation id adds a credit that cannot be taken and is recorded as a finding. The sub-unit rounding bound of the earlier cycle is unchanged. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-307 and 349-364; eth_call with a balance override via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io at block 32,584,426
- Arc, cycle 2. Can a contract that gains control in the middle of a user's transaction (a hook, a token, a recipient of a native payout) use Multicall3From or Memo to call the PoolManager or USDC as that user, since CallFrom allows the transaction signer as substituted sender?. Result: No. Multicall3From passes msg.sender as the sender in aggregate, aggregate3, tryAggregate and both block variants, with no caller-supplied sender. A nested contract that calls Multicall3From is itself the sender, and init_subcall rejects a sender that is neither the calling contract nor the transaction signer. CallFrom accepts calls only from Memo and Multicall3From, rejects value and rejects static context. I read the Multicall3From source in the repository and did not compare it with the deployed bytecode, and I did not read Memo. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/contracts/src/batch/Multicall3From.sol; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs (init_subcall, build_subcall_registry)
- Arc, cycle 2. Opcode differential on Arc for the patterns the PoolManager uses: CALL with value, CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE, STATICCALL, return data, MCOPY, PUSH0, TSTORE and TLOAD, gas forwarding, calls to codeless addresses and precompile dispatch. Result: The client replaces one instruction, SELFDESTRUCT, which the PoolManager bytecode does not contain. Value-bearing frames get three extra reject conditions before revm initialises them (zero address, blocklist, recipient self-destructed in the transaction). A native payout therefore reverts only for recipients the caller chose. Calls to codeless addresses return success with empty data as on Ethereum (seen on 0x12, 0x13, the log emitter and the EIP-4788 address). Arc precompiles reject calls from the PoolManager with a revert. Everything else is revm 38 with the Osaka specification. An on-chain probe returned CALLVALUE 0, the overridden SELFBALANCE and a failing inner value call for a caller without balance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/opcode.rs; eth_call with state overrides via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io
- Arc, cycle 2. Known weaknesses of Arc: open issues 513, 514, 517 and 521 on the arc-node repository, the v0.7.0 to v0.8.0 changelog fixes, and public bug bounty notes. Can an ordinary account use any of them against funds in the PoolManager?. Result: None found. Issues 513, 514 and 517 describe ways around the denylist (a pooled transaction of a newly listed sender still executes, the delegate of an EIP-7702 authorisation is not checked, the address created by a CREATE is not checked). They weaken an operator control and do not move or block PoolManager funds. Issue 521 concerns the post-quantum verifier being callable before its fork. The changelog fixes concern gas metering of precompiles, subcall accounting, SELFDESTRUCT warm state, beneficiary checks and pool hygiene. A third-party summary mentions a consensus denial of service reported through Circle's bounty programme, which is a liveness matter. I did not find a published audit report of arc-node. Evidence: https://github.com/circlefin/arc-node/issues/513; https://github.com/circlefin/arc-node/issues/514; https://github.com/circlefin/arc-node/issues/517; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/CHANGELOG.md; https://governance.aave.com/t/al-technical-assessment-aave-arc/25638
- Tempo, cycle 2. Which interpreter runs on Tempo mainnet, where does it clear transient storage, and can PoolManager transient state cross a transaction boundary, a system call or a batch (A1)?. Result: Mainnet reports v1.19.0 at commit 697ea97, whose manifest pins evm2 at revision e25a95fb. evm2 journals every TSTORE and restores it on rollback, and clears transient storage in clear_transaction_state, which runs on commit, discard, detach and drop of the executed transaction handle and on every handler error. Tempo's block executor resolves user transactions and its system calls through those paths. A type 0x76 batch runs all calls under one checkpoint with the account as caller, so only the sender's own calls share transient state. I did not establish whether the JIT backend is active on mainnet or what the v1.18.4 execution fix changed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/Cargo.toml; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/e25a95fb27de49d06ae9a23c4c9ee578a81504fc/crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/e25a95fb27de49d06ae9a23c4c9ee578a81504fc/crates/evm2/src/evm/tx.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/e25a95fb27de49d06ae9a23c4c9ee578a81504fc/crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/block.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/handler.rs
- Tempo, cycle 2. Second sweep of Tempo from the PoolManager address with the revert data classified: do any of the ten hook selectors, unlockCallback, transfer(address,uint256) or empty calldata reach a real function on a precompile, in particular on the precompiles that may pull TIP-20 from their caller without an allowance (FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP20ChannelReserve)?. Result: No. All thirteen selectors return UnknownFunctionSelector (0xaa4bc69a) on TIP20Factory, FeeManager, StablecoinDEX, TIP403Registry, NonceManager, both ValidatorConfig contracts, AccountKeychain, AddressRegistry, SignatureVerifier, ReceivePolicyGuard, CurrentCommittee, TIP20ChannelReserve, ZoneFactory and ZoneVerifier. StorageCredits answers only balanceOf. On a TIP-20 token the ten hook selectors and unlockCallback return UnknownFunctionSelector, so no hook selector collides with a TIP-20 function, and the dispatcher is the same for every token. Empty calldata reverts on every precompile, so the zero amount native take reaches nothing. ZoneMessenger and the ZonePortal implementation revert on every shape. The implicit pull in system_transfer_from can only be reached through functions the PoolManager cannot call. Evidence: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz at block 50,287,321; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs (system_transfer_from)
- Tempo, cycle 2. Can an ordinary account make the PoolManager's TIP-20 balance rise between sync and settle without paying the same amount, or fall without a take (A2)? I listed every balance write in the TIP-20 precompile and simulated transfers from the PoolManager to special recipients. Result: No path found. Credits come from _transfer (matched by a debit of the sender), _mint (issuer role), the fee refund (fee payer, which must sign) and claim_rewards (msg.sender). The PoolManager cannot sign and cannot call claimRewards. A self transfer from the PoolManager returns true and leaves the balance unchanged, because the debit and the credit each read the stored balance. Debits of the PoolManager need its own transfer call, an allowance or a permit signature it cannot produce, or an issuer burn. Spending limits are skipped when the from address is not tx.origin, so a limited signer of the attacker cannot make PoolManager payouts revert for others. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/precompiles/src/tip20/rewards.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/precompiles/src/account_keychain/mod.rs; eth_simulateV1 via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz at block 50,287,321
- Tempo, cycle 2. Can a third party set a receive policy for the PoolManager or for the Uniswap periphery on Tempo, so that payments into them are diverted to ReceivePolicyGuard with the attacker as recovery authority?. Result: Not for the PoolManager. setReceivePolicy(uint64,uint64,address) acts on msg.sender and has no account argument, and the PoolManager can only emit the selectors transfer, balanceOf, unlockCallback and the hook selectors, all of which the registry rejects. receivePolicy is unset for the PoolManager, PositionManager, both Universal Routers, Permit2, Multicall3, Quoter, CreateX and the three EntryPoints at block 50,287,321. A contract that forwards arbitrary calls, such as Multicall3, can be made to set its own policy by anyone. Whether a periphery contract has such a path is left as a lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/contracts/src/precompiles/tip403_registry.rs; eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz at block 50,287,321
- Tempo, cycle 2. The earlier cycle cleared the native branch on Tempo from documentation. Does the interpreter itself refuse value, and what do CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE and BALANCE return inside a call?. Result: An eth_call with override code returned 0 for CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE and BALANCE(PoolManager), and an inner CALL with 1 wei from an account without balance returned 0. With a balance override the same call succeeded, so the interpreter applies the normal balance check and the native branch of take and settle is inert because no account holds a native balance (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52, src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). - Tempo, Arc, cycle 2. Standard precompile addresses as currencies or hooks on Tempo and Arc: can sync and settle create a positive delta, or can a hook call be answered, at 0x01 to 0x11 and 0x100?. Result: No. balanceOf(PoolManager) returns a fixed hash on 0x02 and 0x03 and the echoed calldata on 0x04, so the difference between sync and settle is zero. 0x01, 0x05 and 0x100 return empty data and 0x06 to 0x11 revert, so sync reverts when it decodes the result (src/types/Currency.sol:94). transfer returns empty data on 0x01 and 0x100, which take treats as success and which only debits the caller (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). On the deployed PoolManagers sync succeeds for 0x02 and reverts for 0x01, 0x100 and the codeless 0x12 on Arc, and on Tempo it reverts for an unused TIP-20 address, for the FeeManager and for the codeless ConfigurableAccount address. The identity precompile is the only address that echoes a hook selector, and 0x04 is no valid hook address. Evidence: eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io and https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127
- Tempo, cycle 2. Known weaknesses of Tempo: an automated audit write-up of the reference contracts, the T3 fix bundle TIP-1038, two TIP-20 dispatcher fixes, and the node release notes from v1.17.0 to v1.19.0. - Tempo, Arc, cycle 2. A5 on Tempo and Arc: does any protocol rule read a token or native balance during a transaction and grant something that outlasts it, so that funds taken from the PoolManager for one unlock have value?. Result: None found. Tempo charges fees from the fee payer before execution and refunds after it, classifies payment transactions by their calls, grants storage credits for cleared slots and has no stake in TIP-20 tokens. Arc validators are permissioned through a system contract and fees are debited from the sender before execution. In both cases a balance held only inside an unlock is back in the PoolManager before any of these rules reads it. I did not read the Fee AMM and StablecoinDEX code for flash-style use, which would be ordinary use of borrowed funds and must still be repaid before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112). - Tempo, cycle 4. Transaction types on Tempo: for legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-7702, the type 0x76 batch with fee sponsor, session credential and authorization list, and system transactions, what msg.sender, msg.value and transient storage look like inside the PoolManager, walked through unlock, sync, settle and take. Result: msg.value is 0 in every form, because each prepare function rejects value before execution. msg.sender is the signer or a contract the signer called, and a fee sponsor never becomes a caller. A batch shares one transient map and one checkpoint among the calls of one signer, so a sync or a delta can only reach later calls of the same account, and an unlock cannot stay open between calls. System transactions are limited to the subblock metadata call, which is disabled, and the block level calls to CurrentCommittee and to the EIP-2935 history contract. No form lets a second party run inside another party's transient state, and no form credits or debits the PoolManager's TIP-20 balance outside a transfer call. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/handler.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/block.rs

- Tempo, cycle 4. L-212: can an ordinary account keep liquidity providers out by filling the 30,000,000 gas general limit of every block, given the fee rule and the ordering rule. Result: Not at a bounded cost. PoolManager transactions do count against the general limit. The base fee is dynamic since T7: 30,000,000 gas per block is three times the 10,000,000 target, so the fee rises 25 percent per block from the floor of 600,000,000 to the cap of 12,000,000,000 attodollars within about 14 blocks. At the cap one full general lane costs 0.36 USD per block, about 57,600 USD per day at 0.54 seconds per block. The pool orders by tip, so a withdrawal of a few hundred thousand gas that offers a higher tip than the filler is taken first, and the filler has to pay that tip on 30,000,000 gas in every block. A withdrawal is delayed only while its sender bids below the filler. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/hardfork/src/constants.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/payload/builder/src/lib.rs and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/transaction-pool/src/ordering.rs

- Arc, cycle 4. The rest of L-218 for Arc: does the periphery treat 0x3600 as the wrapped native currency, and what does it do with a route that names both address(0) and 0x3600. Result: It does not. The WETH9 immutable of the PositionManager and of both routers is 0x8bceaa40b9acdfaedf85adf4ff01f5ad6517937f, a contract that reverts on every call, so wrap and unwrap actions fail. The periphery handles address(0) and 0x3600 as two unrelated currencies: a native settle goes through sync(address(0)) and msg.value, a 0x3600 settle through sync(0x3600), a transfer on the token face and settle without value. A user who pays a native debt through the face ends with CurrencyNotSettled and loses nothing. The 2.1.2 router can pay a 0x3600 debt out of the value sent with the call, because its balance on the face is its native balance. Evidence: eth_call and eth_getCode via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io at blocks 32,660,300 to 32,662,000
- Arc, cycle 4. Transaction types and execution contexts on Arc: legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559 and EIP-7702 transactions, the CallFrom subcall behind Memo and Multicall3From, and ERC-4337 bundles. Can any of them give the PoolManager a msg.sender that did not authorise the call, a msg.value without a debit, or a second transient map. Result: No. Memo passes msg.sender as the sender of the subcall, the EVM refuses a child caller that is neither the helper's own caller nor the transaction signer, and the subcall cannot carry value or run in static context. A contract in the middle of a user's transaction is refused when it calls Memo or Multicall3From. Arc has no sponsored or batched transaction type at protocol level. A bundle is one transaction, and the periphery resets a stale sync before a native settle, as the L-199 item shows. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/contracts/src/memo/Memo.sol and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs (lines 884-955)
- Arc, cycle 4. Critic gap of cycle 2: is Zero8 active on Arc mainnet and does mainnet contain the ruint correction of v0.8.0 for shift and overflow handling, on which BalanceDelta, TickMath and BitMath depend (src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:19-66). Result: Zero7 and Zero8 are set for mainnet at timestamp 1789052400 and current blocks are past it, so validators must run a Zero8 capable release, and v0.8.0 is the release that carries both Zero8 and the ruint update. On the endpoint, 1,008 opcode cases with edge shift counts matched the reference, and 64 swaps through the deployed PoolManager at block 32,666,820 matched the transcription of Pool.swap, which uses SAR and SIGNEXTEND on every delta. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/execution-config/src/hardforks.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/CHANGELOG.md and eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io
- Arc, cycle 4. L-259 style test on Arc, which the lead did not list: does a take of the whole PoolManager balance that is paid back in the same unlock hit a per sender limit on native USDC, the token face, EURC, cirBTC or bridged WETH. Result: No. Three full balance rounds inside one unlock succeed for each of the five. The USDC implementation source that cycle 2 read has no volume rule, and the native transfer rules of Arc concern the zero address, the blocklist and self-destructed recipients only. - Arc, cycle 7. Faces angle on Arc, with the moves earlier models left out. One caller, three ids over one balance (address(0) in wei, the token face 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 in units of 10^12 wei, the USDC implementation address 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6), sync before and inside the unlock, settle, take, mint, burn, payment through the face, native value forced in by SELFDESTRUCT, a payout to the PoolManager itself, and collectProtocolFees through the fee adapter that any account can call. Result: No order gains more than one face unit minus one wei per settle, which is less than 0.000001 USDC. On chain at block 32,767,874: (a) 752,591,764,406 wei forced in after sync of the face raised the reading by one unit and settle credited 1 unit, a gain of 247,408,235,594 wei; (b) with the balance on a unit boundary, a native take of 1 wei lowered the face reading by one whole unit, and after a new sync 1 wei forced in was credited as 1 unit; (c) collect of the face through the adapter while the face is synced reverted with ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced, collect of 1 wei of native fees was allowed (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49 exempts address(0)) and lowered the face reading by one unit, after which settle reverted with a panic on the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360; (d) with the implementation address synced, collect of the face was allowed and settle panicked the same way; (e) take of the face with the PoolManager as recipient left the balance unchanged, settle credited 0 and the caller kept the debit; (f) a native take to the PoolManager and any take under the implementation id reverted, also for amount 0. Fee collection therefore only lowers a reading inside a bracket. It gives the caller a free way to place the balance just below a unit boundary, where earlier models needed a native debit of 1 wei. A bounded search over a model with the unit scaled to 4 base units (4,062,481 states at depth 10, fee collection and forced value included) found a best gain of 3 base units with one settle and 6 with two, that is one unit minus one base unit per settle. Each such settle needs a value-bearing call for the forced wei, which costs at least 9,000 gas, 1.8 * 10^14 wei at the 20 gwei fee floor, against a gain below 10^12 wei. Pool operations and hook deltas move amounts inside one currency id and add no cross id move, so they were left out of the model. Evidence: eth_call with state overrides via https://arc.drpc.org at block 32,767,874 (research/network-risk/cycles/007/stablecoin-l1.work/a1_faces.py), model in research/network-risk/cycles/007/stablecoin-l1.work/a4_model.py, src/PoolManager.sol:279-297 and 349-364, src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57, https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/evm-differences.md (20 gwei floor)
- Arc, cycle 7. Critic gap of cycle 6: the code of the Arc fee adapter and of the jar it pays. Can an ordinary account choose the recipient of a fee collection, receive the fees, or re-enter the PoolManager through the payout while it is unlocked. Result: No. collect has no caller check and passes the immutable TOKEN_JAR as recipient, so the caller chooses only currency and amount. The jar has an empty receive function, so the native payout of src/types/Currency.sol:48 runs no code that calls back. The jar pays out only through release, which requires the releaser, a WormholeReleaser contract under the same governance path as the PoolManager owner. triggerFeeUpdate lets any account push the fee that the pool override or the policy gives, and src/ProtocolFees.sol:37 caps it at 1000 pips per direction. With amount 0 and a currency without accrued fees the adapter makes the PoolManager call transfer(jar, 0) on an address of the caller's choice, which is the zero amount shape of P2 without an unlock and moves nothing. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/5042/0x2f2bd3f43880b9644211f16d861b0672aab23782?fields=sources,abi,compilation, https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/5042/0xfd39ac616e630e9db03efb2c9a4fe63edb949233?fields=sources,abi,compilation and eth_call owner(), feeSetter(), policy(), releaser() via https://arc.drpc.org; src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-57

Pooled assets angle on Arc: for native USDC under both ids, EURC, cirBTC and bridged WETH, does transfer or balanceOf do anything a holder can trigger (rebase, fee, callback, share accounting, special amounts), and does a transfer write a counter or a flow limit for the sender. - Arc, cycle 7. Can an ordinary account sign for the PoolManager at the USDC token, through permit, transferWithAuthorization or an ERC-1271 check, and so move the native balance without a take. Result: No. The signature paths of the token need a signature of the owner of the funds. The PoolManager has no private signer, and its code has no isValidSignature function and no fallback (src/PoolManager.sol:80-395), so a contract signature check against it fails. L-284 as far as it can be answered before the fork: what do the ConfigurableAccount precompile and an account with the 0xef marker answer to the call shapes of take, sync, unlock and the hooks once T14 rules apply. Result: The node already contains the T14 code and applies it when a simulated block carries a time after 1796742000. An account with code 0xef and no registered configuration fails every shape with OpcodeNotFound before and after. - Tempo, cycle 7. L-255: does any crate of the Tempo node at commit 697ea97 start a transaction inside a running user call through evm2 committed_copy, call_tx or transact, which would give the inner execution an empty transient map. Result: No. In 351 modules of 13 crates committed_copy and call_tx do not occur at all. transact is used by tests and by the payload builder's prewarming worker, which executes whole pool transactions on a separate EVM and detaches the result. The transaction handler changes the initial call depth around a batch and runs the batch calls on the same state and the same transient map. Precompiles have no way to call a contract, as cycle 3 recorded. The zone crates and the test and fuzz crates were not searched; zones are separate chains. The answer holds for this commit and has to be repeated for the next release that mainnet adopts. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/ (351 files fetched through mod declarations, list in the profile entry), in particular crates/evm/src/handler.rs lines 1693 to 1711 and crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs lines 180 to 200
- Tempo, cycle 7. L-197: what the v1.18.2 item EVM call input hardening and the v1.18.4 fix for EVM execution changed, and whether the PoolManager's call and return data sequences depend on it. Result: v1.18.2 introduced evm2 with a patch that passes call input as a borrowed range of the caller's memory. At the mainnet revision the range is resolved through the caller frame on each read, so growth of the child's memory cannot corrupt it, and output is written to the caller's memory after the child has ended. v1.18.4 added a check that the remaining gas covers the input cost before a precompile or the T14 account marker copies its input, in crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs and crates/evm/src/instructions.rs, and changed no other module of the seven execution crates I compared. The PoolManager's calls use disjoint input and output ranges for transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73), no output range for hooks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and Solidity's same range pattern for balanceOf (src/types/Currency.sol:94). A differential of 32 cases that cover these three patterns, a child that grows its memory and a second call after the memory was rewritten matched revm byte for byte. Cycle 4 established that the jit feature is absent from the default build and that 256 swaps and 288 adds through the deployed bytecode matched the source formulas. Not confirmed: which features each validator compiles in. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/evm2/src/interpreter/message.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/refs/tags/tempo/v1.18.4/crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/refs/tags/tempo/v1.18.4/crates/evm/src/instructions.rs, https://tempo.com/developers/docs/changelog.md and eth_call with override code via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz and https://arc.drpc.org (research/network-risk/cycles/007/stablecoin-l1.work/t5_alias.py)

- Tempo, Arc, cycle 10. Can the process-wide keccak cache in front of KECCAK256 on Tempo and Arc return a hash for the wrong input, which would move a pool id, position key, mapping slot or transient delta slot (src/libraries/Position.sol, src/types/PoolId.sol, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol). Result: No. The key stores length and all bytes and equality compares both; inputs of 0 bytes and above 87 bytes bypass the cache; reads and writes hold the bucket lock through an acquire compare and swap and release on unlock, and a fresh bucket's zero key has length 0 and never equals a nonempty input. Vectors on both endpoints, sent three times in separate requests so later rounds meet cache hits: every length 1 to 96 at offsets 0, 1, 31, 32 and 33, pairs that differ only by one trailing zero byte, and zero inputs of every length, 766 vectors per round, all as specified. - Tempo, cycle 10. Does the aarch64 build of Tempo compute DIV, MOD, MULMOD, ADDMOD, MUL, SHL and SAR the same as the x86-64 build, given that ruint 1.21.1 uses the x86-64 div instruction and _subborrow_u64 on x86-64 and the reciprocal and borrowing_sub fallback elsewhere. Result: Yes on 200 million cases. I built ruint 1.21.1 twice on x86-64, once unchanged and once with every target_arch = "x86_64" condition renamed so the fallback code compiles, and compared wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, mul_mod with a random and with the 2^256 - 1 modulus, add_mod, wrapping_mul, shift left and arithmetic shift right on operands built from zero, all ones, single bits, the top bit, near maximum limbs and shortened limb counts. No result differed, and the fallback quotient and remainder satisfied q*b + r = a with r < b in every case. This is the path FullMath.mulDiv and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp take on an ARM validator. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/stablecoin-l1.work/ruint_fallback/main.rs and Cargo.toml, raw/ruint_fallback.log; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.21.1.crate (src/algorithms/div/small.rs, div/reciprocal.rs, algorithms/mod.rs)

- Tempo, cycle 15. T14 configurable accounts as unlock callers, as hooks and as take recipients. Result: A configurable account has the one-byte marker as code. When the PoolManager calls it (unlockCallback at PoolManager.sol:110 or a hook call at Hooks.sol:131-136), the 0xef instruction runs the shim, which answers only isValidSignature, onERC721Received and empty input and reverts otherwise. So unlock from such an account reverts and a pool naming it as hook cannot initialize. A TIP-20 take to it is an ordinary balance credit. The shim writes no state and makes no calls, so nothing reaches other users' funds. Addresses are hashes of a configuration, so one cannot be placed at an existing contract's address. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/tempo/v1.19.1/crates/precompiles/src/configurable_account/shim.rs and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/tempo/v1.19.1/crates/evm/src/instructions.rs and https://tempo.com/developers/docs/development/configurable-accounts.md

The portal is a canonical runtime that derives the token from msg.sender and does not call the PoolManager. A revert only fails the caller's own take. The fast path requires both operand high limbs at most the modulus high limb, which bounds each operand below twice the modulus, and it handles the carry out of the sum. For modulus 2^256-1 the folded sum plus carry cannot overflow because a carry implies the sum is at most 2^256-2, and a result equal to the modulus is mapped to zero. These are the paths of mulmod(a, b, not(0)) at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/stablecoin-l1.work/ruint/ruint-1.21.1/src/modular.rs; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-25

- Tempo, cycle 20. Does a validator still on tempo/v1.19.0 (evm2 66687c18) compute something different from the v1.19.1 endpoint (evm2 35aa3280) in any instruction the PoolManager uses?. Result: No. The arithmetic, bitwise, signed, control, memory, keccak, stack and jump destination files are byte identical. host.rs moves the SSTORE threshold below which a cold slot is not loaded from 2,000 to 2,100 remaining gas after the 100 gas static charge; a cold SSTORE needs 2,100 more gas in both revisions, so both halt the frame out of gas in that window and differ only in whether the slot was loaded first. system.rs refactors call gas and refunds EIP-8037 new-account state gas to the caller's reservoir when a value-carrying call that would create its target fails; that changes the gas left, not the success flag or return data of the call. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/35aa32800b147b00e616d4e1869a3835aa86701f/crates/evm2/src/interpreter/instructions/host.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/evm2/src/interpreter/instructions/host.rs; research/network-risk/cycles/020/stablecoin-l1.work/evm2 and research/network-risk/cycles/020/stablecoin-l1.work/evm2_66687c18

- Tempo, cycle 23. L-551 and the Tempo half of L-416: can any transaction carry sender address zero to a target of the sender's choice, through a system transaction, a type 0x76 primitive signature, a fee payer signature, a keychain signature naming user_address zero, a key authorization, or a T14 configurable account signature naming account zero?. Result: No. A system transaction (legacy, signature (0,0)) is the only envelope that recovers to zero (envelope.rs 29, 379-384), and the block executor accepts it only with target address zero (cycle 20, block.rs 617-660). Primitive secp256k1, P256 and WebAuthn signatures derive the address from a public key, which needs a keccak preimage of a zero address. A keychain signature returns its claimed user_address after checking only the inner signature (tt_signature.rs 951-976); prepare_keychain then requires user_address to equal the signer (handler.rs 670-676) and either loads an active key of that account from the keychain precompile (validate_keychain_authorization, account_keychain/mod.rs 1309-1333, handler.rs 717-744) or, for a key authorized in the same transaction, requires the authorization to be signed by the account itself (handler.rs 566-573 before T6) or by an admin key the keychain already holds for it (handler.rs 776-792). A full-history scan of the keychain precompile at 0xAAAAAAAA00..00 found 14616 KeyAuthorized and 17 AdminKeyAuthorized logs and none for account zero, and the precompile's own authorizeKey requires msg.sender to be tx.origin. A configurable account signature with account zero is refused when it is decoded (ZeroAccount, primitives configurable_account/mod.rs 332-335, 477-490), and an unregistered account must equal the address derived from its configuration (384-414). So address zero, Tempo's protocolFeeController, cannot call setProtocolFee or collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35, 47). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/evm/src/handler.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/primitives/src/transaction/tt_signature.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/primitives/src/transaction/key_authorization.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/primitives/src/transaction/configurable_account/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/account_keychain/mod.rs; research/network-risk/cycles/023/stablecoin-l1.work/l551/keyscan.json

- Arc, cycle 23. L-957: a native take to an account destroyed earlier in the same transaction, read in arc-node v0.8.6 crates/evm/src/evm.rs, and what it does to the PoolManager either way. Result: The value frame hook loads the target inside a checkpoint and, when it is marked self-destructed, returns a metered revert with ERR_SELFDESTRUCTED_BALANCE_INCREASED before any value moves (evm.rs 569-593). The PoolManager's native transfer then sees success false and reverts with NativeTransferFailed (src/types/Currency.sol:45-53), which undoes the debit that take recorded first (src/PoolManager.sol:291-295) and the whole unlock. If the unpublished builds behaved otherwise and moved the value, the amount would still be debited to the caller of take before the transfer, so only the caller's own credit would leave. Neither outcome reaches other users' funds; the branch itself was not exercised on the running builds. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/v0.8.6/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; src/types/Currency.sol:40-53; src/PoolManager.sol:291-296

- Tempo, cycle 25. A pool whose currency is the T14 configurable account precompile address 0xAACC... (or any address that gains a precompile at a fork): can it hold or release value before or after T14?. Result: No. Before T14 the address has no code, so sync's balanceOf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) gets empty return data and reverts in decoding, and after T14 balanceOf reverts with aa4bc69a. With sync impossible, nobody can settle a debt in that currency (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so no liquidity in it can exist, and take of it (which pays nothing on a codeless address) only moves the caller's own credit. - Tempo, cycle 25. T14 deferred verification: can an ordinary account use the window between notarization and finalization to undo a payment and keep a payout?. Result: No. Only a proposer can put a block with wrong execution in front of the validators, and such a block is not finalized under either mode. Settlement inside the PoolManager is atomic per transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so a transaction is either in a finalized block whole or not at all. What remains is operator level and liveness. Evidence: https://github.com/tempoxyz/tempo/pull/8438

- Tempo, cycle 27. TIP-1060 Refund mode charges 245,000 gas upfront for every zero to nonzero write in a transaction, including slots cleared earlier in the same transaction, and refunds only after the top-level frame. Can an ordinary account use this to make other users' PoolManager calls fail?. Result: No loss or freeze path. The PoolManager forwards all remaining gas to hooks and native recipients (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/types/Currency.sol:48) and never caps a sub-call, so the charge only raises the gas limit a user's own transaction must carry. The writes that can go from zero to nonzero in a swap (feeGrowthGlobal at src/libraries/Pool.sol:446-448, tick crossings at Pool.sol:602, liquidity at Pool.sol:427) are the ones F-064 already prices at TIP-1000 rates; ERC-6909 balances (src/ERC6909.sol:17, PoolManager.sol:322-336) are the caller's own. A withdrawal clears slots and mints credits rather than creating them. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/tips/tip-1060.md ; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/tips/tip-1000.md ; research/network-risk/cycles/027/stablecoin-l1.work/out/trace-a64-r0r1.json, trace-a64-r1r3.json, trace-a64-r2r3.json
- Arc, cycle 27. L-1071 for Arc: cache library and key of the execution cache and precompile cache in reth v2.2.0 (88505c7f), which arc-node main pins for reth-engine-tree and reth-execution-cache. Result: The execution cache (crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs lines 84 and 669-675) uses fixed-cache 0.1.8 with keys B256 code hash, (Address, StorageKey) and Address; fixed-cache's get compares the stored key with key.equivalent before returning a value (src/lib.rs lines 314-339), so a hash collision returns a miss, not another slot's value. The precompile cache (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs lines 44 and 184-186) is a moka cache per precompile address keyed by the whole input bytes plus the spec, and caches only successful outputs. The fixed-cache crate checksum c41c7aa6 matches arc-node's lock. Arc's endpoints run unpublished commits, so this reads the closest published source. The consensus-visible changes between the builds are the memory limit (unreachable by gas), the EIP-3607 gate (Tempo's version keeps EIP-7702), the modexp shortcut (same output and gas) and the T15-gated cold load skip (inactive). The interpreter and storage files are byte equal. Tempo's execution crates that cycle 19 listed as transaction callers (block.rs, handler.rs, handler/config.rs, instructions.rs, evm.rs, context.rs, the TIP-20 precompile, the fee manager, storage credits, the zone executor and the payload builder) are byte equal between a9d6748 and c0c9372. Result: 137 of 137 calls equal to the reference with and without the T14 time, so the lock, the delta count and the settlement logic behave the same after T14 on the new build. Evidence: eth_simulateV1 on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz (2026-11-27); research/network-risk/cycles/033/stablecoin-l1.work/scen-4217-t14.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/033/stablecoin-l1.work/scen-4217-now.json ; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114
- Arc, cycle 33. Lead L-1247: whether the face rounding loop on Arc (sync of the 0x3600 face, a forced native send, settle, take) can pay. Measured base fee and gas prices on the current builds, and looked for a cheaper forced send. Result: The base fee was 20 gwei in all 10,240 blocks to 33,414,439. Of 3,301 transactions in 2,000 sampled blocks (types 0, 2 and 4), none paid below 20 gwei. The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function, and a native settle after a token sync reverts with NonzeroNativeValue, so a forced send still needs SELFDESTRUCT. A contract created earlier can SELFDESTRUCT under EIP-6780 for about 7,600 gas, which is cheaper than CREATE plus SELFDESTRUCT. The loop's gain is bounded by the residue anyway. After one round the PoolManager's native balance is a multiple of 10^12, so the gain is only the remainder present at that moment: 558,794,715,662 wei (about 0.00000056 USD) at block 0x1fdddc5. One round's gas at 20 gwei is far above that, and no repeat yields more. The loop costs more than it can take. Do the cycle 28 to 31 binary lifts of v1.19.1 (arithmetic handlers with ruint mul_mod_by_ref, div_rem_by_ref, rem_by_ref, add_mod_by_ref and div_rem_bits_plus_one, jump destination analysis, keccak, transient storage) speak for the v1.19.2 binary that mainnet runs?. Result: Yes for x86_64. So the results that FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 48, 112), SqrtPriceMath (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252), TickMath (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63, 80-111, 142-150) and the transient delta and lock code (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/Lock.sol:13) depend on come from the same machine code that was lifted and run before. ## Reading of the source (flow-liquidity)

- all 21 networks, cycle 2. Can one owner change or withdraw another owner's position through modifyLiquidity, including by reusing a salt, by passing ticks of another position, or by removing more than it holds. Result: No. The position is looked up under keccak256 of owner, tickLower, tickUpper and salt, and the owner is always msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:161, src/libraries/Position.sol:34-41). The assembly lays the four fields out as 20, 3, 3 and 32 bytes without overlap, and bytes above the address fall outside the hashed range (Position.sol:54-66). I rebuilt the layout byte for byte and compared it with the packed encoding that test/libraries/Position.t.sol:75-80 expects on 3,000 random inputs, with dirty upper bits in the owner word. A removal larger than the position reverts in LiquidityMath.addDelta (Position.sol:88, src/libraries/LiquidityMath.sol:10-18), after the tick updates, and the revert undoes those. In 6,000 random sequences on a Python transcription, every attempt by a second owner, by the same owner under a different salt, or for one unit more than the position held reverted. Evidence: src/libraries/Position.sol:34-67
- all 21 networks, cycle 2. Order of the steps inside Pool.modifyLiquidity: tick update, bitmap flip, fee growth read, Position.update, tick clearing, and the three price cases for the amounts. Covered add, remove, zero delta, full range, one spacing, ranges above, below and around the current tick, and several owners on shared ticks. Result: The order is sound. A new tick gets its feeGrowthOutside before the fee growth inside the range is read (src/libraries/Pool.sol:160-162, 533-539, 184-185). A tick whose liquidityGross returns to zero is deleted only after the last position has been paid from its values (Pool.sol:187-203). A position that still has liquidity keeps both its ticks alive, because liquidityGross is the sum of the positions on the tick, so its checkpoint can never meet a re-initialized tick. A position with zero liquidity earns nothing at its next update because fees use the liquidity held before the update (src/libraries/Position.sol:82-97). Amounts use slot0.tick for the range test and the stored sqrt price for the in range case, add rounds up and remove rounds down (Pool.sol:206-237, src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288). I transcribed Pool, Position, TickBitmap, LiquidityMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath and TickMath into Python and ran 6,000 random sequences (254,069 operations, 50,789 of them reverts) with four owners, two salts, spacings 1, 10, 60, 200, 2000 and 32767, start prices in the middle and within 3,000 ticks of both ends, swaps, donations and protocol fees. After every operation liquidityGross and liquidityNet of each tick equalled the sums over positions, the bitmap bit was set exactly for ticks with liquidityGross above zero, pool liquidity equalled the liquidity of positions in range at slot0.tick, and the pool never owed more of either currency than it had received. At the end every position could be removed in full and all tick data was gone. A second set of 6,000 sequences without swaps or donations, 3,614 of them started in the state where slot0.tick is one below the tick of the price, paid no fees to anyone and left no owner with more than it had paid in. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238
- all 21 networks, cycle 2. Can an ordinary account make a hookless victim position impossible to remove, or leave a tick that can no longer be updated. Listed every revert on the removal path. Result: No path found for a token with fewer than 2^127 base units. On removal the cap is not checked (src/libraries/Pool.sol:165). liquidityGross cannot underflow because it is the sum of the positions. liquidityNet stays inside int128 because its size is bounded by liquidityGross, and the cap is at most 6076470837873901133274546561281575204 (spacing 32767), below 2^127. The same bound keeps pool liquidity inside uint128 when ticks are crossed. flipTick cannot revert for a tick that was initialized, since only aligned ticks can be initialized (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:47-75). FullMath.mulDiv in Position.update cannot revert because the product of a 256 bit growth difference and a 128 bit liquidity divided by 2^128 fits in 256 bits. The casts of the principal amounts can revert for a very large position, and the owner then removes in parts. The sum of principal and fees can exceed int128, and the owner then collects fees with a zero delta first (src/PoolManager.sol:171). What remains is the known case of uncollected fees of 2^127 base units or more (F-005). I checked whether flash accounting gives a cheaper route to that bound: it does not. An account that is the only liquidity in range can donate to itself at no cost and wrap feeGrowthGlobal past 2^256, as the comment at Pool.sol:80-82 says, but positions out of range see no change in their fee growth inside, and after later tick crossings they are owed only real swap fees (six self donations of 2^127 - 1 units in the transcription, then swaps through both victim ranges). When a victim is in range, its share of a donation is real value the donor has to pay. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:159-238
- all 21 networks, cycle 2. Hook deltas on liquidity changes: can afterAddLiquidity or afterRemoveLiquidity move more than the caller's own delta, which hook runs for a zero delta, and what a hook that calls modifyLiquidity itself can skip. Result: The caller delta after the hook is the pool delta minus the hook delta, and the hook is credited the hook delta, so the two always add up to principal plus fees (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:219-244, src/PoolManager.sol:171-183). The hook delta is read only when the matching return-delta bit is set, and then the return data must be exactly 64 bytes (Hooks.sol:159-168). A zero delta runs the remove hooks (Hooks.sol:201-205, 220-244). When the hook itself is the caller, the hook calls are skipped and no delta is taken (Hooks.sol:171-175, 217). A pool without a hook has none of these paths. The hazard for pools whose liquidity providers chose a hook is already recorded as F-004. One comment differs from the code: src/interfaces/IHooks.sol:50 and 81 say the delta passed to the after hooks includes the hook delta, while the code passes principal plus fees before the hook delta is known. This changes no balance. Evidence: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:195-245
- all 21 networks, cycle 2. donate from entry to the last delta: who is debited, who can receive, rounding, the tick and price mismatch at a boundary, and whether a donation can be redirected away from positions that were in range. Result: The donor is debited the two amounts, each cast to int128, and fee growth rises by amount times 2^128 divided by the liquidity in range, rounded down (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480, src/PoolManager.sol:256-276). A donation reverts when no liquidity is in range. The rounding remainder is below one base unit per donation and stays in the PoolManager. In the transcription each in range position was owed at most its exact share and the shares never added up to more than the donation, across all donations in 6,000 sequences. Positions out of range were unchanged. The two concrete values of test/PoolManager.t.sol:841-864 (34028236692093846346337 and 68056473384187692692674 for 100 and 200 units on 1e18 liquidity) come out of the source formula. Two things can redirect a donation, and both are stated in src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:150-155: liquidity added just before the donation takes a share, and after a zeroForOne swap that ends exactly on a tick, slot0.tick is one below the tick of the price, so the donation goes to the range below. Does the liquidity path give the same amounts on each network's EVM. Sent read-only eth_call probes to the PositionManager listed in networks.json: a multicall that initializes a new native pool and mints a position above the price, and a second set that mints and burns the same position in one call. Each probe was sent once with exactly the value the source formulas require and once with one wei less. Result: All 20 networks agree with the source formulas to the wei. Mint and burn probes (6 per network): the caller owes exactly one wei, which is the gap between rounding up on add and rounding down on remove, and the call fails with zero value. - Zora, Base, cycle 2. Lead L-133, second half: is there a hook that must add liquidity on a tick an attacker can fill cheaply. Read the Zora coin hook, which adds liquidity inside afterSwap. Result: Not affected at realistic prices. CoinRewardsV4.mintLpReward runs inside afterSwap without a try block and adds a position one spacing wide that starts two spacings away from the current tick (CoinRewardsV4.sol lines 134-204, ZoraV4CoinHook.sol line 415 on the main branch). A full tick there would make every swap in the pool revert. The fill cost near the current tick is the cap times about 0.01 divided by the sqrt price in currency0, or times the sqrt price in currency1. With the cap of 3.8e34 for spacing 200 this is above the whole supply of a coin with 1e27 base units unless the price ratio in base units is beyond about 1e11, which only the far ends of the tick range reach.
