- all 21 networks, cycle 7. Trail of Bits audit, settlement invariants UNI-SETTLE-1 to UNI-SETTLE-13: a settle never raises what the user is owed beyond the amount paid, the amount paid equals what reached the singleton, and burn, mint and clear move the delta and the claim balance by exactly the stated amount. Result: The source has these properties for a token whose balance changes only by transfers. settle credits msg.value or the checked balance difference and nothing else (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). burn adds the amount to the caller's delta and removes it from the claim balance of from after the operator or allowance check (332-336, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/ERC6909.sol:85-89). mint does the reverse (322-329). clear accepts only the exact positive delta and sets it to zero (310-319). Every amount passes toInt128, which rejects 2^127 and above (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59). Reliance: UNI-SETTLE-3 rests on A2 and A3. It fails by design for a token whose balanceOf rises without a transfer from the settler, and the ledger lists those per network (F-041, F-066, F-067, F-079, F-081, F-091). Evidence: docs/security/audits/TrailOfBits_audit_core.pdf printed pages 19-20; src/PoolManager.sol:300-336, 349-378; src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22
- all 21 networks, cycle 7. Trail of Bits audit, take invariants UNI-TAKE-1 to UNI-TAKE-3: after a take the caller's delta falls by the amount, the recipient's balance rises by it and the singleton's balance falls by it. Result: UNI-TAKE-1 holds from the source alone: the debit is written before the transfer and the call reverts as a whole if the transfer fails (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-53, 81-86). UNI-TAKE-2 and UNI-TAKE-3 rest on A3 and A4 and the source cannot enforce them: the token branch accepts an empty answer or a 32 byte 1 and makes no code size check (Currency.sol:64-74), so a take of an address without code moves nothing, and a token may deliver less to the recipient or charge the sender more. In each case the caller is debited the full amount, so the shortfall falls on the caller, except where a token charges the PoolManager on top, which the ledger holds as F-092 for Ethereum, Arc and BNB Smart Chain. Unit theme-transfer-side-effects of this cycle searches for further tokens of that kind. Evidence: docs/security/audits/TrailOfBits_audit_core.pdf printed page 21; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297; src/types/Currency.sol:40-88
- all 21 networks, cycle 7. Trail of Bits audit, end to end and inter-action invariants UNI-E2E-1 to UNI-E2E-3 and UNI-ACTION-1 to UNI-ACTION-5: no delta is left when the manager locks again, a round trip swap gives no gain, and what is owed to an actor or to the protocol never exceeds the singleton's balance. Result: The source enforces the first directly: unlock reverts unless the count of nonzero deltas is zero and then closes the lock (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113), and the count moves only in _accountDelta when a delta enters or leaves zero (368-378). The others follow from the rounding directions, which I read again: amounts owed by the caller round up and amounts paid to the caller round down in liquidity changes (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288) and in each swap step (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:63-105), and protocol fees are carved out of the fee the swapper already owes (src/libraries/Pool.sol:385-398). Earlier cycles replayed these with models and with the repository tests. Reliance: A2 for the balance side and A1 for the delta count. UNI-ACTION-6 is in the first finding of this file. Whether the ruint 1.21.0 mul_mod fault described in OPCODES.md:120-136, which needs a modulus of four 64 bit limbs and a quotient of the product by the modulus within 2^129 of 2^256, can be reached by any MULMOD of this bytecode, for any input, on a node that runs that release. Result: No. Five MULMODs have the constant modulus 2^256-1 (four limbs), and the inputs of their callers bound the product: liquidity << 96 times a price difference or a price (2^384), a fee growth difference times liquidity (2^384), an amount times Q96 (2^352), an amount times a fee below 10^6, liquidity times a price difference (2^288). Their quotient is at most 2^128. Of the other eight, six have a modulus of at most three limbs: the constants 2^128, 2^96 and 10^6, liquidity (uint128), a sqrt price (uint160) and 10^6 minus the fee. The remaining two take n1 + product and n1 - product of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (SqrtPriceMath.sol:47 and 71), with a product n1 * sqrtPX96 below 2^384. A four limb modulus of at least 2^192 then leaves a quotient below 2^192. Both conditions of the fault never hold together in this code, whatever the input. This is stronger than the in-pool argument of OPCODES.md. Evidence: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24

Removing every E from the default sequence gives a byte identical runtime, and so does removing the first two of the three L. Only the third L (in CTUca[r]LSs) changes the output, and the build fails with stack too deep without it. Rerunning the Yul optimizer of the same compiler on the unoptimized IR up to that L and through it, with tstore and tload substituted by operations of the same storage and memory effect so that the Yul front end accepts the code, shows 32 replaced loads and no replaced keccak256. ## Reading of the source (optimizer-bug)

- all 21 networks, cycle 9. Part one. Which entries of the Solidity bug list apply to solc 0.8.26 with the settings of foundry.toml (via IR, optimizer on with 44,444,444 runs and the default Yul step sequence, Cancun), fetched again on 2026-11-24, and what SOL-2026-7 needs according to the primary source. Result: bugs_by_version.json lists eight entries for 0.8.26 (released 2024-05-21). By the conditions field of bugs.json six can apply to this build: SOL-2026-8 OverlappingRecursiveStorageStructCopyCorruptionViaIR (viaIR, introduced 0.8.13, fixed 0.8.39, needs a storage-to-storage copy of a recursive struct with a dynamic array into a target that contains the source), SOL-2026-7 YulOptimizerKnowledgeBaseStaleBookkeeping (yulOptimizer, 0.8.19 to 0.8.37, fixed 0.8.38, severity low), SOL-2026-6 MisorderedNamedParametersInRequireWithCustomErrors (viaIR, introduced 0.8.26, fixed 0.8.37, needs require(cond, Error({name: value})) ), SOL-2026-4 SpillSlotCollisionAcrossMutualRecursion (viaIR, fixed 0.8.37, needs a cycle of at least two mutually recursive functions), SOL-2026-2 UnsoundSpillInMutualRecursion (viaIR, fixed 0.8.36, needs intersecting recursive cycles) and SOL-2025-1 LostStorageArrayWriteOnSlotOverflow (no conditions, fixed 0.8.32, needs a storage array that crosses slot 2^256). Two cannot apply by their conditions: SOL-2026-8 for the evmasm pipeline (viaIR false) and SOL-2026-5 MemoryByteArrayElementDeleteClearsWholeWord (viaIR false). The post of 2026-10-22 confirms SOL-2026-7: affected steps LoadResolver (L) and EqualStoreEliminator (E), both in the default sequence; the trigger is a variable used to compute memory or storage addresses that is reassigned, one address derived from its value before and one after the reassignment with different constant offsets, and the two addresses equal at run time; then a load is replaced with an outdated value, a store of an equal value is removed, or a keccak256 is replaced. The fix is in 0.8.38 and is confined to KnowledgeBase and DataFlowAnalyzer. The default sequence in libsolidity/interface/OptimiserSettings.h at v0.8.26 contains three L and one E in the main part and none in the cleanup part fDnTOcmuO. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/solidity/develop/docs/bugs.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/solidity/develop/docs/bugs_by_version.json; https://blog.soliditylang.org/2026/10/22/yul-optimizer-knowledge-base-stale-bookkeeping-bug/; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/solidity/v0.8.26/libsolidity/interface/OptimiserSettings.h ; copies in research/network-risk/cycles/009/core-code-optimizer-bug.work/dl/

The Yul of the Solidity pipeline was taken just before and just after that L (prefix sequences with an empty cleanup, no substitution of tload or tstore needed): the runtime loses 68 mload and 5 sload, no keccak256, tload or store changes (L3-loadcount.json). The 18 Yul functions where loads disappear were searched for variables assigned without let and for every mload, sload, mstore, sstore and keccak256 whose address uses such a variable or one derived from it (L3-reassign.json). In 17 of them no memory or storage address uses a reassigned variable, so the precondition of the bug is absent; this covers initialize, the five modifyLiquidity copies, beforeModifyLiquidity, updateTick (two sloads of the same TickInfo slot, Pool.sol:526-527), transferOwnership and onlyOwner (owner slot 0). In fun_swap 12 loads are replaced: 6 of params (a function argument, never reassigned), 2 of the step struct memPtr_1 (declared once, Pool.sol:340), and 4 of the named return result, which is assigned memPtr at the top and memPtr again only on the early return that leaves at once (Pool.sol:320). For all 12 there is no memory write and no call between the earlier load or store and the replaced load (L3-swap-replacements.json), so no aliasing decision of the KnowledgeBase was involved. The loads after the tick clamps (Pool.sol:351-356) stay. With nothing replaced across a store through a reassigned base, a compiler with the fix would make the same decisions on the same input. The lowest tick is -887,272 (MIN_TICK) and the highest is 887,271 (MAX_TICK - 1, at price MAX_SQRT_PRICE - 1). Six events lie beyond |tick| 400,000. - MegaETH, cycle 10. Part two (c), lead L-607: did the block producer roll back the transient unlock flag, the transient deltas and the pool storage of a PoolManager frame that reverted, in mined transactions where a later frame of the same transaction completed an unlock? The test compares, for each transaction, the receipt that the sequencer wrote with the status and surviving logs of debug_traceTransaction (callTracer, withLog) on the replica, which re-executes on the same pre-state. Result: Yes. 7,627 transactions emitted PoolManager Swap or ModifyLiquidity logs between blocks 30,862,220 and 32,724,219. In 1,347 of them a frame that entered PoolManager.unlock reverted. In 1,333 of those the reverted frame contained a swap, the quoter pattern, and a later unlock in the same transaction completed. The receipt status and every surviving log equal the re-execution in all 7,627, with no trace errors. Had the producer kept the unlock flag (src/libraries/Lock.sol), the later unlock would revert with AlreadyUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:105). Had it kept the deltas (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol), the later unlock would fail with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Had it kept the reverted swap's slot0, the later Swap event would carry other prices. The window has no settle, take or sync inside a reverted frame. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/frames.py, research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/raw/frames.json; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc debug_traceTransaction and eth_getTransactionReceipt 2026-11-24
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Part three: whether a MegaETH per-frame budget (compute gas, data size, KV updates, state growth at 98/100 of the parent's remainder) or the detention cap after a volatile read can be breached in a child of the PoolManager's frame and caught there, so that the PoolManager continues with a failed subcall and returns another result than on Ethereum. Result: No. The resource limits spec says a child that exceeds its budget reverts with MegaLimitExceeded and the parent may continue. Every call the PoolManager makes treats failure as fatal: hooks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137), native and ERC-20 transfers (src/types/Currency.sol:48-52, 73-86), balanceOf, a high-level call that reverts on failure (src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/PoolManager.sol:285, 359), and unlockCallback (src/PoolManager.sol:110). The PoolManager reads gas() only to forward it. A breach below the PoolManager therefore reverts the PoolManager frame as a whole. A breach in the PoolManager's own frame reverts it as a whole for its caller. A transaction-level breach halts the transaction. The outcome is either the Ethereum result or a full revert, never a partial result. A token or hook that catches its own failed subcall is a token or hook matter and is not swept here. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md (Per-Call-Frame Runtime Budgets); src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137; src/types/Currency.sol:44-95
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Lead L-610: which per-frame budget a swap that crosses many initialized ticks reaches first, and whether a liquidity removal can reach one. Result: State growth binds first. Each crossing writes feeGrowthOutside0 and feeGrowthOutside1 of one tick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-612). A write counts as state growth only when the slot was zero at transaction start (resource accounting, Storage Slot Growth Rules). Outside values are zero only for ticks initialized above the current tick (Pool.sol:533-538), so an upward swap through freshly planted ticks adds up to 2 per tick. The PoolManager frame at depth 1 gets 980 of the 1,000 per-transaction limit, so it reverts with MegaLimitExceeded after about 490 such ticks, at roughly 24 million compute gas from 2 cold loads, 2 fresh SSTOREs and a bitmap load per tick, inferred from standard gas costs and not measured. Ticks with nonzero outside values cost about 14,000 compute gas per crossing. 200 million compute gas then allows about 14,000 crossings, 28,000 KV updates and 1.1 MB of data size, far below the shares of 490,000 KV updates and 12.8 MB. The swapper can stop at a price limit and continue in a later transaction (Pool.sol:344), and each planted tick adds growth only on its first upward crossing. A removal touches two ticks and one position (Pool.sol:146-238). Cycle 1 recorded the same bound qualitatively. The result is a delay without loss, and an eth_call measurement through a router was not run. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-accounting.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md; src/libraries/Pool.sol:520-545, 602-612
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Part four, lead L-601: is Rex6 active on MegaETH mainnet, and what does it change for the instruction set the PoolManager uses?. Result: Active. The network upgrades overview gives Rex6 mainnet activation at timestamp 1787626800 (25 Aug 2026 03:00 UTC). mega-evm v1.7.3 scheduled it (#371), and the latest block read, 32,724,090, has timestamp 1795521101. Rex6 changes no opcode result. It sets one order for storage-gas and compute-gas charging (only CREATE2 changes), returns forwarded gas to the parent when a CALL or CREATE halts on the compute limit, adds a 32 byte data-size base per log, extends beneficiary detection to SELFDESTRUCT and EIP-7702 delegates, and corrects CREATE, EIP-7702, KeylessDeploy, fee-reward and system-transaction accounting. The PoolManager uses none of CREATE2, SELFDESTRUCT or KeylessDeploy. Its logs add 32 bytes each against a 13.1 MB limit. The forwarded-gas change affects gas_used only. The earlier 550-script pmdiff runs on MegaETH were made on 2026-11-24, after activation. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/network-upgrades/overview.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/network-upgrades/rex6.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/CHANGELOG.md; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc eth_getBlockByNumber latest 2026-11-24
- MegaETH, cycle 10. ruint advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0220, which affects every release before 1.20.0. mega-evm main pins ruint 1.19.0 and the stateless validator pins 1.17.2. In those releases wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr on 256 bit values truncate the shift amount modulo 2^32, and the overflowing and checked shift flags give false negatives. Result: Not reachable from the PoolManager's bytecode. revm v112 (interpreter 37.0.3) calls ruint's shift only when shift < 256 and returns zero or the sign fill otherwise, for SHL, SHR and SAR. BYTE calls byte() only for index < 32 (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). The advisory says the shifted values were correct and only the flag was wrong, apart from the truncation above 2^32, which the guard excludes. The battery of OPCODES.md had already passed shift amounts at and above 256 on MegaETH. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2026-0220.md; https://github.com/alloy-rs/ruint/pull/603; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/v112/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/bitwise.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/Cargo.lock

Result: All 1774545 ticks from -887272 to 887272 except 887272 give back their own tick (0 mismatches); 887272 maps to MAX_SQRT_PRICE, which getTickAtSqrtPrice rejects by design (TickMath.sol:123-130), and none of the 62895279 compiled products (38051663 inline literal multiplies through mul_with_bit_size, the rest variable products through monad_vm_runtime_mul; 0 full width literal multiplies, since TickMath has none) differs from Python integers (0 failures). This covers the high bits 0x20000, 0x40000 and 0x80000 of the absolute tick, which mined swaps reach rarely or never. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/wholetick.py; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/wholetick-summary.json
- Monad, cycle 10. Correction to the cycle 9 note on mined coverage of the compiled MULMOD by 2^96. The 183 Monad swaps of opcodes/monad-rounding.json carry the rounding bit of SqrtPriceMath.sol:252, which is the MULMOD at pc 23094. Result: That MULMOD follows the JUMPDEST at pc 23092 where mulDiv returns, so its modulus arrives from another block and the compiler does not know it as a literal. It compiles to the runtime call with the shared 256 bit library, not to mul_mod2. The mined swaps therefore test the shared library, which earlier cycles also tested through simulated calls, and say nothing about pc 22378 or 22639. The answer for those two sites rests on the transcription above. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/sites.json (pc 23094 operands unknown); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/virtual_stack.cpp lines 281-311
- Monad, cycle 10. Which mined Monad results exercise each compiled path, from 1,580 Swap events of 31 pools in blocks 124,993,964 to 124,996,219 read with eth_getLogs. Result: The TickMath literal multiplies and the multiply by 255738958999603826347141 run on every swap, and bits 0x1 to 0x40000 of the absolute tick all appear in the emitted ticks (0x20000 in 844 swaps, 0x40000 in 463), while 0x80000 appears in none. The general mulDiv 512 bit branch, with the multiply by 3 at pc 22935 and the runtime inverse products, is reachable in these pools: 751 consecutive pairs have (liquidity << 96) times the price at or above 2^256. pc 22639 needs liquidity times the price step at or above 2^256; the largest liquidity seen has 74 bits and the largest product 159 bits, so no mined swap in the window ran it. pc 22378 runs only in Position.update when the fee growth difference times the liquidity reaches 2^256, and ModifyLiquidity events do not carry amounts, so no mined result shows it. The way to confirm either site from blocks without sending a transaction is to find a mined swap or liquidity change whose inputs cross that bound and compare the token amounts of its Swap event or of the token Transfer events with the formulas; none was found in the window. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/chain.json (eth_getLogs and eth_getCode on https://rpc.monad.xyz); src/libraries/Position.sol:94-96; src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:234-254
- Monad, cycle 10. Whether an ordinary account can steer a victim pool into the two inline MULMOD sites, which would matter if they were wrong. Result: It can for pc 22639: liquidity per tick may reach about 2^107 at tick spacing 1, so an account can add liquidity above 2^96 in a range near the top price, paying little token0, and a later swap into that range computes getAmount1Delta through the 512 bit branch. pc 22378 needs fee growth times liquidity at or above 2^256, which a donation to a pool with little liquidity can produce. Both sites compute the specified remainder in the transcription, so steering execution there gains nothing. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:465-480; src/libraries/Pool.sol:565-582; src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:234-254; src/libraries/Position.sol:94-96; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/run-summary.json
- Monad, cycle 10. EXP code generation (exp_optimized, emitter.cpp 8221-8363), including a power of two base with a variable exponent, where the exponent is multiplied by log2 of the base with a shift or an imul and replaced by the raw exponent on overflow. Result: The PoolManager has no EXP instruction in its code; the 0x0a byte at pc 24008 is in the metadata trailer, so this path cannot change any PoolManager result. The variable exponent path was still transcribed and gave 2^(k n) mod 2^256 for 1,000,000 cases with k from 2 to 255. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 8221-8363; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/run-summary.json

The release notes list v0.16.5 on mainnet from 2026-10-22, v0.16.6 with tags only, and v0.16.7 on testnet from 2026-11-19 and not on mainnet. Result: The 27 functions transcribed here (mulx through mul_mod2, mul_optimized, modop_optimized, exp_optimized and its gas helpers, is_uint64_bounded) are byte identical at v0.16.5, v0.16.6 and v0.16.7, emitter.cpp is identical between v0.16.6 and v0.16.7, and math.S is identical in all three. v0.16.6 changes negate, which mul_optimized uses only for a negated power of two literal, and the PoolManager has none. No release note names a change to multiplication. The same question for the other 20 networks: does any of them run a compiled or rewritten multiplication path in block production that simulated calls do not reach. Result: No client read in earlier cycles for these networks compiles EVM code to native code in block production; BNB Smart Chain's fused instruction feature was removed in v1.8.0. ## Reading of the source (theme-closed-producers)

- MegaETH, cycle 11. Part one, lead L-626: every mined PoolManager transaction in blocks 2,900,000 to 30,862,219 and 32,724,220 to 32,731,000 (the windows cycle 10 did not trace), read with debug_traceTransaction (callTracer withLog) on the public replica, which re-executes with the stock interpreter, against the receipt that the sequencer's closed executor wrote. For liquidity removals, fee collections and payments inside a reverted frame, prestateTracer diffMode against eth_getStorageAt at the block (post values when the transaction is the last PoolManager transaction of its block, pre values at block-1 when it is the first). Result: 43,342 transactions traced, 0 errors, 0 status mismatches, 0 log mismatches. 8,580 had a PoolManager frame that was undone and in 8,481 a later unlock completed, so the producer rolled back the unlock flag (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). 87 transactions ran take inside a reverted frame, 2 ran settle, 1 ran sync and 2 ran modifyLiquidity, and each was followed by work that completed with the receipt equal to re-execution, so the producer also rolled back the outgoing transfer and the negative delta of take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and the credit of settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). 151 transactions removed liquidity and 454 collected fees (ModifyLiquidity with negative or zero delta). 681 transactions were compared on storage: 2,042 post slots and 1,819 pre slots, 0 mismatches. The output kept details of the first 600 interesting transactions only; the counts cover all 43,342. With cycle 10 the receipts of 50,969 PoolManager transactions now equal re-execution. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-closed-producers.work/raw/mega.json (frames2.py mega.json); https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc
- MegaETH, cycle 11. Part one: is the public MegaETH stateless validator run by any party that publishes its results or mismatches?. Result: No public publisher was found. The documentation describes the validator, a fatal stop on any header commitment mismatch, and an optional --report-validation-endpoint that sends mega_setValidatedBlocks callbacks to an operator-chosen endpoint, but names no public operator or feed. L2BEAT lists state validation as fraud proofs with fewer than five external challengers. The validator was not run in this unit (no software built), so the producer's storage writes are covered by the replica's re-execution and eth_getStorageAt only, as above. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/node-operation/stateless-validation.md (lines 146, 249); https://l2beat.com/layer2s/projects/megaeth
- HyperEVM, cycle 11. Part two, lead L-627: do nanoreth and hyper-evm-sync compare state root and receipts root with what hl-node produced, and do they stop on a mismatch?. Result: Receipts yes, state no. nanoreth (commit f0cad31, the build at rpc.purroofgroup.com) checks gas used, receipts root and logs bloom after execution and returns an InsertBlockError on a mismatch, which leaves the block invalid and the node unable to advance. Its reth fork replaces the computed state root with zero before comparing it with the header, whose stateRoot is zero. hyper-evm-sync asserts receipts (success, cumulative gas, logs) and panics on a mismatch; its blake3 state hash is not compared. Both inject the results of HyperCore read precompiles from the block files. Both clients also carry the same 18 hard-coded state patches for improper self destructs in blocks 1,467,569 to 1,531,366, which shows that the validator once wrote state that stock revm would not; all are before the PoolManager's first log after block 45,998,366, and the PoolManager bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT. Recorded as an operator level information finding. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/f0cad31/src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/reth/14509628ed37e9a9b7110ea855a67f427c4d61fc/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_validator.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/f0cad31/src/node/evm/patch.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 11. Part two, leads L-627 and L-547: whole PoolManager history (blocks 45,998,000 to 52,124,000), receipt from the official validator endpoint against nanoreth's debug_traceTransaction, and storage for removals, fee collections and undone payments. Result: 2,762 transactions traced, 0 status or log mismatches. Three had a reverted frame that entered unlock followed by a completed unlock (0xb4d698a0... in block 49,336,714, 0x37a3f8b7... in block 50,968,220, 0x2d705617... in block 51,016,868). One, 0xb4d698a0..., ran sync, settle and take inside the reverted frame and the later unlock completed with a receipt equal to re-execution, so the validator rolled back the synced currency, the settle credit and the take transfer. 40 removals and 34 fee collections. 64 transactions compared on storage, 258 post and 227 pre slots, 0 mismatches, and 222 touched slots equal at latest on both endpoints. - Polygon, cycle 11. Part three, lead L-629: the newest 4,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 97,841,208 to 97,881,198, receipts from a bor v2.11.1 node (polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com reports bor/f2a2d63e69f6/v2.11.1-private) against serial re-execution by debug_traceTransaction on polygon.drpc.org, with storage for removals, fee collections and undone payments. Result: 4,000 traced, 0 errors, 0 status or log mismatches. 3,878 called sync, settle or settleFor. 19 had an undone PoolManager frame and in 17 a later unlock completed; 10 ran sync, settle and take inside the reverted frame (9 of them followed by a completed unlock). 48 removals and 38 fee collections. 89 transactions compared on storage (5 prestate calls failed), 426 post and 418 pre slots, 0 mismatches. Which block producers ran BlockSTM for a given block cannot be read from the chain, so this covers whatever the producers ran. - Polygon, cycle 11. Part three: in bor v2.11.1, are transient storage and the access list per transaction under BlockSTM, and does a re-executed incarnation start clean?. Result: Yes. Each incarnation builds its state from a fresh copy of the clean state (core/parallel_state_processor.go:127-138, setupEVM, cleanStateDB.Copy()). ApplyMessage reaches StateTransition, which calls Prepare (core/state_transition.go:561); Prepare creates a new access list (core/state/statedb.go:3023-3026) and a new transient storage map (statedb.go:3050-3051). Transient writes are journaled (statedb.go:1370-1376) and reverted with the frame (core/state/journal.go:419-421). Transient storage is not part of the multi-version write set: MVWriteList omits reverted keys (statedb.go:295-305) and ApplyMVWriteSet copies the incarnation's current value of each persistent path (statedb.go:693-702), so a storage write undone by a reverted frame is settled at its restored value. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/parallel_state_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/state/statedb.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/state_transition.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/state/journal.go

- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, X Layer, Zora, cycle 11. Reread of the fixed-cache 0.1.10 get and insert paths that every cache user in this list runs: key equality, lock protocol, epochs, and what a reader sees while a writer is inserting. Result: No path returns a hash for another input. calc (lib.rs lines 527-540) takes bucket = hash & (capacity - 1) and tag = hash & !(capacity - 1). Key and value are Copy types, so NEEDS_DROP is false and ALIVE_BIT is never set, and EPOCHS is false in both alloy texts, so the epoch bits are not used. The tag never has bit 0 set because the low 17 bits are masked off. get_inner (lines 322-350) succeeds only if a Relaxed load of the bucket state equals the tag exactly and a compare-exchange from tag to tag | LOCKED_BIT with Acquire succeeds (try_lock_ret, lines 593-606). While a writer holds the bucket the state carries LOCKED_BIT, so a reader's expected value does not match and it returns None and hashes the input itself. Under the lock the reader returns the stored value only if key.equivalent holds, which for [u8] against Key compares the slice of length len, so length and every byte must match (alloy keccak_cache.rs line 88 in 1.6.0, line 128 in 1.6.1). insert_inner (lines 389-439) takes the lock with expected None, which fails if the bucket is locked, writes key and value together, and releases with a Release store of the new tag (unlock, line 613). An ABA case in which another key with the same 64 bit hash replaces the entry between the reader's load and its compare-exchange leaves a reader that fails the equality test and recomputes. The value stored is imp(input) computed for the same input as the key (get_or_try_insert_with_ref, lines 506-524). This build has no lock-free read path: the string LOCK_FREE does not occur in lib.rs. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/fixed-cache/fixed-cache-0.1.10.crate (src/lib.rs); https://static.crates.io/crates/alloy-primitives/alloy-primitives-1.6.0.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/alloy-primitives/alloy-primitives-1.6.1.crate
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, X Layer, Zora, Worldchain, Celo, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, cycle 11. Result: Both do where the feature is on, and only the opcode result reaches the PoolManager. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer), 42.0.0 (Base) and 43.0.2 (op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1) implement KECCAK256 in instructions/system.rs lines 18-40 as KECCAK_EMPTY for length 0, else primitives::keccak256 over the memory slice, and revm-primitives 24.0.1, 42.0.0 and 43.0.0 re-export alloy_primitives::keccak256 (lib.rs lines 39-41). evm2 at rev 66687c18, which reth v2.11.0 runs, calls alloy_primitives::keccak256 in interpreter/instructions/crypto.rs lines 2 and 14. alloy-primitives utils/mod.rs lines 147-150 route keccak256 through keccak_cache::compute when keccak-cache-global is set. reth's trie hashes account and slot keys with the same function (crates/trie/common/src/key.rs line 16, hashed_state.rs line 55). Those hashed keys feed the state root. SLOAD and SSTORE look up the plain slot word, so a wrong trie key hash would give a wrong state root and a halted or forked node, while the slot the PoolManager reads and writes comes only from the KECCAK256 opcode result. Result: No wrong hash on any of the 14 endpoints. The bucket index is hash & (2^17 - 1) with hash = rapidhash_v3_micro_inline::<false, false>(input, RapidSecrets::seed(0)) (alloy keccak_cache.rs lines 48-60 in 1.6.0, 88-100 in 1.6.1; fixed-cache calc; rapidhash 4.4.1 and 4.5.1 v3/rapid_const.rs lines 236-310, which are identical in the two versions). The script transcribes that function in Python. A pool of 34,400 inputs (300 random inputs of each length 1 to 88, 3,000 delta-slot inputs of address word then currency word as CurrencyDelta.sol builds them, 2,000 mapping-slot inputs and 3,000 position-key inputs of 58 bytes as Position.sol builds them) fell into 3,723 buckets that hold two or more inputs. 3,528 of those buckets mix lengths and 1,556 hold a PoolManager-shaped input. Each bucket was sent as A B A B A B plus A without its last byte, A with an extra zero byte and A again. 300 extra groups put 87 byte inputs, which are cached, next to their 88 byte extensions, which skip the cache. That is 36,059 hashes per round, in chunks of 500 records, four requests at a time, three rounds per endpoint, 108,177 hashes per endpoint, all as specified. World Chain and Celo do not enable the cache by their manifests and served as controls. Polygon's eth_call does not reach Bor's block-import cache (next item). The transcription of rapidhash could not be compared with the compiled crate because building a Rust harness was not permitted in this session. If it is wrong, the inputs still exercise the cache at random buckets, and every result was checked. Celo: forno answered with reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, which matches the reth-node-core patch to celo-org/reth rev 74cc8bbc in celo-kona tag celo/reth-v1.0.10 (Cargo.toml line 466). The celo-reth crate (crates/celo-reth/Cargo.toml line 146) has default = ["std"] and no cache feature, its Dockerfile builds -p celo-reth with no features, and the patched reth-optimism-node at celo-org/optimism b08a8d0 has default = ["reth-codec"] (line 110). Its lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.0 with fixed-cache 0.1.8, the versions read for Arc. In one of three requests forno answered from a different backend, Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 (go1.24.13), which is a geth-family node with no alloy cache. No full cargo feature resolution was run, so a feature set by a crate outside those read cannot be excluded. The bucket test matched on both. - MegaETH, cycle 11. Does the public MegaETH stateless validator compile the keccak cache. Result: No. Its Cargo.lock (megaeth-labs/stateless-validator, main branch as fetched on 2026-11-24, version 2.1.0, mega-evm tag v1.7.3, revm 40.0.3, ruint 1.17.2) contains no fixed-cache package, and the alloy-primitives 1.6.0 entry does not list it as a dependency, so keccak-cache-global cannot be on in any build of that lock. The RPC node, mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc, is not public, and the bucket test on it found no mismatch. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/stateless-validator/main/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/stateless-validator/main/Cargo.toml
- Polygon, cycle 11. Bor v2.11.1, which the Polygon publicnode endpoint reports (bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private), adds its own cache of 64 byte KECCAK256 results. Can it return a hash for another input. Result: No. opKeccak256 (core/vm/instructions.go lines 259-290) uses the cache only when the input is exactly 64 bytes and evm.Config.Keccak256Cache is set. It copies all 64 bytes into a [64]byte key, and on a miss it hashes the data and stores (key, hash). Keccak256Cache is BoundedCache[[64]byte, common.Hash] (keccak_cache.go line 26), a sync.Map keyed by the whole array, written with LoadOrStore so an entry is never replaced, and capped at 65,536 entries, past which Store does nothing (bounded_cache.go lines 28-59). The cache is created per block in ProcessBlock (blockchain.go lines 1276-1288, 1328-1329 and 1348) and given to the prefetcher and the BlockSTM V2 workers. Speculative runs can only add pairs of an input and its true hash, which are right in any later run. eth_call does not set the field, so the bucket test on Polygon could not reach it. The 64 byte inputs it serves are the delta slots and mapping slots of src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:12-14 and src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:69-70. The same block adds an ecrecover result cache (core/vm/evm.go lines 57-87). The PoolManager source has no ecrecover or staticcall (grep of src/), so that cache is outside its path. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/instructions.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/keccak_cache.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/bounded_cache.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/blockchain.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/evm.go
- BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Avalanche, cycle 11. Do the other geth-family clients put a cache in front of KECCAK256. Result: Not in the sources read. BSC v1.8.2 (the version the BSC endpoint reports) computes crypto.Keccak256Hash(data) on every call (core/vm/instructions.go lines 232-243). The OffchainLabs go-ethereum master branch, which Nitro builds on, and the ava-labs libevm main branch, which avalanchego 1.15.3 builds on, reset a per-interpreter Keccak state and hash the data on every call (instructions.go lines 236-246 in both). For Nitro and libevm these are branch heads, not the commits the endpoints run. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/instructions.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/master/core/vm/instructions.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/main/core/vm/instructions.go
- Base, X Layer, cycle 11. L-633: X Layer pins ruint 1.18.0 and Base ruint 1.19.0, inside RUSTSEC-2026-0220. Does every SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE handler of the revm-interpreter they pin clamp the amount before calling ruint, and does any precompile or handler they run call a ruint shift with an unclamped amount. Result: The handlers clamp, and the other code read has no unclamped shift. The advisory says the shifted values of overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr were right and only the overflow flag was wrong, and that wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr took the amount modulo 2^32. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer) and 42.0.0 (Base) convert the amount with as_usize_saturated (macros.rs lines 122-126) and call << and >> (which are wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr) and arithmetic_shr only when the amount is below 256, else return 0 or the sign fill. BYTE indexes only below 32 (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). SIGNEXTEND shifts by at most 247 (arithmetic.rs lines 126-136). A Python transcription of the ruint 1.19.0 u256 paths of wrapping_shl, wrapping_shr and arithmetic_shr (bits.rs lines 437-467, 573-603, 612-623) matched the EVM definition on 509,184 cases covering every amount 0 to 255. A grep of revm-precompile 36.0.3 and 42.0.1, op-revm 20.0.0, revm-handler 20.0.3 and 42.0.1, alloy-evm 0.36.0 and 0.38.0 and alloy-op-evm 0.32.0 finds no call to a wrapping, overflowing, checked or saturating shift, and every << or >> with a U256 operand uses a constant amount. Base's crates/common/evm sources (precompiles/mod.rs, handler.rs, evm.rs and the other 11 files) shift only by constants. base-common-evm2 is in the Base workspace, but no package in the Base lockfile depends on it. The xlayer-reth crates directory has no EVM or precompile crate (builder, chainspec, flashblocks, intercept, legacy-rpc, monitor, rcs-filter, rpc, tests, version), and those crates were not read line by line. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2026-0220.md; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-37.0.3.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-42.0.0.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.19.0.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-precompile/revm-precompile-42.0.1.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs; https://github.com/okx/xlayer-reth/tree/v0.0.7/crates; research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-keccak-cache.work/ruint119_shift.py

- Monad, cycle 11. Monad: mined liquidity removals and fee collections against the source. Blocks 124841070 to 125010503, newest first. 277 transactions with a ModifyLiquidity event of liquidityDelta at or below zero were read and 169 were taken: every PoolManager event in the transaction is ModifyLiquidity (or Swap, in multi+swap), no other transaction in the block emitted a PoolManager event for the same pool, the pool key hashes to the pool id, and the hook has no liquidity permission bits. Set aside: 17 pool touched by another transaction in the block; 38 other PoolManager events in the transaction; 42 pool key not found; 11 fees of a position touched after a swap in the same transaction. For each taken transaction Pool.modifyLiquidity and Position.update were rerun on the PoolManager storage of the parent block read with extsload (slot0, fee growth, ticks, position), the predicted pool liquidity, tick words and position words were compared with the storage at the block, and the owed amount per currency was compared with what left the PoolManager in the receipt. PoolManager events were read with eth_getLogs in 100-block windows from rpc3.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz and rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, which refuse larger ranges. Native legs were summed from debug_traceTransaction (callTracer) and, independently, from eth_getBalance of the PoolManager at the block and its parent. The trace is a re-execution by the RPC node's interpreter; the balance and the storage are what block production wrote. Of the 108 native legs (92 with a nonzero amount), 69 are alone in their block and all 69 agree with the balance difference; 18 in shared blocks also agree; 21 in shared blocks differ because other transactions moved native value, so those 21 rest on the RPC node's trace alone. The tick bitmap words are not part of the storage comparison. Result: All 169 transactions match to the unit with no storage difference: 82 single removals, 48 single fee collections, and 39 transactions with several liquidity actions (35 of them with a swap). They hold 114 removal events and 65 zero-delta collections, 134 events with nonzero fees, and 297 currency legs with a payment, 108 of them native. No amount is above or below the source's value, so no difference exceeds the rounding the source allows. Out-of-range removals paid exactly the rounded-down principal, which differs from the rounded-up value in every such case checked (sensitivity.py), so the comparison can tell the two apart. ## Reading of the source (theme-monad-settlement-path)

- Monad, cycle 11. Which of the settlement opcodes Monad v0.16.5 compiles inline and which it hands to a runtime function that the interpreter also calls, and how the compiled code passes operands and takes the result of such a call. Result: Inline in compiled code: CALLER and ADDRESS (read_context_address), CALLVALUE (read_context_word), RETURNDATASIZE, CALLDATASIZE and MSIZE (read_context_uint32_to_word), CALLDATALOAD (Emitter::calldataload with the assembly helper monad_vm_runtime_load_bounded_le_raw) and SIGNEXTEND. Handed to a runtime function: KECCAK256 (runtime::sha3), CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE, CALL, STATICCALL and SELFBALANCE (emitter.hpp 388-485, 525-552). The interpreter's instruction table calls the same runtime functions for these (instruction_table.hpp 821-833, 942-954, 1053-1065, 1306-1318, 1360-1390), so the eth_call tests of earlier cycles (the KECCAK256, MCOPY and copy vectors of the battery and the 50 call semantics tests of callsem.py) ran the code that block execution runs for them. The only compiled-specific part is the call glue. RuntimeImpl::pass stores every operand that is in a register into its stack slot, call_impl passes each operand as a pointer to that slot or to a rodata copy of a literal, in pop order, which is the order of the C++ parameters for every function above, and the result is written to a fresh stack slot at the new top (emitter.cpp 443-501). That slot can be the slot of the deepest input, which is the same aliasing the interpreter uses (call_runtime.hpp: the result pointer is the deepest stack argument). Each of these functions reads all its inputs before it writes the result: sha3 reads size and offset first (keccak.hpp 28-45), tload copies the key first (storage.hpp 35-45), and call and staticcall take the operands by reference into call_impl and write the result after it returns (call.cpp 198-221, 272-293). CALLVALUE uses the 32 byte big-endian env.value through movbe per limb or vpermq plus vpshufb, both a full byte reversal. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 443-590, 2238-2281, 3043-3082, 3385-3394, 3816-3892; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.hpp lines 130-205, 388-565; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/interpreter/call_runtime.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/interpreter/instruction_table.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/keccak.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/storage.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/call.cpp; copies in research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-monad-settlement-path.work/src
- Monad, cycle 11. Monad v0.16.5 inline CALLDATALOAD at every offset location the emitter distinguishes (literal up to 2^31-1, literal from 2^31 to 2^32-1 through rodata, literal of 2^32 or more, general register live and not live in each of the three register sets, AVX register, stack slot), with is_bounded_by_bits<32>, the 32 byte load or the bounded load helper for fewer than 32 remaining bytes, and the byte swap. Result: No mismatch with the specification in 411,200 cases: every calldata length from 0 to 300 with every offset from 0 to length plus 40 and nine large offsets at each location, and 50,000 random cases with lengths up to 5,000 and offsets whose upper limbs are set. Every branch of monad_vm_runtime_load_bounded_le_raw ran (sizes 1, 2, 3 to 4, 5 to 8, 9 to 16, 17 to 31 and zero or negative), and no case read a byte outside the calldata buffer. The 17 to 24 byte case depends on shrd and shrx masking a count of 64 to 120 to six bits; the transcription models that masking and the result is right. Seven of ten planted faults were caught (between 280 and 31,960 failing cases each); the three not caught are equivalent for calldata below 2^31 bytes (a 16 bit size read, a 31 bit offset mask and the rodata threshold). The PoolManager runs CALLDATALOAD at 44 sites, 40 with a literal offset; in the 584 scripts compared below the compiled transcription executed it 84,050 times in the PoolManager. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-monad-settlement-path.work/settlejit.py, run_units.py, units.json, mutate.py, mutate.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 636-644, 3155-3258 and is_bounded_by_bits; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/transmute.S lines 22-118
- Monad, cycle 11. Monad v0.16.5 inline CALLER, CALLVALUE and RETURNDATASIZE, which decide who is credited (src/PoolManager.sol:301, 306, 369), how much native currency a settle credits (src/PoolManager.sol:354) and whether a token transfer counts as successful (src/types/Currency.sol:68). Result: No mismatch. CALLER: 50,000 addresses including all limb edges give the 160 bit value, with the top limb zero and the 32 bit movbe clearing the upper half of its register. CALLVALUE: 100,000 values through both the general register and the AVX destination. RETURNDATASIZE: every size from 0 to 4,096 and 5,000 random sizes below 2^24. RETURNDATASIZE reads the low 32 bits of a 64 bit field (static_assert at emitter.cpp 3072-3074); this is exact for return data below 2^32 bytes, which a transaction cannot produce under Monad's memory limit. When a comparison is held in the CPU flags, the three readers write zero with mov instead of xor, so the flags that Currency.transfer's gt(returndatasize(), 31) and eq(mload(0), 1) feed into are kept. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-monad-settlement-path.work/settlejit.py, run_units.py, units.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 2269-2330, 3043-3077, 3816-3892; src/types/Currency.sol:64-74
- Monad, cycle 11. Monad v0.16.5 SIGNEXTEND with a non-literal index: destructive_mov_stack_elem_to_bounded_rax at its three index locations (general register live and not live, AVX, stack slot with and without a free register) and the three value paths signextend_avx_reg_by_bounded_rax, signextend_general_reg_by_bounded_rax and signextend_stack_offset_or_literal_by_bounded_rax. Result: This shape does not occur in the built runtime. All 114 SIGNEXTEND instructions get their index from a PUSH in the same basic block, so the compiler takes the literal path that cycle 9 transcribed (settle_sites.py over build/PoolManager.json, using the block and literal rules of cycle 10's sites.py). Result: A swap step stops short of its target only while the input left is below what the target needs, and each position's deposit is capped below 2^127 by toInt128 (Pool.sol:212-235). ## Reading of the source (theme-code-cache-consistency)

- Polygon, cycle 12. bor v2.11.1 BlockSTM V2: can one Call build a Contract whose CodeHash and Code come from two state versions, so that the bitmap of one bytecode is stored under the PoolManager's code hash in the per-block JUMPDEST cache that V2 workers and the prefetcher share (lead L-645). Result: No. The production parallel path is V2 (core/blockchain.go line 975 builds NewV2StateProcessor), and its workers read code through ParallelStateDB, not through the MVHashMap path of core/state/statedb.go. ParallelStateDB.GetCode and GetCodeHash both go through readCodeKey (core/state/parallel_statedb.go lines 359-381), which caches the first CodePath read of each address for the whole incarnation in codeReadCache, with a comment that names exactly this hazard: the two GetCode(addr) reads of resolveCode and resolveCodeHash (core/vm/evm.go lines 363-370, 721-748) must follow one delegation target. The destruction index is cached the same way (priorDestructedAt, lines 597-620). Both caches are cleared per incarnation in Reset (lines 302-304). For code written by an earlier transaction of the block, GetCodeHash returns cachedCodeHash(addr, val), which is keccak256 of the very bytes GetCode returned (lines 875-888, 897-905). For code from the parent state, both come from SafeBase, a pool of copies of one parent StateDB that is never written (core/state/safe_base.go lines 52-63, 181-209), and a StateDB loads code by its hash. Code set inside the transaction comes from localCode, and every change of localCode clears codeHashCache (SetCode line 949, revertCode and revertCreate in core/state/parallel_statedb_journal.go lines 93-124). So the cache key is always the hash of the bytes analysed, or the trie hash of those same bytes. A bitmap stored by an incarnation that later fails validation is left in syncMapJumpDests (core/vm/jumpdests.go lines 57-78 has no delete), but it is the correct bitmap for the bytes whose hash keys it, so leaving it is harmless. The prefetcher runs each transaction on its own Copy of the parent state (core/state_prefetcher.go lines 240-249), a single-threaded StateDB in which the two reads see the same account. The serial processor (bc.cfg.VmConfig, core/blockchain.go line 1487), the stateless witness path (ExecuteStateless with bc.cfg.VmConfig, line 6477) and the block producer (miner/worker.go lines 3588-3597, which copies the chain VmConfig without the shared cache) each use a per-EVM map, not the shared cache. The same codeReadCache code is in every release since BlockSTM V2 arrived: v2.10.1, v2.10.2, v2.10.3, v2.11.0, v2.11.1 and v2.11.2 all contain it, and core/state/parallel_statedb.go is byte-identical in v2.11.1 and v2.11.2. An ordinary account sending type 4 transactions in any order therefore cannot pair one bitmap with another code hash, and no block producer role changes that. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/state/parallel_statedb.go lines 170-181, 302-304, 359-381, 597-620, 843-949; also https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/state/parallel_statedb_journal.go lines 93-124, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/evm.go lines 363-370 and 721-748, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/contract.go lines 65-113, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/blockchain.go lines 975, 1268-1349, 1487, 6477, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/state_prefetcher.go lines 213-257, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/state/safe_base.go lines 52-209, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/miner/worker.go lines 3588-3597
- Polygon, cycle 12. What a wrong JUMPDEST bitmap could do to this PoolManager if one were ever paired with its code hash: list the 0x5b bytes inside push data of the 24,009 byte runtime and whether any jump could reach them. Result: validJumpdest first requires the byte at the destination to be 0x5b in the real code (bor core/vm/contract.go lines 65-78). The runtime has 610 valid JUMPDESTs and 29 bytes of value 0x5b inside push data, at offsets 50, 261, 470, 885, 1877, 6220, 9058, 9969, 9973, 10775, 11255, 12643, 12678, 12724, 12759, 16550, 17125, 17743, 18038, 19380, 20374, 21025, 23215, 23246, 23300, 23397, 23428, 23486 and 23512. No PUSH constant anywhere in the runtime equals any of these offsets, and the compiler's jump targets are pushed constants (internal returns jump to pushed return addresses), so no jump of the PoolManager can name one of those bytes. A wrong bitmap could only turn valid destinations invalid, which reverts the call on the node that holds it. It could not redirect control. Since the pairing cannot happen (previous item), neither outcome is reachable. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/012/theme-code-cache-consistency.work/pushdata_jumpdest.json (scripts/pushdata_jumpdest.py over research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json)
- Polygon, cycle 12. bor v2.12.0-beta (pre-release, not on mainnet) adds a one-entry memo of the reciprocal of a full-width MULMOD modulus (#2310). FullMath.mulDiv uses mulmod with modulus 2^256-1, which takes this path. Result: core/vm/mulmod_memo.go lines 55-66 compares the whole 256-bit modulus before reusing the reciprocal, recomputes uint256.Reciprocal on a miss, and is per-EVM state with no sharing. holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 MulMod (uint256.go lines 720-730) computes mu = Reciprocal(m) and calls reduce4(p, m, mu), and MulModWithReciprocal (lines 688-697) runs the same umul and reduce4 with the supplied mu, so the result equals stock MulMod for every input. Moduli with a zero top limb, which includes the 2^96 and 2^128 constants of the bytecode, bypass the memo. Nothing to fix; read it again if the final v2.12.0 differs. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/mulmod_memo.go lines 55-66; https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/holiman/uint256/@v/v1.3.2.zip uint256.go lines 688-730
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 12. BNB Smart Chain v1.8.2: JUMPDEST caches shared across transactions or workers, and the pooled Contract objects (lead L-646). Result: BSC keeps the per-EVM map of upstream and adds a process-wide LRU of 2,048 bitmaps keyed by code hash (core/vm/contract.go lines 27-34 and 101-113), shared by block import, the prefetcher, the miner and every RPC call on the node. The LRU is mutex-protected (common/lru/lru.go lines 25-60). The key is the CodeHash set next to the code in Call, CallCode, DelegateCall and StaticCall (core/vm/evm.go lines 353-363, 420-423, 464-467, 517-520), and both come from one single-threaded StateDB; the prefetcher gives each transaction or worker its own statedb.Copy() (core/state_prefetcher.go lines 72 and 154). Every write of code computes the hash from the bytes: StateDB.SetCode (core/state/statedb.go lines 509-514), the journal revert (core/state/journal.go line 408), and the RPC state override, which calls SetCode (internal/ethapi/override/override.go line 108). SetStorage (statedb.go lines 545-548) copies the old object's hash with its lazily loaded code field, and stateObject.Code() loads the bytes by that hash when the field is empty (state_object.go lines 568-587). So a cached bitmap is always the analysis of the bytes whose keccak is its key, and even a poisoned RPC call cannot put a wrong bitmap into the process-wide cache. The Contract pool (core/vm/contract_pool.go lines 17-38) resets Code, CodeHash and analysis on every GetContract. v1.8.2 has no parallel block executor; block processing is serial. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/contract.go lines 27-34, 101-113; also https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/contract_pool.go lines 17-46, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/evm.go lines 353-363, 700-725, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/state/statedb.go lines 509-548, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/state/journal.go line 408, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/internal/ethapi/override/override.go line 108
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 12. reth-bsc v0.1.4 (bsc-rpc.publicnode.com answers reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f): where its JUMPDEST analysis lives. Result: reth-bsc v0.1.4 builds on the bnb-chain/reth fork tag v0.1.3 with revm 38.0.0 and revm-bytecode 10.0.0 (Cargo.toml lines 19-86). In revm-bytecode the jump table is a field of the Bytecode value itself, computed from the bytes by analyze_legacy in new_legacy (src/bytecode/mod.rs lines 43 and 128-139 in 10.0.0). The analysis travels with the bytes and is not looked up by a hash read separately. The hotfix suffix names a build whose source was not found, and the reth fork's own storage encoding of Bytecode was not read (the file path of crates/primitives-traits at that tag returned 404). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/v0.1.4/Cargo.toml lines 19-86; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-bytecode/revm-bytecode-10.0.0.crate src/bytecode/mod.rs lines 43, 128-139
- Avalanche, cycle 12. avalanchego 1.15.3 with libevm d398bc4dbe41: sharing of JUMPDEST analysis, and EIP-7702 delegation. Result: libevm keeps the go-ethereum 1.13 design: each Contract inherits the jumpdests map of its parent frame and a new map is made for the outermost frame of each message (core/vm/contract.go lines 63-72, 99-125), so analysis is never shared across transactions or threads. Call reads code and code hash from one StateDB (core/vm/evm.go lines 243-251). EIP-7702 is not active on the C-Chain: an eth_call to an account overridden with code 0xef0100 followed by the PoolManager address failed with 'invalid opcode: opcode 0xef not defined' on api.avax.network, so the delegation lever does not exist there. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/d398bc4dbe41/core/vm/contract.go lines 63-125; research/network-risk/cycles/012/theme-code-cache-consistency.work/delegated_call.json (eth_call on https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc)
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 12. Nitro v3.12.4 (go-ethereum fork at 0e44603, confirmed as the submodule pin on the v3.12.4 tree page): JUMPDEST cache scope and key. Result: The fork has a cache owned by BlockChain and shared across blocks, block processing and the parallel prefetcher: eight mutex-protected size-bounded LRU shards keyed by code hash (core/jumpdest.go lines 41-76; core/blockchain.go lines 482, 2373 and 2419). The prefetcher runs each transaction on its own statedb.Copy() (core/state_prefetcher.go lines 64-100) and the processor is serial, so the code hash and the code of one Call come from one single-threaded StateDB (core/vm/evm.go lines 343-350 and 812-821), and the key is the hash of the bytes analysed. The endpoints report v3.13.0-rc.9, which is not public, and Elysium's build names no version; for those the reading rests on the public pin. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/0e44603/core/jumpdest.go lines 41-76; also https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/0e44603/core/blockchain.go lines 482, 2373, 2419, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/0e44603/core/vm/contract.go lines 95-115, https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/tree/v3.12.4
- Monad, cycle 12. Monad v0.16.5, and v0.16.7 which rpc.monad.xyz now reports: can the varcode cache (interpreter code and native code keyed by code hash) store or find analysis or machine code of one bytecode under the PoolManager's code hash, for a 7702-delegated account or for an account created and called in the same block under optimistic parallel execution (lead L-647). Result: No. Monad never pairs a code hash with code read separately. execute_call_message reads the hash with state.get_code_hash(msg.code_address) and then fetches the code by that hash, state.read_code(hash), and passes both to the VM (category/execution/ethereum/execute_message.cpp lines 326-330). For a delegated account the delegate address is read first (category/vm/evm/delegation.cpp lines 57-80) and the hash and code are then those of the delegate, the code again fetched by hash. read_code looks up the transaction's own code map, then BlockState, then the code trie, each keyed by hash (state3/state.cpp lines 523-532, state2/block_state.cpp lines 129-153). Every entry of those stores has a key computed from its bytes: State::set_code computes keccak256(code) (state3/state.cpp lines 576-587), BlockState::merge copies a transaction's code map entries under the same hashes (block_state.cpp lines 194-216), and the RPC state override goes through set_code (category/rpc/monad_executor.cpp line 171). VarcodeCache::try_set_raw returns an existing entry for a hash without comparing bytes (category/vm/varcode_cache.cpp lines 74-82), which is safe only because of that invariant, and the invariant holds on every insert path read. Under optimistic execution a transaction that read an account before an earlier transaction changed its code fails can_merge, which compares the recorded code_hash (state3/state.cpp lines 664-666), and runs again. Compiled code is keyed by the same hash and recompiled when the chain revision changes (category/vm/vm.cpp lines 142-160). state.cpp, varcode_cache.cpp, vm.cpp and delegation.cpp are byte-identical in v0.16.7, and the v0.16.7 changes to execute_message.cpp and block_state.cpp touch only the ripemd touch and include comments. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/execution/ethereum/execute_message.cpp lines 326-330; also https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/execution/ethereum/state3/state.cpp lines 523-587, 664-666, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/execution/ethereum/state2/block_state.cpp lines 129-216, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/varcode_cache.cpp lines 41-82, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/evm/delegation.cpp lines 57-80, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/ (same files)
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Tempo, Arc, MegaETH, HyperEVM, cycle 12. revm and evm2 based clients (reth v2.11.0 on Ethereum, op-reth on OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, Base reth v2.5.2, conduit-op-reth on Zora, world-chain, Celo reth, X Layer reth, Tempo v1.19.0, Arc, mega-reth replicas on MegaETH, the HyperEVM public replay clients): does any cache pair a jump table with a code hash read separately from the code. Result: In revm-bytecode 10.0.0 and 11.0.1 (revm 38 and 40) the jump table is a field of the Arc-shared Bytecode, computed from the bytes by analyze_legacy (src/legacy/analysis.rs lines 10-62; src/bytecode/mod.rs lines 22-43 and 131-142 in 11.0.1). reth v2.11.0 (on evm2 via reth-core 275ce4cf) persists the jump table next to the bytes in one Compact record and rebuilds the Bytecode with new_analyzed from that record (crates/primitives-traits/src/account.rs lines 348-421 in reth-core), so the table belongs to the bytes it is stored with. A cache keyed by code hash in front of the database returns that record for that hash. Nothing in these designs reads a hash and code from two state versions. The code caches of the engine tree in each reth build were not read line by line, and the closed MegaETH sequencer and HyperEVM validator cannot be read (see leads). Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-bytecode/revm-bytecode-11.0.1.crate src/legacy/analysis.rs lines 10-62; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth-core/275ce4cf5befeb9f1e8acd935ff2882d2d25fc61/crates/primitives-traits/src/account.rs lines 348-421; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/Cargo.toml lines 436-439, 682-684
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM, cycle 12. Read-only test of the delegated call path on every network: eth_call owner() and extsload(0) on an EOA whose code is overridden with 0xef0100 followed by the PoolManager address and whose slot 0 is overridden with a marker. Result: On 20 networks both calls return the marker word, so the node resolved the delegation, ran the PoolManager's 24,009 bytes under the delegate's code hash with every jump of the owner() and extsload paths accepted, and read the EOA's storage. Avalanche rejects the designator (EIP-7702 not active). The test cannot reach a cross-transaction race inside a block, which only block import can exercise; that question is settled by the source readings above. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/012/theme-code-cache-consistency.work/delegated_call.json (scripts/delegated_call.py, eth_call with state override on each RPC in state/networks.json, 2026-11-24)
- Monad, cycle 12. PoolManager bytecode under EIP-8024 style immediates: revm-bytecode 11.0.1 pads for DUPN, SWAPN and EXCHANGE (0xe6 to 0xe8) whose immediates the jump scan does not skip. Result: A linear disassembly of the runtime finds no 0xe6, 0xe7 or 0xe8 in opcode position, and the only 0xfe is the terminator before the CBOR metadata, so that rule cannot change any jump destination of this contract on a network that activates it. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-bytecode/revm-bytecode-11.0.1.crate src/legacy/analysis.rs lines 38-67; research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json

- Polygon, cycle 12. Polygon: mined liquidity removals and fee collections against the source (lead L-656). Blocks 97846554 to 97885812, newest first. 321 transactions with a ModifyLiquidity event of liquidityDelta at or below zero were read. First cycle 11's analyze2.py was run unchanged apart from the endpoints and a fallback to the balance difference when the endpoint has no tracer: it took 296 (95 collect exact, 88 multi exact, 9 multi under, 104 remove exact) and set aside 9 hook with liquidity permissions; 3 pool touched by another transaction in the block; 13 swap in the transaction. Then analyze3.py reran every PoolManager event of the block on the touched pools in log order from the storage of the parent block: ModifyLiquidity through Pool.modifyLiquidity, Position.update, updateTick, flipTick and clearTick; Swap through the step loop of Pool.swap with crossTick, the protocol fee split and fee growth, accepting only a parameter candidate that reproduces the event's price, tick, liquidity and both amounts; Donate; Initialize; ERC-6909 mints and burns as delta changes. It compares the owed amount per currency with what left the PoolManager, and after the block compares slot0, liquidity, both fee growth globals, every tick, position and tick bitmap word it touched with the storage at the block. Logs from polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (reports bor/a863b8e5cce1/v2.11.1-private/linux-amd64/go1.26.10), state at the parent block and traces from polygon.drpc.org. Result: 321 of 321 transactions were rerun (0 set aside: none). 312 match to the unit. They hold 293 removal events, 143 zero-delta collections, 22 swaps replayed (13 transactions with a swap, 1 crossed ticks), 5 liquidity events that collect fees after a swap in the same transaction, 10 transactions whose pools another transaction of the block also touched, and 581 currency legs with a payment. 1558 storage words were compared, 214 of them tick bitmap words after 398 flips, with no difference. 19 native legs, 11 of them the only PoolManager transaction of their block; in all 11 the PoolManager balance difference that block production wrote equals the payment. Payments were read from: call tracer 19. The 9 transactions that differ paid 797 to 9,999,999,974,048 units of 0xe7c3d8c9a439fede00d2600032d5db0be71c3c29 less than the liquidity events owe. In each the call tracer shows a clear(currency, amount) frame for exactly the missing amount (raw/clear-137.json): the caller forfeited its own positive delta, which src/PoolManager.sol:310-319 allows only for the caller's exact delta. No payout exceeded the source and none fell short for another reason. - all 21 networks, cycle 12. Whether hooks with return-delta permissions change what the PoolManager pays out in total, which decides whether such pools can be checked from events. src/PoolManager.sol:178-183 credits hookDelta to the hook and callerDelta minus hookDelta to the caller after modifyLiquidity (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:209-244), and src/PoolManager.sol:221-226 does the same after swap (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:285-315). unlock reverts unless every account's delta is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Result: The two credits add up to the pool delta of the event, and both accounts must reach zero through take, settle, mint, burn or clear before unlock returns, so the PoolManager's net token flow in a completed unlock equals the sum of the pool deltas of the events, adjusted by ERC-6909 mints and burns and by clear. A hook cannot change that total; it can only move it between its own account and the caller's. analyze3.py therefore checks pools with return-delta hooks (243 transactions on Arc, 41 on Monad, 30 on Elysium, 25 on Robinhood Chain). Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:178-183
- all 21 networks, cycle 12. Whether clear leaves value that someone else can claim. clear (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319) lowers the caller's own positive delta to zero only when the amount equals it exactly, and moves no token. The cleared tokens stay in the PoolManager's balance. Result: A later sync records the whole balance as reserves (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), so the cleared amount is never credited to a later settler, and no function pays it out. It is lost to the caller who chose to clear it and is taken from nobody else. The 9 Polygon transactions above cleared 797 to 9,999,999,974,048 units this way. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:310-319

## Reading of the source (theme-proof-builds)

- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 12. Lead L-663, part two. The consensus-v61 replay is built by go1.25.9 for GOARCH=wasm. Which lowering do bits.Mul64, bits.Add64, bits.Sub64 and bits.Div64 get there, and does holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 on that lowering give the specified result for the MULMOD, MUL, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, shift, BYTE and SIGNEXTEND vectors of targeted.py and battery.py and for the pool math of v4math.py. Result: intrinsics.go of go1.25.9 lists wasm for none of the four (lines 1222-1252: Mul64, Add64 and Sub64 for amd64, arm64, ppc64, s390x, mips64, riscv64 and loong64; Div64 for amd64 only), so the replay runs the generic Go code of math/bits/bits.go lines 386-560. Wasm.rules lines 102-138 lower a shift by a variable amount to Select(shift, 0, amount < 64) unless the prove pass shows the amount below 64, which is Go's own semantics; the uint256 shifts by 64 - shift (uint256.go:520-580, 1042-1149) are therefore 0 for shift 0 as on x86. A Python transcription of the generic bits code and of uint256.go, div.go and mod.go of v1.3.2 (the 332 straight-line bits statements of Reciprocal and reduce4 translated by script, control flow by hand), behind the opSHL, opSHR and opSAR bounds checks of go-ethereum v1.16.4 instructions.go:188-228, matched the reference on all 85,544 targeted vectors, 96,224 arithmetic battery vectors, 25,321 mulDiv, mulDivRoundingUp and bit scan cases and 19,498 ticks of getSqrtPriceAtTick and getTickAtSqrtPrice. The primitives alone matched exact arithmetic on 400,000 cases each and reciprocal2by1 on 400,004 normalised divisors. A planted wrong Mul64 gave 212 mismatches and a planted unguarded wasm shift gave 303 in 3,000 vectors, so the harness can fail. This covers the library and its lowering, not the Go wasm code generator for ordinary 64-bit arithmetic, which was not read. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golang/go/go1.25.9/src/cmd/compile/internal/ssagen/intrinsics.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golang/go/go1.25.9/src/cmd/compile/internal/ssa/_gen/Wasm.rules ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golang/go/go1.25.9/src/math/bits/bits.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.3.2/uint256.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.3.2/mod.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.3.2/div.go ; cycles/012/theme-proof-builds.work/go/uint256-wasm-vectors.json, prims.json, faults.json
- Worldchain, cycle 12. Part one for World Chain: op-program 1.9.0 on Cannon MIPS64 runs op-geth with holiman/uint256 v1.3.2. On mips64 Go intrinsifies Mul64, Add64 and Sub64 and leaves Div64 and Len64 generic. Do the opcode edges of OPCODES.md come out right on that target. Result: The same transcription with Mul64 replaced by the DMULTU semantics of MIPS64Instructions.sol:794-798 (uint128(rs) * uint128(rt), hi = res >> 64) and the generic Div64 (which uses DDIVU, lines 807-813, exact unsigned quotient and remainder) matched all 85,544 targeted vectors, 96,224 battery vectors, the mulDiv and bit scan cases and 19,498 ticks. The 32-bit MULTU and DIVU paths sign-extend their results to 64 bits as the MIPS64 specification asks. The game on World Chain is permissioned, so the program is played by the operator only. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/cannon/libraries/MIPS64Instructions.sol ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golang/go/go1.25.9/src/cmd/compile/internal/ssagen/intrinsics.go ; cycles/012/theme-proof-builds.work/go/uint256-wasm-vectors.json
