## Reading of the source (own-check)

- Monad, cycle 12. Monad v0.16.7 says reverted state depends on whether code ran compiled or interpreted. Can a reverted inner frame leave a CurrencyDelta credit or a synced currency behind (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32) while the payment is rolled back?. Result: Read at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7; the four journal files are byte-identical in the two releases. Every account's balance, nonce, storage, transient storage, touched flag, warm flag and warm slot set live in one AccountState object held in a VersionStack per address (state3/state.hpp line 62, account_state.hpp lines 49-70, account_substate.hpp lines 31-40). The first write in a frame copies the object under the frame's version (version_stack.hpp current(), state.cpp lines 73-86), and a failed frame pops that copy for every address the frame touched (state.cpp pop_reject lines 155-181, version_stack.hpp pop_reject). Logs use the same stack, and post_call asserts a zero refund for every failed frame (execute_message.cpp). So nothing a frame wrote survives its revert on either path: a CurrencyDelta or reserves word set by TSTORE inside a reverted frame is gone together with the token transfer. The developers' comment describes what happens inside a frame that is about to fail: compiled code checks gas once per basic block, so it stops before the block, while the interpreter stops part way through it. The partial work is discarded in both cases. v0.16.5 had one exception, a touch of the ripemd address kept after a revert; v0.16.7 removed it. That flag only decides whether an empty account at address 3 is deleted and no PoolManager path reads it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/execute_message.cpp lines 143-162 ; state3/state.cpp lines 73-86 and 126-181 ; state3/version_stack.hpp ; state3/account_state.hpp ; state3/account_substate.hpp (same text at v0.16.5)
- Monad, cycle 14. On Monad every served receipt, log and trace comes from RPC nodes that interpret (F-130). Do those nodes check their execution against what the validators agreed on, so that mined results stand for validators that may run compiled code? (lead L-737). Result: Own reading of monad-bft at tag v0.16.7 (commit 670b8ce5). A proposal for block N carries delayed_execution_results, the full Ethereum header of block N-D (monad-consensus-types/src/block.rs line 92; EthHeader wraps the alloy Header, monad-eth-types, so it holds state root, receipts root, logs bloom and gas used). EthBlockPolicy::check_coherency reads the header the node's own execution wrote to its triedb (monad-eth-block-policy/src/lib.rs lines 1182-1196 and 1271-1290; monad-triedb-utils/src/lib.rs lines 124-154 and 314-342) and returns ExecutionResultMismatch when the two differ. The block tree then leaves the block incoherent and counts rx_bad_state_root (monad-blocktree/src/blocktree.rs lines 280-308). A block that is not coherent is never committed: get_high_committable_qc skips it (blocktree.rs line 369), try_commit returns early (monad-consensus-state/src/lib.rs lines 1459-1467) and prune asserts coherency (blocktree.rs lines 153 and 169). Only newly coherent blocks are handed to execution (lib.rs lines 1542-1558). A node that is not in the validator set runs the same consensus state; only its votes, timeouts and proposals are filtered out (monad-state/src/consensus.rs lines 591-637). So a full node, tracing or not, whose execution of block N-D gave a different state root, receipts root, logs bloom or gas used than the header the validator quorum certified stops committing at block N. rpc.monad.xyz follows the finalized tip, so its interpreter results equal the quorum's for every block it serves, receipts and logs included. If validators run compiled code, its state root, receipts root, logs bloom and gas used have therefore agreed with the interpreter on every mined block, including the 129,567 swaps through the 512 bit branch of FullMath.mulDiv found in cycle 14. What stays without evidence is input that no mined transaction has used. Evidence: https://github.com/category-labs/monad-bft/tree/v0.16.7
- Tempo, cycle 14. Does the Tempo v1.19.1 release binary contain the evm2 LLVM compiler, now that reth v2.11 ships it by default? (lead L-743). Result: Own reading at tempo/v1.19.1. Tempo depends on reth-evm-ethereum with default features, and at reth 167933d that crate's default is ["std"]; jit is a default feature of the reth binary crate only (bin/reth/Cargo.toml). Tempo's own hook-up of the compiler is behind its jit feature (crates/evm/src/lib.rs lines 19-20, 183-184, 239-265; crates/node/src/node.rs lines 72-79 and 590), which the release workflow and the Dockerfile do not pass (features asm-keccak, jemalloc, otlp). TempoEvmConfig builds evm2::Evm without configure_jit in such a build, so no JitBackend exists in the release binary. Evidence: https://github.com/tempoxyz/tempo/tree/tempo/v1.19.1
- Polygon, cycle 16. L-799: in bor v2.12.0-beta, can the widened keccak result cache return the hash of a different input (key aliasing EVM memory, a fingerprint key, or an entry from an aborted speculative execution), which would give a wrong storage slot for a pool id (160 bytes) or a position key (58 bytes)?. Result: Read on 2026-11-25 in 0xPolygon/bor at tag v2.12.0-beta (core/vm/instructions.go 258-330, interpreter.go 50-71, shared_cache.go, bounded_cache.go, keccak_cache.go). The widened cache keccakResultCache is a sync.Map from string(data) to common.Hash. Store copies the input (string(data)), so a stored key never points into EVM memory, and it takes the hash by value. Load builds a string view of memory without a copy, which sync.Map.Load compares and does not keep, and the calling goroutine owns that memory for the length of the call. The key is the full input, with no fingerprint, so inputs of different lengths or contents cannot share an entry. An entry written by a speculative execution that BlockSTM later discards is still keccak of its own key, since the hash is computed from the same bytes immediately before Store. On a miss the handler falls through to the ordinary path with the freshly computed hash. The cache exists only when a node sets the precompile cache flag (default false) and is dropped at the end of each block. The legacy path for 64 byte inputs, which v2.11.1 already has, copies the key into a [64]byte array. A standalone copy of the Load and Store logic (cycles/016/own-check.work/keccak_cache/main.go, sha256 standing in for keccak) was run with 16 goroutines on inputs of 58 and 160 bytes that differ in one byte, in buffers overwritten after every call: 12,800,000 lookups, 4,809,737 hits, 0 wrong, every stored key still maps to the hash of its own bytes, and a shorter run under the Go race detector reports no race. v2.12.0-beta is the only tag with this code; v2.12.0 does not exist yet and Polygon's endpoint reports v2.11.1. Whether Polygon's validators will set the flag is not known and does not matter for correctness as read. L-664 and L-668 keep the rerun of the opcode checks against a v2.12 node. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/shared_cache.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/instructions.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/instructions.go ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/own-check.work/keccak_cache/main.go
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. L-837: do the seven v3 style swaps of HyperEVM's closed validator that cycle 17 could not reproduce differ from the formulas of src/libraries/FullMath.sol and SqrtPriceMath.sol?. Result: No. The same 7,000 groups (filter m512?, seed 3, limit 20,000, first 7,000 of the sorted sample) were rerun with every mismatch saved. The counts equal the cycle 17 log: 7,282 swaps reproduced, 3,008 with a call on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv, 7 mismatches. Six are in pool 0x0d3e8f6949dcaca02cbd1aaf7ca840f4f36216b7 and one in 0x12e5f773134a6df0fcc74aedddcca0429a08eaa6. Each of the seven blocks holds a 0xd78218c0 Mint variant for the pool before the swap, which the collector does not read, and no other unread topic. With the variant applied, all seven reproduce price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to the unit. About 57,000 groups of the sample are still not run (L-826). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/own-check.work/NOTES.md, v3check_own.py, v3recheck.py, results/mismatches.jsonl, results/recheck.json (https://rpc.purroofgroup.com, 2026-11-25)

## Reading of the source (theme-callee-gas-and-overrides)

- Arc, cycle 13. Arc arc-node v0.8.6, the complete set of instruction, gas and call hooks it adds to revm 38.0.0 (lead L-681). The endpoint answers web3_clientVersion with arc/v1, which names no release. Result: Instruction table: only SELFDESTRUCT is replaced (evm.rs lines 114-134, three variants by hardfork); the PoolManager bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT. Frame hook: every CALL or CREATE with nonzero value passes check_blocklist_and_create_log (evm.rs lines 516-605), recorded as the finding of this unit; the PoolManager reaches it only at the native payout of src/types/Currency.sol:48, and the success flag differs from Ethereum only for a recipient that is address(0), blocklisted or destroyed earlier in the same transaction. A rejected frame returns all of its gas, so the PoolManager has more gas left than after a stock failure. Subcall registry: calls to 0x1800..03 are diverted to CallFrom with an allow list (evm.rs lines 669-711 and 1805-1820), and a caller outside the list gets a 100 gas revert (lines 137-151). Precompile set: the stock Osaka set plus four stateful precompiles at 0x1800..00 (NativeCoinAuthority), 0x1800..01 (NativeCoinControl), 0x1800..02 (SystemAccounting) and 0x1800..04 (PQ) (precompile_provider.rs lines 46-71, pq-precompile lib.rs line 26). Their state-changing selectors run check_staticcall first, which spends all gas (helpers.rs 540-555), but the only staticcall the PoolManager makes is balanceOf(address) at src/types/Currency.sol:94, which none of them implements, so it takes the 200 gas invalid-selector revert. Measured from the PoolManager address: 0x1800..00 to ..04 revert with 100 bytes for 323 to 2,829 gas on all five call shapes; 0x1800..05 to ..09 hold the one byte code 0xef and consume all forwarded gas, which is ordinary EVM semantics for an undefined opcode. KECCAK256, MCOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE, SSTORE, LOG and the arithmetic are the stock revm handlers, as cycle 12 and the stablecoin-l1 unit of this cycle found for v0.8.0 to v0.8.6. - MegaETH, cycle 13. MegaETH mega-evm (main branch; state/cleared.json records Rex6 active on mainnet since 25 August 2026): the handlers it replaces and whether any changes a value, a success flag, return data or gas left for the PoolManager's operands. Result: From MINI_REX on, all 256 table entries are rebuilt (instructions.rs lines 859-916 and following). Arithmetic, comparison, shift, KECCAK256, CALLDATA*, RETURNDATA*, MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE are the revm handler inside compute_gas_ext, which only records compute gas. SSTORE and LOG gain storage gas and data-size limits (storage_gas_ext, additional_limit_ext). CALL, STATICCALL, DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE go through forward_gas_ext, which caps the gas given to the callee at 98/100 of what remains instead of 63/64 (lines 1064-1180), and from Rex4 through volatile_data_ext, which reverts a call to the block beneficiary only when the calling frame has disabled volatile access and caps later compute gas after an oracle or beneficiary access (lines 40-140, 405-445). SELFBALANCE gains the same beneficiary guard. Measured with a callee that returns GAS: a hook or token called from the PoolManager address gets 97.87 percent of the parent's gas on MegaETH against 98.31 percent on 19 other networks (raw/fwdgas.json). The PoolManager keeps more gas after each callee returns, so its own revert wrapping cannot run short; a callee gets about 0.44 percent less, which changes gas only. The PoolManager never touches the beneficiary and never disables volatile access, so the guard cannot fire on its own calls, and an attacker cannot set that flag in a victim's frame (F-018 records the hook author case). - all 21 networks, cycle 13. Callee gas: can an ordinary account make a precompile, predeploy or system contract that burns forwarded gas the recipient of a take or native payout, the hook or a currency inside a transaction that a victim sends through a normal router on an honest pool (lead L-684). Result: No on all 21 networks, on the text of the code. The PoolManager makes outbound calls at four places only: the native payout and the token transfer of src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, whose target is the currency of the take and whose recipient is the `to` argument chosen by the caller of take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297); the balanceOf staticcall of sync at src/types/Currency.sol:94, whose currency the caller chooses (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288); the hook call of src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, whose target is key.hooks, part of the PoolKey that the pool id hashes (src/PoolManager.sol:132, 151); and the unlock callback to msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:110). In a victim's swap or removal on an honest pool, the currencies and the hook are fixed by the pool and the recipient and the callback target are fixed by the victim's router and calldata. No storage that a third party can write steers any of these targets. A gas-burning address can therefore appear only in a transaction the attacker builds, where it costs the attacker gas and reverts the attacker's own unlock. Where a hook address is a special address, the low 14 bits decide which callbacks run: HyperEVM 0x0800 to 0x0813 all set BEFORE_ADD_LIQUIDITY (Hooks.sol:32), so no deposit can enter such a pool; Monad 0x1000 sets AFTER_INITIALIZE (Hooks.sol:30), so the pool cannot be created; Arc 0x1800..00 has no flag bits and is never called. Gas forwarding is 63/64 everywhere except MegaETH (98/100), so after a callee burns its gas the PoolManager keeps at least 1/64 to revert. A victim's swap or removal therefore cannot be made to fail or to cost far more on any of the 21 networks through callee gas. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:48, src/types/Currency.sol:73, src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/PoolManager.sol:110, src/PoolManager.sol:132, src/PoolManager.sol:151, src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:30-47, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-124, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134; research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-callee-gas-and-overrides.work/raw/cg_<chainId>.json and research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-callee-gas-and-overrides.work/raw/calleegas.json (calleegas.py, eth_call with a driver placed by state override at the PoolManager address, 1,000,000 gas forwarded)
- all 21 networks, cycle 13. Whether any client override found in this unit changes what the PoolManager computes, as opposed to gas. Result: No. The handlers replaced on Arc (SELFDESTRUCT, value-call frame hook, CallFrom intercept), MegaETH (gas wrappers, 98/100 forwarding, volatile guards), Tempo (0x4f, SSTORE, 0xef) and Nitro (GASPRICE, BLOCKHASH, NUMBER, SELFDESTRUCT, filter touches) leave every arithmetic, hashing, memory, return data and transient storage result unchanged. The PoolManager's five GAS reads only feed call gas, so a different amount of gas left cannot steer its logic. The one value-visible change is Arc's success flag for value calls to three recipient classes, recorded as the finding. Evidence: research/network-risk/OPCODES.md lines 146, 118; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/v0.8.6/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/evm/instructions.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/0e44603/core/vm/instructions.go

## Reading of the source (theme-proof-builds-2)

- Optimism, Unichain, Ink, cycle 13. Lead L-682: which routines ruint 1.20.0 uses on the kona mips64 target for 64 by 64 to 128 bit products and 128 by 64 divisions, and whether the opcode vectors pass through them. Result: ruint 1.20.0 divides with MG10 reciprocals (reciprocal_mg10 by table and 64 bit products, div_2x1_mg10, div_3x2_mg10, Knuth div_nxm), so no u128 division and no compiler-builtins call (__udivti3, __umodti3, __multi3) occurs: the linked object of the handlers references none, products are DMULTU and DMULT with MFHI and MFLO, and the only divisions are three DDIVU for one-limb operands. The big-endian path of pu128::get (lib.rs:107-118) joins limbs in the right order. Compiled with rustc 1.97.0 for kona's target spec and run in a Cannon-semantics emulator, all 85,544 targeted and 96,876 battery vectors and the pool math checks match; planted faults (MOVN on bit 0, 5 bit DSLLV mask, a DMULTU high word error) give 624, 895 and 1,797 mismatches on 4,278 sampled targeted vectors. Result: eth_call on Ethereum at block 26,487,021: OptimismPortal 0xc5c5D157 version 5.1.1 and AnchorStateRegistry 0x8fe58d21 both return respectedGameType 42. DisputeGameFactory 0xFbAC1621 gameImpls(42) = 0x1736c101, an OP Succinct fault dispute game version 2.1.0 with aggregationVkey 0x006e44fd...4850, rangeVkeyCommitment 0x543e17e8...1746, SP1 verifier 0x3b604117 and access manager 0x2c4e8f33. proposers(0) and challengers(0) are false, so proposing and challenging are allowlisted; FALLBACK_TIMEOUT is 1,209,600 s, after which proposals open. An ordinary account cannot turn a divergence of the SP1 program into a challenge of an honest root; it could at most propose after 14 days of proposer silence. Which op-succinct release and integer library the range vkey belongs to was not determined. - Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, cycle 13. Lead L-677: which go-ethereum commit nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f runs, and whether its jump destination cache and opcode handlers differ from 0e44603. Result: Not readable. raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for OffchainLabs/nitro at b72783f and for v3.13 branch and tag names, and nitro v3.12.4 carries .private-submodules.conf, which rewrites the go-ethereum and wasmer submodules to their private variants when the repository is built privately, so the rc.9 build most likely uses a private go-ethereum. The newest public pin is v3.12.4 at go-ethereum 0e44603 (GitHub tree page), the commit cycles 9 to 12 read; the fork's public master (461e517) is older and differs only by value-versus-pointer operands in the arithmetic handlers. In 0e44603 the jump destination cache is keyed by the hash from StateDB.GetCodeHash of the resolved address and is filled at SetCallCode (evm.go:348-551, contract.go:93-110), so entries describe the bytes of that hash and a reorg or redelegation changes the hash, not the entry. The opcode answers of the rc.9 endpoints were tested by earlier cycles and match. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-proof-builds-2.work/nitro/0e44603_core_vm_evm.go ; research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-proof-builds-2.work/nitro/v3124_private-submodulesconf ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/v3.12.4/.private-submodules.conf ; https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/tree/v3.12.4
- Base, cycle 13. KECCAK256 and keccak caching in the Base range program on the zkVM. Result: In the range program lock alloy-primitives 1.6.1 depends on sha3 0.11.0 and keccak 0.2.0 from the registry, and no crate depends on tiny-keccak or fixed-cache; the sp1-patches entries target tiny-keccak 2.0.2 and sha3 0.10.8, so they do not apply to the hash behind KECCAK256. The opcode therefore runs portable Rust code in the zkVM and no keccak cache is linked. This costs cycles and does not change results; keccak 0.2.0 on RISC-V was not run here. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/6efa75662b57c578d897fea2449035636f6ad9ad/crates/proof/zk/programs/succinct/Cargo.lock ; research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-proof-builds-2.work/base/crates_proof_zk_programs_succinct_Cargo.toml
- all 21 networks, cycle 13. For each of the 21 networks: could an opcode the PoolManager runs give another result in the build that settles state than on the node, and could an ordinary account use it. Result: No on all 21 as far as tested. Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc and HyperEVM settle on the client that produces blocks (no separate proof build; covered by OPCODES.md checks 1 to 4). OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink: kona-client 1.9.0 on MIPS64, permissionless games, no divergence in the compiled handlers or the prestate scan (this unit). World Chain: op-program 1.9.0 on MIPS64, permissioned, no divergence (cycle 12). Zora and Soneium: no proof program, operator only (cycle 12). Base: SP1 range program on RV64IM, permissionless challenges, no divergence (this unit). Celo and X Layer: OP Succinct with allowlisted challengers, program arithmetic not identified, unknown but not usable by an ordinary account. Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium: wasm replay settled in cycle 12; the go-ethereum of the rc.9 nodes is private and unknown, endpoint answers match. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-proof-builds-2.work ; OPCODES.md ; cycles/012/theme-proof-builds.research.json

- all 21 networks, cycle 13. Swap events with amount0 = amount1 = 0 and price, tick and liquidity unchanged, which the step formulas cannot produce. Result: 451 such events across the windows. PoolManager.swap rejects amountSpecified == 0 (src/PoolManager.sol:193), and a nonzero amount always moves the price or spends the amount (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-437, src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:63-105). The only path to a zero swap is a hook with BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA_FLAG whose specified delta cancels the amount (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:266-277), after which Pool.swap returns ZERO_DELTA without touching state (src/libraries/Pool.sol:320). Every such event whose pool key was found has a hook address with bit 3 set; the rest are on pools whose key no public source gave, and they fit only that path. The event is correct and moves no funds. Evidence: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:266-277
- all 21 networks, cycle 13. Pools initialized inside the window, where the parent block has an empty slot0. Result: 611 pools were initialized inside the windows. In a first run that started from the zero slot0 of the parent block, the first swaps of such pools came out unmatched on Ethereum and Zora. Started from the Initialize event (sqrtPriceX96 and tick, lpFee from the key, src/PoolManager.sol:128-138, src/libraries/Pool.sol:100-107) and carried through the liquidity added in the same block, all match. The protocol fee of a new pool is zero in this build: initialize sets no protocol fee (src/libraries/Pool.sol:105-106). Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:100-107
- all 21 networks, cycle 13. Event semantics for pools with hooks that return deltas: the Swap event carries the pool delta of Pool.swap, computed from amountToSwap after the beforeSwap delta, before afterSwap adjusts the caller delta. Result: src/PoolManager.sol:202-250 emits delta.amount0(), delta.amount1() of pool.swap(params) with amountSpecified = amountToSwap, so a hook delta changes the specified amount the loop starts from and never the arithmetic the event reports. The replay therefore needs no special case for return-delta hooks: it derives the specified amount from the event, and all swaps on return-delta hook pools in the windows match. Hook and token behaviour was not swept (owner instruction). Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:230-250

- Monad, cycle 14. Step 2 planted fault: MULMOD(a, b, 2^256 - 1) returns one more than the true remainder, on every call (FAULT=mm1) or only when a*b >= 2^256 (FAULT=mm1big). Result: mm1: 0 of 614,687 v4 pairs and 0 of 49,726 v3 pairs match, because the 1e6 and Q96 denominators then take the 512 bit branch with a wrong high word. mm1big: unmatched v4 pairs rise from 2,414 to 3,167 and v3 from 5,905 to 7,723, and the full-loop replay of the newest 40,000 blocks goes from 0 to 78 unmatched. The fault is caught only for even denominators. With an odd denominator, twos is 1 and add(div(sub(0, twos), twos), 1) is 0 (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:59-75), so prod1 drops out and the result is prod0 times the inverse modulo 2^256, which is exact whenever the quotient fits. oddden.py confirms this on 400,000 inputs: 0 wrong results for 200,129 odd denominators and 199,871 of 199,871 wrong for even ones. A fault in the high word for an odd denominator therefore cannot change a PoolManager amount unless it moves prod1 between zero and nonzero or across the require at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:30. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/014/theme-monad-native-path.work/big-fault-mm1.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/014/theme-monad-native-path.work/big-fault-mm1big.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/014/theme-monad-native-path.work/replay2-v4-fault-mm1big.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/014/theme-monad-native-path.work/oddden.json ; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:59-99

Result: Not decidable without a build of the emitter. The bound is max_code_size = 10,240 (CompilerConfig default, compiler/ir/x86/types.hpp line 141) + 32 x bytecode size (x86.hpp lines 53-64): 778,528 bytes for the PoolManager and 732,992 for the v3 pool. The estimate checked after every instruction and block (x86.cpp lines 308-341 and 466-479) is text size + 32 per pending CALLDATALOAD or BYTE handler + 32 per read-only constant + 4 x bytecode size (emitter.cpp lines 1020-1029), so the jump table alone takes 96,036 and 90,344 bytes and the PoolManager compiles only if its x86 text stays below about 682,000 bytes, 65 bytes per EVM instruction. Over the bound the Nativecode has no entry point and vm.cpp lines 152-157 interpret it for the rest of the revision. The observable the plan proposed does not exist in served data: frames are stored only by tracing nodes, which interpret, and gas is equal in both modes (cycle 13, emitter.cpp 3106-3116). Result: A MULMOD by any modulus other than 2^256-1 that returns one more when the product exceeds 256 bits (the remainder step at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48 and the rounding test at FullMath.sol:112) leaves 0 of the 2,816 (Monad), 3,741 (MegaETH) and 493 (HyperEVM) 512 bit matches standing. A MULMOD by 2^256-1 that returns one more when the high half is nonzero leaves 2,840 of the 3,741 MegaETH matches standing. That is a property of the algorithm, not a weakness of the check: for an odd denominator twos is 1, the flip at FullMath.sol:73 makes it 0 and prod1 * twos at FullMath.sol:75 is 0, so the high half only feeds the bound at FullMath.sol:30 and the branch at FullMath.sol:33. An interpreter fault that moves prod1 by one without making it zero or reaching the denominator would give the same pool results for odd denominators. Result: The constant denominator at pcs 22330-22377 is 2^128, so this copy computes feesOwed. prod1 is nonzero only when the fee growth delta times liquidity is at least 2^256, which makes feesOwed at least 2^128. Pool.modifyLiquidity casts feesOwed with toInt128 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:192), which reverts for any value of 2^127 or more (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-57). On a node that follows the specification, this branch therefore always ends in a revert and its quotient never reaches state. Reaching it needs at least 2^128 units of fees credited to one position, which only a token whose author mints that much can supply (pool-creator). No mined instance exists on the three networks, and none is expected. Evidence: src/libraries/Position.sol:93-96; src/libraries/Pool.sol:188-192; src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-57; research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json runtime pcs 22275-22382
- HyperEVM, cycle 14. HyperEVM contracts that emit the v3 Swap topic with a tick one below getTickAtSqrtPrice of the emitted price (55 of 9,057 events, 53 from 0x586304481f7be6cb7738bbb913a693dfdd801480). Result: These contracts are 5,036 and 14,094 byte programs without factory() or tickSpacing(), so they are not Uniswap v3 pools and their event convention is their own. Their slot0 at the latest block gives a tick equal to getTickAtSqrtPrice of the stored price (for example -235,337 for price 614,990,369,859,390,990,714,731), so the node computes TickMath as the source does. No PoolManager event on HyperEVM breaks the tick relation (2,284 of 2,284). ## Reading of the source (theme-reth-cache-drift)

- all 21 networks, cycle 14. Whether the PoolManager's own storage, its transient storage, or the balanceOf staticcall of sync can read a stale word from the reth execution cache branch for a destroyed account without code. Result: The branch is taken only for accounts whose info at the start of the block had the empty code hash and that the block destroyed. The PoolManager has had code since deployment and cannot be destroyed under EIP-6780, so its account is never on the branch and insert_storage replaces each of its written words after every block. Transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14) lives in the EVM journal and is not in the execution cache. The balanceOf read of sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364, src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) reads the token's storage, which can be stale only for a token created in the block that destroyed its address. The account cache entry of a branch account is removed, so its code hash and balance are read fresh, and code is looked up by code hash. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/reth/74cc8bbce7631c3586ab446460590fef6630d258/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs lines 863-882; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288
- all 21 networks, cycle 14. Which accounts can reach the stale branch, including EIP-7702 delegated accounts, accounts emptied under EIP-161, and the contracts a victim pool depends on. Result: Reachable: an address created and self-destructed in one transaction, an account without code that a creation landed on and that self-destructed in the same transaction, and an empty account removed under EIP-161, each re-created later in the same block. All of them carry code deployed in that block. An EIP-7702 delegated account has a non-empty code hash, so a destroyed one would take the clear-everything branch, and it cannot be destroyed because it was not created in the transaction and its nonce is above zero; after its delegation is cleared it keeps storage and a nonce and still cannot be destroyed or created over. Tokens, hooks, routers, PositionManager and Permit2 already used by a pool had code before any such block and cannot be destroyed; a proxy runs its implementation with the proxy's own storage. A victim pool can therefore depend on a branch account only by choosing a token or hook made in that pattern, which is an attacker-made contract (actor pool-creator). Evidence: https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28148.patch
- Ethereum, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, Tempo, Arc, cycle 14. Is the old branch present at the reth revision the endpoint reports. Result: No. Ethereum reth v2.11.0, op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 (65e80332, pins ethereum-optimism/reth op-v2.7.0-2 ce8cfb1; rc.1 pins op-v2.7.0-1 ed91041, also fixed), Tempo v1.19.1 (paradigmxyz/reth 167933d) and Arc v0.8.6-rc1 and v0.8.5 (circlefin/arc-reth 508cbdf) all remove the account only when its current info is None and otherwise write the re-created account's storage (cached_state.rs lines 1165-1185, Arc 864-884). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/ce8cfb1fd25c2da86004eda677dc55dfa0d5c0af/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/167933d17ad47fe7354f5942ddd6f0d3e343bb41/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-reth/508cbdf7d6ba49b4ce735d678863897067fa381a/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; web3_clientVersion and arc_getVersion queried 2026-11-24
- Optimism, Zora, Worldchain, X Layer, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 14. Does the block producer of OP Mainnet, Zora, World Chain, X Layer or reth-bsc read through the execution cache. Result: No in the public code. The op-reth OP payload builder destructures BuildArguments with .. and reads state_by_block_hash directly (op-reth v2.8.1 rust/op-reth/crates/payload/src/builder.rs line 257, rc.4 line 193). conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 and world-chain v2.8.2 use an op-reth OP builder whose lock entry does not depend on reth-execution-cache, and World Chain's flashblocks builder discards the cache (crates/builder/src/payload_builder.rs line 125, execution_cache: _). xlayer-builder and the X Layer OP builder do not depend on reth-execution-cache. - Unichain, Ink, Soneium, Optimism, cycle 14. Lead L-703: what changed between op-reth v2.10.0-rc.1 and rc.4 in the engine tree, execution cache, prewarming, state root task and op-revm handler. In the optimism repository, op-revm changes only test code in fast_lz.rs (the module after line 99 is cfg(test)); handler.rs is unchanged. op-reth's evm, consensus, payload and node changes remove type parameters (OpEvmConfig now fixed to OpChainSpec and OpReceipt), keep the same EVM factory OpEvmFactory with NullRefundPolicy, and add a test for the Isthmus withdrawals root. No change alters a storage, transient storage, balance or code read inside a transaction. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.1/rust/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/op-revm/src/fast_lz.rs
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, BNB Smart Chain, Tempo, Arc, cycle 14. Other caches in front of state on reth based clients, looking for an index that is not the full content or address. Result: The execution cache indexes code by code hash, accounts by full address and storage by (full address, full slot); clear() keeps the code cache because its mapping cannot change. The precompile cache is per precompile address, indexed by the full input bytes, returns an entry only when the stored spec matches and the call has at least the recorded gas, stores only successful outputs that consumed no state gas, and is applied only through map_cacheable_precompiles, which skips precompiles marked stateful; Celo's transfer precompile is built with .stateful() (alloy-celo-evm lib.rs line 125). The payload builder's CachedReads is indexed by address and slot, is pre-filled from a committed block and used only for a job whose parent is that block hash, and falls through to the database for slots it lacks. Base's txpool prewarm keeps its own CachedReads and starts a fresh one for each head. The sparse trie cache feeds only state root computation. The src/ code calls no precompile. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/ce8cfb1fd25c2da86004eda677dc55dfa0d5c0af/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/3c5f2f11c4e5a5647e6e911cd131ccf1bada4f25/crates/payload/basic/src/lib.rs lines 131-246; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/refs/tags/celo/reth-v1.0.10/crates/alloy-celo-evm/src/lib.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 14. HyperEVM nanoreth execution cache. Result: Blocks are produced by Hyperliquid's own node, which answers web3_clientVersion with hyperliquid evm Mainnet. The archive follower nanoreth pins hl-archive-node/reth 1450962, whose cache invalidates the whole storage of a destroyed account before continuing (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/cached_state.rs lines 381-387), so it has no stale words of that kind. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/reth/14509628ed37e9a9b7110ea855a67f427c4d61fc/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/cached_state.rs
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, Avalanche, Monad, cycle 14. Exposure of non-reth networks to the reth execution cache fault. Result: Not applicable. Their endpoints report nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 and an unversioned nitro, bor v2.11.1, avalanchego 1.15.3 and Monad 0.16.7, none of which uses the reth engine tree. - HyperEVM, cycle 15. L-738. Do mined v3 style swaps on HyperEVM, produced by the closed hl-node validator, match the exact FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and TickMath formulas of src/libraries on the 512 bit product branch, the amount above 2^160 branch, the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp, and on swaps that end on a tick?. Pools were identified from their own getters (factory, token0, token1, fee, tickSpacing) and kept only when factory.getPool(token0, token1, fee) or getPool(token0, token1, tickSpacing) returned the pool, which is what a PoolCreated log would establish; the PoolCreated log scan over 52 million blocks was started and abandoned as too slow. 431 pools of 14 factories pass, holding 2,258,337 swaps (69 percent). The largest factories are 0xff7b3e8c00e57ea31477c32a5b52a58eea47b072 (1,115,904 swaps), 0x07e60782535752be279929e2dffdd136db2e6b45 (495,284), 0xb1c0fa0b789320044a6f623cfe5ebda9562602e3 (278,022) and 0x32b9da73215255d50d84feb51540b75acc1324c2 (220,491). Stage A, without RPC: 1,686,939 swaps equal one v3 swap step to the unit from the price, tick and liquidity of the pool's previous log, 35,596 of them through the 512 bit branch of mulDiv or mulDivRoundingUp. No swap reached the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and no logged amount is at or above 2^160. 2,995 swaps end exactly on the price of a tick that is a multiple of the spacing. Stage B, with eth_call at the parent block for slot0, liquidity, the tick bitmap and liquidityNet, and the block's Mint and Burn logs applied in order: all 2,995 end-on-tick groups and random samples of 3,000 groups with a 512 bit step and 25,000 groups that may need one inside a multi-step swap (two random draws, which can overlap), 30,995 groups in all. 33,760 swaps reproduce price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to the unit, 19,015 of them through the 512 bit branch (65,309 mulDiv calls with a product of 512 bits), 7,359 with several steps. 22,032 needed the pool's real fee, which differs from fee() on dynamic fee pools and was found by search: one free parameter is fitted per swap and price, tick, liquidity and both amounts must then all match; most fees found are multiples of 100 pips between 0 and 4,000, and a few are other values such as 10,562. 4 did not reproduce: 0x47a2f2ff4d1e218bba017d19222073eaa07b5740289dcca39cd3c88a2ddae25c (block 50,624,670); 0x5a64629ddf197c4e3c2addd942cf25e0a55d7d0b4b659d56249adb3f9b471458 (block 51,255,107); 0xd144959f18fd332b6c3c8111486b41111e44e91ca82d1cc28ffd01b848df7eca (block 51,371,005); 0x3d3c51a3d7ee8bbd78940198e2850863299c7c9a20ff4d913a9d16251678cef0 (block 51,370,051). Each is explained by the collector: the pool also emitted a liquidity event with topic 0xd78218c0d304e8893cb3200abe394bbc8d5b7804d9c51f236df9fdcf481d02d3 (a Mint variant with ticks in topics 2 and 3) that the collector does not read, and with that event applied the liquidity before the swap equals the logged liquidity in every case (chkmis.py; for 0x47a2f2ff, 3,174,629,732,523,735,714,636 + 6,417,522,110,843,946,721,988 = 9,592,151,843,367,682,436,624, the logged value). Planted faults: MULMOD one too high on 512 bit products made 131 of 137 swaps fail, and getSqrtPriceAtTick one unit high on multiples of 10 made 117 of 121 fail, so the comparison sees both classes. A fallback fault cannot be shown because no mined swap reaches that branch. The transcription used is tools/opdiff/v4math.py of src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-120, SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-52 and TickMath.sol:57-160. Validator output on the 512 bit branch is now checked on tens of thousands of swaps against 493 before. The fallback branch and amounts above 2^160 still have no mined instance on HyperEVM, in v3 style pools or in the PoolManager. - MegaETH, cycle 15. L-732. Which reth revision do the public MegaETH locks name, and does its execution cache keep stale storage for an account that was destroyed and re-created without code in one block?. Result: mega-reth itself is not public (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-reth/main/Cargo.toml returns 404) and the public RPC reports mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc; reth has no v2.2.3 tag (the execution cache file at that tag returns 404). mega-evm v1.7.4's Cargo.toml says it is built against reth v2.3.0 (revm 40.0.3, alloy-evm 0.36.0), and the stateless-validator lock at e1618ed7 pins reth tag v2.3.0 at commit 9384bc53d8c0c77e59cac83fdaaf3b372c6d2216. The branch only touches an address that held no code at the start of the block and was destroyed and re-created inside it, so it cannot reach the PoolManager's storage or a token or hook that an existing pool already uses; a contract the attacker re-creates is its own, which is at most pool-creator level, and a stale read on the sequencer would publish state that the stateless validator rejects, which is operator level. Which HyperCore action produced the first unsigned system transfer in the name of 0xc20699185c15D0a2fD65779BB5d69f5b0B113c00, and can HyperCore do the same for a contract that no spot token links?. Result: The address is the USDC treasury address that Coinbase named as AQAv2 treasury deployer on 8 June 2026; it has no code (eth_getCode returns 0x) and nonce 1,057,535 at block 52,160,000. Binary search of eth_getTransactionCount on the archive client puts its first transaction in block 37,597,803 (2026-06-12 03:59:16 UTC): system transaction 0x2a36e3161a6271d7bcf0145928660f63fd5a5c0839fdcd2400b081107b991385 (0x01f391a92efbdff628ea8b24a09adaa08a215fca6f7b38cb3db7bbb8ed378b61 on the archive client), USDC transfer(0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24, 2,000,000,000) with gas price 0, next to a system transaction from 0x2000000000000000000000000000000000000000 to that linked contract. This is the AQAv2 rebalance: the Hyperliquid documentation says the treasury deployer designates the treasury address, AQAv2 is activated by validator vote after both deployers stake 500k HYPE and send authorization transactions from their staking accounts, and the linked HyperEVM contract then rebalances with the treasury address in a 9:1 ratio. The address was therefore designated by a staked deployer and activated by validator vote; it is not a contract that HyperCore picked without a record. For the PoolManager to be named the same way, a treasury deployer staking 500k HYPE and a validator vote would be needed, so F-020 stays at operator level. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/aligned-quote-assets; https://www.livebitcoinnews.com/coinbase-activates-aqav2-for-hyperliquid-usdc-treasury/; eth_getTransactionCount, eth_getBlockByNumber 0x23db20b on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com; eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber and eth_getCode on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm

## Reading of the source (theme-evm2-jit-codegen)

- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Can the evm2 JIT crates be built here so that their own differential tests run on the PoolManager runtime?. Result: No. The LLVM backend needs LLVM 23 (crates/jit/README.md), and the machine has LLVM 18.1.3 (llvm-config --version). The workspace Cargo.toml patches the ark crates from a git repository on github.com, which this environment cannot clone, and codeload.github.com returned 403 for source archives of both revisions. The review therefore worked from source: 58 files of crates/jit (codegen, builtins, backend, llvm, runtime, context) were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at 66687c18 and at 35aa3280 by following module declarations (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/crawl.py, copies in research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/r66 and r35), plus crates/evm2 at 66687c18. Between the two revisions 8 of the 58 files differ. In codegen the only change is block_analysis.rs lines 2249-2250, which gives opcodes flagged UNKNOWN no stack inputs, and a test. peephole.rs, const_fold.rs, translate/mod.rs, memory_sections.rs and sections.rs are byte-identical. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/README.md
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Which PoolManager opcodes the JIT sends to builtins that wrap the interpreter's own arithmetic, and whether those builtins match the interpreter. Result: The runtime (24,009 bytes, no metadata trailer) contains 112 distinct opcodes (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/census.json). DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP with an unknown exponent are calls to builtins (translate/mod.rs 776-803). The builtins call ruint wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, add_mod, mul_mod and pow, and evm2's i256_div and i256_mod (builtins/src/lib.rs 112-160). These are the same functions the interpreter uses, linked natively into the same binary at the same ruint version (builtins are resolved by address, builtins/src/ir.rs 1-40). The rev! macro reads the operands top first and writes the result into the lowest slot, which is the specified order. So MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 at FullMath.sol:24 and with a pool denominator at FullMath.sol:48, SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 and FullMath.sol:112 runs the code that the 185,529 vectors already tested through the interpreter. KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, LOG and the calls are builtins as well (lib.rs 162-575, 762-875) and were read: CALLDATALOAD past the end pads with zeros through evm2 read_word_padded, RETURNDATACOPY fails before charging gas when offset plus length exceeds the return data, MCOPY expands memory to max(dst, src) plus length, KECCAK256 of length 0 touches no memory, TSTORE fails in a static frame and TLOAD does not. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/builtins/src/lib.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Inline lowering of SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO and the JUMPI condition, transcribed with LLVM poison semantics. Result: No mismatch. SIGNEXTEND is select(ext < 31, (x << (248 - 8ext)) >>s (248 - 8ext), x), BYTE is select(i < 32, (v >> (248 - 8i)) & 0xff, 0), and the shifts select 0, or for SAR the sign fill, when the count exceeds 255; the poisoned shift result is only in the unselected arm (translate/mod.rs 685-691, 804-875). Comparisons are i256 icmp, ISZERO is icmp eq 0, and JUMPI branches on icmp ne of the whole word (line 1050). jitmodel.py runs these on 631,353 vectors (the battery and targeted sets, every pair of 196 edge values for every index and count, all 256 powers of two and their negations as divisors and moduli) and makes 1,068,620 checks against the specification without a mismatch or undefined operation. Planted faults are caught: BYTE guard < 33 (367 mismatches), shift guard > 256 (1,659), SAR default without the sign (2,746), SIGNEXTEND guard < 30 (31). A SIGNEXTEND guard of < 32 gives no mismatch because index 31 shifts by 0, so that mutation is equivalent. This covers the SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SDIV and SMOD of TickBitmap.compress and position (TickBitmap.sol:20-38, 54-67). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/jitmodel.py
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Every peephole rule in peephole.rs, with most care for MULMOD with the constant moduli 2^96, 2^128 and 2^256-1, SDIV and SMOD by -1 and -2^255, EXP with a constant base or exponent, and the inline EXP gas. Result: No mismatch. A power of two modulus 2^k lowers MULMOD to (a*b mod 2^256) & (2^k - 1) and ADDMOD to (a+b mod 2^256) & (2^k - 1), which is exact because 2^k divides 2^256 (peephole.rs 161-213). This is the path for MULMOD by 2^128 at pc 22378 and by 2^96 at pc 22639, which a PUSH in the same block supplies (census.json). 2^256-1 and 1,000,000 are not powers of two and go to the ruint builtin. SDIV by -1 negates, by -2^255 returns x == -2^255, and by other signed powers of two uses LLVM sdiv, whose only undefined case is excluded; SMOD by 0, 1 or -1 is 0 and by other signed powers of two uses srem, which keeps the dividend's sign (53-160). EXP with a power of two base 2^k is select(e < ceil(256/k), 1 << ke, 0) and charges (263 - clz(e)) / 8 bytes of gas, which equals the specified byte length for every exponent tested (215-305). The PoolManager's own constant operands are a dividend of -887272 or 887272 for SDIV and SMOD (pc 7400-7443) and a dividend of 0xd76453e0 for DIV (BitMath.sol:45), which no rule matches, so they use the builtins. Planting a mask of 2^k instead of 2^k - 1 gives 14,252 mismatches. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/compiler/translate/peephole.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Constant folding and range folding in the bytecode analysis (const_fold.rs), including folded constants that are stored in place of an executed instruction (translate/mod.rs 633-656). Result: No unsound rule. try_const_fold calls ruint and evm2 i256 for the arithmetic and writes its own rules only for DIV and MOD by zero, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE and the three shifts (const_fold.rs 113-168); these were transcribed and match on all vectors. try_range_fold (213-389) gives a range below 2^31 that must hold every result when at least one input is a range or an unknown value. 60,000 random abstract inputs (ranges, inline constants, large constants including the BitMath byte table words, and unknown values) were each tested on sampled concrete values: 657,425 cases, none outside the range. Planting a range one smaller for MOD gives 30 failures. EXP folds only when its exponent is constant, so its gas stays static (bytecode/mod.rs 751-767). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/const_fold.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Edge refinement after a JUMPI in block_analysis.rs: the DUP, LT and GT patterns with ISZERO chains that bound a stack value on one edge, and at_most. Result: Sound. branch() (block_analysis.rs 1943-2017) recognises PUSH-target JUMPI after a DUP or a DUP and PUSH compared with LT or GT in either order, with any number of ISZEROs, and bounds the original value by c - 1 or c on the edge where the test says so. 38,465 random stacks, depths, constants and patterns were executed concretely and the bound held on every taken edge; a planted bound of c - 2 fails 20 times. at_most (160-168) keeps an infeasible edge's value unchanged and never widens a constant. Ranges only hold values below 2^31. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/block_analysis.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Dynamic JUMP and JUMPI through the dispatch table, jump target conversion, and multi-target jumps that switch on the low 64 bits. Result: No mismatch. A dynamic target saturates to 2^64-1 when it does not fit in 64 bits (u256_to_u64_saturating, translate/mod.rs 2269-2277), and the table holds every valid JUMPDEST of the code (2102-2172). jumptable.py transcribes the rank table and finds that each of the 24,030 tested pcs (0 to max_pc + 64, 2^40 and 2^64-1) dispatches to its own JUMPDEST when it is one of the 610 valid ones and to the invalid jump block otherwise; shifting the bitmap by one plants 1,220 errors. A multi-target jump truncates to 64 bits only when the analysis committed every value: constant sets hold only valid targets, ranges are below 2^31, an enumerated invalid constant must fit in 64 bits (fits_switch_case, 1938-1941), and an unknown operand marks the state failed (1686-1742), so no value of 2^64 or more can alias a valid pc. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/jumptable.py
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Memory expansion in compiled code: MLOAD and MSTORE inline checks, the per-section cache of checked ranges, the memory section analysis that skips checks, and mresize. Result: Correct as read. build_ensure_memory (translate/mod.rs 1858-1920) saturates offsets at 2^63-1, and mresize calls resize_evm with length 0, which still grows memory to the offset (evm2 memory.rs 101-114). A later access is exempt only if its base equals an earlier checked base and its constant addend is at least the earlier one, so its offset cannot exceed 2^64 and its end lies below memory already allocated. memory_sections.rs propagates a lower bound on memory size that is the minimum over predecessors (join_state 285-297) and only counts constant accesses that always expand memory; MCOPY counts max(dst, src) (bytecode/mod.rs 790-806). Checks are skipped only where that bound covers the exact required size. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/memory_sections.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Gas charged per section against per-instruction charging, and stack checks at section entry: can compiled code return a different result from a call or decide a branch differently?. Result: No. Gas sections end at every branching instruction and at every instruction whose host effect depends on the remaining gas: calls, creates, SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, EXTCODE*, SELFDESTRUCT and host-table opcodes (sections.rs 229-256, bytecode/mod.rs 1214-1240). The static gas of the section is charged at its head, so a frame that runs out of gas inside a section halts at its head instead of a few instructions later, with the same exceptional halt, all frame gas consumed and every effect reverted. GAS returns the remaining gas plus the gas owed by later instructions of its section (translate/mod.rs 1143-1153, sections.rs 109-141), which is the specified value. Sections without a check carry the deficit as negative remaining gas until a signed check before any builtin that charges or reads gas. Stack bounds are checked at the head of a stack section and never ahead of a host-effect instruction. At 35aa3280 the SSTORE builtin skips a cold load when the remaining gas is below the full cold cost, as the interpreter at that revision does; the SLOAD builtin is unchanged and uses the additional cold cost like the interpreter (evm2 host.rs 14-31 at both revisions). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/sections.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. How a node decides to compile a contract, whether compiled and interpreted frames mix in one transaction, and what happens to a block when they disagree. Result: evm2 compiles a code hash after 8 lookups (jit_hot_threshold) when the code is at most 24 KiB, 24,576 bytes (runtime/config.rs 17, 280-290, 368-377). The PoolManager's deployed code is 24,009 bytes on Ethereum and on Tempo (eth_getCode, queried 2026-11-25), so it is eligible even under evm2's default, and reth v2.11.0 removes the limit (max-bytecode-len default 0) and keeps the threshold of 8. The decision is per frame: run_supported looks up the code hash and spec, runs the compiled function if it is resident and otherwise returns None so that the interpreter runs the frame (runtime/src/evm2_evm.rs 59-104). Compilation runs in background workers, so one transaction can run the PoolManager frame compiled and a hook or token frame interpreted, or the reverse. On Ethereum, a reth node whose compiled code disagreed with the specification would compute a different state root and fork itself off, while geth and the other clients decide the canonical chain (F-129). Tempo has one client; its release binary is built without the JIT feature (cleared in cycle 14), so no Tempo validator runs this code. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/runtime/src/runtime/config.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Whether an ordinary account can reach compiled code on the networks.json endpoints through eth_call or switch it on. Result: No. The Ethereum endpoint reports reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc, rpc_modules lists rpc, net, web3, txpool, debug, eth and trace, and reth_jit returns Method not found (queried 2026-11-25). Tempo reports tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 and refuses rpc_modules. Only an operator can enable the JIT, so the actor for any JIT fault is operator. Evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc, HyperEVM, cycle 15. Does any of the other 19 networks run the evm2 JIT?. Result: No. web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-25 (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/clientversions.json): OP Mainnet op-reth v2.8.1, Unichain, Ink and Soneium op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, Base reth v2.5.2 base v1.5.6, Zora conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, Worldchain world-chain v2.8.2, Celo reth v2.2.0, X Layer reth v2.3.0. op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and v2.8.1 build on revm 43 and op-revm with no evm2 dependency (rust/Cargo.toml of those tags), and reth v2.2.0, v2.3.0, v2.5.2 and v2.8.2 have no evm2 entry in their manifests. Arbitrum One and Elysium run Nitro, Polygon bor, BNB Smart Chain geth, Avalanche avalanchego, Arc its revm based node, and Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM their own executors, which earlier cycles read separately. Robinhood Chain answered 429 to this query and runs Nitro by earlier cycles. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/Cargo.toml

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-emitter-blocks)

- Monad, cycle 15. Task 2 (lead L-726): is the PoolManager compiled at all by Monad's x86 emitter. Method: the emitter was built from downloaded source (category-labs/monad v0.16.7 and v0.16.5 category/vm and category/core from cdn.jsdelivr.net, asmjit at commit 9eb6edbf711ceb25346ee40bae68b40a4505cdf5 from raw.githubusercontent.com, evmc master of category-labs/evmc with the fork's four struct fields added by hand), the runtime symbols it only references were stubbed, and native::compile was run with the production CompilerConfig on the build of this checkout and on the code read with eth_getCode from 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e at https://rpc.monad.xyz (24,009 bytes, sha256 prefix 288b97729c9e4f34; it differs from build/PoolManager.json only in the 20 immutable bytes at offset 13606, which hold the PoolManager address). Result: It is compiled. The size check compares Emitter::estimate_size() (text size + 32 per pending CALLDATALOAD handler + read-only data + 4 x bytecode size, emitter.cpp 1020-1030) with max_code_size(10,240, 24,009) = 10,240 + 32 x 24,009 = 778,528 bytes (x86.hpp 53-65, types.hpp CompilerConfig max_code_size_offset = 10 x 1024, x86.cpp 308-315 and 468-479). The built emitter prints 285,084 bytes for the deployed code and 285,059 for the build with a zero immutable under v0.16.7, and 284,482 and 284,425 under v0.16.5, for MonadTraits MONAD_EIGHT, NINE and TEN alike, and returns an entry point (error_code NoError). This is a measurement from a build, not a bound. The asmjit commit is the vcpkg pin of 2025-05-08, not the submodule pin of the release, which could not be read without the GitHub API; a different asmjit could move the estimate by a few percent at most, and the margin is a factor of 2.7. Evidence: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.hpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vcpkg/master/ports/asmjit/portfile.cmake ; eth_getCode 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e at https://rpc.monad.xyz block 0x775837e ; cycles/015/theme-monad-emitter-blocks.work/driver.cpp, drv, drv165
- Monad, cycle 15. Task 3 (lead L-725): which execution mode Monad validators run by default and after how much interpreted gas the PoolManager is compiled. Result: The execution daemon builds vm::VM vm{trace_calls ? InterpreterOnly : Dual} (cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7, line 479 at v0.16.5), so a node runs Dual unless it is started with --trace_calls. The published full node instructions recommend --trace_calls only for archive and RPC nodes, and the validator installation page says nothing about execution flags. The docs list monad 0.16.5 for mainnet and 0.16.7 for testnet. In Dual mode VM::execute_raw (vm.cpp 140-191, identical in v0.16.5 and v0.16.7) runs a contract in the interpreter and starts asynchronous compilation once the gas the interpreter has spent on that code hash, summed over all executions, reaches max_code_size(10,240, code size), which is 778,528 gas for the 24,009 byte PoolManager; when the node's code cache is not yet warm it compiles at once. A validator that follows the published setup therefore runs the PoolManager as native code after its first few transactions, and RPC nodes with --trace_calls interpret it. Evidence: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.5/cmd/monad/main.cpp ; cycles/014/theme-monad-native-path.work/src/monad-v0.16.7_cmd_monad_main.cpp lines 484-488 ; https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/full-node-installation.md ; https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/validator-installation.md ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/vm.cpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/code.hpp
- Monad, cycle 15. Task 1: the compiled code of the never-mined paths against Monad's interpreter. A harness (harness.cpp) links Monad's real interpreter (interpreter::execute), the real emitter (native::compile) and the real runtime library from v0.16.7, with one in-memory host that keeps storage, transient storage, warm sets, logs and balances and reverts them per frame. Every transaction runs twice from the same state, once interpreted and once as native code, with MonadTraits MONAD_TEN, and the harness compares every call result (status, gas left, return bytes), all storage and transient storage, balances and logs. Users and an ERC20 are host-level accounts; inside unlockCallback a user runs a script of PoolManager calls and can read its own delta through exttload and pay it, mint it, or clear it exactly. Paths: clear of an exact credit (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319), transferFrom and burn through an allowance or an operator (src/ERC6909.sol:35-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22), approve and setOperator (src/ERC6909.sol:50-64), donate (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480), the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52), the amount above 2^160 branch of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97), and take, mint, clear and swap amounts drawn from edge sets around 2^64, 2^96, 2^127, 2^128, 2^159 to 2^161, 2^255 and 2^256 - 1. Result: No difference. 20,000 mixed scenarios (629,823 transactions and 676,709 calls inside unlocks) and nine per-path batteries of 100,000 calls each (approve, transferFrom, burn, clear, donate, fallback, amount above 2^160, take, swap; 291,020 transactions) give identical results in the interpreter and in native code, gas left included. The v0.16.5 build gives the same on 5,450 scenarios. The only raw difference is the status class of an exceptional halt: native code reports EVMC_FAILURE where the interpreter reports EVMC_OUT_OF_GAS, both with zero gas left; a receipt and a calling frame see only failure, so the harness compares halts as one class. A trace build of the interpreter records coverage: every instruction of clear (17 of 17), transferFrom (60 of 60), approve, setOperator, _burnFrom (37 of 37), Pool.donate (42 of 42), UnsafeMath.simpleMulDiv (35 of 35) and the fallback at SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 (12 of 12) ran; 7,505 of 10,418 PoolManager instructions ran in total. Two planted emitter faults are caught: SUB without borrow propagation (emitter.cpp 2481) makes 200 of 200 mixed and 90 of 90 battery scenarios differ, and an off-by-one in LT with a literal left operand (emitter.cpp 4029) makes 111 of 200 mixed and 48 of 90 battery scenarios differ. Evidence: cycles/015/theme-monad-emitter-blocks.work/harness.cpp, gen.py, gen_mass.py, runs/summary.txt, mass/summary.txt, v165/summary.txt, fault/summary.txt, fault/out14_f1.txt, fault/out14_f2.txt, cov/regions.json ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/interpreter/execute.cpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp
- Monad, cycle 15. Task 1: the exact basic blocks of each path and the emitter routines chosen for them. The emitter's own assembly log (CompilerConfig asm_log_path, with a comment for every EVM instruction and block) was written for the deployed code (pm.asm, 48,691 lines) and cut into the blocks that hold an instruction of each path (blocks/*.asm, blocks/summary.json, blocks/routines.json). Result: The paths occupy 85 blocks with 940 EVM instructions and 3,264 x86 instructions: clear 5 blocks (0xde6 to 0xe31), transferFrom 11, approve 1 (0x2518), setOperator 1 (0x20c1), _burnFrom 7, Pool.donate 8, the fallback 3 (0x5d5d, 0x5d6c, 0x5d71), getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp 15, getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown 13, simpleMulDiv 6. Of the EVM instructions, 624 emit no code (PUSH, DUP, SWAP and POP live in the virtual stack), 163 call runtime routines (DIV and MOD of variable operands, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, KECCAK256, LOG, CALL, memory growth), 112 use AVX moves for block-exit spills and wide literals, 52 are four-limb GPR arithmetic or comparisons (cmp or sub followed by sbb, add followed by adc), and the rest are shifts, setcc after fused ISZERO pairs, and branches. A comparison feeding JUMPI stays in CPU flags, and a dynamic JUMP checks the target below 24,009 with the three upper limbs zero and then goes through a jump table over every byte offset (fallback block 0x5d71). The comparison of whole transactions above runs exactly these instruction sequences on all their entries, so a Python model of each routine was not needed; the comparison is with Monad's interpreter, which cycles 1 to 14 matched to the specification on 185,529 vectors and the mined replays, and not with pyevm.py. Evidence: cycles/015/theme-monad-emitter-blocks.work/asmlog.cpp, pm.asm, blocks.py, routines.py, blocks/summary.json, blocks/routines.json ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp (lt 4008-4048, sub 2447-2481, jumpi 3499, udiv 3427, estimate_size 1020-1030)
- Monad, cycle 15. Whether the overflow fallback at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 and the amount above 2^160 branches at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 can decide the outcome of a swap that succeeds, which would make a compiled-only fault there reach funds. Result: They cannot. The fallback runs only on an exact-input step that stops short of its target (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:74-82) with amountRemainingLessFee times the current price sqrtC at or above 2^256 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:41-43), so the input is at least 2^256 / sqrtC. Inside one step the token1 output equals input times sqrtC times sqrtN / 2^192, where sqrtN is the price at which the step stops, so the output is at least 2^64 times sqrtN. A zeroForOne step searches for its target inside the current bitmap word (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:94-104, src/libraries/Pool.sol:348), and word 0 begins at compressed tick 0. A step that starts at a positive tick therefore never has a target below tick 0, where the price is 2^96, so sqrtN is at least 2^96 and the output is at least 2^160, which reverts in the toInt128 of src/libraries/Pool.sol:455 or :459. A step that starts at or below tick 0 has sqrtC of at most about 2^96, so the input is at least 2^160 and reverts the same way. The price limit can only move the target closer. The verifier of this cycle supplied this argument; the bound on liquidity alone does not exclude the fallback. The harness agrees: all 100,000 fallback calls and all 100,000 calls above 2^160 reverted with 0x93dafdf1 in both engines. Branch :105 (exact output above 2^160) needs more than 2^160 of output and was never reached, as cycle 12 found (jumpmap neverReached). A wrong result in these blocks could only change which error a reverting frame returns. Evidence: src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-52 ; src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:60-100 ; src/libraries/Pool.sol:453-460 ; cycles/015/theme-monad-emitter-blocks.work/mass/summary.txt

Whether any of the other 20 networks runs EVM bytecode through a compiler like Monad's. Result: No other network in networks.json runs Monad's emitter. The reth JIT (evm2 with reth_jit) was read in cycle 14 and is off on the public endpoints, and Stylus compiles WASM, not EVM bytecode (OPCODES.md, cycle 14 ethereum-reference and arbitrum-family). This unit tested nothing on these networks. Evidence: research/network-risk/OPCODES.md ; research/network-risk/cycles/014/critic.json

Condition for the untaken side: the success word is zero at 9048 (or 15094) while it was nonzero at 9042 (or 15088). Result: Unreachable on every network for any value a CALL or STATICCALL can push. The disassembly of the build reads CALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI at 9035-9042 and PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x241a, JUMPI at 9043-9048, and STATICCALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI, PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x3afa, JUMPI at 15081-15094. Both JUMPIs of a pair test the same stack word: the first leaves through 0x24c2 (9410: RETURNDATACOPY of all return data and REVERT) when the word is zero, the second runs only when it is nonzero and then jumps. Result: The fee manager debits max_fee from the fee payer and credits the refund to the fee payer through protocol-internal hooks, not public calls (Tempo fee spec). A type 0x76 batch and a sponsored transaction carry the calls of one signer, with the fee payer adding only a signature (earlier cleared item on carriers). Result: Parlia system transactions run with their own transient map and system contracts do not call arbitrary contracts (earlier cleared item). CCTP v2 proxy code is present at the shared addresses, but Circle's address page does not list BNB Smart Chain as a CCTP domain, so no attested mint is expected there; if one is enabled the CCTP finding applies. ## Reading of the source (theme-megaeth-validator-build)

- MegaETH, cycle 16. L-768 and L-626, Task 1: can the public MegaETH stateless validator at e1618ed7 be built here without installing a toolchain?. Result: Task 1. The MegaETH stateless validator at e1618ed7 builds and runs with the installed stable toolchain (rustc 1.97.0, cargo 1.97.0) and no RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP. rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly-2026-04-23 with components only (rustfmt, clippy, rust-src, miri, rust-analyzer); no crate of the workspace, of mega-evm v1.7.3 or of salt carries a #![feature] attribute (grep over the fetched trees), and the workspace declares rust-version 1.94. The work copy drops rust-toolchain.toml so the installed compiler is used. Two steps failed and were resolved: (1) cargo build --offline against the cycle 15 cargohome stops at dependency resolution with 'no matching package named bincode' because that fetch was partial (483 crates); cargo fetch from crates.io inside the work directory completed it. (2) the build script of mega-system-contracts v1.7.3 (crates/system-contracts/build.rs:318-347) panics with 'forge command not found' when the crate's scripts/ directory exists, because in a repository build it re-derives the five system contract bytecodes with Foundry. The scripts/ directory of the work copy was renamed, which makes build.rs take its published crate path: it skips the forge re-derivation and still runs Phase 2, which checks the checked-in constants in src/generated against the versioned artifacts (build.rs:364-385). cargo build --release --offline -p stateless-validator then finished (build/build2.log, EXIT 0). The binary uses revm 40.0.3, revm-handler 20.0.3, revm-interpreter 37.0.3 and ruint 1.17.2 from the validator's own Cargo.lock. The forge attestation of system contract bytecode is the one check this build did not run.
