- MegaETH, cycle 16. L-768 and L-626, Task 2: does the closed MegaETH sequencer's post-state for PoolManager liquidity removals, fee collections, ERC-6909 mints and burns and take inside reverted frames equal an independent re-execution?. Result: Task 2. In --block-list mode the validator fetched each block's witness with mega_getBlockWitness and the block from https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, verified the witness, re-executed every transaction with mega-evm v1.7.3 on the stock revm interpreter and compared state root, receipts root, logs bloom, withdrawals root and gas used with the header the sequencer published. Target set: every block holding a PoolManager ModifyLiquidity with negative liquidityDelta (210 events in 210 blocks), with zero liquidityDelta, i.e. fee collection (545 in 545), an ERC-6909 mint (40 in 40) or burn (81 in 81) from the full PoolManager log history of blocks 2,900,000 to 32,766,000 (cycles/013/theme-mined-branches.work/raw/logs-4326.json and cycles/015/theme-closed-producers-2.work/raw/pmtail-4326.jsonl), plus the 75 blocks of the take, settle and sync inside reverted frames listed in cycles/011/theme-closed-producers.work/raw/mega.json (75 of the 87 cycle 11 counted are in that file's sample). Result: 911 distinct blocks, 911 validated, 0 failed. Anchored check: 45 of these blocks (15 removal, 10 fee collection, 5 burn, 5 mint, 10 reverted-frame blocks, seed 16) were also run in chain-following mode with --start-block set to the parent block hash and --end-block to the block, which in addition checks the witness pre-state against the parent's state root (stateless-core executor.rs:837-841); 45 of 45 validated. Wider sweep: all other blocks that hold any PoolManager log or a cycle 11 sampled transaction, 42734 blocks; all 42734 were run, 42734 validated and 0 failed. Control: the same 911 blocks run with a build whose revm-interpreter MULMOD returns one more than the correct result whenever the 512 bit product exceeds 2^256 (patched copy under build/plant, [patch.crates-io] in build/sv-plant) give 611 validated and 300 failed, mostly with a receipts root mismatch; the failures cover 138 of 210 removal blocks, 67 of 545 fee collection blocks, 25 of 81 burn blocks and 75 of 75 reverted-frame blocks, so the comparison sees a wrong product in these blocks. So for every mined MegaETH liquidity removal, fee collection, ERC-6909 mint and burn and every sampled take inside a reverted frame, the closed sequencer's post-state equals an independent re-execution by the open interpreter, to the state root. Task 3 was not needed. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work/blocks.txt, cats.json, runall/results.jsonl, anch/summary.txt, runrest/results.jsonl, runplant/results.jsonl; mega_getBlockWitness and eth_getBlockByNumber on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc
- MegaETH, cycle 16. Task 4: when a PoolManager call inside unlock meets a mega-evm compute gas, data size, key-value update or state growth limit, can an inner frame stop while outer frames continue with PoolManager state the source assumes rolled back?. Result: Task 4. mega-evm v1.7.3 meters four extra dimensions per transaction (Rex constants: compute gas 200,000,000, data 12.5 MiB, key-value updates 500,000, state growth 1,000; crates/mega-evm/src/constants.rs:192-211) and, from Rex4, gives each inner frame 98/100 of its parent's remaining budget (limit/frame_limit.rs:162-171). A transaction-level exceed is latched and reported as OutOfGas; once latched, every later metered opcode in every frame halts (record_compute_gas returns false on a latched exceed, limit/limit.rs:460-480, and the instruction wrapper sets a halt action, evm/instructions.rs:581-594), and every frame return is marked OutOfGas (limit.rs:846-856), so the top frame halts and revm reverts the whole transaction apart from nonce and fee. A frame-local exceed found during execution ends that frame with Revert and revert data MegaLimitExceeded(kind, limit); revm's process_next_action reverts the frame's journal checkpoint for any non-ok result (revm-handler 20.0.3 src/frame.rs:416-423), which undoes storage, transient storage and logs of that frame, and the parent continues. A frame-local exceed found only when the frame returns (before_frame_return_result, limit.rs:801-845) rewrites a successful result to Revert after revm has already committed the frame; the source says so at limit.rs:827-830. The late detection exists for CREATE frames (code size recorded in after_frame_run, limit/data_size.rs:324-335) and for a SELFDESTRUCT whose usage was recorded before its inner instruction halted (limit.rs:450-456); the PoolManager bytecode has neither opcode, so no PoolManager frame can be committed and reported failed. Every outward call of the PoolManager reverts the PoolManager frame when the callee reports failure: the native and ERC-20 transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40-84), the hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-139) and the balanceOf read of sync and settle (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365). So a callee frame reported failed, whether rolled back or not, ends with the PoolManager frame reverted, and that revert undoes Lock (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-19), NonzeroDeltaCount (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:20-32) and CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:35-39) together with the payment. No rewrite goes from failure to success, so a payment frame can never be reported successful with its transfer undone. Read-only test on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc with eth_call and code overrides (probe/limits.py, probe/loop.py; the test contracts touch no PoolManager state): a child that creates 990 new storage slots under a parent that gave it all its gas returns success 0 with MegaLimitExceeded(3, 980) and the parent completes; through DELEGATECALL the child's writes are read back as zero after the failed call and the parent's own later write is present, while 900 and 979 slots succeed and persist. A child in an endless loop returns MegaLimitExceeded(2, 58,776,709) and the parent completes. These match the reading: a frame-local exceed rolls back that frame and only that frame. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.3/crates/mega-evm/src/limit/limit.rs (fetched, identical to the work copy) and the v1.7.3 checkout in research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work/build/cargohome/git/checkouts/mega-evm-86ab85a902904159/59b8e39; src/types/Currency.sol:40-84; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-139; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114; eth_call on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc via research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work/probe/limits.py
- MegaETH, cycle 16. The validator's lock pins ruint 1.17.2 and revm-interpreter 37.0.3, and earlier cycles read mega-evm v1.7.4 with ruint 1.19.0. Does the version split leave PoolManager arithmetic unchecked?. Result: The validator binary built here, with ruint 1.17.2, reproduces the sequencer's state root on every block run, including the 300 blocks in which a wrong 512 bit MULMOD is visible. A ruint difference between the two builds on any operation these blocks use would show as a mismatch, and none did. Operands that no mined block reaches are covered only by the battery of OPCODES.md. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work/build/sv/Cargo.lock (ruint 1.17.2, revm-interpreter 37.0.3), runall/results.jsonl, runplant/results.jsonl

- Monad, cycle 16. Task 1, pins. Which asmjit and category-labs/evmc commits do the monad releases v0.16.7 and v0.16.5 pin as submodules, and how do they differ from what the cycle 15 harness used (asmjit 9eb6edbf, evmc master with four struct fields added by hand). The GitHub tree API and github.com are refused in this environment (HTTP 403), and add_repo was denied, so the gitlinks were read through the Sourcegraph GraphQL API (repository github.com/category-labs/monad, commit(rev) tree(path: third_party) entries submodule {commit url}); the answers are stored in research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/sg-submodules-v0.16.7.json and -v0.16.5.json. Result: Tag v0.16.7 resolves to commit 2690448babbf78f664611aa7c4382446ad1a174e and v0.16.5 to a3b16af1ac3637a262b8b1872798bccc746e81cb. Both pin third_party/asmjit at e8c8e2e48a1a38154c8e8864eb3bc61db80a1e31. third_party/evmc (url https://github.com/category-labs/evmc.git in .gitmodules) is f6b7c57e071d4eb0020d2cda3aee51e05ad8c726 at v0.16.7 and 34795f4eb4fd43cf8212d2b525a359236bad891c at v0.16.5. raw.githubusercontent.com serves the same .gitmodules at commit 2690448b as at the tag (equal md5), which ties the Sourcegraph commit to the GitHub tag, and serves a file at a3b16af1. The three trees were fetched from cdn.jsdelivr.net at those exact commits. Against cycle 15: asmjit 9eb6edbf and e8c8e2e4 differ in 19 files, and in src/asmjit/x86 only in x86rapass.cpp, which is the register allocator of asmjit's Compiler; Monad's emitter writes through x86::Assembler (the as_ member). The other 18 files are in src/asmjit/core (assembler.h, builder.h, cpuinfo, func, the register allocator and others), so the core code under the assembler did change; the asm log of the PoolManager is the same text under both commits (see the rerun item), and the harness now runs the pinned commit. evmc.h of f6b7c57e differs from the hand-patched header only in comments and in where evmc_page_storage_status and evmc_update_page_fn are declared; the field order of evmc_message, evmc_tx_context and evmc_host_interface and every enumerator value are the same. evmc.hpp differs in API (get_tx_context returns a pointer, update_page is a pure virtual of evmc::Host, noexcept on copy_code and access_account), which the new harness adapts to. evmc.h is identical between 34795f4e and f6b7c57e; evmc.hpp differs only in noexcept and formatting. - Monad, cycle 16. Task 3. The emitter source between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 (category/vm/compiler and category/vm/runtime, file by file), and which changes reach instructions of the deployed PoolManager. The PoolManager's blocks were located by an instrumented copy of the emitter that writes a marker for every emitter function entered and every branch arm taken while each EVM instruction is emitted (shapes/instrument.py; the markers are logger calls and the emitted asm text is identical to the uninstrumented build). Result: Only compiler/ir/x86.cpp, x86/emitter.cpp, emitter.hpp, types.hpp, virtual_stack.hpp and runtime/allocator.hpp and cached_allocator.hpp differ; no runtime .cpp or .S file changed, so the arithmetic routines (math.S, the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP calls) are the same. Changes that reach the PoolManager: (a) shift_literal_by_non_literal (emitter.cpp 5231-5235 and 5254-5328) handles SHL, SHR and SAR of a literal value by a variable count with two unaligned loads from a 96-byte read-only window and per-qword shifts; it is used at 6 PoolManager sites, SHL at pcs 16643 (inside the TickBitmap.flipTick code, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:47-75), 16691 (the mask shl(and(tick, 0xff), 1), src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:72), 21183 (1 << bitPos, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:110) and 21364 (the De Bruijn table of BitMath.leastSignificantBit, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:40-42), SHR at 19356 (type(uint256).max >> (255 - bitPos), src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:96) and 23648 (the table of BitMath.mostSignificantBit, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:21-22); under v0.16.5 the same sites move the literal into an AVX register and take shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal. The window arithmetic was checked by hand: for shift 8k+b with k up to 32 the loads stay inside bytes 31 to 95 of the window and the mask sits at bytes 0-15 (SHL) or 80-95 (SHR, SAR), and for every bit i the two loads contribute the same stream bit. (b) touch_memory skips the bound check and memory growth when the same non-literal offset element was already checked with at least the same size in the block (6301-6313); 15 PoolManager MLOAD and MSTORE sites use it, and 14 of them run in the cycle 15 scenarios (the one left, pc 16254, is next to the hook call revert path at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). Since the element is the same value and memory never shrinks inside a frame, the skipped check would have passed. (c) The block-exit stack write orders elements by stack index through a preallocated count array and loads GPR-held words into a YMM register word by word (mov_words_to_ymm, 2061); every block exit with register-held values uses it. (d) block_prologue jumps straight to the error label when max_delta - min_delta > 1024 (1342), where v0.16.5 tested min_delta < -1024 or max_delta > 1024; no stack size satisfies both runtime checks in exactly the cases the new test catches, so the outcome is the same. (e) Read-only data alignment 32 to 64 bytes (735) and add96. Changes that do not reach it: MSTORE8 of a value held at a stack offset (3399-3412; the PoolManager has no MSTORE8), the CLZ rewrite (2692-2733 and 8266-8293; no CLZ opcode), debug comments, the allocator refactor (stack memory allocation only). Both versions were run on every input of this unit with no difference between engines or between versions. - Monad, cycle 16. Task 4, shapes. For MULMOD, ADDMOD, SDIV, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, BYTE, SHL, SHR, EXP, CALLDATALOAD, MSTORE8, MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE: every shape the v0.16.7 emitter can pick (read from the dispatch code), which shapes the deployed PoolManager's blocks use (from the instrumented asm log), and whether PoolManager scenarios execute each site (operand classes recorded at the same pc in the interpreter, which runs the same path as the native code because every result is equal). Result: Shapes the emitter can pick. SHL, SHR, SAR: fold of two literals; literal count of 256 or more (0, or the sign fill for SAR) or 0 (identity); literal count with the value in an AVX register (shift_avx_reg_by_literal) or in general registers or a stack slot (shift_general_reg_or_stack_offset_by_literal); variable count with a literal value of 0 (or all ones for SAR, identity), any other literal value (shift_literal_by_non_literal, new in v0.16.6/7), the value in an AVX register (shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal, count bounded to 256 in rax) or in general registers, or a stack slot moved to them (shift_general_reg_by_non_literal with test_high_bits192). BYTE: literal index of 32 or more gives 0; fold; literal or variable index with the source in general registers, an AVX register, or a stack slot (6 leaves). SIGNEXTEND: fold; literal index of 31 or more gives the value; literal index with the source in AVX or general registers or a stack slot; variable index bounded to 31 with the source in AVX, general registers, or a stack slot or literal (5 leaves). MULMOD and ADDMOD: literal modulus 0 or 1 gives 0; folds; a literal operand equal to the absorbing element; a power-of-two literal modulus becomes an AND mask (operand equal to 1 or 0) or mul_mod2 / add_mod2, which inline the product or sum truncated to n bits for n up to 128 and call runtime mul_192 or mul above; anything else calls the runtime. SDIV and SMOD: literal folds, divisor 0, power-of-two divisor (sdiv_by_sar with negation, smod_by_mask), otherwise the runtime call. EXP: literal folds and gas by exponent width, otherwise the runtime. CALLDATALOAD: literal offset bounded or out of range, variable offset bounded by bits with a runtime check. MSTORE8: value literal, in general registers, AVX, or a stack slot (general register or AVX temporary). MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE: runtime calls only. - Monad, cycle 16. Task 4, edges. Micro programs that put each instruction into each shape with edge operands (0, 1, 2, 31, 32, 63 to 65, 127 to 129, 191 to 193, 254, 255, 256, 257, 511, 2^64-1, 2^64, 2^64+1, 2^128+5, 2^192+255, 2^255, 2^255+1, 2^256-2, 2^256-1, byte indexes 0 to 33 and above, power-of-two and other moduli including 2^96 and 2^128, and random words), run in the same harness (interpreter against native) and checked against the specification in Python; the shape each program gets was confirmed with the instrumented emitter (micro/shapes.json). Result: 2,154 programs and 158,802 calls: v0.16.7 scenarios=2154 mismatches=0, v0.16.5 scenarios=2154 mismatches=0, AVX-512 build scenarios=2154 mismatches=0. Every coarse PoolManager shape of the 12 instructions that occur is reached by micro programs except MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE, which are plain runtime calls shared with the interpreter and run in every PoolManager scenario. 155,196 interpreter results of SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD, MULMOD and ADDMOD equal the specification, and the native result equals the interpreter in every call. Ten further programs cover the two v0.16.7 memory changes: an offset element reused for MLOAD, MSTORE, MLOAD (the skip path, confirmed by its marker), MSTORE8 then MLOAD (no skip, as required), and MSTORE8 of a literal, register, AVX and stack-slot value, at 16 offsets up to 2^256-1 and two gas limits: no difference on v0.16.7 or v0.16.5. Planted faults: changing the carry offset of the SHR window load in shift_literal_by_non_literal (fault f3) breaks all 46 SHR programs of that shape; changing the bit width of mul_mod2 to n-1 for 2^128 and 2^96 in the stack-slot branch (f5) breaks the m2^128 and m2^96 programs of that branch; in the register branch for 2^128 (f4) it breaks those of that branch. On PoolManager inputs: f3 gives 539 mismatches in 2090 scenarios, f5 gives 0 in 2090 scenarios (4 scenario files and the first battery file of each path), and f5 changes nothing in the 2,007 mined transactions (0 differences). The PoolManager scenarios do run the 2^96 site (pc 22639) 113,230 times, always with a product above 2^256, yet f5 changes none of their results: on a correct node that branch returns an amount of at least 2^160, which either loses the comparison at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:68 or :90 or reverts later in a cast, and a garbage remainder almost always gives a garbage amount that does the same. The evidence for the two mul_mod2 sites is therefore the micro programs: 52,224 MULMOD results equal to the specification, including the moduli 2^96 and 2^128 in the register and stack-slot arms. The PoolManager scenarios only show that the site runs. ## Reading of the source (theme-revert-rollback-mined)

- Tempo, cycle 16. Task 1, mined transactions with a reverted and then completed PoolManager frame: Tempo: 1139 of 1139 transactions that emitted PoolManager logs in blocks 49,902,371 to 50,702,370 were read with debug_traceTransaction (callTracer with logs). In 1 of them a frame into the PoolManager was undone (it or a frame above it failed) and a later PoolManager frame of the same transaction was not, and in 1 an unlock that had been entered and undone was followed by an unlock that completed. Receipt status equals the trace status in every transaction. Every receipt carries one log more than the trace, a TIP-20 Transfer from pathUSD to the fee manager 0xfeec000000000000000000000000000000000000 at the end, which is the fee the protocol charges outside the call tree; with that log removed the receipt logs equal the surviving trace logs in order in all 51 transactions checked. The reference replay cannot run Tempo transactions, because the TIP-20 tokens the pools use are precompiles (code 0xef at 0x20c0...) that pyevm does not implement. Result: In the one hit, 0xba5c0224452fbe54eb5198aad0bba1cf5a4b86db6e40eb4f4265024a79bdfa27, an unlock that swapped reverted and the next unlock (take, sync, settle, swap) completed on chain with status 1, which it could not have done had the unlock flag survived (src/PoolManager.sol:105). The receipt the producer wrote agrees with the trace the RPC node computed. There is no independent reference rerun on Tempo, so the check rests on the node's own re-execution and the producer's receipt. The own success flag of all 132 PoolManager frames is the same in order, the top level status is the same in 6, and the final value of all 99 storage slots the chain changed (44 of them PoolManager slots) is the same, with 0 differences. Logs are equal in 6. Result: No reverted unlock occurs in the window; the undone frames are extsload reads inside quotes that reverted. No transaction shows a later PoolManager frame that succeeds on the chain and fails in the reference, or the other way round, so neither the block producer nor the tracing node kept an unlock flag, delta, count or synced reserve of an undone frame. src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:12-32, CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41 and CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38 get the rollback they rely on, and unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) saw a locked manager after each undone unlock. Evidence: debug_traceTransaction and eth_getTransactionReceipt on https://unichain.drpc.org and eth_getLogs on https://mainnet.unichain.org, 2026-11-25; prestateTracer reruns in cycles/016/theme-revert-rollback-mined.work/replay.py with pyevm_tx.py; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114
- all 21 networks, cycle 16. Task 2, halts other than REVERT, constructed with eth_call and state overrides against the deployed PoolManager of each of the 21 networks (HaltProbe.sol, halt.py, halt_fix.py in the work directory). A probe frame writes its own transient slot and then either (variant 1) enters unlock and, in the callback, mints 5 claims, syncs a currency and writes a second slot, or (variant 2) syncs a currency outside unlock, and then halts. Kinds: REVERT as control, INVALID (0xfe), stack overflow by unbounded internal recursion, out of gas by an endless loop, and, under STATICCALL, a TSTORE by the probe, PoolManager.sync and PoolManager.unlock. A later frame then reads the unlock flag, the nonzero delta count, the probe's delta, the synced currency and reserves with exttload (src/Exttload.sol:10-15), the probe's claim balance and the probe's own two slots. In a second test the call into the probe was given every gas value from 1 up to the first value at which it succeeds (step 1 over the last 8,000 gas below that value and step 9 or coarser below), so that out of gas falls at every reachable point inside the PoolManager, the callback and the balanceOf staticcall: 362,827 attempts, 362,743 of them failing. The first successful gas is 39,572 on most networks, 39,324 on Monad, 81,193 on MegaETH and 281,586 on Tempo, where creating a storage slot costs more. Result: No leak on any network: 0 failed attempts read back a write. The successful controls show every written slot (synced currency 0x00000000000000000000000000000000c0ffee16 and reserves 1000 plus the attempt id, the probe slots 7 and 9), so the reads can see a write that survives. A static call into PoolManager.sync or unlock fails at its first TSTORE (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:29-30) and writes nothing, so a static violation cannot leave a write by construction. PoolManager never catches a failed callee: the hook call bubbles the failure (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137), token and native payouts revert (src/types/Currency.sol:48-52 and 73-83), and the callback is a plain high level call (src/PoolManager.sol:110), so a halt in any of them reverts the whole unlock. On MegaETH the simulated call runs on the RPC node, not the closed sequencer (OPCODES.md, MegaETH row). Evidence: eth_call with state overrides on the rpc URL of each network in state/networks.json, 2026-11-25, results in cycles/016/theme-revert-rollback-mined.work/raw/halt_all.json and raw/halt_fix.json; https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153 (a reverted frame undoes its transient writes and those of inner calls); src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288
- all 21 networks, cycle 16. Task 2, call depth 1024: how deep a chain of self calls with all gas gets under a 30,000,000 gas eth_call, and what the PoolManager does when a call it makes fails for depth. Result: The chain stops at depth 358 on 18 networks, 357 on Tempo and 291 on MegaETH (98/100 forwarding), well short of 1,024, because each level keeps 1/64 of the gas: (63/64)^1024 is 9.9e-8, so reaching depth 1,024 needs about 10^10 gas at the top, and (98/100)^1024 is 1.0e-9 on MegaETH. Where depth were reached, the failed outgoing call returns 0 without halting the PoolManager frame, and every outgoing call of the PoolManager turns a failure into a revert (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, src/types/Currency.sol:52 and 83, src/PoolManager.sol:110), so the unlock reverts and its transient writes go with it. Evidence: eth_call depthRun() with state override on every rpc URL in state/networks.json, 2026-11-25 (raw/halt_all.json); src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-137; src/types/Currency.sol:40-83
- Base, Tempo, Celo, Arc, cycle 16. Tokens the node implements natively, inside frames that revert or halt: the probe TokenRollbackProbe.sol was placed by state override at the PoolManager address of Base, Tempo, Celo and Arc so that it holds what the PoolManager holds, and it transferred 1 unit of Base B20 OUSD (0xB2000000000000000000002fEb517dFeC7415344) and AMDc (0xb2000000000000000000000d8ce462e99ee7a47b), Tempo TIP-20 pathUSD (0x20c0000000000000000000000000000000000000), the CELO ERC-20 face (0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438) and the Arc USDC face (0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000) inside a frame that then reverted, hit INVALID, overflowed the stack or ran out of gas, and under STATICCALL; on Celo and Arc also a native value transfer read back through the face. A take or settle inside an undone frame is only safe if these precompile balances roll back with the transient delta. Result: All eight cases roll back: in every halted or static case the sender and recipient balances of both faces read afterwards equal those before, and the successful control moves one unit (raw/token_rollback.json). Ethereum USDC was run as a bytecode control with the same result. On Arc a native transfer of 1 wei lowers the sender's face balance by one face unit (10^12 wei) and the recipient's face shows 0, because the face reports floor(balance / 10^12); this is the rounding of the existing two-face hazard (F-100, F-108), and one face unit is worth 10^-6 USDC, far below the gas of a round. Evidence: eth_call with state overrides on https://base-rpc.publicnode.com, https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz, https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io, 2026-11-25; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 349-364; src/types/Currency.sol:60-94

- all 21 networks, cycle 16. Task 3, ERC-4337 bundles on every network, which join several users' operations into one transaction. Whether transient storage is cleared between operations, and a mined bundle in which two unrelated senders' operations both called the PoolManager. Bundles among PoolManager transactions (UserOperationEvent of EntryPoint 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, aa.py): Base 5,610 PoolManager transactions in blocks 61,965,599 to 61,973,598, 170 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Ethereum 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 26,489,705 to 26,490,154, 65 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Polygon 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 97,904,651 to 97,919,750, 223 bundles, 2 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Arbitrum One 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 527,245,513 to 527,333,512, 59 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Optimism 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 159,986,660 to 159,993,159, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Robinhood Chain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 122,805,462 to 122,811,461, 64 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Unichain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 64,830,284 to 64,836,583, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager. Result: Transient storage is not cleared between operations: EIP-1153 discards it only at the end of the transaction, and the EntryPoint runs every operation as a nested call of the one handleOps transaction. The unlock flag and the deltas cannot pass from one operation to the next, because unlock clears the flag and requires every delta to be zero before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Only the synced currency and reserves can. No mined bundle with two senders' PoolManager calls was found: the only multi-sender bundles have one operation that reaches the PoolManager, for example Base 0x61046bec99fa8dc23efda3e63f0bedc7e18b233fb191c09ff26edfbaced2b66c (EntryPoint 0.6, senders 0x0de04d745d88dc18e7c519f1935a3e27917e795f and 0xcbeebaf9d1f94a6678dad25e14afd2fb042bc579, only the second calls unlock, sync, settle, swap, mint and take). sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims. Evidence: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153; eth_getLogs, eth_getTransactionReceipt and debug_traceTransaction on the endpoints in aa.py, 2026-11-25 (raw/aa2_*.json, raw/aa_*.json); src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288, 300-307, 349-364
- Tempo, cycle 16. Task 3, Tempo type 0x76 batched and sponsored transactions: does transient storage survive between the calls of a batch, and can two unrelated users share it?. Result: The calls of a batch share one transient map: execute_batch takes one checkpoint before the first call, runs every call with the transaction's caller as sender, rolls the checkpoint back when any call fails and keeps all writes otherwise (handler.rs execute_batch, lines 1284-1366 on main). Every call has the same msg.sender, so only the signer's own calls share the state, and a fee sponsor pays fees without becoming a caller. Two unrelated users cannot share a batch, so no mined transaction of that kind can exist; zone portal batches are the one Tempo context that joins parties and are recorded as F-135. sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/crates/evm/src/handler.rs (execute_batch, lines 1267-1366), fetched 2026-11-25; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364
- HyperEVM, cycle 16. Task 3, HyperEVM system transactions: are they joined with user transactions so that transient storage is shared?. Result: No. The public replay client builds the environment for each system transaction and each signed transaction separately, calls transact once per transaction and commits state after each (run.rs lines 99-168 and the loop over system_txs at line 217). Each system transaction is its own transaction and starts with empty transient storage, so nothing joins it with a user's PoolManager call. The validator itself is closed (F-120). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs, fetched 2026-11-25; src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, cycle 16. Task 3, OP Stack deposit transactions: are deposits joined with other transactions?. Result: No. The deposit specification processes each deposit as a transaction of its own with its own receipt, sender and gas accounting, and the revm journal used by op-reth clears transient storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize at the end of every transaction (inner.rs lines 141, 174 and 207) and restores it on checkpoint_revert (line 622). A deposit therefore shares no transient state with a user's PoolManager call. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/deposits.html; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs, both fetched 2026-11-25
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 16. Task 3, Arbitrum retryable redeems, automatic and manual: does a redeem run inside the transaction that scheduled it?. Result: No. A redeem is returned by TxProcessor.ScheduledTxes as a new transaction (tx_processor.go lines 924-957) and the block processor applies it after the originating transaction as a transaction of its own, keeping the group's redeems and checkpoint (block_processor.go lines 91 and 126-159), and every transaction passes through StateDB.Prepare, which resets transient storage before code runs (state_transition.go lines 735-736). A redeem shares no transient state with the transaction that created or redeemed it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/block_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/tx_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/master/core/state_transition.go, all fetched 2026-11-25
- all 21 networks, cycle 16. The reference interpreter tools/opdiff/pyevm.py, used by earlier cycles to judge PoolManager behaviour, was extended here for whole mined transactions and gave one wrong result first. Result: pyevm.py gives a DELEGATECALL frame CALLVALUE 0 instead of the value of the calling frame (tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:205 passes 0 as value). This unit's copy (pyevm_tx.py) carries the value through and also adds block context, logs, ecrecover, modexp, EIP-7702 designators and an approximate GAS. The PoolManager build contains no DELEGATECALL (OPCODES.md, bytecode census), and the delegate calls of pmdiff6.py run inside the unlock callback, which the PoolManager calls without value, so no earlier PoolManager comparison is affected. Evidence: tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:195-205; tools/opdiff/pmdiff6.py:5-6 and 62; research/network-risk/OPCODES.md:146

## Reading of the source (theme-library-paths)

- HyperEVM, cycle 17. L-808, RUSTSEC-2025-0137: which functions of ruint 1.15.0 (hyper-evm-sync, revm 19.2.0, revm-interpreter 15.2.0) and 1.16.0 (nanoreth f0cad31, hl-archive-node/revm fdf9b16, revm-interpreter 25.0.3) call reciprocal_mg10, and is the divisor normalised on the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD paths?. Result: Yes on every path. reciprocal_mg10 is exported as reciprocal and called by reciprocal_2_mg10 (reciprocal.rs line 111), div_nx1_normalized and div_nx1 (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 39 and 75, 1.15.0 lines 27 and 62); reciprocal_2 is called by div_nx2_normalized, div_nx2, div_nxm_normalized and div_nxm (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 112 and 144, knuth.rs lines 35 and 120). The only non-test callers of those are algorithms::div (1.15.0 mod.rs lines 49-99) and div_inlined (1.16.0 mod.rs lines 56-107), which trim zero limbs, send one limb divisors with a one limb numerator to native division and route the rest to div_nx1, div_nx2 or div_nxm. Each of these shifts the divisor by its leading zeros before the reciprocal (small.rs lines 69-75 and 138-144, knuth.rs lines 105-120) and calls the normalized variant only when the shift is zero. Uint::div_rem, wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, reduce_mod, add_mod and mul_mod reach only those two entry points (div.rs and modular.rs of both tags). revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and 25.0.3 call wrapping_div and wrapping_rem after a zero check, add_mod and mul_mod directly, and / and % on absolute values in i256_div and i256_mod (arithmetic.rs lines 26-63 and 31-83, i256.rs lines 80-130 and 92-143); the hl-archive-node fork's arithmetic.rs, i256.rs and bitwise.rs equal the crates.io 25.0.3 files. The precondition d >= 2^63 therefore always holds, and FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 35, 48, 62-73, 112), SqrtPriceMath (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:62, 252), UnsafeMath (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14, 26) and TickBitmap (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26, 57-64) cannot hand it an unnormalised divisor. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2025-0137.md; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.15.0.crate and ruint-1.16.0.crate (sha256 11256b5f and 9ecb38f8, the second equal to the checksum in nanoreth f0cad31 Cargo.lock); https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-25.0.3.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/revm/fdf9b16bdd4388a680c97440c6e7f085647ece01/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/arithmetic.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/f0cad31/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/Cargo.lock

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-exact-sites)

- Monad, cycle 17. Task 1, method and proof of execution. The harness of cycle 16 (category-labs/monad v0.16.7 with asmjit e8c8e2e4 and evmc f6b7c57e, v0.16.5 with evmc 34795f4e, the release keccak) was relinked with two recompiled objects only: a copy of category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp that, at chosen EVM pcs, emits an execution counter before the instruction (rax saved to and restored from a fixed address, mov and lea only, so flags and the virtual stack are untouched) and optionally, after the instruction, a call that records the word the instruction left on top of the stack (the code of Emitter::runtime_print_top1); and interpreter/execute.cpp built with a copy of instruction_table.hpp whose MONAD_VM_NEXT and MONAD_VM_NEXT_PUSH record the stack top at the same pcs. emitter.cpp is not changed. Two ways of reaching the sites were used: PoolManager calls (pc 12232, 15519, 22378, 22639) and, for operands no call can supply and for pc 16642, an entry into the deployed runtime's own basic block: bytes 0..46 of the 24,009-byte runtime are replaced by a 45-byte prologue (copy calldata[0x120:] to memory 0, push eight calldata words, jump to calldata word 0; a JUMPDEST at pc 38 stores the top word and returns it), the other 23,962 bytes unchanged. Entries used: 0x5703 (the 2^128 copy of mulDiv, called from Position.update at pcs 5969 and 5981), 0x5810 (the 2^96 copy, called from getAmount1Delta at pcs 23088 and 23161), 0x3c94 (Hooks.beforeSwap after the hook call) and 0x40d7 (the bytes4 mask block). Result: Arm identity. In the v0.16.7 asm log (which prints a comment per EVM instruction) the text emitted for each of the five site instructions is identical between the plain build, the counter build (once the five counter lines are removed; the rest of the 48,691-line log is identical) and the single-site capture builds (the plain text is a prefix of the capture build's text). The texts are: pc 22378 MULMOD loads a from [rbp-128..-104] into r13,r14,r15,r12 and b0,b1 from [rbp-96],[rbp-88], computes r10 = lo(a0*b0) by mulx, r11 = hi(a0*b0) + a1*b0 + a0*b1 (64-bit imul) and zeroes r8, r9; pc 22639 is the same with 32-bit imul and add on limb 1 (mod 2^96); pc 15519 SAR(128) of the word in r12..r15 is mov rax,r15; sar rax,63; mov r10,r14; mov r11,r15; mov r8,rax; mov r9,rax; pc 16642 SHL(3) of the word in r12..r15 is three shld and one shl by 3; pc 12232 CALLDATALOAD is the bswap_to_ymm arm with the bound test on the offset limbs and the 32-byte vmovups read. In v0.16.5 the same instructions open each site's text (v0.16.5 prints no per-instruction comment, so the text was located by the counter lines). Compiled from the prologue runtime, the enclosing blocks B5703, B5810, B3c94 and B40d7 equal the deployed runtime's blocks once label numbers, block numbers and read-only data offsets are replaced by the bytes they point to (both compiled in one process so that host pointers agree); the one exception, B3c94 under v0.16.5, differs only in the order of three independent stores at the block exit (see the v0.16.5 heap-address item). Marker counts, native = interpreter in every file and on both releases: pc 22378 274 (prologue) + 18 (ordinary calls); pc 22639 200 (prologue) + 57 (ordinary swaps) + 188 (hook swaps); pc 15519 116 (prologue) + 648 (ordinary swaps through a returns-delta hook); pc 16642 47 (prologue only); pc 12232 1,220 (ordinary extsload and exttload calls). Every file gives 0 mismatches between interpreter and native in status, gas, return data, storage, transient storage, balances, logs and the captured site words. - all 21 networks, cycle 17. Task 2 from the source: which callers pass a constant denominator, which pc each compiles to, and whether a wrong remainder at prod1 = 1 could become an accepted amount. Result: Callers. Position.update passes FixedPoint128.Q128 (src/libraries/Position.sol:93-96); both calls jump to 0x5703 (pcs 5969 and 5981), whose MULMOD is pc 22378. SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta passes denominator = FixedPoint96.Q96 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:240, :250); both of its compiled copies jump to 0x5810 (pcs 23088 and 23161), whose MULMOD is pc 22639. SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 pass Q96 as the multiplier with liquidity as the denominator (copy at 0x588a and mulDivRoundingUp, MULMOD by a runtime call), and SwapMath.sol:65, :74 and :104 use the denominator 1e6 (copy with MULMOD at pc 22513, runtime call); these are not mul_mod2 sites. Arithmetic. For a power-of-two denominator N = 2^k the correct remainder is prod0 mod N, which is never above prod0, so gt(remainder, prod0) at FullMath.sol:52 is 0 on a correct node and prod1 stays 1. The emitted arm can only produce a value below N (limbs 2 and 3 are zeroed, limb 1 is 32-bit for 2^96). With any remainder r below N, FullMath.sol:52-75 return at least 2^(256-k) - 1: 200,000 random cases per site of a Python transcription give a least value of exactly 2^160 - 1 for k = 96 and 2^128 - 1 for k = 128 (the borrow case r > prod0 with prod0 < N). Such a result cannot be accepted: Position.update returns it as feesOwed and Pool.modifyLiquidity casts it with toInt128 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:192, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-58), which reverts at 2^127 and above; getAmount1Delta returns at least 2^160 - 1, and every use reverts in a cast (Pool.sol:222-223 and :232-234 through SqrtPriceMath.sol:278-287 in modifyLiquidity; in a swap, SwapMath.sol:68-69 and :89-91 either cap the step at the target, after which the amount of at least 2^160 - 1 reaches the toInt128 casts at Pool.sol:455 or :459, or the comparison fails and the faulty value is replaced by amountRemaining). A quotient below 2^127 needs a remainder above 2^256 - 2^223 + prod0 at the 2^96 site and above 2^255 + prod0 at the 2^128 site, more than 2^222 above anything the arm can write. So the borrow of L-800 cannot be produced by this arm, and a remainder that stays below N changes an accepted amount on no path. Result: 7 scenarios reach pc 22378 (18 executions, all prod1 = 1; native = interpreter = Python on both releases), and every call that reaches it reverts with SafeCastOverflow at Pool.sol:192. prod1 >= 1 here means fees owed to one position of at least 2^128 units of one currency, so on a correct node the site only runs in a call that reverts. Fee growth is credited by donations that the donor pays within the same unlock, so building that state needs 2^128 units of a currency, which only a token the attacker issues provides; the position concerned then holds that token. - Monad, cycle 17. Task 4. A fault planted in the native code after each site's instruction, one at a time (HX_FAULT_PC): bit 127 of the remainder cleared at pc 22378, bit 95 at pc 22639, no sign fill in the top word at pc 15519, carries between words lost at pc 16642, the last byte of the word lost at pc 12232. Every input file was run against every fault on both releases, comparing whole runs (counter build) and the site word (capture build). Result: Site-level tests catch every fault: pc 22378 q128 112 and ordinary 5 scenarios differ; pc 22639 q96 80 and ordinary 21; pc 15519 prologue 44 and hook 324; pc 16642 35; pc 12232 756. Whole-run comparisons catch only the pc 12232 fault (588 of 1,348). The other four change no PoolManager result, for reasons the source fixes: a remainder smaller than the true one leaves (prod0 - r) >> k unchanged, so the quotient at FullMath.sol:66-75 is the same; the SAR result at pc 15519 is consumed only by SIGNEXTEND 15 at pc 15522, which ignores bits 128 to 255; pc 16642 is unreachable. This is why cycle 16 saw no effect of its fault at pc 22639, and it means that whole-output differential testing cannot see faults of these kinds at these sites. They are also faults that move no funds. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/fault/summary.txt ; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:52-75
- Monad, cycle 17. Whether Monad's native code for the PoolManager is a function of the bytecode alone, on both releases. Result: Not under v0.16.5. Its block-exit writer collects stack elements in std::unordered_map<StackElem *, int32_t> dep_counts and emits the writes in that map's iteration order (category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1433 and :1466 at v0.16.5), which follows heap addresses. One extra early allocation in the compiling process changes 322 to 414 lines of the 48,757-line asm log of the deployed PoolManager. v0.16.7 replaced the map with a vector in stack index order, with the comment that this keeps the emitted code independent of heap addresses (emitter.cpp:1456-1469 and :1502), and its log is identical across the same perturbations. The orders seen are reorderings of independent stores. Four heap layouts of v0.16.5 give 2,000 of 2,000 cycle 15 scenarios equal between engines with identical native digests, and all v0.16.5 runs of this unit used a third and fourth layout. Different v0.16.5 validators can therefore run different machine code for the same contract, but no case where the order changes a result was found. Evidence: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp ; research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/layout/

## Reading of the source (theme-real-address-runs)

- all 21 networks, cycle 17. Task 1 method. A driver (scripts/realrun.py in the work directory) regenerates script sets 1, 2 and 6 of tools/opdiff (pmdiff.py seed 7_2026_11_24, 250 scripts; pmdiff2.py seed 11_2026_11_24, 300 scripts; pmdiff6.py, 706 scripts) with every reference to the PoolManager pointed at the network's real PoolManager address from state/networks.json, and runs each as one eth_call at 25 million gas against 'latest'. The state override contains only the driver (unlock callback, which also pays native value from its own overridden balance in set 6), the token doubles at 0xc0ffee01, 0xc0ffee02 and 0xc0ffee05 and the hook doubles at 0x486b.... and 0x486c....; the PoolManager's code, storage and balance are left as on chain. Pools are created by the scripts with those currencies and hooks, so no existing pool is touched. For each network the code at the real address was fetched in the same run (24,009 bytes, 24,050 on Unichain). Records were compared call by call with Ethereum's record at Ethereum's real address after replacing the 20 bytes of each PoolManager address with a marker (scripts/compare.py, scripts/alldiffs.py), and with the fresh-address results stored in opcodes/pmdiff.json, pmdiff2.json and pmdiff6.json. Every script whose answer differed from the stored fresh answer was run again at the real address with 2,000,000,000, 150,000,000, 50,000,000 or 30,000,000 gas, the first the endpoint accepts (scripts/gasretry.py). Ethereum's fresh-address answers for sets 2 and 6 were rerun the same day for a call-by-call comparison. Result: At Ethereum's real address 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 the 250 set 1 records and the 300 set 2 records are byte-identical to the stored fresh-address reference hashes, and the 706 set 6 records equal this cycle's Ethereum fresh-address rerun except where a script reads the PoolManager's own storage (owner, controller, accrued fees, extsload ranges) and in script 260, where the revert data of a native take to the PoolManager itself names the PoolManager's address; scripts 275 to 277 are byte-identical between the two addresses. So placing the scripts at the real address, with real code and storage, changes no amount, delta, slot or revert reason that does not come from the stored state itself. - all 21 networks, cycle 17. Task 1, set 6 (706 scripts for the jump sides sets 1 to 5 missed) at the real address. At the fresh address pmdiff6 made the driver the owner (storage slot 0 override) and gave the PoolManager 10^19 wei; at the real address the owner, protocol fee controller, accrued protocol fees and native balance are each network's own. Every differing call was tested against the network's state read independently with eth_getStorageAt and eth_call (scripts/explain.py): a call counts as explained when both sides succeeded with equal length and each differing word is the network's value of the same state item whose Ethereum value appears on the Ethereum side. Result: On every network the only set 6 scripts that differ from Ethereum's real-address record are: 246, 662, 671, 696 (reads of owner(), slot 0 through delegatecall, short calldata and callback paths: the word is the network's owner, slot 0, equal to the owner in networks.json); 672 (protocolFeeController(), slot 2); 641 to 643, 673, 676, 685 (protocolFeesAccrued(address(0)) words, and owner-only or controller-only calls that revert with UNAUTHORIZED or InvalidCaller because the driver is not the owner); 698 to 702 (extsload(0, n) and extsload(2^256-2, n), whose slot counter wraps to slot 0 in Extsload.sol:34, so they return slot 0 and slot 2); 657 on Base only (balanceOf(address(0), 0) returns 45,056,898,864, a native ERC-6909 claim balance that someone minted to address(0) on Base, read at several blocks back to 61,054,597 with the same value, 0 on the other 20 networks); 239, 241, 248 to 260 (native payouts that need more native than the real PoolManager holds: Zora 0.152, World Chain 5.42, MegaETH 1.997 and HyperEVM 11.35 units against takes of 10^18 to 2*10^19+1 wei, Tempo none); 275 to 277 and 279 (an initialize at the price limits followed by swaps that run out of the 25 million gas on every network, Ethereum included, and become identical to the stored reference with more gas, the reference interpreter rerun of script 275 confirming the stored hash); 681 and 682 on Monad, Polygon and BNB Chain (currency 0x1000, a system contract or the staking precompile there, as recorded in cycle 12). All other words are equal on all 21 networks, so the 690 or so remaining scripts per network give the same amounts, deltas, slots and revert data at the real address as at Ethereum's. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/compare.json (set6), research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/alldiffs6.json, research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/explain.json, research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/gas/s6-*.json, research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/ref275.json, src/ProtocolFees.sol:21-24, src/Extsload.sol:18-38
- Arc, Avalanche, Tempo, MegaETH, Monad, cycle 17. Address-keyed rules that the fresh-address runs could not meet (lead L-810): Arc's check on every call that carries value (F-125), Avalanche's fold of bit 248 of storage indexes onto existing slots (F-040), Tempo's transfer policies, MegaETH's per-account accounting, and any compile or cache decision keyed by address, code hash or use count. Result: Arc: all native payouts of sets 2 and 6 from the real PoolManager (to an account without code, to precompiles 1 and 4, to the driver, to hooks that revert) give Ethereum's words; the real PoolManager is not refused as a sender. Avalanche: all 1,256 scripts give Ethereum's words while the real PoolManager has its real storage, so no slot the scripts write or read is folded onto an existing PoolManager slot. MegaETH: the only differences are the native balance cases; no per-account gas rule changed a result at 25 million gas. Tempo: no difference outside native value; the token doubles are not TIP-20 tokens, so Tempo's TIP-403 transfer policies were not exercised by these sets. Monad: eth_call always interprets (F-130), so the hotness-keyed compiler is not reachable by this method, and the compiled code of the deployed PoolManager was compared with the interpreter in cycles 15 and 16. Every client named in OPCODES.md as keeping a code or jump cache keys it by content, and the real address runs are consistent with that. - Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM, cycle 17. Task 2 (lead L-802). cycles/016/arbitrum-family.work/scripts/offsets.py, copied to scripts/offsets.py with the network list taken from the command line and execution errors no longer retried, was run on the 18 networks where it had not run: 200 vectors per network, CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY with length 64 and 0, CODECOPY, KECCAK256 of length 0, MCOPY of length 0, and RETURNDATACOPY of 8 and 0 bytes after a 40 byte return, each with 25 offsets from 0 through 2^31, 2^32, 2^63, 2^64, 2^128 and 2^256-1. Result: 3600 vectors, 0 mismatches. Every word equals the specification and the word the three Arbitrum chains returned in cycle 16 (3,600 of 3,600 equal to Arbitrum One's). On every network the same 43 vectors fail, exactly the return data copies the specification makes an exceptional halt (offset plus length above 40, including the wrapped 2^256-1 + 8), and nothing else fails: zero-length copies and hashes at offsets up to 2^256-1 succeed without memory expansion. The failure messages differ by client and not in outcome: 'EVM error: OutOfOffset' on the reth based nodes, 'return data out of bounds' on bor, BNB Chain geth, Avalanche and Celo's op-geth backend (7 of Celo's 43 came from that backend, 36 from reth), 'revert: OutOfOffset' on Arc, and 'out of gas' on Monad. Monad reporting the halt as out of gas does not change what the PoolManager sees, because a failed frame returns 0 to its caller either way and the PoolManager copies return data only up to RETURNDATASIZE (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/offsets-*.json and offsets-*.log; cycles/016/arbitrum-family.work/raw/offsets.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 17. Task 3. At the real address of each network, scripts/tslots.py read IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT (Lock.sol:8), NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT (NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:8-9), RESERVES_OF_SLOT and CURRENCY_SLOT (CurrencyReserves.sol:11,13, each recomputed as keccak256 of its name minus 1) and the delta slots of the driver for three currencies: (A) by a plain eth_call of exttload(bytes32[]) at 'latest' and 'pending' from address 0, 0xdead and the driver; (B) in one simulated call with only the driver overridden: before unlock, first thing inside the callback, after sync of a token double holding 1000, after mint(driver, id, 5), after burn of the same, and after unlock returned; (C) the same four constants and slots 0 and 1 through extsload, as persistent slots. Result: 21 of 21 networks pass all three. A: all seven words are 0 in all six calls, so no unlock flag, delta count, synced currency, reserve or delta from an earlier transaction of the block is visible to a simulated call. B: before unlock 0,0,0,0; inside the callback unlocked 1 and the rest 0; after sync the currency and 1000; count 1 and delta -5 after mint, count 0 and delta 0 after burn; after unlock the flag is 0 and the count 0, while the synced currency and reserves stay set, which is what the source writes (sync is cleared only by settle, CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, PoolManager.sol:279-288). C: the four constants read 0 as persistent slots, so no client mixes the transient and persistent spaces at these indexes. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/tslots.json

- Base, cycle 17. Base, ERC-6909 claims held by address(0). balanceOf(address(0), 0) on the real PoolManager returns 45,056,898,864 (about 4.5e-8 ETH of native claims). Result: This is existing state, not an interpreter effect: the value is the same at blocks 61,054,597 to 62,054,600 on two endpoints. mint accepts any recipient (PoolManager.sol:322-329, ERC6909.sol:79-83), so somebody minted claims to address(0) and paid for them; those claims can never be burned or moved, because burn and transferFrom need msg.sender to be address(0) or approved by it (ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, ERC6909.sol:35-48). The native backing stays in the PoolManager as surplus. No other user loses anything. Evidence: eth_call balanceOf(address,uint256)(0,0) on https://mainnet.base.org/ and https://base-rpc.publicnode.com at seven block heights; src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22
- Monad, cycle 17. Monad reports a RETURNDATACOPY past the end of return data as 'out of gas' (JSON-RPC code -32603), where the specification and the other clients name it an out-of-bounds halt. Result: Both are exceptional halts that consume the frame's gas and return failure to the caller, and the vector's outcome equals the specification. The PoolManager never copies return data beyond RETURNDATASIZE (Hooks.callHook and CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith use returndatasize as the length), so the label cannot change a result of the bytecode. Only an off-chain tool that parses the error text would see it. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/offsets-143.json (failMessages)

## Reading of the source (theme-reference-interpreter-audit)

- all 21 networks, cycle 17. Reference interpreter fault 1, stack limit: tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:102-110 handles PUSH1 to PUSH32, DUP1 to DUP16 and PUSH0 with `continue`, which skips the only overflow check at pyevm.py:218, so a frame can hold 1025 or more items and still succeed. The same lines are in cycles/013/theme-mined-branches.work/pyevm2.py:143-151 (check at :281) and cycles/016/theme-revert-rollback-mined.work/pyevm_tx.py:131-139 (check at :266). The specification halts when a push meets a full stack of 1024 (cancun/vm/stack.py:55). Result: Confirmed as a reference fault: of seven frames that reach 1025 items, the chain halts all seven and all three copies let four of them succeed (1025 PUSH0, 1024 PUSH0 then DUP1, 1025 PUSH1 then POP, 1024 PUSH0 then DUP1 then ADD). All 21 networks halt them, so no network differs. No PoolManager comparison can rest on the fault: the built PoolManager reaches at most 49 stack items over 60 buildcheck cases (111 liquidity changes, 242 swaps), far from 1024, and a reference that wrongly succeeds can only add a mismatch, never hide one. Fixed in this unit's copy pyevm_tx17.py. Result: The override turns the precompile off for that call: identity with 128 bytes returns success and 0 bytes with the override and 128 bytes without it, while reth endpoints keep the precompile. Task 3: Tempo transaction 0xba5c0224452fbe54eb5198aad0bba1cf5a4b86db6e40eb4f4265024a79bdfa27 (block 50439947: unlock undone, then swap, unlock, take, sync, settle, swap complete), rerun whole in pyevm_tx17.py with the ten calls into TIP-20 tokens and the fee manager answered from the chain's call tree (tempo/v1.19.1 trace endpoint). Result: All 7 PoolManager frames end as on chain, both PoolManager slots and the third changed bytecode slot are equal, and every call the reference made into a node contract had exactly the chain's input (10 used, 0 left). ## Reading of the source (theme-monad-exit-writer)

- Monad, cycle 18. L-840 question 1. Does the spill step before the dependency loop of Emitter::write_to_final_stack_offsets in monad v0.16.5 remove every dependency cycle?. Result: No, and it does not need to. The spill step (emitter.cpp:1401-1418) only frees one AVX register as scratch (init_yx1): when no register is free it moves the value of the first unreserved AVX holder (virtual_stack.cpp:530-541) to memory, or drops the register when the element already has a stack offset, general register or literal (virtual_stack.cpp:553-565). It runs before the dependency count is built at 1433-1461, so a spilled element is counted as a memory element. Cycles are left for the second loop (1564-1621). The dependency relation is a function: an element has at most one stack offset, so it blocks at most one other element (the owner of that offset). Every element that is not on a cycle is reached from a leaf and is written in the first loop (1478-1542), so after it exactly the cycle members have a count, and that count is 1. The second loop rotates each cycle through two AVX registers. yx1 is init_yx1 and yx2 is a free register or, when none is free, the register of the last AVX element written in the first loop (1550-1561). When no register is free, 15 of the 16 registers belong to elements other than init1; at most one of them (the popped jump target) is off the stack, so at least 14 AVX stack elements are written in the first loop and yx1 != yx2 holds in every order. Each cycle member's slot is read before it is overwritten, because the slots of a cycle are final indices of its own members only and stack indices of distinct elements are disjoint. The iteration order of the map decides which cycle is rotated first and which register serves as yx2; neither changes a stored word. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1401-1418 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1433-1461 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1550-1621 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/virtual_stack.cpp:530-565 ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp
- Monad, cycle 18. L-840 question 2. Is a dependency skipped at the AVX register check (emitter.cpp:1457-1459) ever read later from a register that an earlier write in the loop reassigned?. Result: No. Every register write the writer emits goes to yx1 or yx2: the loads at 1496, 1499 and 1511 in the first loop and 1588-1598 in the cycle loop. In the first loop yx1 is init_yx1 until the first AVX element is popped, and from then on it is the register of the AVX element popped most recently (1484-1487). An AVX element x whose memory slot is a final index of another element e is not counted as a blocker of e, so e may be written over x's slot first. x is then read from its own register when it is popped. That register can be overwritten only after it became yx1, which happens when x itself is popped, and x is fully written by then. init_yx1 is a register no stack element holds. AVX elements are never on a cycle, because they have no outgoing edge, so all of them are written in the first loop, before any cycle-loop write to yx1 or yx2. The writer writes no general register: mov_general_reg_to_mem (1833-1840) only reads them, and mov_literal_to_ymm (1961-1988) writes only the target ymm and does not change flags. The pc of a popped jump target is taken into its operand before the writer runs (3544-3576). - Monad, cycle 18. L-840 question 3. Can an element whose stack offset lies below min_delta be left with a nonzero dependency count?. Result: No element has such an offset. Stack offsets come from three places only: the entry elements of each index from -1 down to the new min_delta (virtual_stack.cpp:298-302 and 326-330), the positive offsets 0..max_delta-1 (305-308, 334-337) and offsets that a destroyed or moved element returned (free_stack_offset, 202-208), all of which were handed out from the first two. min_delta never rises inside a block (continue_block takes the minimum, 321). Stack::get also asserts its index is at most top_index and at() asserts it is inside negative_elems_ (365-383). An offset above top_index is skipped at 1450 and creates no count. Any element with a count after the first loop is on a cycle and has its count set to zero at 1577-1579. The instrumented build counted offset_below_min=0 and nonzero_after_cycles=0 in every compile. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/virtual_stack.cpp:281-344 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/virtual_stack.cpp:365-383 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1446-1452 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1564-1580
- Monad, cycle 18. L-840 task 2. The block-exit writer of v0.16.5 run in every forced order on the deployed Monad PoolManager runtime (24,009 bytes, the cycle 16 copy monad-pm-runtime.hex, sha256 9f68b8fc of the hex file), with a symbolic check of every block exit and a runtime replay of mined transactions. Result: The writer was rebuilt from the v0.16.5 file (sha256 1294ce58, equal to the jsDelivr copy fetched here) with both loops over dep_counts taken from a vector holding the same keys (src/patch_writer.py). The emitted instructions are the original ones in the forced order. Each emitted load and store also drives a symbolic machine, and at every block exit each final index must hold the element that owns it. One compile of the PoolManager has 659 block exits with something on the stack, 3314 stack elements in all, at most 24 elements and 9 blocked elements in one exit, 26 dependencies skipped at the AVX check, 98 cycles (longest 7) and no exit that has to spill an AVX register. Exits by element count: 1 to 6 elements 475, 7 to 15 170, 16 or more 14. Permutation indices 0 to 719 gave every block with up to 6 elements all its orders, with a seeded shuffle for larger ones (seed = index), and shuffle seeds 1 to 200 reordered every block: 920 compiles, 0 wrong final words, 0 AVX elements read after their register was overwritten, and the same final-state digest 18e601f3245c1db8 as the map's own order. The orders do change the machine code: two forced orders differ by 2,312 to 3,306 lines of the 48,757-line asm log. Two planted faults show the check can fail: one temporary register for cycles gave 140 to 141 wrong words per compile, and rereading AVX elements from memory gave 16 to 27 wrong words depending on the order (200 seeds). At run time the instrumented build replayed the 2,007 mined Monad PoolManager transactions of cycle 16 from their pre-state under 12 orders (map order, permutation indices 1 to 5, shuffle seeds 101 to 106): 24084 transaction runs, 0 mismatches between interpreter and native code, 0 divergences from the block. With the planted reread fault 1382 of 2,007 transactions mismatched. The runtime comparison is per transaction frame, not per block exit; the per-exit comparison is the symbolic one. - Monad, cycle 18. Whether the read-only data that the writer's literal loads use depends on the order. Result: The order changes where a literal lands in the read-only table, not its value. RoData keys each entry by its bytes and returns the offset of the existing entry on a repeat (emitter.cpp:339-436). Full-width literals are 32-byte entries at 32-byte offsets, which vmovaps needs; 16, 8 and 4 byte entries are read with vmovups, vmovq and vmovd, which need no alignment. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:339-436 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1961-1988
- Monad, cycle 18. L-812 and L-849. Which Monad release mainnet validators run, from headers, RPC client strings and release records. Result: The release page lists v0.16.5 as released to mainnet on 2026-10-22 and v0.16.7 as released to testnet on 2026-11-19 with mainnet N/A; the monad-bft v0.16.7 release tells operators not to upgrade without an announcement, and the v0.16.7 upgrade page says it applies to testnet only. The latest mainnet header has extraData of 32 zero bytes and no version field, and admin_nodeInfo is disabled on rpc3.monad.xyz. web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-25 (out/rpc/clientversion.txt): Monad/0.16.7 on rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz, rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com and the Tatum gateway; Monad/unknown on rpc3.monad.xyz, rpc4.monad.xyz and Ankr; proxy strings on rpc2.monad.xyz (eRPC), Originstake (eRPC), dRPC and thirdweb. So validators are on v0.16.5 by the published schedule while some mainnet full nodes run v0.16.7. No vote, proposal or validator-set field naming a version was found. This unit shows that the two releases store the same words at every block exit, so the mix gives no split. Evidence: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/changelog/releases ; https://github.com/category-labs/monad-bft/releases/tag/v0.16.7 ; https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/upgrade-instructions/v0.16.7 ; eth_getBlockByNumber latest and web3_clientVersion on the endpoints named, 2026-11-25

- MegaETH, cycle 18. L-842, task 1: every MegaETH PoolManager transaction that ends successfully with an ERC-20 still synced, and every later transaction of the same block that calls settle, settleFor or take. Result: None found. debug_traceTransaction with callTracer (https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42 at start and end) was run on 72,184 transactions: the 51,233 of the cycle 15 list (PoolManager logs or an ERC-20 Transfer to the PoolManager, blocks 7,009,653 to 32,770,383), 93 found by eth_getLogs for PoolManager logs and Transfers from or to the PoolManager from 32,770,384 to 32,814,962, and 20,858 more that appear only in Blockscout's internal transaction list (frames without a log, mostly failed). Every trace returned. The PoolManager frames were put in execution order with the reverted flag of the frame or an ancestor, and the source's transient model was replayed: sync(X) sets the synced currency and the reserves from the PoolManager's own balanceOf child call (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), sync(0) and settle reset it (src/PoolManager.sol:283, 362), the state is empty at the start of each transaction. 36,875 completed ERC-20 syncs and 12,598 native ones; 54,803 completed settle calls each returned exactly what the model predicts (msg.value with nothing synced, balance rise since the sync otherwise, src/PoolManager.sol:349-364): zero mismatches. No successful transaction ends with an ERC-20 synced, so there is no later same-block settle to examine; 8,312 of 46,201 blocks hold several of these transactions. A settle credited from another transaction's sync would also show as a mismatch here, independently of finding the first transaction. Planted check (seed 18018, 200 sampled traces): dropping the first ERC-20 sync was detected 200 of 200 times, dropping the last settle left an ERC-20 synced or a mismatch 197 of 200 times (the other 3 end with a native settle). Not covered: a transaction that calls only sync and emits no log, makes no token transfer and is outside the Blockscout ranges read; it changes nothing unless a later settle is credited, and every later settle in the set was checked. - Monad, cycle 18. L-842, task 1 on Monad: PoolManager transactions that end with an ERC-20 synced, and settles of later transactions of the same block. Result: None found in a contiguous sample. Monad has about 650 PoolManager transactions per 1,000 blocks and eth_getLogs is limited to 100 blocks, so a full census was not possible from public endpoints. All 30,092 transactions with a PoolManager log or an ERC-20 Transfer from or to the PoolManager in blocks 125,250,001 to 125,295,000 (eth_getLogs in 450 windows of 100 blocks, https://rpc.monad.xyz and https://rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, Monad/0.16.7 at start and end) were traced with callTracer. 33,893 completed ERC-20 syncs, 24,580 syncs inside reverted frames, 42,244 completed settles, all equal to the model's value; no transaction ends with an ERC-20 synced; 6,771 of 16,675 blocks hold several. The client source explains why: every transaction, and every re-execution after a failed optimistic merge, runs on a fresh State built over the block state (execute_transaction.cpp lines 458 to 497), transient storage lives in AccountState::transient_storage_ (account_state.hpp line 70), and BlockState::merge copies only the account and storage_ of each address (block_state.cpp lines 194 to 250), so transient storage never reaches the next transaction. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/execute_transaction.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/state2/block_state.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/state3/account_state.hpp ; research/network-risk/cycles/018/theme-sync-leak-census.work/raw/census-143.jsonl, raw/logs-143.json
- MegaETH, cycle 18. MegaETH client source: where transient storage is cleared between transactions. Result: mega-evm (main, version 1.7.4; crates.io 1.7.2) pins revm 40.0.3, which uses revm-context 18.0.3. TLOAD and TSTORE are the stock host handlers wrapped for compute gas (mega-evm src/evm/instructions.rs lines 611-612 and 2205-2206) and the host delegates tstore and tload to the stock journal (src/evm/host.rs lines 90-91). That journal clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize (revm-context 18.0.3 src/journal/inner.rs lines 154, 188, 246). The sandbox that mega-evm uses for keyless deploys merges accounts and storage only, and its own path calls commit_tx (src/evm/execution.rs line 1023). EIP-1153 requires all transient values to be discarded at the end of the transaction. The producer itself is closed; the mined census above is the evidence that it behaves this way. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/Cargo.toml ; https://static.crates.io/crates/mega-evm/mega-evm-1.7.2.crate ; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-context/revm-context-18.0.3.crate ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-1153.md

## Reading of the source (theme-hyperevm-algebra)

- HyperEVM, cycle 19. Task 1 (lead L-867), strict rerun of the cycle 18 swaps on the 512 bit branch. Group set: every group of cycles/018/theme-hyperevm-v3-rest.work/out/rest-*.json.groups.jsonl whose counts hold branch:m512, 34,534 groups with 39,752 swaps (v3strict19.py). Each swap was run twice from parent-block state on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (web3_clientVersion reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 at 16:35:50 UTC, every 5,000 groups and at the end of each shard, last at 17:45:01 UTC on 2026-11-25). The lenient run repeats the cycle 18 rule and finds the 36,665 swaps with 104,643 calls on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv again, the same counts as cycle 18. The strict run reads the fee and never searches it: fee() at block-1, moved by FeeAdjustment(uint24,uint24) logs (topic 0x0cba8718, 117 groups) earlier in the block. It uses only the open price limit (MIN+1 or MAX-1), exact input with the logged paid amount or exact output with the logged received amount. The logged price may serve as the limit only when its bytes, without leading zeros, stand at a byte boundary in the transaction input. A pass 2 over the groups that failed pass 1 adds two values read from debug_traceTransaction (callTracer) of the swap's own transaction: the one word answer of the first STATICCALL that the pool's swap call makes to an address other than its two tokens (the fee the pool's code asked for), and the zeroForOne, amountSpecified and sqrtPriceLimitX96 arguments of the pool's own swap call. For every strict match that touched the branch, the same rerun was repeated with every 512 bit result of mulDiv and mulDivRoundingUp replaced by result + 1. The swap counts as needing the branch when that rerun fails. Result: All 36,665 swaps that cycle 18 counted on the 512 bit branch match price, tick, liquidity, amount0 and amount1 to the unit under the strict rule (out/strict-final-summary.json). All 36,665 take the branch in their strict rerun (104,643 calls), and 31,044 fail when the branch result is made one unit wrong, so 31,044 swaps need src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 on 512 bit products to come out right. That is far more than the cycle 18 estimate of about 11,900. The reason is that the strict rerun cannot fall back on a limit set at the logged price. By factory: 0x07e60782 24,077 of 28,482, 0x32b9da73 3,405 of 3,460, 0xff7b3e8c 2,028 of 2,644, 0xb1c0fa0b 896 of 1,395, 0xecfa11c2 341 of 341, others 297 of 343. Modes: 32,427 exact input and 1,292 exact output with the fee from fee(), 2,792 with the fee read from the trace, 89 with the limit found in calldata, 65 with the arguments read from the trace. 28,516 of these had matched in cycle 18 only through the fee search or the limit at the logged price. Pass 1 matched 39,331 of the 39,752 swaps and failed 421, 406 of them on the branch. Pass 2 matched every one of the 421 (out/strict2.log, empty out/strict2.mismatch.jsonl). The causes all sit in the pools' own code. 341 are pools of factory 0xecfa11c2, for example 0x215aa7599bf881377cd2e8d03cd619ba3fe8eff8, whose swap asks fee contract 0x1d067a971008897baa4e0fb4fbd61cce985a12e8 (selector 0x0802f3f1) for the fee. That contract reads the HyperCore precompile 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000808, and the answers run from 1,500 to 33,872 pips while fee() answers 2,500. The other 80 are swaps whose router computes the price limit, for example the packed calldata of 0x0db606949817a021aad17dfdead276a5513dda0f13a88e52ad3a95d703bdb0c0, and the pool call's own limit reproduces them. The 3,460 swaps of the Slipstream style factory 0x32b9da73 match with the fee its swap reads from factory selector 0x35458dcc, which forwards to fee module 0x4992d95c (selector 0xb88c9148). That module answered 0 inside keeper transactions of 0x2d10ba71f994d20e5280e47eb9401a4f563e98af, after a call to its selector 0x51ac4e0b, and fee() answered 306 or 9. No swap is left without a match. Nothing points to validator MULMOD, DIV or comparison results that differ from src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 or SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-252.
