- Arc, cycle 21. Task 3 of L-944: native take from the real PoolManager at 0x8366a39c...0951 by eth_call with state overrides (a driver at a fresh address calls unlock, runs the items, records success, return data and balances, and reverts), sent in JSON-RPC batches bracketed by web3_clientVersion and arc_getVersion to both Arc endpoints at the same block 33,142,279, and the same scripts to the Ethereum PoolManager 0x000000000004444c...8A90 at block 26,495,018. Recipients: a codeless address, a contract that reverts, a contract that loops until out of gas, an address made blocklisted by a state override of its slot at 0x1800...01 (no public blocklisted address could be listed: getLogs over the precompile's Blocklisted event needs more than the 1,000 block range the official endpoint allows, dRPC allows 100, and the explorer API returned a challenge), address(0), the precompiles 0x01, 0x02, 0x04 and 0x100, the Arc addresses 0x1800...00 to ...03 and the USDC face 0x3600...00, the PoolManager itself, and a contract that self-destructs when called. Amounts 0, 1 and the rest of the balance (2,410,964.98 USDC on Arc). Also settle with value 1, sync(address(0)) with value, settle with value 0 and take with value. Result: The two Arc endpoints return byte-identical records on all 17 scripts (54 items), so the builds 37812c61 and 8e8edb7a agree on every probed value path. Against Ethereum, success flags, return data and balance changes are equal except where F-125 and F-049 already say: a payout of 1 or of the full balance to address(0) or to the blocklisted address fails on Arc with NativeTransferFailed wrapping Error('Zero address not allowed') or Error('Blocked address') and moves nothing, and every take to 0x1800...00 to ...03 or to 0x3600...00 fails on Arc even with amount 0, because those addresses reject empty calldata, while they are plain accounts on Ethereum. Each failure reverts only the take, so the caller's delta is never debited without a transfer or the reverse (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). The reverting and gas burning recipients give identical wrapped errors on both chains. The precompiles 0x01, 0x02, 0x04 and 0x100 accept value on both, and the full PoolManager balance can be paid to them, which the caller owes and must settle. A take to the PoolManager fails on both, since no contract in src/ outside src/test declares receive or fallback. The self-destructing contract was created before the transaction, so it is not marked destroyed and the take succeeds on both; the destroyed-in-transaction branch of the hook was not reached by these probes. The settle items behave alike on all three: settle credits msg.value, sync and take are not payable. - Arc, cycle 21. Do the Arc precompiles that the USDC face calls (NativeCoinAuthority.transfer at 0x1800...00, NativeCoinControl.isBlocklisted at 0x1800...01) behave in mined transactions as the v0.8.6 source says, given that most mined native settlements and payouts on Arc pass through the face 0x3600 as well. Result: Yes in the mined sample. The replay models transfer(from, to, amount) as: caller must be 0x3600, zero addresses and blocklisted accounts refused, a zero amount moves nothing and logs nothing, otherwise balances move by exactly amount and a Transfer log from 0xff...fe is emitted when from differs from to (native_coin_authority.rs v0.8.6 lines 286-345), and isBlocklisted as a read of slot keccak(account, 2) of 0x1800...01. With that model every one of the 1,998 rerun transactions gives the mined emitter logs, and the PoolManager balance changes equal those logs to the wei in all 1,671 isolated blocks. The 18 versus 6 decimal split and its rounding are cleared in earlier cycles and were not reopened. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-arc-running-code.work/dl/src/v0.8.6/crates/precompiles/src/native_coin_authority.rs:286-345, research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-arc-running-code.work/dl/src/v0.8.6/crates/precompiles/src/native_coin_control.rs:183-215, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/v0.8.6/crates/precompiles/src/native_coin_authority.rs, research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-arc-running-code.work/raw/summary.json

## Reading of the source (theme-blind-read)

- Ethereum, Optimism, BNB Smart Chain, Unichain, Polygon, X Layer, Worldchain, Soneium, Tempo, Robinhood Chain, Base, Arbitrum One, Celo, Ink, Elysium, Zora, cycle 21. Assumption T3, ranked first in the blind list: transient slots of the real PoolManager written in one transaction must be empty in the next transaction of the same block. eth_simulateV1 at the real PoolManager address ran, in one simulated block, a driver (state override) that calls unlock and syncs a stub token inside the callback, ending (1) in success with the currency still synced, (2) INVALID inside and at the top, (3) REVERT, (4) a completed unlock followed by INVALID at the top. After each transaction a separate transaction read IS_UNLOCKED, NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT, RESERVES_OF and CURRENCY through exttload(bytes32[]), and the driver read its own transient slot; a second block read them again. Worldchain, Celo and X Layer were run on thirdweb, ankr and drpc endpoints because the networks.json endpoints refused eth_simulateV1 with HTTP 401 and 403. Result: On all 16 networks the in-transaction read returned the synced stub token, so the write happened, and every later transaction and the next block read 0 in all four PoolManager slots and in the driver slot. An IS_UNLOCKED value of 1 would have let any later caller run take() outside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99,291-297,112). No leak exists on the simulation path of these endpoints. Raw answers with web3_clientVersion before and after are in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json and xtx-alt.json, script research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/scripts/xtx.py. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Assumption C5, ranked third: CALLVALUE must equal a real debit, because native settle credits msg.value with no balance check (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). eth_call of a top-level transfer of 1 wei and of 1e18 wei from an address with zero balance on all 21 networks. Result: All 21 endpoints refused both calls with an insufficient funds or OutOfFunds error, and the sender balance is 0. Together with the earlier internal-call value tests (tools/opdiff/callsem.py) no endpoint lets a call carry value that was not debited. Results in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Assumption T5, never isolated before: TSTORE must fail in a static context. The earlier static write test wrote TSTORE and SSTORE together, so the SSTORE alone would fail the frame. Probe C staticcalls the real PoolManager's sync(X), which writes only transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-31), then reads CURRENCY and RESERVES_OF. In the same eth_call it checks that sync(X) by plain call sets the slot and sync(address(0)) clears it, that a sub-frame that unlocks, syncs in the callback and then reverts or halts with INVALID leaves CURRENCY, IS_UNLOCKED and NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT at 0, and that a completed unlock leaves IS_UNLOCKED at 0 with the currency still synced. Result: 18 of 18 words as specified on all 21 networks, including Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc and HyperEVM whose endpoints have no eth_simulateV1. The review's reference interpreter (tools/opdiff/pyevm.py) running the build of this checkout gives the same 18 words. Results in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/static-all.json, scripts research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/scripts/static_rollback.py and scripts/local_ref.py. The first run gave out of gas on every network because a failed static frame burns all forwarded gas; the rerun gives each call a fixed allowance. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/static-all.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Blind reading of every file in src/ outside src/test: every assembly block listed in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/assumptions.md with the opcode result it needs. Constants recomputed in python3: the 19 TickMath multipliers equal floor(2^128 / sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i)) plus 0 or 1, the log constant 255738958999603826347141 equals floor(2^64/log2(sqrt(1.0001))) plus 1, the four transient slot constants equal keccak256(name) minus 1, and getSqrtPriceAtTick(+-887272) returns MAX_SQRT_PRICE and MIN_SQRT_PRICE. Result: No line computes or decides differently from what its comments and the specification say. take, mint, burn, settle and clear are gated only by IS_UNLOCKED (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99) and the only settlement check is NonzeroDeltaCount at the end of unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:112), so the code's safety rests on transient storage rules T2 to T4, which probes A and C and the earlier work test. The checked addition in CurrencyDelta.applyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:37) and the checked subtraction in _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:360) revert rather than wrap. PoolManager has no receive or fallback, so native value enters only through settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307) or through value that bypasses code. Evidence: src/libraries/TickMath.sol:80-111
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Step 3 comparison of the fifteen highest ranked blind assumptions with OPCODES.md, findings.json and cleared.json. Result: Twelve of the fifteen were already tested with evidence that exercises the scenario itself (arithmetic, signed opcodes, division by zero, call output buffers, keccak lengths, jump analysis, gas, sender spoofing, empty-code calls, shared transient frames, frame rollback, dual faces). Three were exercised only near the scenario: transient storage across transactions (one generic simulation on Arbitrum), top-level value without a debit (internal calls only) and TSTORE alone in a static frame. Probes A, B and C close those on the networks whose endpoints serve the method. The table is in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/assumptions.md. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/assumptions.md

## Reading of the source (theme-fullrange-and-claims)

- Ethereum, cycle 21. Task 1 (L-945), validation of the split form for set 2 script 189 (pmdiff2.py seed 11_2026_11_24, 71 calls, native payouts, hook flags 0x0F03 with no swap callbacks). scripts/splitn.py generalises cycle 18's split.py to set 2 and to any number of cuts. Cuts after calls 14 and 34, each just after a full-range swap and before the sync at call 41, so each part holds one of the three heavy swaps. At each cut the PoolManager storage slots that pyevm writes are read with extsload and carried as stateDiff, and the driver's deltas are rebuilt by mint and burn from an operator-approved dummy. The hook's deltas are read and required to be zero. The only other nonzero transient slots are IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT (src/libraries/Lock.sol:8) and NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10), which the preamble rebuilds. Result: At 49,978,998 gas per part the split gives sha256 9ffffd01...136a on eth-mainnet.public.blastapi.io (reth/v2.10.0-f5192ac) and on ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (reth v2.11.0-b9abbcc). That is the unsplit 500M answer stored in cycle 18 (gasUsed 71,521,335), which publicnode cannot give unsplit. At 29,978,998 gas per part the split gives 545529ec...33ec, the stored 25M hash: the swap at call 34 fails with empty data, so a single full-range swap of this script needs more than about 29.4M gas in its frame. The rebuilt transient values equal the ones read in every part. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-fullrange-and-claims.work/raw/split189-eth-blast-50M.json, raw/split189-eth-pn-50M.json, raw/split189-eth-blast-30M.json, scripts/splitn.py; research/network-risk/cycles/018/theme-full-range-swaps.work/raw/eth-blast-s2.json
- Elysium, cycle 21. Task 1 (L-945) on Elysium. Gas cap of https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz (nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/linux-amd64/go1.25.12) probed with a GAS stub: a 2e9 request is accepted and the frame sees 49,978,998. Script 189 run unsplit at that cap, then in the split form validated on Ethereum (cuts 14|15 and 34|35). Result: Unsplit, the driver uses 47,244,353 gas and the answer equals the stored 25M Ethereum hash 545529ec...33ec, which is the truncated answer. In split form at 49,978,998 per part the answer is 9ffffd01...136a, equal to the full Ethereum answer in every word. Hook deltas are zero at both cuts and the rebuilt transient slots equal those read. Script 189 is no longer an open difference on Elysium. - HyperEVM, cycle 21. Task 1 (L-945) on HyperEVM. Caps probed: rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, rpc.hypurrscan.io, hyperliquid-json-rpc.stakely.io and hyperliquid.rpc.blxrbdn.com (all 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet') grant 29,978,998; hyperliquid.drpc.org (Geth/v10.0.0/drpc, backend hidden) 49,978,998; rpc.hyperlend.finance (reth/v0.1.0-b92ad36, nanoreth nb-20261125-2) 199,978,998, consistent with nanoreth's RPC gas ceiling taken from the big block limit (src/node/rpc/mod.rs lines 75-78 of nb-20261125-2); rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/nanoreth 404. Result: On rpc.hyperlend.finance at 199,000,000 gas script 189 runs unsplit to the end and returns 9ffffd01...136a, the full Ethereum answer, using 71,558,335 gas against 71,521,335 on Ethereum. The 37,000 gas difference does not change any word. One part of it fits the empty account 0x04 on HyperEVM (eth_getBalance 0 on rpc.purroofgroup.com, nonzero on Ethereum), which a native take with value pays the new-account charge for; I did not attribute the rest. On hyperliquid.drpc.org the split form at 49,978,998 per part gives 9ffffd01...136a as well. The official endpoint cannot give the full answer: unsplit at its cap it uses 28,452,360 gas and returns 545529ec...33ec, and in split form at 29,978,998 per part (also with the swaps isolated in single-call parts) it returns 545529ec...33ec, the same bytes Ethereum gives in split form at the same gas. The validator's own result for the full-range swap at call 34 is therefore not observable through any official endpoint. - Polygon, Monad, Tempo, Elysium, HyperEVM, cycle 21. Does a full-range swap that no endpoint can run within one transaction matter for user funds? Script 189 makes all three liquidity additions fail, so the pool has no liquidity and the swaps at calls 14, 34 and 57 walk the tick range word by word in the loop at src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-348. Result: No. The loop stops at the caller's own sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a swapper who meets a long walk can bound it with a price limit, and nobody needs a swap to remove liquidity or redeem claims. The words returned on every network that finished the script equal Ethereum's, so no network computes the walk differently. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-348; research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-fullrange-and-claims.work/raw/split189-elysium-50M.json, raw/hyper-hyperlend-189.json

- HyperEVM, cycle 21. Task 3 (L-946). Which HyperEVM clearances rest on system transaction data that the header does not authenticate, and do the official endpoint and the archive client agree on it? nanoreth nb-20261125-2 says in its executor that system transaction receipts are not committed to by the header (src/node/evm/executor.rs lines 322-340) and checks them against keccak256(rlp([[tx_type, success, cumulative_gas_used, logs], ...])) supplied by the block source (src/node/types/mod.rs lines 37-61, executor.rs lines 293-306); blocks without that commitment run unchecked. The clearances that rest on system transaction data: the cycle 20 census of senders (theme-outside-signature-senders, eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on the official endpoint, blocks 52,231,708 to 52,233,207), the system transaction censuses of cycles 2, 14 and 19 on rpc.purroofgroup.com, the L-184 reading that coreReceiveWithData calls carry 200,000 gas and precede signed transactions, the HYPE credit and AQAv2 sender items, and F-044 and F-020, whose ordering statement (system transactions before all signed ones) comes from the same data and the documentation. For 200 blocks drawn with random.Random(2120261125) from the 100,000 blocks below head, eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on the official endpoint was compared with eth_getBlockByNumber(full) and eth_getBlockReceipts on the archive: once with rpc.purroofgroup.com (nanoreth f0cad31) and once with rpc.hyperlend.finance (nanoreth b92ad36, nb-20261125-2, which runs the commitment check). Result: They agree. purroofgroup: 200 of 200 blocks answered, 69 with system transactions, 118 system transactions; type, chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gas, to, value, input and from equal in all 118; every one is listed before the signed transactions at its official index; the signed transaction lists and block hash, receiptsRoot, transactionsRoot, stateRoot and gasUsed equal in all 200; all archive receipts of system transactions have status 1; none names the PoolManager. hyperlend: the same on its draw (head moved), 200 blocks, 66 with system transactions, 104 system transactions, no mismatch. The two clients compute different hashes for the same system transaction (0 of 222 equal), so a census must match by content and not by hash. Because nb-20261125-2 fails a block whose re-executed system receipts differ from the source commitment, every block hyperlend served had matching system receipts. That commitment comes from the operator's own block source, so it shows the archive client and hl-node agree, not that the header authenticates them. The ordering that the sync and settle clearances need (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) holds in every sampled block, and nothing found lets an ordinary account place a system transaction between a user's sync and settle. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-fullrange-and-claims.work/raw/systx-purroof.json, raw/systx-hyperlend.json, scripts/systx_cmp.py, dl/nanoreth/src_node_evm_executor.rs, dl/nanoreth/src_node_types_mod.rs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/src/node/evm/executor.rs and /src/node/types/mod.rs)

## Reading of the source (theme-ruint-releases)

- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Task 1, fix #681 (mul_mod quotient skip). The quotient-skip test was read in the crate sources of ruint 1.18.0, 1.19.0, 1.20.0, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 from static.crates.io (sha256 of the .crate files are listed in the work directory). Result: Releases 1.18.0 to 1.20.1 do not have the fault. Their mul_mod (src/modular.rs:94-102) forms the full double-width product and runs the general division, and they do not contain rem_nxm_spare_limb. 1.21.1 contains the fix: src/algorithms/div/knuth.rs:133-136 skips the top quotient limb only when the top two normalized numerator limbs are strictly less than the divisor's. That condition is sufficient, so the skipped digit is always zero. The main-branch CHANGELOG still lists #681 under Unreleased and has no 1.21.1 section. The statement that 1.21.1 holds the fix therefore rests on the crate code, not on the changelog. When the harness copy was changed to <=, as in 1.21.0, it gave 109,148 wrong mul_mod results in 1,000,000 cases (seed 21024). The five releases gave none. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.21.1.crate (src/algorithms/div/knuth.rs:133-136, src/modular.rs:114-150); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/main/CHANGELOG.md
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Task 1, change #634 (Shl and Shr by primitive integer types). The impl_shift macro and the overflowing_shl_big and wrapping_shl paths were read in all five releases. Result: In 1.18.0, 1.19.0 and 1.20.0 the operators exist only for usize, u8, u16, u32, isize, i8, i16 and i32, plus u64 and i64 on 64-bit targets (src/bits.rs:924-928 in 1.20.0). They convert with `rhs as usize`. 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 add u128 and i128 and convert with usize::try_from(rhs).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) (1.20.1 src/bits.rs:858-924). On 64-bit hosts, the change itself changes no value for any type the older releases implement. The value faults in this area come from the release-specific code listed in the next entries. - all 21 networks, cycle 21. Task 4: 24,413 eth_call vectors (seed 2102101) through the battery dispatcher. They cover SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE and SIGNEXTEND with amounts 2^32+k, 2^33+k, 3*2^32+k, 2^63+k, 2^64+k, 2^128+k, 2^192+k and 2^64-1-k; EXP with every power of two base up to 2^63 and exponents 0 to 39, 63 to 257, 2^32, 2^64 and 2^256-1; 1,500 MULMOD and 1,500 MULDIV512 cases in the mul_mod fault shape; 1,000 ADDMOD cases near the modulus; limb-edge comparisons; and CALLDATALOAD with high-bit offsets. 28 single probes cover JUMP and JUMPI to 0x30 plus 2^32, 2^64, 2^128, 2^192 and 2^255, and MLOAD and RETURN with high-limb offsets. Each network batch is bracketed by web3_clientVersion. Result: All 21 networks returned the specified word for all 24,413 vectors. Every probe that a node answered was as specified: jumps with high limbs gave InvalidJump, and oversize offsets failed. Exceptions are limited to transport refusals. The publicnode endpoints for Ethereum and Polygon refused some probes with HTTP 403. drpc (eth.drpc.org and polygon.drpc.org, whose backend client is hidden) answered all 28 as specified. Result: The handler is BaseHandler in base-common-evm, its own copy of the OP handler. execution_result turns a halted deposit into the error HaltedDepositPostRegolith before any commit (crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs lines 334-336); run sends every error to catch_error (revm-handler 42.0.1 src/handler.rs lines 100-108). catch_error, for a transaction error of a deposit, calls checkpoint_revert(JournalCheckpoint::default()) (line 368), bumps the nonce and adds the mint, then commit_tx (line 377); any other error goes to discard_tx (line 386). The Cargo.lock at tag v1.5.6 pins revm 42.0.1 and revm-context 42.0.0 from crates.io and reth from base/reth tag base-v2.5.2.11 commit 9e380dd, the commit the endpoint names. In revm-context 42.0.0 checkpoint_revert replays the journal with the transient map (src/journal/inner.rs lines 622-640, and revm-context-interface 42.0.0 entry.rs lines 432-440 put back or remove each TSTORE), commit_tx clears transient_storage (inner.rs lines 141-158), and so do discard_tx (174-192) and finalize (207-250). Every block transaction runs through ExecuteEvm::transact (executor/block_executor.rs line 255, evm.rs line 450), which calls finalize after transact_one even on error. So a failed or halted deposit leaves no transient value, first because its own TSTOREs are replayed away, then because the commit and the finalize clear the map. - Celo, cycle 22. Celo: CIP-64 fee currency debit and credit calls, the core contract reads, and the system calls. Is transient storage cleared between them and the user transaction, and does the user choose their code?. Result: The debit runs before the user frames, through the non-committing system call inside a checkpoint. On success the checkpoint is committed and the debit's transient storage is cleared before the user transaction runs (crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs lines 635-676, clear at line 668); on rejection checkpoint_revert undoes it (line 678). The credit runs after the user frames, inside build_execution_result (line 876), through core_contracts::call, which runs a committing system call and then clears transient_storage itself (contracts/core_contracts.rs lines 211-248, clear at line 243). Inside that call execution_result calls commit_tx (handler.rs line 1298), which clears the user transaction's transient map too, after the user's last frame has returned. The fee currency's code therefore runs once with the user transaction's transient values present, but transient storage is keyed by address, the PoolManager's lock is already false after a completed unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:113), and the fee currency must be on the governance-held FeeCurrencyDirectory list, so the user picks among listed currencies and chooses none of their code. Core contract reads use call_read_only inside a checkpoint that is reverted (core_contracts.rs lines 142-173). EIP-2935 and EIP-4788 run through OpBlockExecutor as on the other OP chains (alloy-celo-evm block/executor_factory.rs line 114). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/celo/reth-v1.0.10/crates/celo-revm/src/contracts/core_contracts.rs

- all 21 networks, cycle 22. What a carried transient slot would do to src/, and whether a failed deposit could leave one. Result: A failed deposit cannot leave a PoolManager transient value even on a client that skipped the clear at commit: any TSTORE the deposit made is a journal entry, and the revert to the first checkpoint puts the previous value back or removes the key (revm-context-interface 43.0.2 src/journaled_state/entry.rs lines 455-470). The only values that can outlive a successful transaction on a faulty client are the synced currency and reserves, because unlock writes the lock false (src/PoolManager.sol:113) and reverts unless the delta count is 0 (line 112). A carried synced currency would be read by the next transaction's settle as paid = balanceOf - reservesBefore (src/PoolManager.sol:349-361) and could credit one account with another's transfer. All builds read here clear the map at the end of every transaction, so that case does not arise. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349

The deployer has its 69 byte code on Polygon, Avalanche, BNB Smart Chain and World Chain, and the original call carries no signature of its own, so any account can send the same call there and get the same 2,488 byte runtime, because the address commits to the init code. That runtime has no SSTORE, SLOAD or ORIGIN; it keeps the Ethereum PoolManager address 0x000000000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de08a90 as an immutable, checks CALLER against it (PC 0x37b to 0x3aa), and answers beforeRemoveLiquidity with HookNotImplemented (0x0a85dc29) on Ethereum, Base and OP Mainnet. eth_call of the third-party removals with that runtime placed at the hook address by state override reverts with WrappedError(0xf8c3..., 0x21d0ee70, HookNotImplemented, HookCallFailed) in all 8 runs on Polygon and Avalanche, so the pools stay frozen after a replay. Other code cannot reach the address: a CREATE2 or CREATE output equal to a fixed 160 bit address, or the signing secret of a CREATE2 output, needs about 2^160 work. The address has nonce 0 on all four networks. - all 21 networks, cycle 22. Whether the permissionless deterministic factories that a hook deployed on one network could be replayed through exist on all 21 networks. Result: Yes. The CREATE2 deployer 0x4e59b44847b379578588920ca78fbf26c0b4956c has its 69 byte code and CreateX 0xba5ed099633d3b313e4d5f7bdc1305d3c28ba5ed its 11,838 byte code on all 21 networks. So a hook address made through 0x4e59b448 or through CreateX CREATE2 on one network can be filled on any other by whoever has the init code, and what that account controls is decided by the init code alone. A CreateX CREATE3 address does not depend on the init code, so when its salt does not carry the deployer in its first 20 bytes (the permissioned deploy protection in the CreateX README) any account can place any code at it on another network. Of the 82 hook addresses in use that are empty on some network, 25 have contract code on another network (raw/xchain.json); only 0xf8c3f424...4300 among them sets bit 9, 8, 5 or 4, and it is cleared above. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-empty-hook-pools.work/raw/factories.json, raw/xchain.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pcaversaccio/createx/main/README.md (Permissioned Deploy Protection and Cross-Chain Redeploy Protection, lines 576 and 709-734 of the fetched copy)

## Reading of the source (theme-outflow-census)

- all 21 networks, cycle 22. Task 1, the rule as cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/census2.py applies it (cycle 18 and 19 census.py scripts are a different test: they replay sync and settle in callTracer frames, they do not balance flows). Result: Task 1, the rule as cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/census2.py applies it (cycle 18 and 19 census.py scripts are a different test: they replay sync and settle in callTracer frames, they do not balance flows). Inputs per block range: ERC-20 Transfer logs with the PoolManager as topic1 (out) or topic2 (in), counted only when the log has exactly three topics and 32 bytes of data (census2.py:69); WETH style Deposit(dst) logs naming the PoolManager, counted as in (census2.py:73-74); and every PoolManager log: Swap amounts as signed int128, Donate amounts, ModifyLiquidity pool ids, Initialize keys, and ERC-6909 Transfer logs with from = 0 (claims minted) or to = 0 (claims burned) (census2.py:76-91). Per transaction and currency: net = out + minted - in - burned; owed = sum of Swap amount0/amount1 of pools holding the currency, positive when the pool pays, minus Donate amounts (census2.py:106-111). A row is flagged only when net > owed and the transaction holds no ModifyLiquidity log of a pool with that currency (skipped-liquidity) and no pool event on a pool missing from the Initialize list (skipped-unknown-pool) (census2.py:118-123). Hook deltas have no event (src/PoolManager.sol:181, 224) and enter only through the Transfer and claim logs they cause; protocol fee collection has no event (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57) and is recognised afterwards by rule.py from the trace (collectProtocolFees output) or from a fall of protocolFeesAccrued (cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/rule.py:171, 185). Native currency: a native transfer leaves no log, so a native row exists only when a claim of id 0 is minted or burned, or on Arc where 0xff..fe Transfer logs exist; on every other network such rows are counted as native-no-logs and skipped (census2.py:116). What the rule cannot see: (a) every native outflow on 20 of 21 networks; (b) any currency of a pool that has a ModifyLiquidity log in the same transaction, because the event carries liquidityDelta and no amounts (src/PoolManager.sol:175), so an outflow dressed as a liquidity removal or fee collection is never judged; (c) pools absent from the Initialize list; (d) a wrong amount that the PoolManager itself computes and logs: the Swap event is emitted from the same delta that is paid (src/PoolManager.sol:234-251), so an arithmetic fault in Pool.swap, SwapMath, SqrtPriceMath or FullMath that overpays a swapper is booked as owed and never flagged; this census therefore cannot test the opcode and integer library hypotheses of this cycle, which the mined swap replays in OPCODES.md test instead; (e) ERC-6909 transfers between accounts (from and to both nonzero, src/ERC6909.sol:30, 45), so claims moved from a victim and then burned for a take net to zero; (f) balance changes without a standard Transfer log, in either direction (rebases, mints that log only Deposit, tokens with nonstandard events); (g) freezes, which move nothing; (h) the flag is one sided: an inflow larger than owed is not reported. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/census2.py:1-125; research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-currency-lists.work/rule.py:1-190; src/PoolManager.sol:175; src/PoolManager.sol:241

The module trees of base/base v1.5.6 (crates/common/precompiles and crates/common/precompile-storage), mega-evm v1.7.4 (crates/mega-evm), xlayer-reth v0.0.7 (builder, chainspec, flashblocks, intercept, rpc, monitor, bin/node), tempo a9d6748 (crates/precompiles and crates/contracts), arc-node v0.8.6 (crates/precompiles, crates/evm, crates/execution-config) and nanoreth nb-20261125-2 (src) were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com by following every mod declaration (scripts/crawl.py, 558 requests in dl/fetchlog.txt, no module left unresolved). scripts/scan.py listed every shift operator, every shift method (checked_shl, overflowing_shl, wrapping_shl and the rest), and every wrapping_from, saturating_from, try_from, try_into, I256 and Signed use in non-test code (scan-*.json). web3_clientVersion at the start and end of the session returned base/v1.5.6, xlayer/v0.0.7, tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748, mega-reth/v2.3.1, arc/v1 and hyperliquid evm Mainnet (rpc/clientversion-start.txt and rpc/clientversion-end.txt). Result: The lockfiles read in cycle 21 pin ruint 1.19.0 for Base v1.5.6 and mega-evm v1.7.4, 1.18.0 for xlayer v0.0.7, 1.20.0 for arc-node v0.8.6 and 1.20.1 for nanoreth. Tempo a9d6748 pins ruint 1.21.1 and alloy-primitives 1.7.3 (Cargo.lock fetched this session). Across all six trees the whole non-test search returns one shift method call (Base pausable_feature.rs:31), no call of wrapping_from or saturating_from on a Uint, no I256 or Signed integer arithmetic, and Uint shifts only in the storage packing helpers, Base string length decoding and the Tempo order book bitmap. Every other shift is on a primitive u8, u64, u128 or i16 and does not go through ruint. A reading of ruint 1.21.1 src/from.rs:160-225 and 494-512 narrows the conversion fault: TryFrom of a negative primitive returns an error and saturating_from returns zero, which are correct. Only wrapping_from returns the zero-extended payload of the ValueNegative error. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-rust-native-ruint.work/scan-base_base@v1.5.6.json; research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-rust-native-ruint.work/scan-tempoxyz_tempo@a9d6748.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/Cargo.lock; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.21.1.crate (src/from.rs:188-225, 494-512)
- Base, cycle 22. L-967, Base v1.5.6 B20 precompiles, factory, policy registry and precompile storage under ruint 1.19.0. The sites are packing.rs:87, 114, 142, 144 and 161 (U256 shifted by usize offset*8 or byte_count*8), types/vec.rs:316 (byte_offset*8), types/bytes_like.rs:305 (shift by the constant 1), policy logic v1/v2/v3 (u64 shifts by the constant POLICY_ID_TYPE_SHIFT) and pausable_feature.rs:31 (U256::ONE.checked_shl(feature as u8)). Result: No faulty input is reachable. Every packing shift is reached only after the check offset + bytes > 32 returns an error (packing.rs:102, 129 and 152), so offset*8 is at most 248, and create_element_mask shifts only when byte_count < 32 (at most 248). vec.rs:316 uses (index % elems_per_slot) * T::BYTES, which is below 32. The 1.19.0 truncation needs an amount of 2^32 or more. checked_shl uses the overflowing_shl flag, which in 1.19.0 (src/bits.rs:394-409) inspects only the carry out of the last limb it moves and ignores limbs dropped whole. U256::ONE has no bits in dropped limbs, and the amount is a u8 enum value, so the flag is correct for every reachable input. B20 balances, supply and allowances use checked_add and checked_sub on U256 (b20_stablecoin/logic/v3.rs:111-115, 138, 322, 332), which the 1.19.0 faults do not touch. balanceOf returns the stored balance without the UI multiplier (b20_asset/logic/v3.rs:940-980, multiplier capped at type(uint128).max). The PoolManager reads these values through balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90) in sync and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-289, 349-364), and no value it reads passes through a faulty ruint path. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompile-storage/src/packing.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompile-storage/src/types/vec.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/common/pausable_feature.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_stablecoin/logic/v3.rs; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.19.0.crate (src/bits.rs:343-348, 394-409)

- Tempo, cycle 22. L-968, Tempo a9d6748 tip20/mod.rs, tip20/rewards.rs, stablecoin_dex/mod.rs and orderbook.rs, tip_fee_manager/amm.rs and tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs under ruint 1.21.1: Uint shifts and signed to Uint conversions. Result: ruint 1.21.1 has neither shift fault, so only wrapping_from matters, and no file calls it. tip20, rewards, amm and the channel reserve use only checked U256 arithmetic and unsigned conversions (U256::from of u128 or u64 and try_into to u128, for example rewards.rs:164-171 and 362-373). The order book shifts U256::ONE and U256::MAX by (tick & 0xFF) as usize, which is 0 to 255, or by 255 - bit_index with bit_index below 255 (orderbook.rs:508-509, 588-596, 638-646). Word indices are i16 values shifted as i16 and never reach ruint. The signed tick arithmetic is tick_to_price(tick) = (PRICE_SCALE as i32 + i32::from(tick)) as u32 (orderbook.rs:693-695). Its least value over all of i16 is 100000 - 32768 = 67232, so it is never negative, and base_to_quote and quote_to_base turn it into U256 with U256::from of a u32 (orderbook.rs:119-160). stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:2059 is inside the test module that starts at line 1863 and repeats the same formula. The signed credit deltas at stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:196 and tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs:825 are i128 differences of u64 counters (storage_credits/mod.rs:228-245) cast to u64, without ruint. An eth_call of tickToPrice and priceToTick on the DEX precompile at block 0x307b756 (50,837,334) gave 100000 + tick for all 13 aligned ticks from -32760 to 32760, InvalidTick for unaligned ticks and TickOutOfBounds outside 98000 to 102000 (rpc/tempo-ticktoprice.json). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/stablecoin_dex/orderbook.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/stablecoin_dex/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/tip20/rewards.rs; research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-rust-native-ruint.work/rpc/tempo-ticktoprice.json

- Tempo, cycle 22. L-969, every caller of TIP20Token::system_transfer_from and channel_reserve_transfer at a9d6748. The tag tempo/v1.19.1 holds byte-identical copies of tip20/mod.rs, tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs, stablecoin_dex/mod.rs and tip_fee_manager/amm.rs. It schedules T14 for mainnet at 1,796,742,000 and leaves T15 unscheduled for mainnet (crates/hardfork/src/constants.rs:254, hardfork lib.rs:438-440). Probes for later tags (tempo/v1.19.2, v1.20.0, v1.20.1, v1.21.0, v2.0.0) returned 404. The latest block read was 50,837,521 at timestamp 1,795,657,040, so T14 is not active yet. Result: No caller lets an ordinary account move the PoolManager's TIP-20 balance. The StablecoinDEX pulls from sender in decrement_balance_or_transfer_from (stablecoin_dex/mod.rs:299-305, 325-351), and every caller passes the dispatcher's msg_sender (swap_exact_amount_in:428, swap_exact_amount_out:494, place:697, place_flip:869; dispatch.rs:25-66). TipFeeAMM rebalance_swap and mint pull from msg_sender (amm.rs:239, 360; dispatch.rs:56-68). The fee path uses transfer_fee_pre_tx from the transaction's fee payer (tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:158-177), which must sign. In the channel reserve the payer is always msg_sender at open (mod.rs:168-247), and top_up, request_close and withdraw require msg_sender == descriptor.payer (mod.rs:380, 481, 623). Pulls come only from msg_sender, at mod.rs:232-243 and 422-438. settle and close move only reserve custody. They require the payee or operator (mod.rs:854-864), and they need a voucher from the payer or the authorized signer for any amount above what is already settled. The PoolManager can be a payer only by calling the reserve itself. Its code calls only currency contracts and hooks (src/types/Currency.sol:40-90, src/libraries/Hooks.sol). eth_call from the PoolManager address to the reserve 0x4D50500000000000000000000000000000000000 with the transfer, balanceOf and withdraw(uint256) selectors reverted with the unknown selector error 0xaa4bc69a (rpc/tempo-reserve-selectors.txt), so a pool that uses the reserve address as a currency cannot make the PoolManager open, fund or capture a channel. receive_policy_sender differs from the account whose balance moves only when the reserve pays out. For a payee it is the descriptor payer when the channel was opened at T12 or later, and the reserve itself otherwise. For a refund it is the reserve (mod.rs:94-100, 324-329, 553-565, 642-647). In both cases only reserve custody that the payer deposited moves. A channel whose payee is the PoolManager only donates the payer's own tokens to it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs (lines 945-1027); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/tip20_channel_reserve/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/stablecoin_dex/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/tip_fee_manager/amm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/address_registry/mod.rs (lines 27-45); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/hardfork/src/constants.rs; research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-rust-native-ruint.work/rpc/tempo-reserve-selectors.txt
- all 21 networks, cycle 22. What the PoolManager source would compute differently if a Rust-native token balance were wrong. Result: The PoolManager learns a precompile token balance only through balanceOfSelf in sync and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-289, 349-364; src/types/Currency.sol:90) and moves it only through transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40). A wrong native balance would change paid in _settle with all opcodes correct. On the six networks with Rust-native token code, no ruint fault from cycle 21 is reachable from that code, so no such balance can be computed wrongly by this route. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349

- HyperEVM, cycle 22. Task 2 (L-966) on HyperEVM: blocks 45,998,366 to 52,253,230 (the whole history from the deployment block), newest first. Candidates are every transaction with a PoolManager log or an ERC-20 Transfer from or to the PoolManager (eth_getLogs). Every candidate block was traced whole with debug_traceBlockByNumber (callTracer, withLog), so PoolManager frames of non-candidate transactions in those blocks are included. For every PoolManager CALL frame the PoolManager unlock frames above it were tracked. (a) successful take, settle, settleFor, mint, burn, clear, swap, modifyLiquidity or donate frames with no unlock above them; (b) a failed unlock followed by a successful frame of those functions outside a new unlock; also unlock frames with no unlock above them that revert with AlreadyUnlocked (0x5090d6c6), delta frames inside a live unlock that revert with ManagerLocked (0x54e3ca0d), every settle and settleFor output against the transient model of the source, trace status and logs against the mined receipt, and the PoolManager native balance change over the whole range against the native value of all traced frames. Result: 2,820 candidate transactions in 2,392 blocks; 2,392 blocks traced holding 15,960 transactions; 2,838 transactions with a PoolManager frame (18 of them not candidates), 20,088 PoolManager frames, 10,659 delta frames, 2,928 unlock frames. (a) 0, (b) 0, AlreadyUnlocked at top 0, ManagerLocked inside a live unlock 0. 2,546 settle and settleFor outputs all equal the model. 14 transactions have a reverted or halted unlock, 2 of them with a later unlock that completed. - Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 22. Task 3 (L-960, L-976): Arbitrum retryable redeems at Nitro consensus-v61 and its go-ethereum fork. Is the callvalue of a scheduled redeem taken from the ticket escrow in state, and is transient storage empty when the redeem starts?. Result: Yes to both. ArbitrumRetryTx in StartTxHook moves tx.Value from the escrow address to tx.From with util.TransferBalance, which fails with ErrInsufficientBalance when the escrow holds less (arbos/tx_processor.go lines 472-477; arbos/util/transfer.go lines 67-76), and tx.Value is the retryable callvalue stored at submission (arbos/retryables/retryable.go lines 366-381). At submission the callvalue is moved from the sender to the escrow with the same checked transfer (tx_processor.go line 320). The EVM call then checks CanTransfer for tx.From and debits it (fork core/state_transition.go line 725, core/vm/evm.go Call, core/evm.go lines 139-147). Each redeem, scheduled or made by ArbRetryableTx.redeem, runs as its own ApplyTransaction in the block loop (arbos/block_processor.go lines 373-375, 483, 612), and every transaction goes through StateDB.Prepare, which replaces transient storage before execution (fork core/state_transition.go line 737, core/state/statedb.go lines 1598-1599). A plain ArbitrumDepositTx mints and moves value without running any code (tx_processor.go lines 225-233), so it can only raise the PoolManager balance, which native settle does not read (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). The fork was read at f3a966e, the pin of v3.11.3; the pin of consensus-v61 could not be confirmed without the GitHub API, and the same lines are identical on the fork master branch. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/consensus-v61/arbos/tx_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/f3a966e/core/state_transition.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/f3a966e/core/state/statedb.go (copies in research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-unlockless-frames.work/dl/nitro)
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, MegaETH, cycle 22. Task 3 (L-960): OP Stack deposits with a mint field. Is the CALLVALUE of a deposit debited from the sender after the mint?. Result: Yes. op-geth adds the mint to msg.From before execution (core/state_transition.go lines 474-480) and then applies the ordinary CanTransfer check and EVM transfer of msg.value from msg.From (lines 574-579). op-revm at op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4 adds the mint to the caller balance and subtracts the balance spending, and only raises the balance to the value when the configuration disables the balance check (rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs lines 137-151), a switch used by eth_call, not by block execution. The minted ETH was locked in the portal on L1 by the depositor, so the PoolManager is credited with value that its caller paid. The handler builds of Base, Zora, World Chain, Celo, X Layer and MegaETH were not read here; the op-stack-eth unit of this cycle covers failed deposits. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/optimism/core/state_transition.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs
- Tempo, cycle 22. Task 3 (L-960): Tempo batched calls (AA transactions). Can a call in a batch carry a value that no balance pays?. Result: No. Tempo v1.19.1 (the endpoint answers tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748) rejects any AA transaction in which a call carries a nonzero value, in intrinsic gas and in validation (crates/evm/src/handler.rs lines 372-375 and 1445-1448). - HyperEVM, cycle 22. Task 3 (L-960): HyperEVM system transactions that carry HYPE value. Is the value debited?. Result: In the public replica code, yes. hyper-evm-sync runs each system transaction through stock revm transact with the sender set to 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 for native HYPE, value from the transaction, base fee 0 and only EIP-3607 disabled; the balance check is not disabled, and a failed transact panics (src/run.rs lines 123-162 and 217-236). 0x2222...2222 holds 0x30d464db24353838a0d1e7d wei (about 944 million HYPE) on both the official endpoint and the archive client. Each system transaction is its own transact with a fresh journal, so transient storage starts empty. The closed validator itself was not read; its receipts are checked against this execution by the archive clients (run.rs line 236). No HyperEVM PoolManager native movement in the whole history escapes the traced frames (task 2). - all 21 networks, cycle 22. Code reading: which functions reach _accountDelta and whether each is gated by the transient unlock flag. Result: _accountDelta (src/PoolManager.sol:368-379) is called only from take, settle and settleFor through _settle, clear, mint, burn and _accountPoolBalanceDelta, which is called only from modifyLiquidity, swap and donate (lines 181-183, 224-226, 270, 294, 317, 326, 334, 364). All nine carry onlyWhenUnlocked (lines 96-99, 147, 189, 258, 291, 300, 305, 310, 322, 332). The flag is set at line 107 and cleared at line 113 only after the delta count check at line 112. sync (lines 279-288), initialize, updateDynamicLPFee, the ERC-6909 functions and collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57, controller only) need no unlock and write no currency delta. So every payout path depends on the transient flag and the count, as the theme assumes, and on these six networks no mined frame shows either failing. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:96-114

## Reading of the source (theme-hook-replay)

- Arbitrum One, Polygon, Optimism, BNB Smart Chain, Base, cycle 23. Task 1 and 2 for 0x4cd3be8768aea2a0297c22c17a7a3cae65adc0cc (bits 0xcc: before swap, after swap and both swap return delta flags), which has code on Base only and pools on Arbitrum One (0x92d3cd91 and 0xadc18cdb with liquidity, 0xca14c58b, 0x40b40b25), Polygon (0x03d67bb3, 0x2a5b1492, both with liquidity), OP Mainnet (0x1264c6d2, two live positions) and BNB Smart Chain (0xb00fbbe3, ticks -882000 and 882000, liquidity 1,501,245,608,435,103,539). How was it made, who can place code at it where it is empty, and who holds a role after a replay. Result: Nobody but the original deployer's key gains a role, and the replayed code refuses the local PoolManager. The address was not made through CreateX, as the lead said. It was made at Base block 29,366,975 by transaction 0x69dee05880d3369001b4541aefe445520b3770ec1a3ac4f0e77d9171ac65fc3e from 0x2cd524394a4463a4e6f1829124dccbac436c4061 (nonce 3, type 2, chainId 0x2105) to the CREATE2 deployer 0x4e59b448 with salt 0x...0850 and 22,842 bytes of init code; keccak256(0xff ++ 0x4e59b448 ++ salt ++ keccak256(init)) gives 0x4cd3be87...c0cc. Its nonce of 543 comes from a CREATE in its own runtime, not from the factory. The init code ends with five constructor words: PoolManager 0x498581ff (Base), 0x2cd52439, 0x680a9840, 0xe4b1b173 and 0x2cd52439. Running the init code in the reference interpreter (tools/opdiff/pyevm.py) with CALLER 0x4e59b448 executes no ORIGIN, CALLER, CHAINID, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER or external call, writes slot 0 (owner) and slot 9 both = 0x2cd52439 from the arguments, emits OwnershipTransferred(0, 0x2cd52439) as the mined receipt does, and returns a runtime whose SHA-256 equals the Base runtime. An eth_call from 0x...5afe to 0x4e59b448 with the original calldata returns 0x4cd3be87...c0cc on Arbitrum One (nitro v3.13.0-rc.9), Polygon (Tenderly), OP Mainnet (op-reth v2.8.1) and BNB Smart Chain (Geth v1.8.2), so any account can fill the address on all four, and the result has owner 0x2cd52439 (the account that deployed it on Base; the Base owner today is 0xe184cba6 after a transfer) and the Base PoolManager as an immutable. With that runtime and storage placed at the address by state override, beforeSwap and afterSwap called from the local PoolManager revert with 0xae18210a, NotPoolManager(), on all four networks (8 calls). So a replay leaves every swap in these pools reverting as today, gives the replaying account no role, and removal stays open because bits 9 and 8 are clear (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:203-205, 232-243). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-hook-replay.work/raw/tx_0x69dee05880.json, raw/ctor_0x4cd3be87.json, raw/replaycall_0x4cd3be87_{42161,137,10,56}.json, raw/replaysim_0x4cd3be87_{42161,137,10,56}.json, raw/storage_now.json
- Polygon, Worldchain, Soneium, Avalanche, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 23. Tasks 1 and 2 for 0xa6c8d7514785c4314ee05ed566cb41151d43c0c0 (bits 0xc0: before and after swap, no return delta), with code on Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain and Arbitrum One and pools with liquidity on Polygon (0xaa8cf9a9, 0x6e71d4ef, 0xf8e60965), World Chain (0xf43b9efe), Soneium (0x6cfb943c, 0x0b8caca2), Avalanche (0xfdc01c61, 0x4f794b60) and BNB Smart Chain (0x71c1a013, 0x520df565 with liquidity, 0xb792a829 without). Core gives no protection on any network: initialize checks tick spacing, currency order and isValidHookAddress, which reads only the low 14 bits of the address and the fee (src/PoolManager.sol:117-126, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127), and never reads code; whatever code later sits at the address receives the callbacks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160), and the return delta flags let it move amounts against the swapper (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:248-315). For an address that no factory call and no known key reaches, placing code needs a 160 bit preimage, so the only effect is the freeze already recorded in F-004. ## Reading of the source (theme-hyperevm-twin-state)

- HyperEVM, cycle 23. L-994 twin state: every PoolManager storage slot that the logs show was ever written (whole history, 5,570 logs from deployment block 45,998,366 to 52,275,542: 414 Initialize, 2,284 Swap, 846 ModifyLiquidity, 2,023 ERC-6909 Transfer, 2 OperatorSet), the native balance and balanceOf(PoolManager) of all 316 pooled ERC-20 currencies, read on the official endpoint (validator state) and on two nanoreth replicas at the same block. Result: 8,464 slots were derived from the source layout (owner slot 0, protocolFeesAccrued 1, protocolFeeController 2, isOperator 3, balanceOf 4, allowance 5, _pools 6, Pool.State +0..+6, TickInfo and Position.State 3 words each, bitmap key sar(8, compressed)): 1,656 pool words, 3,240 tick words, 2,277 position words, 934 bitmap words, 317 protocol fee counters, 36 ERC-6909 balances, 2 operator flags. All 414 slot0 words read nonzero, as did 747 position words and 1,016 tick words, which confirms the derivation. The official endpoint answers only latest, so every batch of 18 reads was bracketed with eth_blockNumber; all 489 brackets had equal ends, between 52,276,229 and 52,276,658. rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31) returned the same word for all 8,781 items at the bracket block. rpc.hyperlend.finance (reth/v0.1.0-b92ad36) returned the same word for 8,761 items; one batch of 20 was lost to HTTP 429 refusals (227 refusals recorded and retried). No difference was found, so no neighbour re-read was needed. The last 10,000 blocks held only 4 Initialize logs (blocks 52,266,188 to 52,266,493), so the whole-history set was used to make the comparison meaningful. PoolManager native balance 0x9d908ef23bc0864f on all three. Files official_reads.json, replica_purroof.json, replica_hyperlend.json, slots.json. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-hyperevm-twin-state.work/raw/official_reads.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 23. L-995 base fee: whether any HyperEVM block after genesis had a base fee below the 100,000,000 wei level, which would let a legacy transaction with gas price 0 pass the standard EIP-1559 check. Result: eth_feeHistory over all 52,276,001 blocks from 0 to 52,276,000 (8 workers on rpc.purroofgroup.com f0cad31 and rpc.hyperlend.finance b92ad36, 387 HTTP 429 refusals retried) shows base fee 0 only in block 0 (genesis) and no block below 100,000,000 wei after it. Under the EIP-1559 rule a legacy or EIP-2930 transaction needs gas price at least the base fee, so a public transaction with gas price 0 would be invalid in every block. The base fees come from the validator's own headers, which nanoreth does not recompute (its parent base fee check is commented out, src/node/consensus/mod.rs:92-96), and the validator's admission rule itself is closed. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-hyperevm-twin-state.work/raw/feehist_0.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 23. L-995 census: gas price 0 transactions in every block with a PoolManager log (2,405 blocks) and in 3,000 blocks drawn uniformly over the chain (seed 2026112623, range 1 to 52,276,000), grouped by decoded sender and target, with the official block of each read for comparison. Result: 1,579 gas price 0 transactions in 1,089 blocks, all of type 0, all at the start of their block. 45 senders: 0x2222...2222 (98, native HYPE credits), 42 addresses with prefix 0x20 (token system addresses), and two others: 0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24 (488, the USDC linked contract per spotMeta, a 2,175 byte proxy) and 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00 (191, no code, nonce 1,069,810), each calling USDC transfer to the other. None targets the PoolManager or carries its address in the first word. In each of the 5,405 blocks the replica's transaction count minus the official count of regular transactions equals the number of gas price 0 transactions (29,012 minus 27,433 = 1,579), no official regular transaction has gas price 0 or a fee cap of 0, and for 150 blocks the official eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber lists exactly the same senders, targets and selectors in the same order. Over the full history, the 2,642 ERC-20 Transfer logs with the PoolManager as source sit in 2,293 transactions, none with gas price 0. The PoolManager nonce is 1 on the official endpoint and on both replicas at latest, and nanoreth increments the sender nonce of system transactions (0x6b9e77... has nonce 2,399,458), so no transaction in history has run with the PoolManager as sender on either replica. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-hyperevm-twin-state.work/raw/census.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 23. Whether the nanoreth rule that gas price 0 means system transaction can classify an EIP-1559, EIP-7702 or EIP-4844 transaction as a system transaction. Result: is_system_transaction tests tx.gas_price() == Some(0) (src/node/primitives/transaction.rs:182-184, src/node/evm/executor.rs:44-49). In alloy-consensus 2.5.0, the version in nanoreth's Cargo.lock, gas_price() returns None for EIP-1559, EIP-7702 and EIP-4844 transactions (src/transaction/eip1559.rs:174-176, eip7702.rs:162-164, eip4844.rs:488-490) and Some for legacy and EIP-2930. Only a type 0 or type 1 transaction with gas price 0 is taken as a system transaction. The rule is byte identical in the b92ad36 build behind rpc.hyperlend.finance; the f0cad31 build behind rpc.purroofgroup.com differs only in imports and trait plumbing. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/src/node/evm/executor.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 23. Whether the zero BASEFEE that nanoreth gives to gas price 0 transactions (src/node/evm/mod.rs:135-145) or a gas price of 0 reaches any decision in src/. Result: src/ reads no BASEFEE, GASPRICE or ORIGIN. The only gas reads are GAS as the forwarded amount of three calls (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). A system transaction that calls a token runs the token's code, not the PoolManager's, and the PoolManager compares token balances only between sync and settle of one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and :349-365). Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-365
- HyperEVM, cycle 23. Past divergence between the closed validator and revm: the state patches nanoreth applies after particular transactions. Result: nanoreth drops the state changes of 19 listed transactions to match the validator (src/node/evm/patch.rs:7-27), all in blocks 1,467,569 to 1,531,366. The PoolManager was deployed at block 45,998,366 (binary search with eth_getCode on rpc.purroofgroup.com), so no patch touches it. The patch list cites a hyper-evm-sync commit that could not be fetched in this session (GitHub access refused), so the cause of those divergences is not confirmed. ## Reading of the source (theme-monad-compiled-coverage)

- Monad, cycle 23. Which Monad release the validators and the public endpoint run on 2026-11-26, and whether the harness sources match those releases. No tag v0.16.8, v0.16.9 or v0.17.0 exists. The harness was rebuilt in this cycle's work directory from 791 files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at tags v0.16.5 and v0.16.7, asmjit e8c8e2e4 and evmc f6b7c57e and 34795f4e; every one is byte identical to the cycle 16 copies. The one header that differs is ankerl/unordered_dense.h, taken here from the release's own submodule pin a570a0e8 (version 4.1) where cycle 16 used 5.3.3; it is a hash map header used by address and bytes32 containers, not by the emitter. eth_getCode of the PoolManager at block 125,516,153 equals the build of this checkout with its immutable set to the Monad address (sha256 288b9772...). - Monad, cycle 23. Does the coverage instrumentation change what the compiled PoolManager computes?. Result: No. The patched emitter binds one extra asmjit label at the start of each IR block (a label emits no bytes) and records its address after the code is placed (tools/patch_emitter.py). The harness then sets a one-shot INT3 at every native basic block leader found by disassembling the placed code, and the trap handler restores the byte and resumes at the same address. Every leader decoded as an instruction start and no undecodable instruction was met. The 2,007 mined transactions replayed under instrumentation give the same summary lines as cycle 16 on both releases (2,007 transactions, 55,690 PoolManager frames, every frame and log equal to the block), and the 20,450 cycle 15 scenarios give 0 mismatches as in cycle 16. ## Reading of the source (theme-refund-arithmetic)

- Tempo, cycle 23. Tempo v1.19.1-a9d6748 (the build rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz reported on 2026-11-26): fee charge and refund arithmetic, integer types and casts, and whether a signed, wrapped or truncated value can reach a TIP-20 balance write. Result: The upfront fee is calc_gas_balance_spending(gas_limit, gas_price) = U256(gas_limit u64) saturating_mul U256(gas_price u128), div_ceil 10^12 (primitives transaction/mod.rs:61-65); the gas price is converted with u128::try_from and fails the block on overflow (handler/config.rs:257-258), the base fee with u64::try_from (config.rs:319-320). settle_transaction computes actual_spending the same way from tx_gas_used and takes refund = collected.checked_sub(actual_spending), a fatal error otherwise (config.rs:269-273). The TIP-20 side uses U256 with checked decrement_balance and checked opted-in supply updates (tip20/mod.rs:1525-1552, 1558-1594), and the fee manager refunds from its own custody of that transaction's prepayment (tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:234-273). The one signed value is the i64 refund counter. Tempo maps a negative counter to i64::MAX on purpose (config.rs:260-264) and evm2's final_refund caps it at spent / MaxRefundQuotient (evm2 interpreter/host.rs:70-83). From T7 (timestamp 1,783,605,600, 9 July 2026, constants.rs:233) the quotient is 1 and SstoreClearingSlotRefund is 0 (hardfork gas_params.rs:71-73, 120-132). sstore_refund only goes negative by subtracting the clearing refund (evm2 version/gas_params.rs:344-379), which is now 0; storage-credit refunds are non-negative u64 counts times STORAGE_CREDIT_VALUE with saturating_mul (config.rs:444-487); batch refunds are summed with saturating_add (handler.rs:1306, 1357, 1371); EIP-7702 auth refunds are 0 from T1 (gas_params.rs:109-110). So the counter cannot end negative today, and if it did the result would still be a refund bounded by the payer's own prepayment. No wrapped value reaches a balance write. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs
- Tempo, cycle 23. Tempo: which accounts pay and receive fees and refunds, and whether an ordinary account can make the PoolManager (0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029) the fee payer or make the fee flow touch a TIP-20 balance the PoolManager holds. Result: collect_fee_pre_tx moves max_amount from fee_payer to TIP_FEE_MANAGER_ADDRESS (tip20/mod.rs:1548-1549, tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:158-187), and collect_fee_post_tx refunds from the fee manager to fee_payer and credits the validator ledger (tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:234-273). fee_payer comes from envelope.fee_payer(), a recovered signature (config.rs:279-281, 316-318); a self-sponsored payer signature is refused from T2 (handler.rs:1451-1457). The cycle 23 stablecoin-l1 unit showed that no envelope recovers to an address without a key, and the PoolManager has no key. Both fee moves run outside the call frames: the debit before the first call and the refund after the last (handler.rs:1581-1588 and 1717-1731), so no balanceOf(PoolManager) read between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) can see them. AA batches carry no value (handler.rs:1446-1449). The fee path never names the PoolManager as payer or recipient. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/tip_fee_manager/mod.rs
- Tempo, cycle 23. Tempo T14 (8 December 2026, constants.rs:254): does the release that schedules it change the fee or refund arithmetic?. Result: a9d6748 already carries MAINNET_T14_TIMESTAMP. Its T14 branches in the AA handler change only the warming order and the configurable-account intrinsic gas (handler.rs:1494-1510); settle_transaction and the fee manager have no T14 branch (config.rs:251-305, tip_fee_manager/mod.rs:158-273). Nothing in the refund arithmetic changes at T14. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/evm/src/handler.rs
- Celo, cycle 23. Celo (forno.celo.org reports reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, read as celo-reth v1.0.10 in cycle 22): CIP-64 debit and credit amounts, types and casts, and whether the F-144 wrapped refund can reach a fee-currency balance write in a way that moves funds other than the sender's own prepayment. Result: The debit is gas_limit as u128 checked_mul effective_gas_price, converted to U256 (handler.rs:543-545). The credit runs after the refund step (handler.rs:864-876; refund at 1213-1215), so refunded() is already the capped value: revm's set_final_refund returns min(refunded as u64, gas_used / 5) as i64, which is non-negative. refund_in_erc20 = price saturating_mul (remaining + refunded as u64) as u128, tip and base charge use spent_sub_refunded (handler.rs:327-343). The three parts add up to price times gas_limit, which is what the debit took, so the wrapped refund only moves value between the sender and the fee recipients. The credit pays caller, block beneficiary (or the fee handler when it is zero) and the fee handler (handler.rs:296-304, 354-364). None is the PoolManager unless the sequencer names it as beneficiary, which is an operator action, and the credit runs after execution. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/refs/tags/celo/reth-v1.0.10/crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs
- Celo, cycle 23. Celo mined evidence for the F-144 shape: CIP-64 transactions whose main call transfers the fee token back to the sender, and whether the debit had cleared the sender's slot first. Result: A read-only scan of the 300 blocks up to 83,781,134 (forno, reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb at both ends) found 4,452 CIP-64 transactions; 3,197 of them receive a transfer of the debited token from a third address inside the main call. In a seeded sample of 40 (seed 23023), the sender's balance at the previous block never equalled the debit, so the debit did not clear the slot and the counter could not go negative. No mined example of the wrapped refund was found. forno refuses debug_traceTransaction ('rpc method is not whitelisted'), so the gas used before refunds, and with it the refund applied, cannot be read from that endpoint. Data: research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-refund-arithmetic.work/raw/celo_cip64_scan.json and raw/celo_zero_debit.json. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-refund-arithmetic.work/raw/celo_zero_debit.json
- X Layer, cycle 23. X Layer (reth/v2.3.0-f60420a xlayer/v0.0.7): post_exec_settlement_deltas and gasless transactions, amounts, types and recipients. Result: Read at okx/optimism a492b62, the deps/optimism submodule commit used in cycle 22. The submodule pin of the running build could not be confirmed, because the GitHub API is not available. The post-exec refund is a u64 from the sequencer's payload or the producer's inspector. It is rejected when it exceeds evm_gas_used (block/mod.rs:566-599, 1003-1016). Deltas are U256 saturating_mul of the gas delta by base fee, priority price and effective price (block/mod.rs:702-752). The sender gains with saturating_add, and beneficiary, BASE_FEE_RECIPIENT and the operator vault lose with checked_sub, an underflow failing the block (block/mod.rs:645-679, 754-780). The code comment limits it to forks after Karst. Gasless status comes from a view call to the fixed contract 0x19787404b0c70021b4752028f7e3a92313885B27 returning (bool, uint64); malformed output decodes to not gasless (xlayer_gasless_contract.rs:47-48, 124-165). A gasless transaction only has its price set to zero, so no fee moves. The sender is the transaction signer, and every adjustment is applied after the transaction has run. No PoolManager balance or msg.value is involved. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/optimism/a492b62bbecbdcf3be90719e042c9abca47c8cc6/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs
- Base, cycle 23. Base v1.5.6 (endpoint build) and v1.6.0-rc.1: fee charge, refund and reimbursement, including the EIP-8130 phase loop and payer settlement. Result: v1.5.6 uses revm's post_execution::refund unchanged and pays fees only to the L1, base and operator fee vaults and the beneficiary, with a U256 base fee amount from basefee as u128 saturating_mul gas used (handler.rs:242-320). No pre-execution storage write exists on Base, so the counter cannot end negative there. EIP-8130 settlement clamps a negative counter to zero before the 1/5 cap: u64::try_from(signed_refund.max(0)) (v1.5.6 eip8130.rs:1716-1718; v1.6.0-rc.1 eip8130.rs:1917-1919). The fee, base amount and priority amount use checked_mul and checked_sub, and the payer refund uses prepay.checked_sub(total_cost) and a checked balance add (v1.6.0-rc.1 eip8130.rs:1841-1909). The payer is the sender or the account a payer_auth signature recovers to (eip8130.rs:945). v1.6.0-rc.1 adds gas-limit billing, which spends all gas and sets the refund to 0 (handler.rs:265-313). EIP-8130 is gated on Everest, which has no date (OPCODES.md). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.6.0-rc.1/crates/common/evm/src/eip8130.rs
- MegaETH, cycle 23. MegaETH (mega-reth v2.3.1, mega-evm v1.7.4): storage gas and resource refunds in the fee path. Result: mega-evm delegates reimburse_caller and refund to the op-revm handler (execution.rs:580-592). Storage gas is charged as extra regular gas (execution.rs:759-764, 848-864). The resource refunds in limit/data_size.rs, kv_update.rs and state_growth.rs lower the per-block resource counters and are never added to the gas refund counter. The only gas refund records are in precompiles.rs:322 and the EIP-7702 refund, both non-negative. Fees are native ETH and go to the beneficiary and the three vaults (execution.rs:341-358). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.4/crates/mega-evm/src/evm/execution.rs
- Arc, cycle 23. Arc v0.8.6: fees in native USDC, amount computation and recipient. Result: reward_beneficiary sends U256(effective_gas_price u128) * U256(gas_used u64), at most 192 bits, to the block beneficiary, which takes both the base fee and the tip (handler.rs:85-118). It refuses a self-destructed beneficiary from Zero8. Charging and reimbursing are revm's mainnet steps. The only per-transaction pre-execution action is a blocklist read (handler.rs:65-82), and it writes no storage. The beneficiary is chosen by the validator. Native USDC also has an ERC-20 face, but every fee move happens outside the call frames, so no PoolManager read between sync and settle sees it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/v0.8.6/crates/evm/src/handler.rs
- Monad, cycle 23. Monad 0.16.7: charge on gas limit, the refund counter and the reserve balance rule. Result: execute_final asserts gas_refund >= 0 and gas_left <= gas_limit (execute_transaction.cpp:376-378). With charges_gas_limit, compute_gas_refund returns 0, so the counter is never cast or used (monad_transaction_gas.cpp:22-31) and the sender is billed gas_limit times price. The reward is a uint256 product sent to the beneficiary or the staking contract (execute_transaction.cpp:381-411). dipped_into_reserve skips every account whose code is not an EIP-7702 delegation (reserve_balance.cpp:86-96), so the PoolManager is exempt. A violation reverts the whole transaction, which is atomic for the PoolManager. The only transactions it can revert are those of the account whose own balance fell. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/monad/reserve_balance.cpp
- HyperEVM, cycle 23. HyperEVM (official endpoint 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet', replica nanoreth nb-20261125-2): fee and refund handler. Result: The replica's block executor marks a transaction with gas price 0 as a system transaction and leaves its gas out of the block total (executor.rs:44-49, 261-283). It calls the stock revm transact with no fee or refund hook of its own. Without a pre-execution storage write the counter cannot end negative. The official validator is closed and was not read. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/src/node/evm/executor.rs
- all 21 networks, cycle 23. Whether any of these fee paths changes a value the PoolManager reads inside a call: msg.value, a balance read between sync and settle, or gas forwarded to a hook or a token. Result: All fee debits run before the first call frame and all refunds and credits run after the last. msg.value is the signed transaction value or a call value, and no handler read changes it. Tempo AA batches carry no value. The PoolManager reads balances only inside its own frames (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), so a fee move cannot fall between its sync and settle. Inside the main call, Celo and Tempo price SSTOREs on slots the debit wrote as already written, so gas readings differ from Ethereum. The PoolManager forwards all remaining gas and never branches on a gas value (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, and no gasleft() outside src/test), so no line of src/ computes or decides differently. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-364

## Reading of the source (theme-state-replay)

- Ethereum, cycle 23. Task 1 to 4 on Ethereum: every mined PoolManager transaction of the window re-run through a model of src/ from its prestate and compared word by word with what the chain returned, logged and stored. scripts/model.py rewrites every PoolManager entry point from the text of src/ (PoolManager.sol:103-377, ProtocolFees.sol, ERC6909.sol, ERC6909Claims.sol, Extsload.sol, Exttload.sol, Pool.sol:100-612, Position.sol, TickBitmap.sol, Hooks.sol:131-320) with the pool math of tools/opdiff/v4math.py, and walks the mined call trace frame by frame. It starts persistent storage from the transaction's own prestate (prestateTracer), so tick bitmap words, liquidityNet and fee growth outside are the values at the transaction's position in its block, and starts transient storage empty. It takes from the trace only what the source takes from outside: calldata, msg.sender, msg.value, hook return data and token balanceOf return data. For every PoolManager frame it compares the frame output (swap and modifyLiquidity deltas, feesAccrued, settle amount, unlock result, every extsload and exttload word), every PoolManager log word (Swap, ModifyLiquidity, Donate, Initialize, ERC-6909 Transfer and others), and the deltas the PoolManager wrote into the calldata of afterSwap and afterAdd or afterRemoveLiquidity hooks. At the end it compares every PoolManager storage word in the prestateTracer diff (slot0, liquidity, both fee growth globals, tick words, bitmap words, positions, protocolFeesAccrued, ERC-6909 balances, allowances, operators) and flags any word it wrote that the chain did not, and any word the chain wrote that it did not. A model read of a word that is not in the prestate is also flagged. Result: 20000 transactions replayed (the newest 20000 PoolManager transactions with a log, blocks 26495693 to 26497048, listed from eth_getLogs on https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at 2026-11-26T04:42:15Z; blocks 26495693 to 26497048). 451530 words compared (62673 storage words changed by the chain, plus outputs, logs and hook calldata), 0 mismatches left after explanation. The transactions held 25217 swaps (2944 of more than one step), 768 liquidity changes, 55 donates, 143 initializations, 637 mint or burn of claims and 14 PoolManager frames that reverted and were caught. Native balance: 13217 transactions moved the PoolManager balance, and in all 20000 the change equals native settles minus native takes and fee collection, and equals the traced value frames, to the wei. ERC-20: 30338 currency and transaction pairs compared Transfer flows with settle, take and fee collection; residue explained: 1 interest-bearing token: balanceOf rose 1 or 2 units more than the Transfer amount. Trace endpoints answered: https://eth.api.pocket.network answered Geth/v1.17.9-stable-9dffe6e9/linux-amd64/go1.25.14; https://eth.api.pocket.network answered erigon/3.8.1-cf6f1413/linux-amd64/go1.27.3; https://eth.api.pocket.network answered erigon/3.8.2-8a3f3b2c/linux-amd64/go1.27.2; https://eth.api.pocket.network answered erigon/3.8.2-8a3f3b2c/linux-amd64/go1.27.4; https://eth.api.pocket.network answered reth/v2.10.1-58ebce1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu; https://eth.api.pocket.network answered reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. The traces come from the public replica https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31); the validator is closed and the official endpoint https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm serves no traces. The official endpoint answers eth_getStorageAt with the latest value whatever block is named (raw/999/official-not-archive.json: slot 0x4239...247e is 0 at blocks 51,818,751 to 51,818,753 there and 0x1239bc2b12e04 at 51,818,752 on the replica and on hyperliquid.drpc.org), so a per-block comparison with it is void (raw/committed-999.log, 4,409 differences, all of this kind). Instead the last traced post value of every PoolManager word any transaction of the whole history changed was compared with the official latest state (scripts/latest999.py).
