- Monad, cycle 23. Monad: which code path the traces and the committed state come from, read in the v0.16.7 source that the endpoints report (Monad/0.16.7). Result: Trace requests re-execute from the parent block with the RPC VM, declared as vm::VM vm_{vm::VM::InterpreterOnly} (category/rpc/monad_executor.cpp:1306-1309, used at 1821-1824). Block execution builds vm::VM vm{trace_calls ? InterpreterOnly : Dual} (cmd/monad/main.cpp:485-488), so validators that do not record call traces run compiled native code. Every node asserts that the delayed execution results carried in each consensus header hash to the block headers it computed itself (category/execution/runloop/runloop_monad.cpp:125-155, MONAD_ASSERT at 680-681). So the 20,000 transactions checked against the source above were run by the interpreter, and the committed state they match (1,500 blocks, scripts/committed.py) is accepted by the node only while its own results equal what the validator quorum executed. Whether rpc.monad.xyz itself runs with trace_calls was not confirmed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/runloop/runloop_monad.cpp
- Ethereum, Base, Unichain, cycle 23. ERC-20 residue: wrapped native minted to the PoolManager without a Transfer log. Native is debited and WETH credited by the same amount, and both legs match the source. Counting Deposit and Withdrawal logs as flows (scripts/run.py) leaves no residue. - Unichain, cycle 23. Reading of unlock when the callback returns data whose first word is 0. Result: Two Unichain transactions return 64 bytes from unlockCallback with a head word of 0. abi.decode reads the length at offset 0, which is 0, and unlock returns empty bytes (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The chain did the same. The model first assumed an offset of 32 and was corrected. The other corrections made during the unit were a read of tick liquidity words in the fee growth computation that the source does not make (Pool.sol:493-494 reads only the fee growth words; the prestate showed it) and the counting of wrapped native Deposit and Withdrawal logs. After them every transaction of every window replays. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114

## Reading of the source (theme-failed-tx-replay)

- Ethereum, Base, Unichain, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Polygon, Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM, cycle 24. Task 1 (L-1036): mined transactions with receipt status 0 that entered the PoolManager, inside the cycle 23 replay windows, replayed from their own prestate through the cycle 23 source model (cycle 23 scripts/model.py) with failed frames rolled back as the EVM does, and every failed PoolManager frame classified as a source revert, an out of gas, or unexplained. A source revert here is one the model raises from the replayed state with the same error (PriceLimitAlreadyExceeded, CurrencyNotSettled, PoolNotInitialized), a failed child carried up byte for byte by unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:110) or wrapped in WrappedError naming that child (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-137, src/types/Currency.sol:44-86), or one unlock whose callback returned 0 bytes, which do not ABI-decode as bytes at src/PoolManager.sol:110 (Ethereum 0x473141491726885afa424e614e5c0b53c365f3c4ce0533e97dad225c2d6bdc32); in all 192,815 successful unlocks stored by cycles 23 and 24 the callback return decodes. The out of gas frames are swaps given 4,337 to 221,156 gas and two unlocks that carry an out of gas callback. One Ethereum take is counted as a source revert: its USDC transfer stopped at the EIP-2200 SSTORE sentry inside USDC for lack of gas, and Currency.transfer wrapped that failure (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86). No failed frame is a burn, a modifyLiquidity or a take with a reason other than these. The successful PoolManager frames inside the failed transactions were compared word by word as in cycle 23 (outputs and hook calldata; the tracer clears logs under a failed frame) with no mismatch. The 2 BNB Smart Chain transactions that entered the PoolManager both failed outside it. Each run is bracketed with web3_clientVersion and eth_blockNumber. Result: The official endpoint answers like the revm and reth family on every probe where the families differ. On the eight error probes it returns the reth texts and code -32003 ('EVM error: StackUnderflow', 'EVM error: InvalidJump', 'out of gas: gas required exceeds: 100000', 'EVM error: InvalidFEOpcode', 'EVM error: OpcodeNotFound'), the same strings as f0cad31 and reth v2.11.0, where both geth builds say 'stack underflow (0 <=> 2)', 'invalid jump destination', 'out of gas' and 'invalid opcode: INVALID' with code -32000. It equals f0cad31 on all 30 probes that do not depend on the moment of the call, including eth_estimateGas results that no Ethereum client gives (0x536a, 0x535e and 0x1185a, where reth v2.11.0 says 0x5448, 0x542a, 0x11670 and geth 0x5448, 0x542a, 0x116f5), the same rejection text for an override with both state and stateDiff, and ECRECOVER priced at 15,000 gas (gas difference 0x3b19 against 0xc39 on Ethereum), which is nanoreth's HlSpecId::V2 multiplied precompile price. Opcode results, cold and warm access gas (0xef036, 0xee7fb, 0xee790, 0xedd50, 0xed321 everywhere), failed precompiles that consume all forwarded gas, and the absence of Prague and Osaka precompiles 0x0b and 0x100 also agree. The nine probes that differ all describe the call context: the official endpoint runs eth_call in a block numbered latest plus one with the parent's timestamp and hash chain (BLOCKHASH(NUMBER-1) equals the hash of the latest block on both endpoints), a gas limit of 30,000,000, ignores the block argument (an old number, a block hash, 'pending' and a nonexistent hash all give the latest-plus-one context), and returns a live HyperCore oracle value from 0x807 (0x93fda) where f0cad31 forwards an unrecorded call and returns 0x93fe4 and b92ad36 halts out of gas. So official eth_call runs revm, behind reth's RPC types, inside a process that holds live HyperCore state. The node README states that the same hl-node binary runs run-validator and run-non-validator and that --serve-eth-rpc serves this RPC; whether the RPC path calls the same execution code that builds blocks cannot be seen from outside, and the hl-node binary itself was not obtainable (binaries.hyperliquid.xyz/Mainnet/hl-node answered HTTP 403). None of the context differences reaches src/: the PoolManager reads no NUMBER, TIMESTAMP, BLOCKHASH, BASEFEE, PREVRANDAO or GASPRICE and calls no precompile; its only gas reads are the forwarded gas of three calls. - Zora, cycle 24. L-1044 Task 2 on Zora: replay of mined PoolManager transactions from parent-block storage, because no public endpoint serves traces for this window. Method: scripts/gdrive.py runs each transaction whole in the reference interpreter scripts/pyevm_tx24.py through scripts/lazyreplay24.py, reading every account, code, balance, nonce and storage word lazily from the parent block (eth_getCode, eth_getBalance, eth_getTransactionCount, eth_getStorageAt). It compares status, every receipt log in order, every PoolManager storage word read or written against eth_getStorageAt at the block when no later transaction of the block emits a PoolManager log, and the PoolManager native balance change when the transaction is the only one of the block with a PoolManager log. A transaction whose status, PoolManager logs, PoolManager words or native balance differ is run again after every earlier transaction of its block on the same state (up to 120 earlier transactions). Gas is not modelled, so ERC-4337 EntryPoint events that report gas cost differ by design. Result: 2000 transactions replayed from parent-block storage on https://rpc.zora.energy (window lwindow.json: newest PoolManager transactions with a log, newest first, blocks 44906432 to 54490122). Outcome: 1861 match; 100 match after block prefix; 39 PoolManager status, logs, words and balance equal, only logs of other contracts differ (emitters of the differing logs, by first bytes of the address: 0x5ff137d4 39; 0x00000000 is EntryPoint v0.7 0x0000000071727De2..., 0x5ff137d4 is EntryPoint v0.6, 0x4337084d is EntryPoint v0.8, whose UserOperationEvent carries gas figures the reference does not model; the others are contracts whose state an earlier transaction of the block changed). No transaction differs in a PoolManager log, status, PoolManager storage word or native balance. Compared: 13085 receipt logs (2186 of them PoolManager logs), 11542 PoolManager storage words in 1889 transactions after which no later transaction of the block touches the PoolManager, and the native balance change in 1802 transactions (1179 moved the PoolManager balance). The run executed 6 CREATE or CREATE2, 31 P256VERIFY calls and 0 NativeCoinAuthority mints. Builds that answered: https://rpc.zora.energy answered conduit-op-reth/v2.5.1-8f0ccac/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. The whole Zora history holds 15873 PoolManager transactions with a log (eth_getLogs from block 0 to 54497955); the replay covers the newest 2,000 of them, because one parent-storage replay takes several seconds of CPU and this unit ran on four cores. Zora: rpc.zora.energy needs an API key for debug and trace methods (HTTP 401), zora.drpc.org and the thirdweb endpoint refuse or rate limit, and no other public trace endpoint was found. Evidence: cycles/024/theme-replay-eleven.work/raw/7777777/lazy_*.jsonl; src/PoolManager.sol:104

## Reading of the source (theme-storage-key-mapping)

- all 21 networks, cycle 24. Task 4: at the real PoolManager address of each network, one eth_call (no transaction) runs a probe through unlock. Inside the callback the probe calls mint(Q, 0x1234, 5), sync on a stub token that reports a balance of 0x77, then exttload and extsload of the same 20 indexes, then burn(Q, 0x1234, 5), so the unlock settles. A stateDiff override first writes a distinct marker into the persistent slot of every index except the ERC-6909 balance of Q and slots 0 and 6. The indexes are the five transient slots the PoolManager writes (IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT, NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT, CURRENCY_SLOT, RESERVES_OF_SLOT, the delta slot keccak(Q, 0x1234)), the balance slot balanceOf[Q][0x1234], a pool state slot keccak(id, 6) and its +6 word, slots 0 and 6, and each of these with bit 248 flipped. Can a persistent and a transient slot with one index share an entry, and does any network fold a pair of these real PoolManager keys?. Result: No transient fold and no persistent fold outside Avalanche. On 20 networks every read equals the Ethereum answer: exttload returns 1, 1, the stub token, 0x77 and -5 for the five transient slots and zero for their bit 248 partners, while extsload of the same indexes returns the persistent markers, and extsload of the balance slot returns 5 from the mint inside the same call. So a TSTORE at an index leaves the persistent slot of that index untouched and the reverse, on every network, including during an unlock. On Avalanche the transient reads are also exact, and every persistent pair reads one shared value, which is the F-040 rule acting on real PoolManager keys: the two overrides of a pair land on one entry, the override of slot 0 with bit 248 set replaced the owner word, and the mint of 5 to balanceOf[Q][0x1234] (whose index has bit 248 set) was added to the marker written for the partner index with bit 248 clear. The persistent and transient key spaces stay separate there too. The client version was read before and after each call; the build strings are in the output file. The source lines this rests on are src/libraries/Lock.sol:8-26, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:8-32, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:13-36, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:11-39, src/Extsload.sol:10-15 and src/Exttload.sol:10-15. - Ethereum, cycle 24. Task 1 for reth v2.11.0, the build the Ethereum endpoint reports (reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc), which runs on evm2 at rev 66687c18. How is (address, slot) keyed in the EVM state, the transient map, the execution cache, the txpool prewarm snapshot and the reuse of speculative results?. Result: Every map is keyed by the full address and the full 256 bit slot. evm2's StorageKey is a 52 byte repr(C) struct of the address and the slot, and equality compares all 52 bytes (crates/evm2/src/storage_key.rs lines 12-56). Transient storage is a separate map of that key (crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs lines 58-59, 799-812) and persistent slots sit in per-account maps keyed by the slot word (lines 653-690). The execution cache keys storage by (Address, StorageKey) in fixed-cache 0.1.10 (cached_state.rs lines 967-968, 1063-1100); the crate's get compares the full key with key.equivalent and treats any other occupant of the bucket as a miss, and a colliding insert replaces the entry (fixed-cache lib.rs lines 316-350, 386-440; crate checksum 2fe63500 matches the lock file). The txpool snapshot looks up the full address and U256::from_be_bytes of the full slot, per parent hash (txpool.rs lines 13-38). The reuse of speculative results commits a prewarm result only when every recorded (address, slot) read still equals the current value and every account read matches, with balance differences allowed only where the transaction did not observe the balance and both balances are nonzero (reuse.rs lines 284-342, 367-401). No key is truncated, hashed down or reused across transactions. - Avalanche, cycle 24. Task 1 for avalanchego 1.15.3 (commit 983815fd, libevm d398bc4dbe41): is there a second key rule next to the bit 248 fold of F-040, and does any rule cross accounts or reach transient storage?. Result: There is one rule. libevm's StateDBHooks interface has a single method, TransformStateKey (core/state/statedb.libevm.go lines 41-53), applied in GetState, GetCommittedState and SetState (core/state/statedb.go lines 349, 359, 422). The C-Chain hook clears bit 0 of byte 0 and ignores the address (vms/saevm/cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go, partitionStateKeysHook). The only other variant is the skip option, used for asset balances and for GetCommittedState before Apricot Phase 1, which is history. The rule maps a key of an account into the same account, so a write by one contract cannot reach the PoolManager's storage. Firewood was not read; the transform sits above the state store, so a store behind it receives keys that are already folded. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/983815fd993acf846a27749b598f0fea4d876a75/vms/saevm/cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/d398bc4dbe41/core/state/statedb.libevm.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/d398bc4dbe41/core/state/statedb.go
- Avalanche, cycle 24. Task 3 for the Avalanche fold: can an ordinary account make a PoolManager write land on, or a PoolManager read return, another user's entry?. Result: No. The PoolManager writes only fixed slots 0 to 6 (src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:11 and the declarations in src/ProtocolFees.sol, src/ERC6909.sol, src/PoolManager.sol), keccak256 outputs of mapping keys (src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:66-73, src/ERC6909.sol balance and allowance mappings, src/libraries/Position.sol:34-62) and such outputs plus an offset of at most 6 (src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:324-347). Under the fold two of these collide only if they agree in 255 bits. An account that picks pool ids, owners, ticks and salts to aim one of its own slots at one fixed victim slot needs about 2^255 tries; two slots it controls both are useless to it. A fixed slot S with bit 248 set is 2^248 + S, and a keccak output equal to it is a preimage search of the same size. Adding an offset of at most 6 changes bit 248 only if the lower 248 bits of the hash are within 6 of 2^248, which has probability about 2^-245. No PoolManager function writes a caller-chosen index; extsload and exttload only read (src/Extsload.sol:10-15, src/Exttload.sol:10-15). The live test shows half of the keccak slots used (the balance slot 0x8f57 for instance) already live at their folded index on chain, which is harmless because every access to them goes through the same rule. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/024/theme-storage-key-mapping.work/out/pmkeys.json ; src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:324-347 ; src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91
- Monad, cycle 24. Task 1 for Monad v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 (the endpoint reports Monad/0.16.7): TrieDb key encoding, the page encoding of storage, the account and storage cache, and the per-transaction state of parallel execution. Result: No two (address, slot) pairs share an entry. With the monad state machine the TrieDb is page encoded: the trie path is keccak(address) then keccak(page key), the page key is the slot shifted right by 7 and the offset in the page is the low 7 bits (category/execution/monad/db/storage_page.hpp lines 41-44, 173-191; trie_db.cpp lines 87, 134-194; db.hpp lines 84-87). Page key and offset together give back the whole slot (compute_slot_key), so the split is one to one. The storage cache key is the 20 byte address, the incarnation and the 32 byte page key, compared with memcmp over all bytes (storage_key.hpp; bytes_hash_compare.hpp lines 31-44; db_cache.hpp lines 50-64, 102-160). In execution, persistent and transient storage are two separate immer maps keyed by the full bytes32 slot of one account state (account_state.hpp lines 52-70, 126-153), and the native runtime passes the full 32 byte key and the recipient address to the host (category/vm/runtime/storage.cpp lines 37-110). trie_db.cpp differs between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 only in include comments, and state.cpp and block_state.cpp are identical. The runtime's sha3 hashes the memory range directly with no cache (category/vm/runtime/keccak.hpp). The bucket is a 64 bit hash of the plain key modulo the bucket count (salt/src/state/hasher.rs lines 40-43), so many keys share a bucket, but every lookup compares the stored plain key with the whole requested key (salt/src/state/state.rs lines 833-840 and 993-1000). ## Reading of the source (theme-avalanche-sae)

- Avalanche, cycle 25. Task 1: which state eth_call, eth_getStorageAt, eth_getBalance and debug_traceCall run against for each block tag under the SAE backend of avalanchego 1.15.3 (commit 983815fd, libevm d398bc4dbe41). Result: latest resolves to the last executed block, not the last accepted one (blocks/access.go:133-134). safe and finalized resolve to the last settled block (blocks/access.go:135-136). pending resolves to the last accepted block only when api-resolve-pending-to-last-executed is false; the C-Chain default is true (cchain/config.go:138, blocks/access.go:125-127), and a node with it false refuses state for pending (sae/rpc/stateful.go:79-83). An explicit number is accepted up to the last accepted block and refused above it (blocks/access.go:139-146). Every state method then opens the post-execution root of the resolved block through restoreExecutedBlock, which waits for execution of an accepted block (sae/rpc/blocks.go:59-86, WaitUntilExecuted at line 82), and the header handed to the EVM is rewritten to carry that post-execution root and the executed base fee (sae/rpc/stateful.go:537-542). debug_traceCall uses the same post-execution state (traceCallBackend, sae/rpc/stateful.go:578-580). So no tag names a block whose state does not exist: latest is executed by construction, and a number between latest and the accepted tip blocks until it is executed. The cycle 24 statement that latest is the last accepted block is corrected by this reading; the eth_call results of earlier cycles at latest ran on executed post-state with the same interpreter configuration (vm.Config{}) as block execution (saexec/execution.go:360). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/blocks/access.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/sae/rpc/stateful.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/sae/rpc/blocks.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/config.go

- Avalanche, cycle 25. Task 2: which checks a transaction passes at acceptance and which run only at execution, and every way a transaction of an accepted block can end differently from what the builder assumed. Result: At building and at verification (VerifyBlock rebuilds the block and compares hashes, sae/blocks.go:59-98) worstcase.ApplyTx runs txpool.ValidateTransaction against the worst-case header (legacy, 2930 and 1559 types only, so no EIP-7702 delegation can appear, worstcase/state.go:181-195), refuses senders with code (lines 207-209), checks exact nonce, fee cap against the worst-case base fee, block gas left, and balance for gasLimit times the worst-case price plus value, on the settled state minus every earlier debit of the unsettled blocks (lines 239-322, sae/block_builder.go:181-235). At execution saexec.Execute applies every transaction of the block in order with core.ApplyTransaction on the state left by the previous one (saexec/execution.go:346-364). An error that is not a revert is fatal and stops the node (lines 362-364, 97-103); nothing is skipped and nothing is reordered. The libevm checks that run only at execution are CanExecuteTransaction, which returns nil on the C-Chain (cchain/hooks.go:245-247), and InvalidateExecution, which no code in avalanchego 1.15.3 calls (search of the whole tree). The only values that differ from the header are BASEFEE and the effective GASPRICE: the header carries the worst-case base fee (ACP-194 baseFeePerGas rule) and execution uses the gas clock base fee, which is at most that (saexec/execution.go:325-332). Gas charged is max(gasUsed, ceil(gasLimit/2)) after execution (hook/hook.go:218-221); this does not change the GAS opcode or what any call returns. A transaction that reverts rolls back all of its PoolManager writes as on Ethereum, and transient storage is replaced per transaction by StateDB.Prepare (libevm core/state_transition.go:436, core/state/statedb.go:1335). So the PoolManager cannot be left with an unlock half applied (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25), with transient storage from an earlier transaction, or with a native payout made and the rest of the transaction dropped (src/types/Currency.sol:48). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/worstcase/state.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/saexec/execution.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/sae/blocks.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/hooks.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/hook/hook.go; https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/ava-labs/libevm/@v/v1.13.15-0.20261028200218-d398bc4dbe41.zip (core/state_transition.go, core/state/statedb.go, core/state_transition.libevm.go); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avalanche-foundation/ACPs/main/ACPs/194-continuous-execution/README.md

Result: NUMBER and TIMESTAMP equal the header; BLOCKHASH(NUMBER-1) equals the header parentHash in all 8 blocks; COINBASE is 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000000; PREVRANDAO and BLOBBASEFEE are 1; BASEFEE is 0x1bf08eb00 (7.5 gwei) when a gas price is given and 0 without one, as in go-ethereum. Receipt effectiveGasPrice equals 7.5 gwei plus the tip in every sampled transaction, so the executed base fee equals the header base fee at present. The executor sets the block context from the same header (saexec/execution.go:332-341) and BLOCKHASH from recent consensus headers (saexec/context.go:26-40). The PoolManager reads none of these (ASSUMPTIONS A10); it reads SELFBALANCE and GAS (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 73, 92; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), whose semantics the SAE path does not change. Evidence: raw/probe_ctx.json (eth_call, eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_getTransactionReceipt on https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc and https://avax.api.pocket.network); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/saexec/context.go
- Avalanche, cycle 25. Task 3: can an ordinary account use the gap between acceptance and execution against another user, and how receipts and logs are served for accepted blocks not yet executed. Result: Receipts exist only after execution: RecentReceipt blocks until the transaction has executed (saexec/receipts.go:48-73), getReceipts goes through restoreExecutedBlock and returns nothing for an unexecuted block (sae/rpc/receipts.go:28-41), logs are read from the database written at MarkExecuted (sae/rpc/receipts.go:77-79, blocks/execution.go:142), and the log filter backend treats any header above the last executed block as absent and resolves latest through the same rule (sae/rpc/filters.go:34-35, 121-127). Execution is deterministic and the order is fixed at acceptance, so a receipt served at latest is what every honest node computes; settlement (safe) about five seconds later records the agreed state root (ACP-194, blocks/access.go:110-123). An attacker cannot place a transaction ahead of one already accepted, and a victim transaction priced against latest executes on latest plus at most the accepted blocks ahead of it, which is the same exposure as pending transactions on Ethereum and is bounded by the victim router slippage limit. No path lets an ordinary account take or freeze another user funds through the gap. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/saexec/receipts.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/sae/rpc/receipts.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/sae/rpc/filters.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/blocks/execution.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avalanche-foundation/ACPs/main/ACPs/194-continuous-execution/README.md

The state scheme defaults to the empty string (cchain/config.go:85, not set in defaultConfig at 127-139), and the empty scheme selects HashDB (saedb/tracker.go:121-126). When Firewood is chosen, its storage key is keccak256(address) followed by keccak256 of the full 32-byte slot as handed down by the StateDB (firewood/base_trie.go:18-33), the same path an MPT uses; the slot it receives is already the output of the bit 248 transform (cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go:47-56). Firewood therefore adds no fold of its own. Validators must agree on the settled state root in every header (ACP-194 block settlement), so a store that keyed differently would fork the node away. No public endpoint states which scheme it runs. - Monad, cycle 25. Task 3 for Monad: which release the testnet validators run and whether they compile contracts under the mainnet rule. Result: Monad's testnet page names v0.16.7 and revision MONAD_TEN; the mainnet page names v0.16.5 and MONAD_TEN. Both public RPCs answer Monad/0.16.7. category/vm/vm.cpp is byte-identical at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 (sha256 cd311187...04da), and vm.hpp differs only by a new mode() accessor. The compile rule in VM::execute_raw does not read the chain: compiled code runs when present and built for the current revision, a cold cache compiles at once, and otherwise the code is compiled asynchronously once the interpreter gas spent on it reaches max_code_size(max_code_size_offset, code size). The default mode is Dual (vm.hpp: explicit VM(Mode mode = Dual)). So a testnet validator in the default mode compiles the PoolManager build under the mainnet rule. Which mode and release each testnet and mainnet validator runs is not public. The testnet PoolManagers saw 64 swaps in their whole searched history, so they add almost nothing. - Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 25. Task 1 for reth v2.11.0 (Ethereum endpoint as recorded in cycle 24) and Tempo's pinned reth rev 167933d (reth-engine-tree 2.11.0 in Tempo's Cargo.lock). Where the commit-without-rerun path is, what it records, how it validates, and whether producers use it. Result: The path is PrewarmResults::take_valid in payload_processor/reuse.rs. The Tempo rev differs from the v2.11.0 tag only in test attributes. The read set holds every storage word loaded from the database with its value (RecordingDb::get_storage, lines 917-937), every account loaded with nonce, balance and code hash but not the code bytes (get_account, lines 882-900; without_code, 945-949), a flag that rejects the result when code was loaded by a hash the database does not know (902-915, 460), and the block environment fields COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, PREVRANDAO and GASLIMIT (1027-1049). Block hashes and transient storage are not recorded: block hashes are fixed by the parent, and transient storage is not a database input. Before commit, every storage read must equal the current value (validate, 285-290) and every account must be identical, except that a balance may differ when the transaction did not observe it, both balances are nonzero and below 2^128, and the account was not created, destroyed or wiped (compare, 375-402; 305-307). BALANCE, SELFBALANCE, SELFDESTRUCT and an out-of-funds call make a balance exact (61-71, 1027-1055, 1070-1078). A value send records the smallest balance left, which becomes an AtLeast bound (1001-1019, 484-496). The path runs only in engine validation of received blocks (ConfigureEvm::reuses_prewarm_results doc, reth crates/evm/evm/src/lib.rs lines 669-686). It needs the flag --engine.prewarm-reuse, which defaults to false (crates/node/core/src/args/engine.rs lines 570-577; TreeConfig default prewarm_reuse false, crates/engine/primitives/src/config.rs lines 286, 376). Ethereum's EthEvmConfig opts in (crates/ethereum/evm/src/lib.rs lines 489-493). TempoEvmConfig's ConfigureEvm impl (tempo crates/evm/src/lib.rs line 224) does not override the default of false, so a Tempo node never reuses through this path, whatever the flag says. A wrong reuse during validation could only make a node reject a correct block, because the header's state root is checked. It cannot make a wrong state canonical. - Tempo, cycle 25. Tempo v1.19.1 block producer (payload builder): does it commit a speculative result without running the transaction again?. Result: It can, under narrow conditions. With prewarming on (the default) and the hidden flag --builder.parallel (default false; the node warns that it 'is still in development and should not be used', crates/node/src/node.rs lines 131-133, 172, 194-201, 1054-1072), the builder commits a recorded replay through execute_transaction_with_actions (crates/payload/builder/src/lib.rs lines 653-668). Replays are made only for transactions that is_parallel_candidate accepts: TIP-1045 payment-lane transactions with a nonzero nonce key (crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs lines 177-178, 497-508). A payment-lane transaction must call a TIP-20 token or the TIP-20 channel reserve with payment calldata (crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs lines 299-312, 622-637). No call to the PoolManager can qualify. Replay checks every recorded account (lines 96-111 of crates/evm/src/action_replay.rs), rechecks exact SLOADs, and applies balance changes as Sinc and Sdec deltas on the current value with overflow and underflow checks (lines 123-170). A reverted transaction is not replayed (lines 45-48). So a TIP-20 transfer to the PoolManager committed by replay in transaction A credits the exact delta. Transaction B's sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) then run normally on the committed state. With the default flags every pool transaction runs normally (lines 474-489, 93, 113-120 of prewarming.rs return without_replay when not parallel). Tempo validators have no reuse path (previous item). - Monad, cycle 25. Monad v0.16.7 optimistic execution and merge: read set, validation before merge, and whether producer and validator share it. Result: Every transaction runs against the block state up to that point. After the previous transaction is done, it is merged only if BlockState::can_merge accepts its originals; otherwise it runs again and must merge (execute_transaction.cpp lines 456-497). Validators run the same code, so this one path decides the canonical state. can_merge compares every original storage word with the block's current word, and a word the block state has not seen must be zero (block_state.cpp lines 156-192). An account that differs passes only through try_fix_account_mismatch (state.cpp lines 650-710). That function refuses when either side is dead, or the code hash, incarnation or nonce differ, or relaxed validation is off, or the balance was read exactly, or the new balance is below the recorded minimum. Otherwise it shifts the current balance by the difference. Every balance read through the host sets validate_exact_balance (evmc_host.cpp line 87 calls State::get_balance, state.cpp lines 233-241). A debit records a minimum or exact balance (state.cpp line 712 onward). Original values for SSTORE gas are the recorded originals. Transient storage belongs to the per-transaction State object. Code is keyed by the code hash that is compared. Every PoolManager input listed in the task is in this read set. On error the node falls back to the serial result (core/blockchain.go lines 1308-1420). The block producer (miner/worker.go) has no parallel or BlockSTM path, so Polygon blocks are produced serially. - all 21 networks, cycle 25. Task 2: the PoolManager inputs that a speculative result could get wrong. These are its own native balance, a token balance changed earlier in the block, transient storage, hook code created earlier in the block, and original slot values for SSTORE gas. Result: The PoolManager never reads its own native balance. Currency.balanceOfSelf with address zero (src/types/Currency.sol:90-92) is reachable only from sync and settle, and both take the native branch first: sync resets the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283) and settle uses msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). Native take sends value with CALL (src/types/Currency.sol:45-49). A send with too little balance fails, and both reth and Monad record such a send as a minimum or exact balance. Case by case for reth v2.11.0. (a) Native transfer in A, then native settle or take in B: the balance is unobserved and B's changes are applied as a delta on the current balance (reuse.rs lines 296-321), and a take is bounded by AtLeast. (b) Token transfer in A, then sync and settle in B: balanceOf reads token storage, which is compared exactly (285-290). (c) Initialize in A, then swap in B: slot0 and the pool words are storage, compared exactly. (d) Hook deployed in A and called in B: B's account read of the hook changes from None to Some and gives Differs (376-379), or the code hash comes from A's published prediction and is compared. Unknown code is rejected (902-915). (e) ERC-6909 mint in A, then burn in B: storage. (f) A reverts after a successful speculative run: B is validated against the state that block execution actually committed (take_valid reads the executor's database, 223-247), and a replaced prediction is retracted (179-187). (g) SSTORE gas and refunds: the first SSTORE of a word loads it through get_storage, so the original value is a recorded read. Transient storage (src/libraries/Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol) is per transaction in evm2 (cycle 24, evm2 state/mod.rs lines 799-812) and is not an input across transactions. Monad answers each case the same way through can_merge, with exact storage and code hash and an exact observed balance. No input of a PoolManager transaction falls outside these read sets. Task 3: does Arc's consensus vote before the execution result is checked, in arc-node main and in what v0.9.0 announces, and what each tag resolves to on rpc.mainnet.arc.io and arc.drpc.org. Result: In arc-node main a validator that receives a full proposal calls the engine newPayload and sets the block validity from the VALID or INVALID answer before it hands the proposed value to Malachite (crates/malachite-app/src/handlers/received_proposal_part.rs:368-410, crates/malachite-app/src/payload.rs:234-307 and 319-361), so execution is checked before the prevote. The decided block is made canonical by forkchoiceUpdated after the decision (crates/malachite-app/src/finalize.rs:89-119), and the IPC engine sets head, safe and finalized to the same hash (crates/eth-engine/src/ipc/engine_ipc.rs:98-109). v0.9.0 is announced only as the removal of the HTTP transport between the two layers in favour of IPC (CHANGELOG v0.8.0, docs.arc.io run-an-arc-node); nothing announced changes when execution is checked. On chain latest, safe and finalized were equal in every snapshot on both endpoints and 700 blocks read at latest kept their hash. The endpoints run unpublished commits (arc/v1), so the reading applies to the public branch. - Tempo, cycle 26. L-1100: with --builder.parallel or the T15 test is_payment_v3, can a replayed action reach a contract other than a TIP-20 token or the channel reserve, for example a TIP-20 transfer to the PoolManager followed by settle. Result: A transaction is a replay candidate only if it is a payment (is_payment_v2 today, is_payment_v3 after T15) and uses a nonzero 2D or expiring nonce (crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs:497-506). Both payment rules require every call to target a TIP-20 address (0x20c0 prefix) with a recognised payment selector or the channel reserve, and forbid access lists and authorization lists (crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs:282-330, 622-637); v3 only adds trailing bytes and voucher signatures. A TIP-20 transfer whose recipient is the PoolManager is a candidate, but a TIP-20 transfer is a precompile write and runs no code at the recipient, so no PoolManager code runs in the replay. The PoolManager's settle in the next transaction is not a payment and always runs serially (crates/payload/builder/src/lib.rs:653-668), reading the token balance the replay wrote. A replay that no longer applies is skipped as invalid_replay (lib.rs:713-731). Replay exists only in the block builder; other validators execute the block through newPayload, so a replay that diverged from serial execution gives a state root they reject and the block is not finalized. Parallel building is off unless the operator enables it (lib.rs:153-154). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/payload/builder/src/lib.rs

- all 21 networks, cycle 26. Task 5: does anything in src/ depend on finality, including ERC-6909 claims and protocol fee accrual. Result: No. unlock opens the lock, runs the callback and reverts unless the nonzero delta count is zero before it locks again (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114); take, settle, settleFor, clear, mint and burn all require the lock and only move transient deltas besides the transfer or claim write (src/PoolManager.sol:291-336, 349-364). The lock, deltas, delta count and synced reserves live in transient storage (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32), so nothing carries between transactions. sync may run without the lock but only writes transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). ERC-6909 transfer, transferFrom, approve and setOperator are plain storage writes (src/ERC6909.sol:25-64). Protocol fees accrue in persistent storage within the same swap transaction (src/ProtocolFees.sol:66-70) and are withdrawn only by the controller (lines 44-57). No file in src/ outside src/test reads block.number, block.timestamp, blockhash, tx.origin or any other block field (search of src/). A replaced block removes every PoolManager effect of its transactions together, so core has no state that a later block can see half applied. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114; src/PoolManager.sol:279-364; src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-70; src/ERC6909.sol:25-64; src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25; src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32
- Tempo, cycle 26. Task 1: what happens to a notarized block whose execution turns out wrong under T14. Result: It is not finalized. A validator whose certify returns false broadcasts nullify for that view and does not build on the block; a finalization needs a quorum of certify results (commonware-consensus 2026.11.0 simplex/mod.rs:106-111, 138-140). The chain does not halt on one bad block: the view is nullified and the next leader proposes on a certified parent. Validators that cannot complete verification withhold their finalize vote and count as faulty for that view (marshal/standard/deferred.rs:33-37). No slashing of the proposer was found in the files read. The executor treats an INVALID answer as the verdict and caches it (crates/consensus/src/executor/actor.rs:64-80). Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/commonware-consensus/commonware-consensus-2026.11.0.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/consensus/src/executor/actor.rs

- Avalanche, HyperEVM, Polygon, cycle 26. Which precompile addresses answer a value call with empty input differently from Ethereum (Prague and Osaka rules: 0x09 to 0x11 fail on empty input, EIP-2537 says an error burns all gas supplied). Result: On Avalanche and HyperEVM the addresses 0x0b to 0x11 accept the payout, so they hold no BLS12-381 precompile at the endpoint's fork, and a native take there leaves the caller's own value at that address. The call to 0x100 with empty input succeeds on these two and on Ethereum alike (checked on reth v2.11.0 and on eth.drpc.org on 2026-11-26), so it says nothing about a P-256 precompile. On Polygon 0x0a accepts the payout on the drpc gateway and on polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), so bor has no point evaluation precompile there. On api.avax.network 0x0a fails with invalid input length and 0x0b accepts. On every other network these addresses fail as on Ethereum. The PoolManager neither calls precompiles itself nor reads their answers apart from the success flag of a payout the caller chose. Evidence: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2537 and eth_call results in research/network-risk/cycles/026/theme-hook-and-native-sides.work/out/single/chain-43114.json, chain-999.json, chain-137.json

The same PoolManager call sent alone (initialize with an afterInitialize hook that returns 1 to 31 bytes) gives InvalidHookResponse in both engines, a rebuild of the harness that only records each call's result after it returns makes 10 of the 13 agree and leaves 3 others different, and zeroing or filling the native stack changes nothing. A result that moves with host-side bookkeeping points at the harness's host process, not at Monad's EVM semantics. The root cause was not found; it is a lead. - Monad, cycle 26. Task 3, effect 1: the interpreter side of the cycle 25 harness gave different results for one scenario when the world held 3,066 token accounts (rep1369.txt). Rerun here: the scenario five times in one process with the large world gives five different top level gasleft values on each engine (for example 149823397 interpreted and 149808185 native on the first repetition), the same sequence in two processes, while the small world gives 149618850 on both engines in every repetition. Only the driver's top level gas differs; every step line, storage word, balance and log is the same. Result: The cause is the harness host. Host::call copies the whole World before each call and assigns the copy back when the call fails (research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/src/harness.cpp:413, 424). libstdc++ map assignment destroys and rebuilds each node, so the code vector of every contract is freed and allocated again. The calling frame still runs with runtime::Context::env.code pointing at the old code buffer (research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/src/harness.cpp:236, 244). Valgrind reports 50 contexts of invalid reads in copy_impl called from CODECOPY, all inside the freed 9,537 byte block that holds the driver contract, from the interpreter and from native code. What CODECOPY reads then depends on how the allocator reused the freed block, which the 3,066 token entries copied on every call change. Controls: under valgrind, which never reuses a freed block at once, the large world gives 149618850 on both engines in all five repetitions (SAME); with MALLOC_PERTURB_=165 or 90 the small world varies too. The PoolManager runtime has no CODECOPY (scan of build/PoolManager.json), so no PoolManager code was read from freed memory. In the node, Context::from takes the code span from the Intercode, which a shared pointer keeps alive for the whole call (vm.cpp:83-84, code.hpp:36-62), and a revert does not free it. This is not Monad code and a validator cannot hit it. - Monad, cycle 26. Task 4, places where the interpreter and native code of v0.16.5 could differ by design. Native code subtracts a block's whole static gas on entry (x86.cpp:443-448) and tests the sign only at JUMPDEST blocks or after 1,000 gas of unchecked static work (emitter.cpp:1030-1046, 1284-1298, emitter.hpp:51). Stack bounds are tested once per block in block_prologue (emitter.cpp:1301-1333). Runtime routines add the remaining block base gas back before the CALL 63/64 rule and the SSTORE sentry (call.cpp:136-147, storage.cpp:70-73), and the depth limit and memory expansion are runtime code shared by both engines (call.cpp:152-154, types.hpp:330-341). copy_result_data turns a negative gas_remaining at STOP, RETURN or REVERT into out of gas (context.cpp:174-176). Result: When a frame cannot pay a block, both engines fail the frame with all gas consumed; native code may fail earlier inside the block, or at the next check up to 1,000 gas later, and reports Error where the interpreter reports out of gas, which a caller sees only as failure. The static cost of a block is paid by the interpreter before it leaves the block, and dynamic costs are computed by the same runtime, so a block that fails on one engine fails on the other. In the PoolManager build there are 917 blocks by Monad's splitting rule (cycle 23 counted 913 entered or reachable); 49 of them hold 64 instructions with an effect outside the frame (39 SSTORE, 8 TSTORE, 12 LOG, 4 CALL, 1 STATICCALL) followed by more instructions of the same block. Every block with static gas has its out of gas test moved to its start. In those 49 blocks, an out of gas run lists an outgoing call or a write on the interpreter side that native code never makes. The failing frame is reverted on both sides, so no PoolManager storage word, transient word, balance, log or outgoing call that persists can differ, which matches the 20 cycle 23 runs whose frame lists differed with equal state. These files were read at v0.16.5; mainnet runs 0.16.7, and the reread at that tag is an open lead. ## Reading of the source (theme-stateful-interpreter)

- Polygon, cycle 26. Task 4: bor's MULMOD memo at the newest tag that has it (v2.12.0-beta) and on develop, which is the only ref that carries Salvador (SalvadorBlock 98688600 at params/config.go:478 on develop; v2.12.0-beta has no Salvador entry; tags v2.12.0, v2.12.0-beta2, v2.12.0-beta3, v2.12.0-rc1, v2.12.1 and v2.11.3 return 404). Exact reuse condition and proof that a reused reciprocal belongs to the same full 256 bit modulus. Result: core/vm/mulmod_memo.go is byte identical on v2.12.0-beta and develop, and so are core/vm/evm.go, instructions.go and interpreter.go. opMulmod pops x and y by value and passes z = the stack top (instructions.go:200-205). An entry is reused only when z[3] != 0 and mm.ok and mm.mod == *z (mulmod_memo.go:56-57), where mm.mod is a uint256.Int, an array of four uint64, so the comparison is on all 256 bits. On a miss the code stores a value copy of *z in mm.mod and mm.mu = uint256.Reciprocal(z) before z is written (lines 58-60). The reciprocal in mm.mu is therefore always the reciprocal of exactly the value in mm.mod, and a hit requires mm.mod to equal the new modulus in every limb, so a reused reciprocal belongs to the same full modulus. MulModWithReciprocal (holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 uint256.go:688-715) then runs the same umul and reduce4(&p, m, mu) as MulMod (uint256.go:720-735) with mu equal to Reciprocal(m), with z aliasing m in both, so the word is the stock word. Narrow moduli (z[3] == 0) and m == 0 bypass the memo. The memo is a field of the EVM (evm.go:217-219) and is never cleared; it outlives frames, reverts and transactions of one EVM, which is harmless because its value is a function of its key. Direct test: memo.go copied verbatim from v2.12.0-beta, compiled with go1.24.7 against uint256 v1.3.2 source, one memo instance for the whole run, consecutive moduli sharing the top limb, the bottom limb, three limbs, the top or bottom 192 bits, differing by one in the top limb, or repeating, each pair also run as FullMath does with 2^256-1 between: seed 2026112626, 1,000,000 pairs, 5,000,000 MULMODs, 1,271,986 memo hits, 0 mismatches against math/big; seed 2026112627, 250,000 pairs, 0 mismatches. A planted fault keying the memo on limb 3 only does not finish 10 pairs in 20 seconds (reduce4's final subtraction loop at mod.go:450-461 runs with the reciprocal of another modulus), so a stale entry cannot pass unseen. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/mulmod_memo.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/core/vm/mulmod_memo.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/params/config.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.3.2/uint256.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.3.2/mod.go; research/network-risk/cycles/026/theme-stateful-interpreter.work/build/memotest/main.go
- Polygon, cycle 26. How often the PoolManager itself can meet the memo with a repeated or a near-equal modulus. Every MULMOD the PoolManager frames execute in sequences a64, a512 and b was traced in the reference interpreter. Result: a512: 5288 MULMODs, 3328 with a full-width modulus, 257 distinct full-width moduli, 2816 of them 2^256-1, 512 changes of modulus, none to a modulus that shares limb 3 or limb 0 with the one before. Every full-width denominator is preceded by mulmod(a, b, not(0)) (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24), so a one-entry memo holds 2^256-1 whenever a new denominator arrives; the only hits on a denominator are FullMath.sol:48 followed by :112 for the same denominator in mulDivRoundingUp. A memo that keyed on one limb would therefore be exposed by PoolManager swaps only for a denominator whose keyed limb is all ones, and the a512 sequence exposes it 0 times. The memo check rests on the raw sequences of established-l1 (20,000 records on every Polygon endpoint) and on the direct test above; the PoolManager sequences check that the whole path returns the same words. Result: EIP-6780 keeps the code of an account destroyed in its creation transaction until the transaction ends, so a CREATE2 to the same address in the same transaction collides. Sequence e gives this on 20 networks, and on Tempo the trace of the reverted call (out/trace-4217-e.json) shows the same contract address collision: second CREATE2 returns 0 and the hook keeps its first runtime. Between transactions a redeployed hook has a new code hash. A hook author who replaces hook code between transactions is the pool-creator case and is outside this unit (one line: hooks that are EIP-7702 delegated accounts or metamorphic factories can change behaviour between transactions; pool creator level). ## Reading of the source (theme-caller-and-callee-identity)

- HyperEVM, cycle 27. L-1129, the rule. How the HyperEVM archive client nanoreth (tag nb-20261125-2) decides that a transaction is a system transaction and where it takes the sender from. Result: A transaction is a system transaction when gas_price() is Some(0) (src/node/primitives/transaction.rs:182-184, src/node/evm/executor.rs:44-49). For such a transaction recover_signer, recover_signer_unchecked and recover_unchecked_with_buf return s_to_address(s): s equal to 1 gives 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, s equal to (1<<160)|1 gives 0x00..01, and any other s gives its low 20 bytes (transaction.rs:49-58 and 77-97). The file header calls this a pseudo signer for system transactions, and address_to_s (transaction.rs:61-69) is the encoder. The system transactions come from the block source as a separate list system_txs with an optional from field (src/node/types/mod.rs:114-128 and 285-290), and the official endpoint serves them under its own method eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber. The synthetic signature is therefore the replica's encoding of what the producer wrote, not a rule that any public endpoint applies to a signed transaction a user submits. If the producer ever put a regular transaction with gas price 0 into a block, the replica would take its sender from s and show state the producer did not compute; that would mislead replica readers and would not change the chain. Under EIP-1559 such a transaction is invalid because the base fee is nonzero in every block read. The cycle 23 census of mined blocks found none below 100,000,000 wei; during verification eth_feeHistory predicted 96,659,059 and 89,439,317 wei for a next block, so 100,000,000 is not a confirmed protocol floor, and any nonzero base fee is enough here. The producer's own admission rule is closed and was not read; no Hyperliquid page that states it was found. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/src/node/primitives/transaction.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 27. L-1129, the blocks since the MRB fork. 2,000 blocks drawn uniformly from 50,988,232 (MRB activation) to 52,328,897 with seed 2027027, read in full on rpc.purroofgroup.com (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 before and after), with eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm ('hyperliquid evm Mainnet' before and after) for every tenth block. Result: 10,771 transactions, of which 1,096 in 661 blocks have gas price 0. All 1,096 are type 0, and in all 1,096 the from field equals the address decoded from s. The 38 senders are 0x2222...2222 (16 native HYPE credits), 35 token system addresses of the form 0x20 followed by the token index (433), and the two AQAv2 addresses that cycle 23 already recorded under F-020: 0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24, the USDC linked contract (427), and 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00, the USDC treasury (220). None has the PoolManager 0x12D4Fd9C...6B1F as sender, target or first argument. For all 200 compared blocks the official system transaction list has the same senders, targets and selectors in the same order as the replica. The PoolManager nonce is 1 on the official endpoint. So since the fork no gas price 0 transaction has run in the name of the PoolManager or of an account without a HyperCore role, and the only senders outside 0x2222 and 0x20.. are the two AQAv2 addresses whose case F-020 covers. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-caller-and-callee-identity.work/raw/hl_sysciensus.json (script scripts/hl_syscensus.py)
- all 21 networks, cycle 27. Task 1 test: eth_call and eth_estimateGas with from set to the PoolManager and gasPrice 0, with value 0 and 1 wei, plus an extsload read, on every network (endpoints of networks.json, web3_clientVersion before and after; Ethereum and Polygon repeated on eth.drpc.org and polygon.drpc.org after HTTP 403 from publicnode). Result: Every endpoint accepts from = PoolManager at gas price 0. eth_call of a plain call returns 0x and eth_estimateGas returns 21,000 (Arbitrum One 21,305, Robinhood Chain 21,292, MegaETH 60,000) on all 21; value 1 wei is accepted on the 20 networks with native value, and Tempo refuses value with 'value transfer not allowed' (-32003). This shows only that the simulation layer skips the EIP-3607 code check and the fee check, as these methods are specified to; it does not show that a transaction from the PoolManager can be signed, admitted or mined. The PoolManager nonce is 1 on 20 networks and 0 on Unichain, where it is a genesis predeploy; no transaction has used it as sender anywhere. No public read-only method takes a signed raw transaction and reports the sender that a producer would derive, so the HyperEVM part of L-1129 that asks for a raw transaction with the PoolManager as derived sender has no read-only test. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-caller-and-callee-identity.work/raw/from_pm.json, raw/from_pm_alt.json (script scripts/from_pm.py)
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, MegaETH, cycle 27. OP Stack deposits and aliasing (OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, MegaETH): can an ordinary L1 account produce a deposit whose L2 sender is the PoolManager. Result: No. The portal sets from to msg.sender only when EOA.isSenderEOA() holds, that is msg.sender == tx.origin, or code of exactly 23 bytes that starts with 0xEF0100 (an EIP-7702 delegation); otherwise from is the L1 to L2 alias (OptimismPortal2.sol:939-943, EOA.sol:9-24 on the develop branch). EIP-3541 forbids deployed code starting with 0xEF, so a contract cannot pass the check, and the first two cases need a key for the L1 address. The PoolManager addresses and their alias preimages have no code and nonce 0 on Ethereum (F-140), and finding a key or CREATE2 input for a chosen 160-bit address costs about 2^160. Only a portal upgrade by its upgrader can emit such a deposit, which F-140 records at governance level. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/libraries/EOA.sol
- Tempo, cycle 27. Tempo type 0x76: can a batch, a Keychain signature, a key authorization, a fee payer, a Tempo authorization list or a configurable account make the PoolManager the sender (tempo v1.19.1-a9d6748 answers on the endpoint; source tree of v1.19.1 read). Result: No. The sender is the address derived from a secp256k1, P256 or WebAuthn public key (spec, Address Derivation). A Keychain signature names user_address, prepare_keychain rejects it unless it equals the recovered signer, and the access key must be registered for that account in AccountKeychain (crates/evm/src/handler.rs:655-676). A key authorization must be signed by the root key of the account or by an admin access key already registered for it, with account equal to the signer (handler.rs:504-627). A configurable account role is refused when the account has code other than the configurable account code (valid_account_code, crates/precompiles/src/configurable_account/mod.rs:272-279, used in handler/configurable_account/mod.rs:350-356), and without a stored commitment its address must equal the hash derivation of the config (crates/primitives/src/transaction/configurable_account/mod.rs:384-414). The PoolManager has 24,009 bytes of code and no key, so none of these paths can name it. A fee payer pays fees and never becomes a caller, and every call of a batch has the one signer as caller (cycle 21 clearances). Evidence: https://docs.tempo.xyz/protocol/transactions/spec-tempo-transaction
- all 21 networks, cycle 27. Task 1 across networks: which senders the PoolManager trusts and whether any network-level sender can be made equal to the PoolManager, a router or a holder of claims or positions by an ordinary account. Result: The PoolManager keys deltas, claims, allowances, operators and positions on msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:110, 161, 183, 226, 270, 294, 301, 311-317, 326, 334; src/ERC6909.sol:26-61; position owner in src/libraries/Position.sol:48-56), so whoever is CALLER owns those records. Per network: Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc: no (cycle 20 client readings, F-058, Arc CallFrom limited to tx.origin). OP Stack and Celo, X Layer, MegaETH deposits: no for ordinary accounts, governance only (F-140, item above). Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium: unsigned messages and retryables are aliased for every L1 caller, only governance can post a contract transaction as the PoolManager (F-138). HyperEVM: no; system transaction senders are HyperCore system addresses and the two AQAv2 addresses (F-020 covers the operator case). Tempo: no (item above). EIP-7702 on every network that has it: an authority must sign, and an authority whose code is not a delegation is skipped, so the PoolManager cannot be delegated; an EOA that holds claims or positions and delegates gives its own records to the delegate code it chose. No precompile on the 21 networks forwards a call with a caller chosen by its input (Arc CallFrom checks tx.origin; HyperEVM CoreWriter takes actions for its caller only). Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:291-336
- all 21 networks, cycle 27. Task 2: what one party of a shared transaction can leave for a later party through the transient state of sync (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36), and whether any of it moves funds. Result: Only the synced currency and its reserves outlive a call; unlock clears the lock flag and requires every delta to be zero before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Left behind, a synced token makes a later native settle revert with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356), which F-071 records as low. A stale reserve R makes a later settle without its own sync credit balanceOf minus R: if the balance fell since (a take), the subtraction reverts (checked arithmetic, src/PoolManager.sol:360); if it rose, the extra is a payment some account made to the PoolManager after that sync without settling it, which is the first party's own gift or the F-137 pattern. resetCurrency clears only the currency slot (CurrencyReserves.sol:21-25), and sync writes currency and reserves together (CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so no sequence pairs a currency with a reserve from another moment. Nothing moves funds of pools or claim holders. Clearing between transactions was shown on 16 networks with eth_simulateV1 in cycle 21; Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc and HyperEVM still have no eth_simulateV1 today, so they rest on the client readings of earlier cycles. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-caller-and-callee-identity.work/raw/sim_tclear_5.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 27. Task 3 and 4: the four outgoing shapes (value call with empty calldata, transfer, balanceOf, hook selector) sent from the PoolManager address to every listed precompile, predeploy and system contract. Result: Already measured: cycle 13 calleegas.py on all 21 networks and L-166 with balances read before and after. Reanalysed here from cycle 13 raw data: transfer returns success with no return data at addresses without code, at precompiles 0x01 and 0x100 and several system addresses, which src/types/Currency.sol:60-80 treats as success; such a take debits the caller in that currency id and moves nothing, so the loss is the caller's own. 0x02, 0x03 and 0x04 return a 32 byte word for balanceOf, so they can be synced as currencies with nonsense reserves, which only affects pools whose creator named them. 0x04 echoes every hook selector but fails the hook address check (Hooks.sol:109-124, cycle 13). The real currencies with a second face (Celo CELO token, Polygon 0x1010, Arc USDC 0x3600) were walked in earlier cycles without a double credit. No answer registers, stakes, bridges or burns in the PoolManager's name except the native payout cases of F-021, F-047, F-048 and F-049, which lose only the caller's payout. Balance rises outside a transfer can be booked between a sync and a settle only when the rise is triggered inside the same transaction: system credits on HyperEVM run as separate transactions, native value is never credited without msg.value, and the bridge and token cases are F-137 and the token findings. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-callee-gas-and-overrides.work/raw/summary.json

- Monad, cycle 27. Task 1. The harness host of cycle 23 was repaired in a copy at src/harness_fixed.cpp. Each frame now copies the code of its code address into a local vector for its whole life (harness_fixed.cpp:242), so a failed nested call that assigns the World snapshot back (harness_fixed.cpp:427, 438) can no longer free code that a running frame reads. Execution is chosen and run by the code address, so a DELEGATECALL runs the callee's code (harness_fixed.cpp:242, 435), and compiled and interpreted code objects are cached by the keccak of the code (harness_fixed.cpp:243-245, 255, 270). It was built with the clang++ already present at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7, linked against the Monad VM objects that cycle 23 compiled from the tagged source (scripts/build.sh). With MALLOC_PERTURB_ unset, 165 and 90 the fixed build gives byte-identical harness output for all 1,150 runs of the 575 cycle 26 cases (unset against 165) and the same digests for cases 1369 and 1528 in every layout, while the cycle 23 build changes its answer with the perturbation value. (a) The count is first clamped to 256 by destructive_mov_stack_elem_to_bounded_rax (emitter.cpp:4122-4190, unchanged), k = count/8 selects a byte offset into the value placed next to 32 bytes of zero fill (SHL below it, SHR and SAR above it, the fill all ones for a negative SAR literal), b = count mod 8 shifts each lane and a second load one byte further supplies the b carried bits, which for SAR come from the fill and give the sign; for count 256 both loads read only fill; rax is outside the three register groups (emitter.cpp:639), so the base register cannot overwrite the count. (b) The order of the writes changes, the dependency counting and cycle resolution do not; the temporary register is taken while free and no allocation happens before its last use. (c) Memory never shrinks inside a frame, so a passed check stays passed, and the gas for that size has been paid. (d) and (f) give the same byte and count. (e) No stack size can pass both bounds of such a block. It exits out of gas when gas_remaining plus the block's remaining base gas is negative, clamps the gas word to INT64_MAX when any bit above 63 is set, computes gas_left_here - (gas_left_here >> 6) with an arithmetic shift on a non-negative value and takes the minimum (call.cpp:136-145), adds the 2,300 stipend to both the child gas and gas_remaining for a value call (call.cpp:147-151) and returns 0 with the buffer empty at depth 1024 or more (cmp edx,0x3ff; jg). After host->call it stores result.output_data and output_size as the new return buffer whatever the status (call.cpp:178), deducts gas - gas_left with the out-of-gas exit of deduct_gas, adds the refund, and copies min(ret_size, output_size) bytes into memory. returndatacopy exits when offset + size overflows 32 bits or exceeds the return buffer size, clamps an offset above 32 bits to 0xffffffff first, charges 3 gas per word and copies from the buffer. tload and tstore byte-swap key and value and call the host's transient storage entries; tstore exits with an error in a static frame. So Hooks.sol:132-150 and CustomRevert.sol read returndatasize and returndatacopy of the hook's own result, and a failed call leaves its revert data there, as on Ethereum. A native-code OOG after a call can come where the interpreter would still run some instructions of the same block, but the interpreter runs out of gas before that block ends, so both revert the frame (the shape cycle 26 recorded). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/028/theme-monad-shipped-emitter.work/out/fn/call_impl_monad11.s ; research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl/dis/monad-0.16.7.s ; research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/dl/monad-0.16.7/category/vm/runtime/call.cpp:57-187 ; research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/dl/monad-0.16.7/category/vm/runtime/data.cpp:164-191 ; research/network-risk/cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/dl/monad-0.16.7/category/vm/runtime/types.hpp:252-258 ; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:132-150

Every PoolManager value an ordinary account can leave for a later frame of the same transaction without holding the lock: lock flag, nonzero delta count, currency deltas, synced currency, synced reserves. Result: Only the synced currency and the synced reserves survive. Lock: set only inside unlock and cleared at its end, a reverting callback rolls the set back (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25). Deltas: every writer is onlyWhenUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:145-147, 187-189, 256-258, 291, 300, 305, 310, 322, 332). _accountDelta increments the count when a slot leaves zero and decrements when it returns to zero, and skips zero deltas (src/PoolManager.sol:368-378, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41 with checked addition at line 139), so the count equals the number of nonzero slots and unlock cannot return while any slot is nonzero (line 112). The decrement at src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:30-32 never runs on a zero count. Synced state: sync writes currency and reserves together for a token (CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32) and only clears the currency for address(0) (PoolManager.sol:283); token settle clears the currency (line 361). Stale reserves after sync(0) are never read, because _settle reads reserves only when the currency is nonzero (lines 353-358). Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114
- all 21 networks, cycle 28. Task 1. Effect of a leftover (currency C, reserves R) on a later party's settle, settleFor, take, sync, clear, mint, burn and fee collection. Result: sync by the later party replaces both slots (PoolManager.sol:286) or clears the currency (283). settle or settleFor with value reverts NonzeroNativeValue (356, F-071). settle with zero value credits balanceOf(C) minus R to the settler or the named recipient, never to the party that synced (358-364), or reverts on the checked subtraction at 360 when the balance fell. A later party that paid C after the foreign sync and settles without its own sync is credited its payment plus any other rise since R, so it gains, not the attacker. A later party that paid token D and settles without syncing is credited the change in C, its D debt stays open and its unlock reverts CurrencyNotSettled (112), so its payment reverts with it. A later party that paid C before the foreign sync and settles without its own sync is credited zero and reverts; this needs payment and settle in different frames with a foreign frame between, which no canonical router and no top unlocker read here does. take, clear, mint and burn never read the synced slots (291-336). collectProtocolFees of C reverts with ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced (ProtocolFees.sol:49-52), a governance hazard already in F-014. Result: All 21 (Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM): yes through ERC-4337. EntryPoint v0.6 to v0.9 have code on every network, handleOps accepts any caller (v0.9 only a top level EOA), and the submitter of handleOps orders the operations, so an ordinary account that holds a victim's pending operation can place its own frame first at the cost of one handleOps transaction; whether outsiders can read pending operations is unknown on every network. Multicall3 and EIP-7702 batches are signed by one party, so a foreign frame enters only if that party includes it. Tempo 0x76: one sender, the fee payer signs fees only, no foreign frame (Tempo spec). Base Everest 0x79: one sender, payer signs fees only, not active (date TBD). X Layer: the gasless whitelist admits EntryPoint v0.7 and the 0x7c5bee2a carrier at zero gas price (F-151), which lowers the cost of the ERC-4337 path to nothing on X Layer and adds no other form. Sequencer or builder ordering (World Chain priority blockspace, OP Stack, Arbitrum, Tempo, MegaETH) orders transactions, not frames inside one, and is out of the attacker's reach. Evidence: eth_getCode on all 21 endpoints, out/ep_code.json; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x433709009B8330FDa32311DF1C2AFA402eD8D009?fields=sources
- all 21 networks, cycle 28. Task 4. Can a foreign sync or a foreign lock make the attacker profit from another party, or make a pool user lose funds?. Result: No path found. The settle credit always goes to the settler or its named recipient (PoolManager.sol:364), so a stale snapshot only pays the attacker for value that reaches the PoolManager between its own sync and its own settle with no other sync or token settle in between. Canonical periphery and the World Chain Settler never let their payment sit in that window, since sync, transfer and settle are consecutive calls of one frame. Value that arrives by a public relay is F-137. Losses found are the victim's gas for a failed operation, paid to the bundler, in F-071 and in this cycle's AlreadyUnlocked finding. Rating for an ordinary attacker: griefing only, low. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-364

## Reading of the source (theme-geth-family-caches-and-slot-walk)

- Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Avalanche, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Celo, cycle 29. L-1171, go-ethereum master: does core/vm at bbafd66 (2026-11-25) hold an operand, result, reciprocal or jump destination cache that could return a value keyed on fewer bits than its input? Read instructions.go, interpreter.go, the generated loop interpreter_gen.go, jump_table.go, stack.go, memory.go, contract.go, jumpdests.go, evm.go and contracts.go, and every file of core/vm in the module archive, which lists precompile_cache.go (copyright 2026) as the newest addition. Result: No arithmetic cache. Every arithmetic, comparison, shift, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND and EXP handler calls the stock uint256 v1.3.2 routine on the stack words (opMulmod is z.MulMod(x, y, z)). opKeccak256 hashes the memory slice each time with no cache. The jump destination cache (jumpdests.go, a map and a layered map) is keyed by the full code hash and stores the bitmap computed from that code. The precompile result cache keys an entry by the fork table pointer, the precompile address and the precompile input or its normalised prefix, stores only results that returned no error, charges gas before the lookup on hit and on miss, and returns a copy. The PoolManager reaches a precompile only when a caller names a precompile address as a currency or a native recipient (P1 to P3 of ASSUMPTIONS.md), and the precompiles that opt in are pure functions of the bytes kept in the key, so a hit returns what a fresh run would; whether a normalisation drops a byte that matters is a question for each precompile and is not one of PoolManager arithmetic. The generated loop was checked case by case: for 70 opcodes the underflow bound, overflow bound, static gas and stack change equal the specification (scripts/genloop.py), DUP and SWAP use n and n+1 as bounds, and every case calls the same handler as the table loop. instructions.go and interpreter_gen.go are byte-identical to release v1.17.10, which Ethereum geth nodes ran in the cycle 29 ethereum-reference unit; between v1.17.10 and master, core/vm changed only by removing the verkle table and in tracer, gas and precompile files. Monad mainnet runs MONAD_TEN (monad_mainnet.cpp:30-31 of monad v0.16.7; the revision names are in category/vm/evm/monad/revision.h:35-39), so the instances read are sload<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x450670 and sstore<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x451fd0 of monad 0.16.7, extracted from the cycle 27 objdump text with research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/scripts/fnaddr.py into research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/out/fn, and compared with runtime/storage.cpp:36-121 of the tagged source, the Context layout (runtime/types.hpp:225-245, 53-60) and the evmc fork f6b7c57e host table. Result: Both follow the source. Keys and values are byte-reversed with vpermq 0x1b and a vpshufb mask whose 32 bytes, read from the ELF at 0x7f52a0, are 07..00 0f..08 07..00 0f..08, which reverses all 32 bytes. sload calls access_storage (host table +0x68) with the recipient at Context+0x28, charges 0x1f40 = 8000 only when the status is 0 (EVMC_ACCESS_COLD), exits OutOfGas (status 3) when gas goes negative, then calls get_storage (+0x08) and stores the reversed word. sstore exits with Error (2) when flag bit 0 (EVMC_STATIC) is set, exits OutOfGas when gas_remaining + remaining_block_base_gas <= 0x898 = 2200, which is the source's test against 2300 with minimum_store_gas 100, charges 8000 on a cold slot, calls set_storage (+0x10) and update_page (+0x80, index 16 of the host table), and charges (first_page_write ? 2800 : 0) + (grew_state ? 17000 : 0). The branch-free form was worked through: sbb gives -1 when first_page_write is 0, masked to -2800; neg and a 32-bit and give 17000 or 0; adding 0xaf0 = 2800 gives the same four values as 100 + 2800a + 17000b - 100 in storage.cpp:91-100. The refund counter is not touched, as in the MIP-8 branch of the source. The MONAD_TEN and MONAD_NEXT instances have identical instruction streams after addresses are removed (research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-register-spill.work/scripts/normdiff.py: 54 and 76 instructions, 0 differ). These routines serve the interpreter and native code alike, so they cannot make the two engines disagree, and they match the source on what PoolManager storage reads and writes return (src/libraries/Pool.sol, src/libraries/Position.sol, src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol).
