- Monad, cycle 29. Task 2 (L-1170), the keccak wrapper and memory growth of the gcc build: sha3<MonadTraits<10>> at 0x343f90 (and the MONAD_NINE instance at 0x343dc0, identical after rip-relative targets are resolved), Context::increase_capacity at 0x433930, monad_vm_runtime_increase_capacity at 0x4335b0, and the hand-written .increase_capacity trampoline at 0x4334b9 that native code reaches from monad_vm_runtime_increase_memory_raw_mip3. Compared with runtime/keccak.hpp:27-46, runtime/types.hpp:266-356, runtime/context.cpp:46-80 and :151-154, and runtime/context.S:91-175. Result: All follow the source. sha3 bounds size and offset below 2^28 (high limbs zero and low limb & 0xfffffffff0000000 zero, else OutOfGas), skips memory work for size 0 and hashes zero bytes at offset 0, and for size > 0 grows memory when offset + size exceeds memory.size (Context+0x108). The MIP-3 cost is (min_size + 31) >> 6, which equals ceil(min_size / 32) >> 1 for every input because floor(floor(a/32)/2) = floor(a/64). The new size is (min_size + 31) & ~31, the total bound is data - data_handle + new_size <= 0x800000, the charge is new_cost - memory.cost with the OutOfGas exit, and increase_capacity is called with the old size only when capacity < new size. The word charge is ((size + 31) >> 5) * 6, then monad_keccak256(memory.data + offset, size). monad_vm_runtime_increase_capacity allocates 2 * (parent + new_size) bytes aligned to 32, asserts the allocation, copies the old parent + old_size bytes and zeroes the rest in 32-byte non-temporal stores with the alignment asserts of the source, frees the old handle only when it differs from parent_handle (Context+0x130), and sets capacity, data_handle and data as context.cpp:74-77 do. The trampoline saves ymm0 to ymm4 and rax, r8 to r11 around the gcc call, which together with the SysV callee-saved set covers every register context.S:97-106 declares callee-saved, so a gcc register choice inside the C routine cannot reach native code's live values. The Memory field offsets used (size 0x108, capacity 0x10c, data 0x110, cost 0x118, data_handle 0x120, parent_handle 0x130) follow from runtime/types.hpp:95-117. The PoolManager hashes 64-byte keys and pool keys (src/libraries/Pool.sol, src/libraries/Position.sol:calculatePositionKey, src/types/PoolId.sol) through this path in both engines. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-package-read.work/dl/dis/monad-0.16.7.s (0x343f90, 0x433930, 0x4335b0, 0x4334b9); research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/dl/monad-0.16.7/category/vm/runtime/keccak.hpp:27-46; research/network-risk/cycles/027/theme-monad-engine-agreement.work/dl/monad-0.16.7/category/vm/runtime/context.cpp:46-80

- Monad, cycle 29. What a wrong register or spill decision of the gcc-built emitter could do to a mined block, and whether mined history already rules it out on the paths it has used. Read cmd/monad/main.cpp at v0.16.7 and monad-eth-block-policy/src/lib.rs at monad-bft v0.16.7, and queried three Monad endpoints on 2026-11-27 (rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz, rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, each answering web3_clientVersion Monad/0.16.7). Result: A node started with call tracing executes blocks with vm::VM::InterpreterOnly (main.cpp:485-488), and other nodes use Dual mode, which runs hot contracts as gcc-emitted native code. Every node checks that a proposal's delayed execution header (the full EthHeader of block N minus the execution delay, with state root, receipts root, logs bloom and gas used) equals the header its own execution produced, and rejects the block as not coherent otherwise (monad-eth-block-policy lib.rs:1182-1196, 1271-1289). The three endpoints serve debug_traceTransaction with callTracer for a PoolManager swap of block 125,728,461 (tx 0x239f9e91bf990c6a64f6f8a1d4a3d3aa62b0550c2e987a1af9f8eef84fd0f72f; 99,143 bytes of frames, gasUsed 0x1a9b5f on all three), so they run call tracing and therefore the interpreter, and all three return the same hash, state root and receipts root for block 125,729,880 near the head. So for every block these nodes accepted, the interpreter's result equals what producers running gcc native code committed. A gcc register or spill fault on a path that mined transactions use and that changed state, a log or gas used would have split the tracing nodes from the chain. A fault confined to a PoolManager block that no mined transaction has entered is not excluded by this; see the leads. - Tempo, cycle 29. Task 2 (L-1169), source: how keccak_cache_global keys its cache. Read in alloy-primitives 1.7.3 src/utils/keccak_cache.rs (crate sha256 d5e9dbd4... equal to the Cargo.lock checksum of v1.19.1) and fixed-cache 0.1.10 src/lib.rs (sha256 2fe63500..., equal to the lock). evm2's KECCAK256 handler (crates/evm2/src/interpreter/instructions/crypto.rs:5-17) returns KECCAK256_EMPTY for length 0 and otherwise calls alloy_primitives::keccak256 on the memory slice, which goes through the cache. Result: Inputs of 1 to 87 bytes are cached (MAX_INPUT_LEN = 128 - 32 - 1 - 8 = 87); longer ones are hashed directly. The bucket is chosen by a 64 bit rapidhash v3 of the input; the bucket tag holds the hash bits above the index. A hit needs the tag to match, the stored one-byte length to equal the input length, and Key::eq, which compares the full stored slice with the input (keccak_cache.rs:126-131, fixed-cache lib.rs:322-345). A tag match with a different key, a prefix or an extension is a miss. Insert and lookup hold a per-bucket lock bit taken by compare-and-swap, so a reader never sees half of a write. A partial key match cannot return a stored digest. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/alloy-primitives/alloy-primitives-1.7.3.crate
- Tempo, cycle 29. Task 2, aarch64 binary: KECCAK256 handler (family B 0x3b5aafc, A 0x3b5c3c8 wraps it) and the inlined cache compute at 0x3b487d4 read from the disassembly, then the cache compute and the four Keccak-256 routines it calls (20 byte 0x18ead54, 32 byte 0x18eb104, 64 byte 0x18eb4c4, generic 0x18ea188, long entry 0x18ef7e8) run in the cycle 28 a64emu model extended with ld1r, shl, usra, fneg, zip1 and stlr (scripts/keccak_a64.py, seed 2026112729). The model cache had 256 buckets; the shipped code reads the capacity from the cache global and only the index and tag masks depend on it. Result: 7,687 cases, no mismatch with Python Keccak-256 and no model error: 764 direct calls of the four routines (lengths 1 to 299 and 1,023 and 1,024 for the generic one), the 114 battery KECCAK256 offset and length pairs with non-zero length, each twice so the second is a cache hit, 900 CurrencyDelta preimages (target, currency) over 30 addresses including 0, 1, 2^160-1, Tempo's 0x20c0... token prefix, and their 900 cache hits (900 distinct digests), 2,800 PoolManager mapping preimages (pools with slot 6, ticks, bitmap, positions, 58 byte position keys, ERC-6909 nested keys), 1,796 near-miss cache cases (last bit flipped, one byte shorter, one byte longer) and 299 hand-planted buckets that carry the right tag with another key of the same length, a one byte shorter prefix, or a one byte longer extension and a poison digest. No planted bucket returned the poison digest. The handler checks the upper limbs of offset and length (status 36), charges words times the keccak word cost, saturates offset+length before the memory size check, and writes the digest byte-reversed into the stack word. 1,736 of the 1,771 extracted instructions ran. Planted faults are caught: one eor of the 64 byte routine turned into orr fails 4,388 cases, a cache that ignores the bcmp result gives 115 false hits, and removing the length byte comparison gives 88. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/029/theme-tempo-binary-keccak-transient.work/results/keccak_a64_none.json

- Tempo, cycle 29. Task 3, aarch64 binary: CALLDATALOAD (B 0x3b60e34, A 0x3b5c6cc) and MCOPY (B 0x3b561e4, A 0x3b5db9c) handlers run in the a64emu model, extended with rev64 and ext (scripts/mem_a64.py, seed 2026112730). Calldata buffers of 14 lengths from 0 to 260 bytes were followed by junk bytes 0x5a, and offsets were taken around each length and at 2^32, 2^64, 2^255 and 2^256-1. MCOPY ran on the 310 battery vectors, 600 overlapping copies within 0x400 bytes and zero-length copies with huge offsets. The evm2 source of both handlers (instructions/env.rs:73-76, utils.rs:297-310, instructions/memory.rs:31-40, interpreter/memory.rs:230-232) was read. Result: 3,138 cases, no mismatch and no model error. CALLDATALOAD saturates an offset whose upper limbs are non-zero, returns zero when the offset is at or past the end, and copies only the remaining bytes into a zeroed word, so no byte past calldata is read. MCOPY with zero length skips the offset checks and memory growth, checks the upper limbs of the other operands (status 36), sizes memory to max(dst, src) + length with saturation, and copies with memmove. Faults are caught: a forward byte loop in place of memmove fails 466 overlap cases, and an in-bounds test of 31 in place of 32 fails 11 CALLDATALOAD cases by reading a junk byte. The x86_64 versions were not lifted; the live x86_64 endpoint passed the battery's CDLOAD and MCOPY vectors in earlier cycles. - Tempo, cycle 29. Task 4: which src/ lines depend on these handlers, and whether any difference was found. CurrencyDelta._computeSlot (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-15) hashes two masked words at memory 0 and 32, so its preimage is always 64 bytes and goes through the cached 64 byte routine. applyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41) loads and stores that slot. unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) reverts unless NonzeroDeltaCount reads zero. The transient constants were recomputed: NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT, IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT, CURRENCY_SLOT and RESERVES_OF_SLOT each equal keccak256 of their name minus 1. Result: Neither architecture differed on any case, so no src/ line computes or decides anything else on Tempo because of these handlers. A cache that aliased two 64 byte preimages, or a transient map that aliased two keys, would have booked one account's debt against another's credit and let unlock pass with a debt outstanding. The reading shows the cache compares the whole input and the transient map compares the whole 52 byte key, and every test with planted faults shows the checks can see such a fault. Nothing in this unit gives an ordinary account a way to take or lock funds. Evidence: src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-gcc-allocator-model)

- Monad, cycle 30. Which PoolManager shift, SIGNEXTEND and BYTE sites reach the non-literal arms of Monad's emitter. research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-gcc-allocator-model.work/scripts/varsites.py walks the runtime of research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (24,009 bytes) and removes the 1,205 literal sites of cycle 28 (sitearms.json); src lines come from the cycle 12 source map of the same build. Result: Totals: SHR 99, SHL 46, SAR 19, SIGNEXTEND 114, BYTE 3. Sites with both operands non-literal: SHR 20, SHL 2, SAR 0, SIGNEXTEND 0, and one BYTE at pc 24006, which is inside the metadata trailer and is never executed. So signextend_by_non_literal and BYTE with a run-time index are not reached by PoolManager code, and the arms that matter are SHR and SHL with a run-time count: r := shr(f, r) in the 13 assembly blocks of getTickAtSqrtPrice (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:141-213, f = shr(128, r) in {0, 1}), shr(r, x) in mostSignificantBit (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:15-19, counts 0 to 248), the shift in leastSignificantBit (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:34), Slot0.setTick (src/types/Slot0.sol:73) and two compiler-generated sites at pc 18088 and 18651. ## Reading of the source (theme-monad-mined-native-coverage)

- Monad, cycle 30. When the PoolManager runs as native code on a Monad validator, read in the v0.16.7 source and the release pages. VM::execute_raw (vm.cpp lines 141-189) runs native code when the varcode cache holds it. Without native code it schedules an asynchronous compile at once while the cache is cold, and otherwise once the interpreter gas spent on the code hash reaches max_code_size(offset, size) = offset + 32 x size (x86.hpp lines 53-64) with offset 10 x 1024 (x86/types.hpp lines 141-142). The cache counts as warm at three quarters of its 4 GiB weight (varcode_cache.hpp lines 29-33 and 61-64). The release page lists v0.16.5 on mainnet on 2026-10-22 and v0.16.7 on mainnet on 2026-11-26, and the v0.16.7 upgrade page calls it a rolling upgrade with dates sent through official channels. The first Monad blocks with a timestamp on or after 00:00 UTC of those dates are 115,463,613 and 125,426,597 (eth_getBlockByNumber binary search on rpc.monad.xyz). The PoolManager has code from block 29,255,895 (eth_getCode binary search on rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com). Result: For the 24,009 byte PoolManager the threshold is 10,240 + 32 x 24,009 = 778,528 gas. The median transaction in the sample spends 180,478 gas inside PoolManager frames, so a validator with a warm cache compiles it after about five PoolManager transactions, and one with a cold cache (every node after a restart until about 3 GiB of code is cached) compiles it at the first call. The network carries about 0.8 PoolManager transactions per second (108,489 transactions with PoolManager logs in blocks 125,426,597 to 125,760,000). Each validator therefore ran the PoolManager natively within seconds of starting the 0.16.7 package. The hour at which each validator restarted is not published, so the sample period starts at the release date. Only the gas threshold decides; no on-chain state or caller choice keeps the PoolManager in the interpreter. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/vm.cpp lines 141-189; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.hpp lines 53-64; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/types.hpp lines 141-142; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/varcode_cache.hpp lines 29-33 and 61-64; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler.cpp lines 106-140; https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/changelog/releases.md; https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/upgrade-instructions/v0.16.7.md; rpc.monad.xyz eth_getBlockByNumber (research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-mined-native-coverage.work/out/dateblocks.json); rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com eth_getCode (research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-mined-native-coverage.work/out/monad-deploy.json)

A rollback that kept a reverted frame's write, restored a transient word to zero, undid one entry too few or too many, or skipped an entry kind would let a frame that reverted leave a credit or erase a debt and then close the unlock. The shipped code of both architectures restores every value on every sequence, every such fault planted in it is caught by the same sequences, and the live node returns the reference bytes. No path to take or lock funds follows from these routines. Evidence: src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:28 ; src/PoolManager.sol:112 ; src/PoolManager.sol:368

The binary-only names are instantiations of the generic BoundedCache, closures and inlined helpers. Three shared caches exist: a keccak cache keyed by the whole 64-byte input (instructions.go:265-278, used by every mapping and CurrencyDelta slot such as src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:14), an ecrecover cache keyed by the input right-padded to 128 bytes, which equals ecrecover's own padding (evm.go:65-90), and a per-block jump destination cache keyed by code hash (core/parallel_state_processor.go:418). The jump cache can only pair a hash with other code if GetCode and GetCodeHash disagree within one execution; ParallelStateDB caches the code read per address for the whole incarnation (core/state/parallel_statedb.go:365-377) and computes the hash from that same value (:843-935), so they agree. No arithmetic, shift, comparison or jump handler reads a writable global: their data references are .rodata, ErrInvalidJump and errStopToken. ## Reading of the source (theme-monad-gcc-real-states)

- Monad, cycle 31. Task 1. The clang harness emitter path of monad v0.16.7 was rebuilt from the source cycle 23 fetched, with every monad object compiled fresh, and one hook added to category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp (research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/scripts/mkhook.py, src/x86_hook.cpp). The hook writes the virtual stack at entry to each compiled block, before each instruction's emit call and before the terminator's emit call: per element every location (literal, general register, AVX register, stack offset with its PrevLoc), its stack indices and reserve counts, the free general and AVX register queues, the available stack offsets, top_index, min_delta, max_delta, delta, the register owner tables and the deferred comparison. Private members are read through pointers to members, so no access specifier or layout changes. The local x86.cpp, emitter.cpp and virtual_stack.hpp were checked byte-equal to the v0.16.7 tag on GitHub. Result: The hooked build writes 10,748 states for the 24,009-byte PoolManager runtime and emits a listing of 48,690 lines that equals the unhooked rebuild and the cycle 27 listing used by cycles 28 to 30 (pm-asm-0.16.7.txt) line for line, with 0 differing read-only data bytes once the 22 eight-byte words that hold runtime routine addresses, which ASLR moves between two runs of the same binary, are masked (out/asmcmp.txt). The hook therefore does not change what is emitted. Because compilation emits every block whether or not it runs, the log holds the real compile-time state of every instruction of all 128 un-entered value blocks: 2,138 states over 1,882 instructions (out/value128-ops.json). The runtime on chain 143 equals the compiled runtime byte for byte (eth_getCode at block 0x77f6d37, sha256 288b9772...). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/virtual_stack.hpp ; https://rpc.monad.xyz eth_getCode 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e latest, web3_clientVersion Monad/0.16.7 before and after (research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/out/rpc/rpc.log) ; research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/out/asmcmp.txt
- Monad, cycle 31. Whole-program compiler dependence of the emitter on the PoolManager. The same emitter, virtual stack, basic block and runtime sources were built a second time with the system gcc 13.3.0 at -O2 -march=haswell (the interpreter object is left out because gcc 13 lacks musttail, and a two-line shim supplies __builtin_addcll and __builtin_subcll, which gcc 13 lacks). The gcc build then compiled the PoolManager with and without the hook. Result: The gcc 13.3 listing equals the clang 18 listing on all 48,690 lines and all unmasked read-only data bytes, so all 913 compiled blocks, the 128 un-entered value blocks among them, get the same instructions from both compilers. The 10,748 hook states of the gcc build equal those of the clang build once element pointers are renamed (out/statecmp-gcc13.txt). So no unspecified argument evaluation order, implementation-defined behaviour or undefined behaviour in the emitter source resolves differently between clang and gcc on this bytecode. This is gcc 13.3, not the gcc 15.2.0 that built the shipped validator, so it does not exclude a fault introduced by gcc 15.2.0 code generation itself. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/scripts/build.sh ; research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/out/asmcmp-gcc13.txt ; research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/out/statecmp-gcc13.txt ; research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/src/gcc13_shim.h

## Reading of the source (theme-nitro-binary-storage-lift)

- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, cycle 31. Transient storage path of the Nitro b72783f release binaries run in the cycle 30 x86-64 and AArch64 models: opTstore, opTload, (*StateDB).SetTransientState, (*StateDB).GetTransientState, (*journal).append, (*journal).revert and the transientStorageChange revert and mutation methods, with the StateDB and journalEntry interface calls dispatched through the itabs read from each file. Go runtime map calls were stubbed (runtime.mapaccess1, mapassign, mapdelete, memequal, convTnoptr, growslice, mallocgcSmallNoScanSC3). 20007 sequences (seed 31_1211_01) over the PoolManager's delta slots keccak256(target, currency), the NonzeroDeltaCount, Lock and two reserves slots, and slots one limb or one byte away from a delta slot, with nested snapshots, reverts of inner frames, commits and 4014 writes of an equal value. Result: Every one of 448662 reads per architecture equals tools/opdiff/pyevm.py after 171624 stores and 29011 reverts, no model error. Planted faults were caught on both architectures (mismatching sequences amd64/arm64): revert writes zero 10/10, journal entry skipped 15/15, snapshot index off by one 13/13, TLOAD key loses 16 bytes 26/26, equal-value skip inverted 26/26. The binary keys the map by the 52-byte (address, slot) struct: the map type's key size is 52 and its hasher and equal closures are memhash_varlen and memequal_varlen over 52 bytes. SetTransientState returns early only when the stored word equals the new one, journals (address, slot, previous) before writing, and deletes the entry when the new word is zero. journal.revert undoes entries newest first down to the snapshot index and truncates the journal there; revertToSnapshot passes revision.journalIndex and truncates validRevisions to the found index. A delta written in a reverted frame does not survive in either build, so src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:35-39, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol and Lock.sol read the committed word. Everything else unreached is stack growth or a bounds, divide or overflow panic. The aimed vectors reached the Exp bit-length branches for exponents whose top limb is limb 1 or 2 and the zero-result branches of SDiv and SMod, with no mismatch. The rest are paths that callers in uint256 v1.3.2 exclude: udivrem's divisor of length zero, numerator of length zero and numerator shorter than the divisor (Div, Mod and DivMod return before udivrem unless x > y > 0, AddMod passes a five-limb sum, MulMod passes eight limbs with a nonzero high half), the branch jumps that lead to panicBounds, and Reciprocal's early return for m[3] == 0 (MulMod calls it only when m[3] != 0). FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-48) issues MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 or the denominator and DIV after the x > y checks inside the library, so it cannot reach these instructions. A deposit or retryable to the PoolManager address can only add native balance, which the PoolManager credits to nobody until a caller syncs and settles, as on Ethereum. Result: Both binaries do what the source does, with no Tempo-only branch between checkpoint and commit other than the precompile provider call. Depth check first (depth above initial depth plus 1024 gives CallTooDeep 0x11 with no checkpoint). The checkpoint is the journal length and log length (State+0x30 and +0x48) read before the value transfer. The transfer runs for kinds 0, 2 and 5 (bit mask 0x25: Call, CallCode, StaticCall), not for DelegateCall; a short balance gives OutOfFunds 0x12 with nothing to undo. Then the provider vtable decides precompile or not (aarch64 [evm+0x5d0]+0x38). Empty code gives Stop with full gas. Otherwise run_frame saves and restores the frame checkpoint and finish_call_message_run calls State::rollback when the stop byte is 4 or more, which is every status except Stop 1, Return 2 and SelfDestruct 3 (InstrStop, interpreter/mod.rs:55-130). On the precompile path, Ok gives Return with no rollback unless gas remaining exceeds the limit (then PrecompileOOG 0x23 with rollback); Revert gives 0x10 with its output and a rollback; OutOfGas gives 0x23 and other halts 0x30, both with empty output and a rollback; database and fatal errors roll back and return an error. execute_message (aarch64 0x42b0fbc) also rolls back to its own checkpoint on any host error. In the CALL body the success word pushed is (stop - 1) < 3, gas comes back for the stop mask 0xf000e (success and the four frame-revert codes), refunds merge only when stop is 3 or less, FatalExternalError 0x34 propagates, min(output length, out size) bytes are copied to memory, and the return data buffer is set to the output for every non-fatal stop: the revert data after REVERT, empty after a halt or out of gas. Task 3: does a TIP-20 transfer made by a precompile inside a frame that later reverts get undone by the same journal, and can a precompile open a path that commits after a revert status. Result: Yes it is undone, and no such path was found. Tempo's precompile storage provider writes through the evm2 account handle and slot handle (sstore_journal: state.account(), account.storage(), slot.write(), storage/evm.rs:185-211), so every TIP-20 balance write is a StorageChange entry in the journal that execute_call_message's rollback pops. Its own checkpoint and checkpoint_revert call State::checkpoint and State::rollback (storage/evm.rs:743-759), and nested calls from a precompile are refused while any precompile checkpoint is open (storage/evm.rs:677-693), so a precompile cannot commit a callee and then roll back around it. The live run below shows the effect on the deployed PoolManager. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d67483a4c21c39cd84d019a45c877ba792c8e2/crates/precompiles/src/storage/evm.rs

- Tempo, cycle 31. Writer side of AccountChange entries in evm2 35aa3280: when is the entry recorded and pushed, and can a handle override what a revert restores. Result: AccountHandle records one snapshot of present and flags before its first mutation and pushes it when the handle is dropped (state/account.rs:286-372). A handle borrows State mutably, so none can be held across a nested call, and every frame's changes land after its checkpoint. override_balance and override_nonce change the live value and the snapshot together (state/account.rs:709-731), so a revert would not undo them; no call to them appears outside tests in the evm2 and Tempo files read here, and the rest of both trees was not searched. On Tempo the native value the arm restores is not an asset the PoolManager can hold: the node refuses value transfers (earlier cycles), so pools on Tempo hold TIP-20 balances, whose undo is the StorageChange arm. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/35aa32800b147b00e616d4e1869a3835aa86701f/crates/evm2/src/evm/state/account.rs
- Tempo, cycle 31. One-line token and fee note met in passing. Result: Refund mode of TIP-1060 pays refunds from the storage-owning account's credits, which for PoolManager slots are the PoolManager's credits; that is gas and was treated in earlier cycles (L-264 and the Refund mode item), not a token balance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d67483a4c21c39cd84d019a45c877ba792c8e2/crates/precompiles/src/storage_credits/accounting.rs

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-gcc-real-arith)

- Monad, cycle 32. Task 1 (L-1222). Every MUL, DIV, MOD and MULMOD instruction of the 128 un-entered value blocks, 33 sites in blocks 0x28f2, 0x2907, 0x4f43, 0x51cf, 0x56cb, 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58db and 0x5d71: 16 non-literal MUL, 2 MUL with a literal operand, 6 non-literal DIV, 2 DIV with the literal 1,000,000, 1 MOD, and 6 MULMOD (modulus 2^128 at 0x576a and 2^96 at 0x586f, both inline; the all-ones modulus at 0x58c1; 1,000,000 at 0x57f1; a run-time modulus at 0x51de and 0x58eb). The cycle 31 hook state before each site (research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/out/states.jsonl) was laid out as the gcc 15.2.0 build reads the Stack, including the deferred comparison at 0x5d78 (Stack+0x128 and +0x130 hold raw StackElem pointers, +0x138 the Comparison, read from Stack::discharge_deferred_comparison 0x3ac3b0). The package's whole Emitter::mul(long) 0x3838e0, udiv(long) 0x383a20, umod(long) 0x387840 or mulmod(long) 0x387590 then ran in the cycle 27 x86 model with its whole direct-call closure from the package text (137 functions, out/closure.txt: mul_optimized, div_optimized<false>, mod_optimized<false>, modop_optimized<mulmod> with mul_mod2, MulEmitter, call_runtime_impl, spill_all_caller_save_general_regs, spill_avx_reg_range, RuntimeImpl::pass, mov_arg with its jump table, RuntimeImpl::call_impl, Stack::pop, push and alloc_stack_offset, the allocators). Only asmjit _emitI, RoData::add4, add8 and add32, operator new and delete, memcpy, memset and the libstdc++ tree routines are stubs. Every asmjit call was recorded. The model gained vshufps (VEX.128, used by MulEmitter::mul_sequence<false> at 0x3a1a92) and indirect jmp and call through a register or memory operand. Result: All 33 gcc streams equal the clang listing body at the same pc up to consistent renaming. At 0x5934 the clang listing uses limb orders r10, r11, r8, r9 and rdi, rcx, rsi, rdx for the second and third register rows, which earlier blocks leave behind and the hook log does not carry; with that table read from the listing's stores the gcc stream is equal. At all 33 sites the gcc Stack after the call equals the clang hook state before the next instruction in every element location, available offset, free register queue, delta and deferred comparison. 66,000 runs of the gcc streams (2,000 per site, seed 3232, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath shaped words, denominators and moduli with a top limb of 0, 1 and all ones, edge words) gave no wrong result and no overwritten live word against pyevm.py (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/realarith.json). The runtime calls in these runs executed the package's own helper text, so the helpers' real register and memory clobbers acted on the live state. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/scripts/realarith.py ; research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/realarith.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/closure.txt ; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:21-99
- Monad, cycle 32. Task 2. At each of the 30 runtime calls the gcc streams make (the two power-of-two MULMOD sites and the literal MUL at 0x58f9 emit no call): which registers carry the arguments and the result pointer, what is saved before the call, whether vector registers survive it, whether the stack is aligned, and whether the result pointer may alias an argument (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/task2.json). Result: Every call is lea rsi, lea rdx (and lea rcx for MULMOD) to the operand slots [rbp+32k] or to RoData constants, lea rdi to the result slot that Stack::alloc_stack_offset returned, then call qword ptr [ROD+k] whose 8-byte constant is the helper address (0x44e160 monad_vm_runtime_mul, 0x397250 runtime::udiv, 0x397710 runtime::umod, 0x398a70 runtime::mulmod). Stack::spill_all_caller_save_general_regs stores the r8 to r11 and rcx, rsi, rdx, rdi rows of every live element before the call; after the emit only the callee-saved r12 to r15 row holds live words in general registers. udiv, umod and mulmod pass spill_avx 1 (bytes at 0x383a9e, 0x3878be, 0x38760e), spill every AVX register and emit vzeroupper; mul passes 0 (0x38395e) and keeps live AVX words in ymm across the call (0x56dd keeps ymm0 and ymm1), which is safe because monad_vm_runtime_mul (0x44e160 to 0x44e1f6) uses only rax, rcx, rdx, r8 to r13, saves r12 and r13, and has no vector instruction. The emitted code does not move rsp around the call; udiv, umod, mulmod and udivrem<4,4> realign their own frames with and rsp,-32 before their vmovdqa stores, and mul uses no stack, so the native frame's alignment cannot change a result. The result pointer equals an argument pointer at 14 sites (for example 0x5920 rdi = rsi, 0x5901 rdi = rdx, 0x51de rdi = rcx, the modulus); mul reads every limb of an operand before writing that limb, and the other helpers copy their operands first, and the runs at those sites and 27,000 aliased standalone helper runs agree with Python. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/task2.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/fn/000000000044e160.s ; research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/fn/00000000003aca10.s ; research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/fn/000000000037ede0.s
- Monad, cycle 32. Task 3. The runtime helpers interpreted from the package text in the x86 model: monad_vm_runtime_mul 0x44e160, runtime::udiv 0x397250, runtime::umod 0x397710, runtime::mulmod 0x398a70, and what they call, udivrem<4,4> 0x2125b0, udivrem<8,4> 0x398560, monad::mulmod 0x3988b0 and knuth_div 0x212400. 12,000 operand sets per helper (seed 3233): the 27 by 27 grid of edge words (0, 1, 2, 3, 2^64, 2^128, 2^192, 2^255 and neighbours, 2^96, 2^160, 1e6, MIN_SQRT_PRICE, MAX_SQRT_PRICE), FullMath products of 128 to 256 bit words, SqrtPriceMath shapes (liquidity << 96 with 160-bit prices), SwapMath fee shapes, products just below and above 2^256, and denominators and moduli with a top limb of 0, 1, all ones and 2^63. Each helper also ran with the result pointer equal to each argument pointer (6,000 to 9,000 cases). Results were compared with Python integers. Result: 48,000 standalone cases and 27,000 aliased cases, 0 mismatches, 0 stops (research/network-risk/cycles/032/theme-monad-gcc-real-arith.work/out/model/helpers.json). The helpers use BMI2 mulx (23), shlx and shrx, LZCNT, the 64-bit div (7), shld and shrd, and AVX2 vinserti128, vpinsrq, vmovq, vmovdqa, vmovdqu, vpxor and vzeroupper; none uses ADX adcx or adox. A contract placed by code override writes TSTORE or SSTORE values at depth 0, then at depths 1 to 4 in a chain of calls, and makes the frame at depth d = 1, 2 or 3 end by REVERT, INVALID, an endless loop under a 300,000 gas cap, or entry by STATICCALL, with a successful child write inside the failing frame. The parent reads the four slots back. 15 transient and 15 persistent cases per endpoint, each compared with tools/opdiff/pyevm.py on the same code and calldata (the gas case run there as INVALID, since pyevm has no gas). Result: Every answer equals the reference on every build that answered: Arc 37812c61 (rpc.mainnet.arc.io and QuickNode, 60 cases), 8e8edb7a (both dRPC hosts, 60), 602eed3b (PublicNode, 30), db2d22c1 (Blockdaemon, 30); Elysium nitro vlocal go1.25.12 (Kinetiq and Conduit, 60) and dRPC (30); HyperEVM 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet' (official and hypurrscan, 60), nanoreth b92ad36 (HyperLend and Stakely, 60), dRPC 27; MegaETH mega-reth v2.3.1-4499c42 (30), v2.2.1-7d0dbf3 (30), dRPC 28; BNB Chain dataseed v1.8.2 and 4e1c8247 (90), reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f (30), 48 Club 9b93ce23 and 132104cd (30). The five dRPC requests that did not answer were HTTP 429 refusals, not answers. In every failed frame the slots return to the parent's words (0xAA00+i), writes of frames above the failing one are kept, and a static frame's TSTORE or SSTORE is refused. These are the semantics that Lock, NonzeroDeltaCount, CurrencyDelta and CurrencyReserves rely on. - MegaETH, HyperEVM, cycle 33. Task 5: for each operand class that neither closed producer has executed in a checked block, can any PoolManager instruction receive operands of that class, and so compute something from a wrong word there?. Result: No. The classes neither producer executed are SDIV of -2^255 by -1, MOD by zero, SMOD by zero or by a negative divisor, MULMOD and ADDMOD by modulus zero, SIGNEXTEND with an index of 31 or more, BYTE with an index of 32 or more, and SAR by 256 or more; HyperEVM also has no SHL by 256 or more. The PoolManager text cannot produce any of them. The only signed divisors are tick spacings (TickBitmap.sol:24, :26, :57, :64 and Pool.sol:577-578), which PoolManager.sol:119-120 holds between 1 and 32767 at initialize and which reach later calls only through the pool id of an initialized key. Every MOD and assembly DIV divisor is nonzero by an earlier check: UnsafeMath.sol:14 is called with liquidity after SqrtPriceMath.sol:134 and :163 reject zero, with sqrtPriceAX96 (at least MIN_SQRT_PRICE) and with numerator1 / sqrtPX96 + amount after SqrtPriceMath.sol:37 returns on amount 0; UnsafeMath.sol:26 runs only after Pool.sol:401 and :468 test liquidity; FullMath.sol:35 and :48 run after FullMath.sol:30 requires denominator > prod1; FullMath.sol:112 runs after mulDiv has already required a nonzero denominator. MULMOD moduli are not(0), a checked denominator or the constant Q96 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:252). SIGNEXTEND indices are the constants 1, 2 and 15, SAR counts are the constants 8, 128 and 255, and the BYTE indices at BitMath.sol:22 and :45 are masked with and(0x1f, ...), so they are always 0 to 31. The run-time shift counts are bitPos values of at most 255 (TickBitmap.sol:71), masked values, BitMath counts below 256, and getTickAtSqrtPrice counts derived from a most significant bit of at most 159. The PoolManager bytecode has no ADDMOD (out/pm-inventory.json). A wrong word in these classes can therefore change no amount, tick or revert of the PoolManager, and nobody loses through it. Evidence: src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:19-28; src/PoolManager.sol:119-120; src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:37,52,104,134,163,208,252; src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:12-27; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-48,112; src/libraries/BitMath.sol:22,45; src/libraries/Pool.sol:401,468,575-581
- MegaETH, cycle 33. Task 2: PoolManager instructions that no validated MegaETH block has executed with an operand of the class their source line can produce, mapped to src/ through the solc source map of the build (cycles/012/theme-bytecode-coverage.work/srcmap.py, whose runtime equals build/PoolManager.json), and whether one swap, liquidity change or donate reaches them. Result: Wide-product MULMOD sites without a validated run at that pc: the getAmount1Delta copy of mulDiv (pc 22585, FullMath.sol:24, and pc 22639, FullMath.sol:48, reached from SqrtPriceMath.sol:250) and the round-up MULMOD at pc 23094 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:252), which need liquidity times the price difference of 2^256 or more; the exact-input fee copy (pcs 22445 and 22513, SwapMath.sol:65) for an amountRemaining near 2^236; the Position fee copy (pcs 22316 and 22378, Position.sol:94-96) and the amount above uint160 copy (pcs 22721 and 22763, SqrtPriceMath.sol:97), whose results are only computed in transactions that revert at Pool.sol:192 or Pool.sol:455 and :459 (cycle 24); and the mulDivRoundingUp copy at pc 20958 (FullMath.sol:112 via SqrtPriceMath.sol:105). An ordinary account reaches the getAmount1Delta and fee copies with one swap or one liquidity change in a pool of its own token, as cycle 25 showed through eth_call on all 21 networks with the reference words. The same opcode with the same modulus form has validated wide runs at other pcs (pc 22892 68988 runs in 13570 blocks, pc 22921 68988 in 13570, pc 23678 65106 in 12769), and the producer computed the class in other contracts too. Other sites without the class are unreachable for it: SAR at pc 6059 unpacks feesAccrued, which is never negative (PoolManager.sol:171), SIGNEXTEND at pc 16661 and SDIV/SMOD divisors take tick spacings of at least 1, and the SHL and SHR sites take constant counts or counts bounded below 256 (masked bitPos, BitMath and getTickAtSqrtPrice counts). A wrong word at a wide MULMOD site would change amount1 of one swap step or of a liquidity change in that pool by the error; with liquidity times price difference of 2^256 or more, amount1 exceeds 2^160 units, so currency1 must be a token the account mints itself, and the amount that a wrong word changes directly is in that token. The full list is in out/pm-unexecuted-megaeth.json and out/pm-sites.json. - HyperEVM, cycle 33. Task 4 (L-1242): do the HyperEVM replicas nanoreth b92ad36 (rpc.hyperlend.finance) and f0cad31 (rpc.purroofgroup.com) re-execute each block, what do they compare with the producer, and what do they do on a mismatch?. Result: They re-execute every block through the reth engine (block import calls engine.new_payload and turns an Invalid status into a BlockImportError, src/node/network/block_import/service.rs:96-106 at b92ad36, :102 and :143 at f0cad31) and then compare gas used, the receipts root of the receipts with nonzero cumulative gas, the logs bloom and the requests hash with the header (src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs:12-66, called from src/node/consensus/mod.rs:163 at b92ad36 and :161 at f0cad31). They compare no state root. The hl-archive-node reth fork they pin removes that check: at rev c6e0a06 (b92ad36) crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_validator.rs:890-892 discards the computed root with the comment that HyperEVM headers carry a zero state root, and at rev 14509628 (f0cad31) lines 626-627 set the root to zero before comparing it with the header. eth_getBlockByNumber on rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm returns stateRoot 0x00..00 for blocks 33,554,432 and 52,385,694. So a replica rejects a block whose status, gas, logs or bloom differ from the producer, and stops importing there, but it cannot see a storage word that differs without changing a log or gas. This is the measurement behind F-120, which stands. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/b92ad36/src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/reth/c6e0a06b6f2739b63ccd625823d17d333bfdc31b/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_validator.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/reth/14509628ed37e9a9b7110ea855a67f427c4d61fc/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_validator.rs

Whether this theme applies to the other 20 networks. Result: It does not. The terminators, memory emitters and block streams examined here are those of Monad's native compiler, which only Monad's validators run. The other networks execute the PoolManager in their own interpreters, whose jump, comparison and memory handling OPCODES.md checks 1 to 4 cover. Nothing in this unit changes a result for them. Evidence: research/network-risk/OPCODES.md
- Monad, cycle 33. The source lines whose branches these blocks hold, read in this repository: FullMath.mulDiv computes prod0 and prod1 by mulmod with not(0) and sub (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:21-26), requires denominator > prod1 (:30), returns div(prod0, denominator) when prod1 == 0 (:33-37), otherwise subtracts the remainder, factors out twos and multiplies by the Newton inverse (:46-99); mulDivRoundingUp adds one when mulmod(a, b, denominator) != 0 and requires the sum to be non-zero (:111-114). Result: The text does what its comments say. With the branches at :30, :33 and :112 emitted and taken as pyevm.py takes them on Monad's shipped build, no ordinary account can make mulDiv skip the overflow revert, take the 256-bit division on a 512-bit product, or drop a rounding unit. Evidence: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116

Task 2, the new nested dispatch in evm2 7c9f3b6d crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs read line by line: fields at 250-264, enter_execution at 464-473, ExecutionGuard and its Drop at 1301-1324, execute_tx at 1399-1420, the inspected frame entry at 1951-1980, and State::clear_transaction_state at evm/state/mod.rs:564-580. Result: suspended_frames counts frames suspended under a transaction started while one runs and is used only by the assertion in set_initial_call_depth (1144). execute_tx takes current_frame, sets enclosing_refund to 0 and, when running was already true, tells the guard to put back the outer frame pointer and outer refund; Drop restores running, enclosing_refund, current_frame and the counter on return, on error and on unwinding. enclosing_refund only feeds Evm::tx_refunded for inspectors. Nothing in the new code touches the State: the transient map, journal, checkpoints, warm set and logs are the single State of the Evm, exactly as at 35aa3280 (execute_tx at old 1313-1322 only called enter_execution). A transaction dispatched while another runs therefore shares the outer transient map, and its discard or error path calls clear_transaction_state, which clears transient_storage, the journal, the prewarm set and logs of the outer transaction as well. That behaviour is unchanged by the release. It is not reachable on Tempo because no production caller dispatches a transaction while a user transaction runs (next entry). - Tempo, cycle 33. Task 6 (L-1139), the 100 MiB per-frame memory limit and the changed EIP-7702 check. evm2 version/mod.rs:46-47 and 147, evm/config.rs:191-200, interpreter/runtime.rs:513; ethereum/mod.rs:432-450; Tempo tx gas cap in crates/hardfork/src/constants.rs:91 and lib.rs:319-323. Result: The memory limit applies per frame. Reaching 100 MiB needs 3,276,800 words, whose expansion cost 3w + w^2/512 is 20,981,350,400 gas, about 700 times the 30,000,000 transaction cap, so no hook or token frame can hit it before running out of gas, and the PoolManager sees the same failed call it would see for out of gas. The EIP-7702 change is in validate_sender_and_bump_nonce, which checks the transaction sender, not CALL setup; it only rejects a delegated sender when the EIP-7702 feature is off, which is not the case on Tempo's Prague based rules. A delegated account as hook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) or as native take recipient (src/types/Currency.sol:48) runs through the unchanged CALL path. The 575 cycle 26 cases were not rerun because their scripts are not on disk under that cycle's work directory. - Tempo, cycle 33. Transient storage shared between the calls of a 0x76 batch transaction, as a path for one call to inherit another call's unlock. Result: unlock relocks before it returns and requires NonzeroDeltaCount to be zero (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), and a reverted call rolls back its transient writes, so no call of a batch can leave the PoolManager unlocked or with an open delta for the next call. The live probe and callsem rollback cases agree. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114

Every way it ends clears the whole transaction scratch: a handler error clears it in execute_tx (mod.rs:1415-1417), a finalisation error in finish_executed_tx (mod.rs:1041-1043), ExecutedTx::commit calls commit_transaction and then clear_transaction_state (tx.rs:231-237), discard and drop call clear_pending_state (tx.rs:223-228, :365-369), and an EVM-level revert returns Ok and takes the commit or discard path. clear_transaction_state (state/mod.rs:564-580) empties transient_storage, the journal, warm sets, logs and the account overlay. After the inner transaction the outer frame's TLOAD (state/mod.rs:841-843) returns 0 for the lock slot, NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT_SLOT (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10), every currency delta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:18-23) and CURRENCY_SLOT (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:13) in all three outcomes. Calls inside the callback then revert ManagerLocked, and the check in unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:112) reads a count of 0 and accepts debts taken before the inner transaction; on commit the overlay that held the outer transaction's earlier transfers is written to the accepted state, on discard it is dropped, and in both cases the outer journal is gone, so a later revert of the outer frame cannot undo them. This is what a future caller of the path would do. Precompile providers receive &mut Evm (evm/precompile.rs:79-84), so a chain precompile is the place such a caller would appear. The product needs a high price: with one position of maxLiquidityPerTick the step must start at tick 818,728 or above for spacing 1, 647,280 for spacing 60, 339,000 for spacing 1000 (out/bounds.json). There it is cheap. For spacing 1 the cheapest setup found is a pool of two ordinary tokens created by the account itself at tick 818728, one position [818728, 818984] of liquidity 191757530477355301479181766273477, which costs 4070057427382 units of currency0 and nothing of currency1 because the price sits at the lower tick. A swap of currency1 for currency0 with an exact input of 10^18 units then computes amountIn to the target as about 2^160 units at SwapMath.sol:68 and discards it at :69. A modifyLiquidity call that the PoolManager rejects reaches the same 512 bit branch with no tokens at all: the amount1 of a position below the price is computed at Pool.sol:229-236 and then fails toInt128. So the verifier's premise is wrong: the wide branch is open to any account on all 21 networks. Its conclusion still holds for the arithmetic, for a reason it did not give. On a successful call a wide amount1 is never settled. Where the step uses it (amountRemaining at least amountIn), the consumed amount is at least 2^160 and the cast at Pool.sol:452-458 reverts. Where the step discards it, it decides only the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69 or :91, against an amountRemaining below 2^127 for any call that can succeed, so a margin of at least 2^33 separates the two sides. Only a MULMOD answer wrong by a large amount could flip it. A wrong remainder at pc 22639 can do that: FullMath.sol:51-54 subtracts it from the product before the division, so a remainder near 2^256 gives a near-zero quotient. A wrong answer at pc 23094 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:252) changes amount1 by one unit of rounding at most. ## Reading of the source (theme-reth-journal-and-execution-cache)

- Ethereum, cycle 34. Task 2 at reth v2.11.0 (the Ethereum endpoint answered reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc on 2026-11-27): the key of each execution cache entry and where every cached value comes from. Result: Code is keyed by the full 32 byte code hash, storage by the full (Address, StorageKey) pair and accounts by the full address (cached_state.rs lines 963-971), in fixed-cache tables that compare the stored key before returning a value, as cycle 32 recorded. Values enter the cache in three ways only. insert_state writes the final present_value of every slot and the final info of every modified account of an executed block (lines 1133-1206). get_or_try_insert_*_with inserts, on a miss, the value the underlying state provider returns, and only providers built with CacheFillMode::FillOnMiss do that (lines 276-278, 846-941); block execution uses LookupOnly except on the paths payload_validator.rs lines 650-690 name. clear() empties storage and accounts and keeps code, whose hash mapping cannot change (lines 1213-1219). No path inserts a value that a transaction wrote and later reverted, because a speculative execution keeps its writes in its own EVM state and the provider underneath only sees reads. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs
- Ethereum, cycle 34. Task 2 at reth v2.11.0: when the cross-block cache is kept, replaced or dropped after a block. Result: save_cache runs only after every prewarm worker has finished and the Terminate event carries the block output (prewarm.rs lines 653-715). Under the mutex it applies insert_state of the executed block to the checked out cache, waits for the validity signal, and on an insert error or an invalid block takes the stored cache out, so nothing is kept (prewarm.rs lines 468-517). get_cache_for hands a cache out only when no other handle exists and clears it with clear_with_hash when its block hash is not the parent of the new block (lib.rs lines 59-105); a cache still held elsewhere is not reused and a fresh empty one is built (mod.rs lines 501-514). Locally built blocks go through on_inserted_executed_block, which skips the update when the stored hash is not the parent or the cache is in use (mod.rs lines 523-566). A later block therefore starts from either the post-state of its exact parent or an empty cache. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/prewarm.rs
- Ethereum, cycle 34. Task 2 at reth v2.11.0: insert_state for an account created and destroyed in one transaction (EIP-6780), a slot written back to zero, and an account whose code changed through EIP-7702 delegation. Result: A destroyed account whose original info had code clears the whole storage and account cache and returns (cached_state.rs lines 1165-1182); a destroyed account without original code and with no current info is removed from the account cache, and one re-created in the block has its new storage and info written (lines 1183-1203). A slot whose final value is zero is inserted as zero (insert_storage, line 1100) and read back through nonzero_storage_value as absent, which the EVM reads as zero (lines 841-843, 877-910). A delegation changes the account code hash, which insert_account replaces, and the designator bytecode is looked up by its own hash; a code hash missing from the cache goes to the provider. None of these leaves a word that differs from the post-block state. The PoolManager has code and cannot be destroyed, so only the plain write path ever touches its slots. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs
- Ethereum, cycle 34. Task 2 at reth v2.11.0: can a prewarm result, a txpool snapshot or a block access list prefetch put a word into the cache that the state does not hold?. Result: No on any path. Prewarm workers wrap the provider in new_prewarm (FillOnMiss) and insert only what the parent state provider returns (prewarm.rs lines 800-806, 920-928); their EVM writes stay in the worker. The txpool snapshot is a copy of CachedReads, which records only values the inner provider returned (crates/evm/evm/src/cached.rs lines 100-155), is built over the head the worker was started for, and is served only to a block whose parent hash equals it (tree/txpool_prewarm/control.rs lines 50-56). The block access list prefetch takes only the addresses and slot keys from the list and reads their values from the parent state provider (prewarm.rs lines 604-631, bal_prewarm_pool.rs lines 159-199); end_block waits until every worker has drained its queue and dropped its provider before the cache is saved (bal_prewarm_pool.rs lines 108-122). Txpool prewarming and result reuse are off by default (engine primitives config.rs lines 263-286; node args engine.rs lines 392-397, 572-577), and no listed network has block access lists active. A speculative result is reused only after every recorded storage read matches and every account read matches or is rebased on balance alone (reuse.rs lines 223-348), as cycle 31 recorded. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/prewarm.rs
- Optimism, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, Zora, Worldchain, cycle 34. Task 2 at the ethereum-optimism/reth revisions behind the OP Stack endpoints: op-v2.6.0-2 (3c5f2f1; op-reth v2.8.1, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, world-chain v2.8.2) and op-v2.7.0-2 (ce8cfb1; op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4). The PoolManager keeps the lock (Lock.sol:8), the nonzero delta count (NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-32), the deltas (CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39) and the synced currency and reserves (CurrencyReserves.sol:11-29) in transient storage and pool state, positions and ERC-6909 balances in storage; unlock requires the count to be zero before relocking (PoolManager.sol:103-113), and a failed hook call reverts the PoolManager call (Hooks.sol:131-137). Every inner revert in the lifted op-reth and Base journals restored each of these words to its pre-frame value, kept committed writes of inner frames until an outer revert, and left the original values right, so a hook, token or callback that reverts an inner frame cannot leave pool state changed while the deltas that pay for it are undone on these builds. This holds for the builds whose journal was lifted (op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and Base v1.5.6). The journal of world-chain v2.8.2 and of conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 was not lifted; on World Chain, Zora and OP Mainnet a live call with a state override showed inner reverts restoring the transient and storage words. It links the generic x86-64 CRYPTOGAMS routine of keccak-asm (keccak1600-x86_64.pl, the lane complementing variant with six not instructions around each permutation): __KeccakF1600 0x6f67300, KeccakF1600 0x6f675e0, SHA3_absorb 0x6f67680, SHA3_squeeze 0x6f67760, iotas at 0x6f67840. That is the only copy of the round constants in .text (the three other copies are in .rodata for the pure Rust keccak crate), so no AVX2, AVX-512VL or ARMv8 routine is present. sha3-asm 0.1.6 build.rs selects keccak1600-avx512vl.pl only when the target has avx512vl and otherwise keccak1600-x86_64.pl. KECCAK256 is entry 0x20 of the four 256-entry instruction tables at 0x70cb168, 0x70cb968, 0x70cc168 and 0x70cc968; the handlers 0x3bde4a0 and 0x3bde660 return the empty hash constant for length 0 and otherwise call 0x3b6e6c0. That function is alloy-primitives keccak256 with the global cache: lengths 1 to 87 hash with rapidhash (0x3770440, seed 0x3841f612376719ec) into a static table at 0x71fe600 of 131,072 buckets of 128 bytes; a hit needs the bucket word equal to the tag with the lock bit clear, the stored length byte equal to the length, and bcmp of all input bytes equal to zero; other lengths go to 0x2147080 (absorb of whole 136 byte blocks, then pad 0x01 at the tail and 0x80 at byte 135, absorb, squeeze 32 bytes). The verifier of cycle 34 was right that asm-keccak and keccak-cache-global are on; the binary now shows it directly. ## Reading of the source (theme-sync-settle-credit-table)

- all 21 networks, cycle 35. Table row 0, the source both rows rest on. Which places in src turn a balance change that no caller paid into a credit, and which turn a transfer into a loss. Result: Only two. sync(X) stores X.balanceOf(PoolManager) in transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), and _settle credits the caller with balanceOfSelf minus that stored value in checked arithmetic, then resets the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:357-362). For address(0), sync only resets the currency and _settle credits msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:281-283, 352-354); the native balance is never read for settlement. take debits the caller the named amount and calls transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-86). The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function (no receive or fallback declaration in src/, searched this cycle), so native value enters it only through settle, settleFor, SELFDESTRUCT, block level credits and protocol mints. Consequences that hold on every network: (a) a balance rise between sync and settle of an ERC-20 is credited to whoever calls settle, whatever caused it; (b) a fall between sync and settle makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert, which only stops the caller's own settle; (c) a native rise is never credited; (d) a rise that lands before sync is inside the reserves sync records; (e) a rise that lands in another transaction cannot fall between sync and settle, because the synced slots are transient (A1, checked on every network in earlier cycles). So the only rows that matter are features that run inside a user transaction and raise the balanceOf of an ERC-20 currency the PoolManager holds, and features that make a transfer move a different amount than it reports. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-288; src/PoolManager.sol:349-364; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297; src/types/Currency.sol:44-52; src/types/Currency.sol:55-86; src/types/Currency.sol:90-96; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32

- Arc, cycle 35. Table row 4, Arc USDC face rounding, now with the forced send tested live (the earlier clearance said SELFDESTRUCT on Arc was untested). At block 33,459,430 the PoolManager held 2,446,663,383,620,124,987,809,451 wei, a remainder of 124,987,809,451 below the next face unit. One bracket: sync(0x3600), forced inflow of 875,012,190,549 wei, settle, native take of the same 875,012,190,549 wei (scripts/arcround.py, out/arcround.json). Result: The mechanism is live and unprofitable. The face rose by 1 unit, settle credited 1 face unit (10^12 wei), and the native delta was -875,012,190,549, so the round gained 124,987,809,451 wei, 0.000000125 USDC, taken from the native remainder that belongs to native claims. The gain per round is below 10^12 wei because the face is floor(balance / 10^12). The forced send alone needs a CREATE (32,000 gas) or a call to a funded contract that self destructs (at least about 7,600 gas), and the block base fee read at that block was 20 gwei, the floor Arc documents, so the forced send of one round costs at least 1.5 x 10^14 wei, more than 150 times the largest possible gain of 10^12 wei and more than 1,200 times the gain of this round. Arc does not serve eth_simulateV1 (method not supported), so the gas of the bracket was not measured; the bound uses the forced send only. web3_clientVersion answered arc/v1 before and after. Can the debit, the refund or a sponsor charge change balanceOf(PoolManager) inside a user transaction. Result: Nothing. Celo debits and credits st.msg.From, the transaction sender (celo_state_transition.go, fetched this session), before and after execution, and an earlier cycle saw debitGasFees refuse every non VM caller. Tempo collects the fee from the fee payer before execution and credits the refund to the same fee payer, and a fee payer must sign (spec-fee.md, fetched this session). Arc charges native USDC to the sender. The PoolManager has code and no key, so it is never a sender or a fee payer, and none of these debits or credits runs between a sync and a settle. The sponsor rows are untestable by eth_call, because eth_call charges no fee; they rest on the client source and the specification. F-144 records a Celo refund quirk that pays the sender only. A deposit mints its value to its from account before its own execution, and the mint stays even if execution fails (deposits.html, fetched this session); a deposit is its own transaction, so it cannot fall between a sync and a settle of another one. Under Lagoon's sequencer defined metering the refund is credited to tx.from in a post execution transaction appended at the end of the block (sdm.html, fetched this session). The PoolManager is never a deposit sender or a transaction sender, F-140 records the governance path that can make it one. Lagoon is not active, so the refund row is untestable until 11 January 2027. - all 21 networks, cycle 35. Table rows 12 and 13, a change between a take and the settle that pays for it, and a change inside a hook callback. Result: A sync placed before a take of the same currency records the higher balance, so the settle after the take reverts on the checked subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 unless the caller repays more than it took; this stops only the caller's own transaction (and the shared transaction case of F-071). A sync placed after the take records the lower balance and the repayment is credited exactly, as row 6 shows live. A hook runs inside the same transaction as the swap or liquidity call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-157), so it can trigger only the in transaction rows 1, 3 and 4, whose credit is the forced value the triggering party paid itself (or the Arc dust of row 4). Relays that deliver someone else's bridge payment to the PoolManager inside a caller's sync and settle are F-137 and were not retested. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:357-362; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297; research/network-risk/cycles/035/theme-sync-settle-credit-table.work/out/check.json

For the PoolManager this means the following. An unlock opened in one call must relock before that call returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), or the call reverts and the batch with it, so no call inherits an unlock. A sync in one call leaves the synced currency and reserves set (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol), and a later call of the same batch by the same account that unlocks and settles is credited balanceOf(PoolManager) minus the synced reserves (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). Between the two calls only the batch's own calls run and no other account's transaction can interleave, so the credit is what that account itself sent, the same as one contract doing sync and settle in one transaction on Ethereum. A settle or sync in between resets or overwrites the slot. No other user can be charged. ## Reading of the source (theme-erigon-main-frame-cache)

- Ethereum, cycle 36. Task 1: where the stamp is defined and every place that changes it, at erigon main (0ae25bfbdaee8653f1a97c8a4ad844fba24106d3, version 3.9.0-dev in db/version/app.go:33-36) and at v3.8.2. Result: ReadStamp is in execution/state/read_paths.go (main :1573-1587, v3.8.2 :1804-1818). Cycle 35 could not find it because it guessed the wrong file names; sourcegraph's index of the repository found it. These change the stamp. SetState pushes storageChange unless prev == value (intra_block_state.go:1537-1561; in v3.8.2, stateObject.SetState state_object.go:238-279 and setStateVersioned :1856-1880). A same-value write needs no bump. Transient storage pushes transientStorageChange when the value changes (transient_storage.go:52-64). Self-destruct pushes selfdestructChange (:1623-1671). Account creation pushes createObjectChange or resetObjectChange. Access-list warming is journalled (:2385-2398), and SLOAD's gas phase warms before the read whose stamp it stores. revert truncates and bumps the epoch, and Reset or EndTransaction bumps the epoch (journal.go:116-157, intra_block_state.go:2306-2314). In v3.8.2, updateAccount also bumps the epoch at finalization (:2599). The journal is one per IntraBlockState, so a write by another frame at the same address, by a DELEGATECALL frame running other code on the same storage, or at any other address moves the stamp the same way. There is no in-place edit of a journal entry and no coalescing of writes (journal.go push and every constructor append). These paths write without a journal entry. SetStorage (:1566-1593) is used only for debugging and state overrides before execution, and in v3.8.2 it goes through journalled fakeStorage. SetIncarnation (:1597-1607) has callers only in genesis writing, t8n, test utilities and the state layer, none of them the vm (sourcegraph search). In the parallel executor the stamp ignores versionMap. A repeat read returns the first read's value, which is the value the read set records, and Block-STM validation covers it. Funds are not affected. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erigontech/erigon/main/execution/state/read_paths.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erigontech/erigon/main/execution/state/journal.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erigontech/erigon/main/execution/state/intra_block_state.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erigontech/erigon/main/execution/state/transient_storage.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erigontech/erigon/v3.8.2/execution/state/state_object.go
- Ethereum, cycle 36. Task 2 (L-1298): the cache, transcribed line by line into Python (scripts/cachemodel.py), on sequences (a) to (h) plus c2, c3 and a transient-storage case, and on 20000 random frame trees (seed 3620261127), each compared with the state the reads should see. Result: There was no stale word in any sequence. In the random trees there were 185126 reads, 22124 cache hits and 0 stale reads. The sequences were: (a) a nested write by the same contract; (b) the nested frame reverting; (c) a deeper frame reverting only itself; (d) a write through DELEGATECALL; (e) two entries in use, then a third slot evicting one; (f) a slot written back to its original value; (g) reads in a STATICCALL frame; (h) sibling frames reusing the parked context. Why the epoch is not needed inside a transaction: a frame stores its entries at journal length L. A revert can only truncate to a snapshot that some live frame took at or after L, so if the length returns to L, entries 0 to L-1 are unchanged and the state is the same. The epoch matters at Reset. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/036/theme-erigon-main-frame-cache.work/out/seqs.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/036/theme-erigon-main-frame-cache.work/scripts/seqs.py

The nested work is a swap, swaps both ways, a donate, an add and remove of the same position (storage written back), a nested list that reverts, or unlock-free calls (initialize of another pool, approve, setOperator, transfer, extsload). Result: Every SLOAD value, every SSTORE, the returned record of every call (deltas, and extsload reads of slot0, liquidity and fee growth after each step) and the final storage were equal in all 400 scenarios. - Celo, X Layer, cycle 36. Task 3: journal of the Celo and X Layer binaries (SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, checkpoint, commit, checkpoint_revert), first by cmp_journal.py against op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, then by reading the crate source each binary names. Result: cmp_journal.py found 0 normalised function hashes in common with op-reth for either binary (X Layer 98 storage-path functions, Celo 120), because the revm-context versions differ, so nothing carries over from the cycle 35 run. The source each binary names was read instead: celo-org/revm bd28f94 crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs (checkpoint records log, journal and selfdestruct lengths and increments depth; commit only decrements depth; checkpoint_revert truncates logs and replays journal entries in reverse; tstore journals the previous value only when it changes and removes on zero) and entry.rs (StorageChanged restores present_value to had_value; TransientStorageChange removes the key when had_value is zero and reinserts it otherwise). revm-context 18.0.3 from crates.io, which X Layer embeds, has the same checkpoint, commit, revert and tstore text apart from const qualifiers. This matches what src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39 and src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-20 assume. The machine code of these routines was not run in rethj.py, so the 2,000 nested-frame sequences of the task were not run; see the lead. The closure holds 125 functions and 17,736 instructions, and every instruction pair is equal once absolute addresses are masked. The one difference is at 0x42b4778, where the T7 gate in front of the TIP-1060 accounting reads the spec byte at context offset 0x611 instead of 0x605 and still compares it with 11. That is the change cycle 35 called the SSTORE gas check. It moves one field read and changes no gas rule, matching the 12 byte shift that cycle 35 saw in the CALL path. The rollback jump table moved from 0x65fe30 to 0x662dec, and its four journal arms point to the relocated arms. The Tempo source at c0c9372, the commit that rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz reports, has the same SSTORE order: static check, EIP-2200 sentry, the 100 gas static charge, skip_cold_load against ColdStorageAdditionalCost, host sstore, then sstore_storage_credits from T7, then dynamic gas and refund. - Tempo, cycle 36. Task 1, the TIP-1060 credit path: whether it can change the PoolManager's stored word, skip its journal entry or make a write fail that Ethereum would accept with the same gas. Read in the v1.19.2 x86_64 disassembly from 0x42b46b8 to the handler exit, and in accounting.rs at c0c9372. Result: The credit code starts after the write and its StorageChange entry are done (0x42b46b8). It works on stack copies of the present and new words (rsp+0x80 to 0xbf). It tests T7 (spec byte at least 11), then whether the write crosses zero, then that the destination is not 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 (the constant 0x6010 at 0x42b4809). It charges the warm read and, when the credit slot is cold, 2,000 more. It reads and writes only the slot uint256(bytes32(PoolManager)) of 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 and its transient word, through the journaled host routines. The PoolManager's slot pointer is dead by then (r12 is reused as the stop code). The figures for a PoolManager write are 100 gas plus 2,000 when cold on every zero crossing. A clear adds 1 credit to the PoolManager and costs 2,900 more when the credit slot is still clean in the transaction (SstoreResetWithoutColdLoadCost). A creation in the PoolManager's default Refund mode is charged 245,000 (0x3bd08 at 0x42b4dd8 and 0x42b50f8) and records one pending refund for the end of the transaction. A failure inside the credit code returns OutOfGas (stop code 0x20 at 0x42b4844) or a fatal error for an invalid credit state. The first halts the frame, and the frame's checkpoint is rolled back as for any out-of-gas stop. The credit balance is a saturating u64 and the transient state is written only by the precompile, so the fatal path cannot be reached from a PoolManager call. On Ethereum the same write costs at most 22,100 gas. A call with gas sized for Ethereum can therefore run out of gas on Tempo for a zero to non-zero write, which is the gas difference earlier cycles recorded, and the write is then undone. No path changes the word, skips its entry or keeps a write whose frame failed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/c0c9372/crates/precompiles/src/storage_credits/accounting.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/c0c9372/crates/precompiles/src/storage_credits/mod.rs ; research/network-risk/cycles/036/theme-tempo-v1192-storage-lift.work/build/x64v2_42b3290.s

- Worldchain, Zora, cycle 36. What in src/ would compute or decide something else if these journals kept a transient credit while the token transfer rolled back. Result: Nothing differs on these builds. The deltas are transient words written by tload and tstore in CurrencyDelta.applyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:34-40), the count by NonzeroDeltaCount (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:18-33), the lock by Lock (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-20), and unlock reverts unless the count is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:104-113). A settle in an inner frame credits the caller through _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-361) and _accountDelta; if that frame reverts, the lifted World Chain and Zora journals restore the delta word, the count and the synced currency and reserves to their pre-frame values together with the token balance, in every one of the 22114 reverts run and in the 400 live probes. A committed inner frame keeps its writes until an outer revert undoes them, as revm specifies. So an ordinary account cannot keep a credit from a reverted settle, a reverted take or mint cannot leave a debit erased, and no ERC-6909 balance or pool slot can survive the revert that undoes the payment for it on these builds. Evidence: src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:34-40

- HyperEVM, cycle 37. Shapes that no covered block contains, and whether any line of src/ can produce them. Result: Absent: MOD by zero, SMOD by a negative divisor, SMOD by zero, SDIV of -2^255 by -1, ADDMOD and MULMOD with modulus zero, SIGNEXTEND with index 31 or more, BYTE with index 32 or more, SAR of a non-negative value by 256 or more, EXP with exponent 256 or more, and MCOPY with overlapping ranges. None can come from src/. Every MOD in src/ is UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:13) whose divisors are liquidity, guarded nonzero at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:134-140 and :163-169, or numerator1/sqrtP + amount with sqrtP nonzero. Every SDIV and SMOD divides by tickSpacing, which is at least 1 (src/PoolManager.sol:120, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:19-21, src/libraries/Pool.sol:575-577). The MULMOD moduli are not(0), a denominator that src/libraries/FullMath.sol:30 requires to exceed prod1, or Q96 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252). SIGNEXTEND indices are the constants 2 and 15 and SAR shifts the constants 8, 128 and 255 (src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:24-69, src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:38, src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:219). BYTE indices are masked with 0x1f (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:22, :45). src/ has no EXP. The two compiler MCOPY sites of the PoolManager (pc 9186 and 9400) copy an ABI bytes value into a newly allocated buffer above it, and every mined run there had disjoint ranges. Evidence: src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:134-140
- HyperEVM, cycle 37. Task 2: whether the counted blocks are the producer blocks. Result: For 1001 blocks (block 52,363,132 plus 500 of the 2,406 PoolManager blocks and 500 of the newest 50,000, drawn with Python random.seed(37); list in research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-hyperevm-producer-census.work/data/hdr-list-sample.txt) the replica header fields receiptsRoot, gasUsed and logsBloom were compared with eth_getBlockByNumber on the official endpoint rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm (client "hyperliquid evm Mainnet" before and after each group): 1001 equal, 0 differ, 0 not fetched. The official endpoint allows 100 requests per minute (https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/rate-limits-and-user-limits, fetched this cycle), so the other covered blocks were not compared one by one; for them the replica acceptance rule (nanoreth refuses a block whose gas used, receipts root or logs bloom differs from the producer header) is the evidence, and the replica fetches the producer block itself. 0 batch refusals for rate limits were retried. The F-120 limit stands: storage writes are not compared because headers carry a zero state root. Evidence: https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm
