- HyperEVM, cycle 37. Task 4: what a wrong word at each never-executed site would change, who would lose, and whether a replica would refuse the block. Result: A wrong getAmount1Delta or fee word changes amountIn or amountOut of a step and the comparison at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:69, then the Swap amounts (src/PoolManager.sol:241-250) and the token Transfer logs of settlement, so a replica would refuse that block. A wide fee or getAmount1Delta amount that is used reverts at the int128 casts (src/libraries/Pool.sol:452-458), and a discarded one only decides a comparison with a margin of at least 2^33 (cycle 34). Sites whose result reaches storage and no log in the same transaction: fee growth global (src/libraries/Pool.sol:404-405 and :446-448, and donate at :474-477), feeGrowthOutside on a tick cross (src/libraries/Pool.sol:536-537 and crossTick), the tick bitmap word (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol flipTick), tick liquidityGross and liquidityNet (src/libraries/Pool.sol:543-557), pool liquidity after a liquidity change (src/libraries/Pool.sol:226), position liquidity and feeGrowthInsideLast (src/libraries/Position.sol:88, :100-101) and protocolFeesAccrued (src/ProtocolFees.sol:68, reached only with a protocol fee set by governance). A wrong word there would pass the replicas until a later transaction read it and produced a different log; then the replicas would halt and the producer chain would continue. Losers would be the LPs of the pool (fee growth, liquidity) or later swappers (bitmap, ticks). This needs a fault in the producer, which only its operator controls (F-120). Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:404-405
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, cycle 37. Whether the HyperEVM producer census applies to the other 20 networks. Result: It does not. On the other 20 networks the block producer is either the public client that earlier cycles read and ran, or, on MegaETH, a closed producer whose state root the public validator reproduces (cycles 33 and 35). The bounds from src/ used above hold on all 21. Evidence: research/network-risk/OPCODES.md

## Reading of the source (theme-native-face-inflows)

- Celo, Polygon, Arc, Optimism, Zora, cycle 37. Source row: which entries of the PoolManager accept native value, and what a face credit is made of. Result: Only settle and settleFor are payable (src/PoolManager.sol:300, 305). No contract in src declares receive or fallback, so a value call with empty calldata or an unknown selector reverts in the dispatcher. sync(face) stores the face address and balanceOf(PoolManager) in transient slots (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-31). _settle with a face synced reverts on any msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:356) and credits reservesNow minus reservesBefore to the recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:357-363). balanceOfSelf of a face is a call to the face token (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96). A native credit is only ever msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), so native value that arrives without a call to settle is seen by nobody except through a face that a caller has synced in the same transaction. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-288; src/PoolManager.sol:300-307; src/PoolManager.sol:349-364; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-36; src/types/Currency.sol:90-96
- Celo, Polygon, Arc, Optimism, Zora, cycle 37. Row N1, a plain native transfer to the PoolManager (EOA send, CALL with value, a native take by another account naming the PoolManager, MRC20 deposit, StandardBridge finalizeBridgeETH, fee vault withdraw), tested live through the deployed PoolManager on the five face networks. Result: Every such arrival is a CALL into PoolManager code and reverts. Driver by state override at 0x...d21fe035, unlock on the deployed PoolManager, record returned by revert. CALL with value 10^6 wei (10^13 on Arc) and empty calldata, and with selector 0xdeadbeef: ok=0 on all five, PoolManager native balance unchanged. take(address(0), PoolManager, x): reverted with WrappedError(PoolManager, 0x00000000, empty reason, NativeTransferFailed) on all five (src/types/Currency.sol:45-53). Because the payee rejects the value, the paths that end in a value call cannot complete for the PoolManager as recipient: Polygon MRC20.deposit and MRC20._transfer use address.transfer (MRC20.sol lines 44 and 107), OP Stack StandardBridge.finalizeBridgeETH uses SafeCall.call(_to, gasleft(), _amount, empty) and requires success (StandardBridge.sol lines 258-259), and a CrossDomainMessenger replay of such a message reaches the same call (CrossDomainMessenger.sol line 285). A relay message whose calldata is settle() or settleFor(r) does reach the PoolManager: tested as settleFor(X) with value after sync(0), which credited X exactly and left the driver at 0, and after sync(face), which reverted with NonzeroNativeValue 0xb0ec849e. A relayed native payment is therefore credited to the messenger or to the recipient the sender named, never to the account that ran the relay, and a credit to an address that is not the unlock caller leaves NonzeroDeltaCount above zero so that unlock reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Blocks: Celo 83,919,342, Polygon 98,076,417, Arc 33,489,862, OP Mainnet 160,110,665, Zora 54,563,135. Clients before and after: reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb (Celo), bor v2.11.1-private builds a863b8e5cce1 and ebcfea01452d (Polygon, load balanced), arc/v1 v0.8.6-rc1 37812c61 (Arc), op-reth v0.0.0-dev-unknown and v2.8.1-72207294 (OP Mainnet, load balanced), conduit-op-reth/v2.5.1-8f0ccac (Zora). - Celo, cycle 37. Celo row: the transfer precompile at 0xfd called directly, from a contract and from an EOA, in both directions with the PoolManager as from or to; CELO.transfer and transferFrom to the PoolManager between sync(CELO) and settle. Result: The precompile admits only the CELO token as caller (celo-kona transfer.rs lines 51-57, "invalid caller for transfer precompile"). Live: inside the unlock callback 0xfd(from=PoolManager, to=driver, 10^6) and 0xfd(from=driver, to=PoolManager, 10^6) both returned ok=0 and no balance moved; top-level eth_call from an EOA and from the PoolManager address both returned "EVM error: PrecompileError". CELO.transfer(PoolManager, 10^6) by the driver raised balanceOf(PoolManager) and the native balance by exactly 10^6 and settle credited exactly 10^6 to the driver, which is its own money. CELO.transferFrom(X, PoolManager, 1) without allowance reverted ("transfer value exceeded balance of sender"). The CELO token moves value through 0xfd with msg.sender as from or with an allowance (GoldToken.sol lines 152-162 and 248-253), so the only CELO that a third party pays into the PoolManager inside the attacker's transaction is CELO that third party's own contract sends to a recipient the attacker can name, which is the relay pattern of F-137. take(CELO, PoolManager, x) left the balance unchanged and debited the driver by x. forno answered reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb before the eth_call pair and Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 after it, so the endpoint is load balanced across two clients; both agreed on the precompile refusal. eth_simulateV1 is not served by forno (HTTP 403, "rpc method is not whitelisted"). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/inflows.json; research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/extra.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/main/crates/celo-revm/src/precompiles/transfer.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-monorepo/master/packages/protocol/contracts/common/GoldToken.sol
- Celo, cycle 37. Celo system contracts that push CELO: CeloUnreleasedTreasury releases during epoch processing, which any account can start, and validator payments. Result: CeloUnreleasedTreasury.release is onlyEpochManager (CeloUnreleasedTreasury.sol lines 34-37 and 62-70). EpochManager sends the released CELO to the Reserve, to Governance and to the carbon offsetting partner read from the registry and EpochRewards (EpochManager.sol lines 703-706 and 744-751); validator, group and delegatee payments are in the stable token (lines 406-414). startNextEpochProcess is external without a role (line 206), so an attacker can run it inside its own unlock, but no recipient is attacker chosen and none is the PoolManager unless governance sets it, which F-023 already covers on the governance side. Fee currency debits and refunds act on the transaction sender only (cycle 35 row 7). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-monorepo/release/core-contracts/12/packages/protocol/contracts-0.8/common/EpochManager.sol; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-monorepo/release/core-contracts/12/packages/protocol/contracts-0.8/common/CeloUnreleasedTreasury.sol
- Polygon, cycle 37. Polygon row: a native transfer to the PoolManager seen through 0x1010, 0x1010.transfer to the PoolManager with and without value between sync(0x1010) and settle, Bor transfer logs, burn contract and coinbase credits. Result: 0x1010.transfer(PoolManager, 10^6) with value 10^6 reverted (MRC20._transfer calls address.transfer into the PoolManager, which has no receive, MRC20.sol line 107). With value 0 it returned false without moving anything (MRC20.sol lines 92-95). Face balance unchanged, settle returned 0, delta 0. take(0x1010, PoolManager, x) reverted with WrappedError(0x1010, transfer, false), as F-008 records. Bor's Transfer only adds a LogTransfer record after the same SubBalance and AddBalance (bor core/evm.go lines 252-275); it does not move value. The base fee credit to the burnt contract and the tip credit to the coinbase run after execution, to addresses from chain config and the block header (bor core/state_transition.go lines 645-668). State sync deposits of POL reach MRC20.deposit, which uses address.transfer (MRC20.sol line 44), so a deposit or a StateReceiver replay naming the PoolManager reverts. The only intra-transaction native inflow left is SELFDESTRUCT, paid by whoever owns the destructing contract (cycle 35 row 3). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/inflows.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maticnetwork/contracts/main/contracts/child/MRC20.sol; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maticnetwork/bor/develop/core/evm.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maticnetwork/bor/develop/core/state_transition.go
- Arc, cycle 37. Arc row: native value call, face transfers of 0 and 1 unit, forced inflows of 1 wei and of one wei short of the next unit, face take naming the PoolManager, and the Native Coin Authority 0x1800...0000 called directly, all between sync(0x3600...) and settle. Result: Native CALL to the PoolManager with value 10^12 wei: ok=0. face.transfer(PoolManager, 0) returned true and moved nothing. face.transfer(PoolManager, 1) raised the face by 1 and the native balance by exactly 10^12 wei. A forced inflow of 1 wei after that left the face unchanged. settle credited 1 face unit, native delta 0. In a second bracket a forced inflow of 10^12 - r - 1 wei, where r is the PoolManager's native remainder modulo 10^12 at the pinned block, left the face unchanged and settle credited 0, so the sub-unit wei stays as surplus that nobody can claim. take(face, PoolManager, 1) succeeded, left both balances unchanged and debited the driver by 1 (block 33,489,946). Native Coin Authority transfer, mint and burn from the driver reverted with "Not enabled for native coin transfers", "Not enabled native coin minter" and "Not enabled native coin burner". The remainder bracket that crosses a face unit was settled by cycle 35 row 4 (unprofitable, at most 10^12 wei per round against at least 1.5 x 10^14 wei of gas). Circle's CCTP mint to the PoolManager is F-137. Arc does not serve eth_simulateV1. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/inflows.json; research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/extra.json; https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/evm-differences.md; https://docs.arc.io/arc/concepts/execution-layer.md
- Optimism, Zora, cycle 37. OP Mainnet and Zora rows: fee vault recipients and withdrawal networks, deposit transactions with value, the transient state across transactions in one simulated block. Result: SequencerFeeVault, BaseFeeVault and L1FeeVault withdraw to L1 (withdrawal network 0) at recipient 0xa3d596eafab6b13ab18d40fae1a962700c84adea on OP Mainnet and 0xe900b3edc1ba0430cfa9a204a1027b90825ac951 on Zora; OperatorFeeVault withdraws on L2 to BaseFeeVault 0x4200...0019. None names the PoolManager, and a vault withdraw to it would end in a value call that it rejects. eth_simulateV1 with a call typed 0x7e and a mint field was run as an ordinary call and failed with "insufficient funds for gas * price + value: have 0 want 1000000" on both, so the deposit shape cannot be simulated there; the row rests on the deposit specification (a deposit is its own transaction and mints to its from account, cycle 35 row 8). eth_simulateV1 with sync(LegacyERC20ETH) in one transaction and exttload of the synced currency and reserves slots in the next returned zero in both slots on OP Mainnet, Zora and Polygon, so a sync never survives to a later transaction of the same block and no arrival between transactions can be credited. Withdrawal finalisation of the OP Stack runs on L1 and moves no L2 value to the L2 PoolManager. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/extra.json; research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/inflows.json; https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/deposits.html
- Celo, Polygon, Arc, Optimism, Zora, cycle 37. Task 2 table: who pays, who triggers, whether the recipient is free, and whether the arrival can run inside one transaction between an attacker's sync(face) and settle. Result: SELFDESTRUCT (EIP-6780 keeps the balance transfer): payer is the owner of the destructing contract, any account triggers its own, recipient free, intra-transaction yes, credit equals the payer's own value (cycle 35 row 3). Face token transfer on Celo and Arc: payer is the token holder, recipient free, intra-transaction yes, credited once and exactly to the settler; a third party's funds arrive this way only through a contract that pays a recipient the attacker can name, which for bridge relays is F-137 and otherwise is that contract's own fault. Value CALL, native take, MRC20 deposit, StandardBridge ETH finalisation, fee vault withdraw: every one reverts at the PoolManager (row N1). Relay messages that call settle or settleFor with value: credited to the messenger or the named recipient, never to the executor. Coinbase, base fee, burn contract and priority fee credits on all five: post execution, recipients from the header or chain config, not attacker chosen. OP Stack deposits with value and Celo custom gas deposits: separate transaction. Polygon state sync: system call at sprint start, and its replay ends in address.transfer into the PoolManager, which reverts. Block rewards and staking payouts: none paid on these L2s; Polygon validator rewards are on Ethereum; Celo epoch payouts go to governance registered addresses. Celo transfer precompile and Arc Native Coin Authority: refuse any caller other than the CELO token or an enabled minter. Open relays that deliver face value to a recipient named in the message: CCTP receiveMessage with destinationCaller zero on Arc (native USDC through the face) and on OP Mainnet and Polygon for USDC, which is not a native face there; OP Stack relayMessage replays on OP Mainnet, Zora and Celo; Polygon StateReceiver replays. All are recorded in F-137. Evidence: research/network-risk/state/findings.json (F-137, F-071); research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/inflows.json; src/PoolManager.sol:349-364
- Celo, Polygon, Arc, Optimism, Zora, cycle 37. Task 4, value leaving the PoolManager without take while a face is synced: system debits, fees charged to the contract, clawbacks, Arc blocklist enforcement. Result: The PoolManager has code and no key, so it is never a transaction sender or a fee payer, and EIP-7702 cannot delegate it. Native leaves it only through Currency.transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40-53), reached from take and collectProtocolFees. The Celo transfer precompile and the Arc Native Coin Authority refused every non-system caller (rows above). The remaining debits need a privileged party and are recorded: Celo governance moving CELO through the token proxy and 0xfd (F-023), Circle blocklisting the PoolManager on Arc (F-108), Polygon BlockAlloc code writes (F-134). A debit placed by another account between a victim's sync and settle needs a call inside the victim's transaction; in a shared transaction the earlier party can only act before the victim's own sync, which overwrites both slots (src/PoolManager.sol:285-286), and the case of a victim that settles without its own sync is F-071. No path was found by which an ordinary account makes another account's settle underflow at src/PoolManager.sol:360. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:40-53; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288; src/PoolManager.sol:357-360; research/network-risk/state/findings.json (F-023, F-108, F-134, F-071)
- all 21 networks, cycle 37. Legacy ETH token address 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000 on all 21 networks: code, balanceOf(PoolManager) and PoolManager.sync on it. Result: Code (3,671 bytes) only on OP Mainnet and Zora, where balanceOf(PoolManager) equals the native balance and sync succeeds. On the other 19 networks the address has no code and eth_call of sync(legacy) reverts, because balanceOfSelf makes a high level call to an account without code (src/types/Currency.sol:94). The plan expected six such networks; the count of OP Stack networks without the code is eight (Base, Unichain, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, MegaETH, Celo, X Layer), and the other eleven are not OP Stack. A pool using the legacy address there cannot even be synced, so this theme has no target on them. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/out/legacy.json; research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-native-face-inflows.work/scripts/legacy.py; src/types/Currency.sol:90-96
- Ethereum, Base, Unichain, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, HyperEVM, cycle 37. Does the native face theme apply to the 16 networks without an ERC-20 face of the native asset?. Result: No. On these networks no token returns the PoolManager's native balance from balanceOf (cycle 35 row 3 and row 11 tested the protocol tokens on each), and native settlement reads only msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354), so a native arrival without a call to settle is never credited to anyone. It becomes surplus that no caller can claim. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-364; research/network-risk/cycles/035/theme-sync-settle-credit-table.research.json

- BNB Smart Chain, X Layer, Celo, MegaETH, cycle 37. L-1314. What ruint PR 603 changed, read from CHANGELOG.md and src/bits.rs at v1.18.0, v1.19.0 and v1.20.0, and whether the revm-interpreter 35.0.1, 37.0.3 and 43.0.2 handlers for SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE bound the count or index before calling ruint. Result: The 1.20.0 changelog lists #603 as a fix of overflow-flag false negatives in overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr, with the dependent checked, strict and saturating shifts and byte(). The bits.rs diff from 1.19.0 to 1.20.0 shows three changes. (1) overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr now OR the limbs that are shifted out entirely, and for shl the masked top bits, into the carry; the shifted value itself is unchanged. 1.18.0 and 1.19.0 both have the narrower carry. (2) The u64, u128 and u256 fast paths of wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr cast the count with rhs as u32, which in 1.19.0 turns a count of 2^32 + k into k; 1.20.0 replaces it with shift_amount, which saturates at u32::MAX. These fast paths came with #574 in 1.19.0. In 1.18.0 wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr are overflowing_shl(rhs).0 and overflowing_shr(rhs).0, which return zero once rhs / 64 >= LIMBS, so 1.18.0 has no truncating cast. (3) byte() gains a bounds assert on the big-endian path only. Both earlier readings were therefore partly right: the cast exists in 1.19.0 (MegaETH) and not in 1.18.0 (reth-bsc, X Layer, Celo reth), and the flag fix touches both. None of it reaches an EVM word. In revm-interpreter 35.0.1, 37.0.3 and 43.0.2 the shl and shr handlers compute shift = as_usize_saturated!(op1) and call op2 << shift or op2 >> shift only when shift < 256, else return 0; sar calls arithmetic_shr only when shift < 256, else returns all ones or 0 by the sign bit; byte calls op2.byte(31 - o1) only when o1 < 32. The handlers use the wrapping value and never the overflow flag. On the src/ side every shift count is a constant or a value below 256 (BitMath.sol:15-22 and 40-45, TickMath.sol:142-145) and every BYTE index is masked with 0x1f (BitMath.sol:21, 45), so no line of src/ can produce a count of 2^32 or more. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/v1.20.0/CHANGELOG.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/v1.19.0/src/bits.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/v1.18.0/src/bits.rs; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-35.0.1.crate (src/instructions/bitwise.rs:96-143, macros.rs:185-189); revm-interpreter-37.0.3 and 43.0.2 bitwise.rs:107-158; src/libraries/BitMath.sol:15-22

## Reading of the source (theme-arc-subcall-rollback)

- Arc, cycle 38. Task 1: the subcall life cycle as written in arc-node crates/evm/src/evm.rs at v0.8.6 (sha256 1ce0d1e6...bb45, byte identical to v0.8.5) and on main (sha256 e7e6d819...a704e), with crates/precompiles/src/call_from.rs and crates/evm/src/subcall.rs at v0.8.6. Result: frame_init (evm.rs 667-705) refuses a caller outside the allowed set before anything else. init_subcall (897-1109) refuses a non-CALL scheme (911-916), a static context with all gas spent (922-926) and any value (932-937), decodes callFrom (call_from.rs decode_child_call: decode gas 100 plus 3 per word, child value fixed at zero), refuses a sender that is neither the caller nor tx.origin (961-968), loads the sender and the target (and a 7702 delegate) and charges 2600 or 100 for each, all before the checkpoint so that warm entries persist (981-1042). It then takes a journal checkpoint and commits it at once (1052-1053): commit only lowers the depth counter (revm-context 16.0.1 inner.rs 589-591), so the saved index pair (log_i, journal_i, selfdestructed_i) stays valid and later journal entries stay in the one linear journal. The child gets depth+1 and 63/64 of what is left (1063-1072). The continuation (subcall.rs: precompile, gas_limit, init overhead, return range, opaque data, checkpoint) is stored under the precompile call's depth (1081-1091), or completion runs at once for an immediate child such as CallTooDeep or an empty target (1096-1106). complete_subcall (1127-1238) has these exits: child returned and completion fits, a Return to the caller with the child's refund; child reverted or halted, no journal call because the child's own frame already reverted (revm-handler 18.1.0 frame.rs 418-420) and the precompile returns success with (false, data), the halt costing the whole limit; completion out of gas (1185-1197), all gas spent and revert_subcall_checkpoint when the child succeeded; completion error or rejection (1215-1236), unreachable for CallFrom because its complete_subcall always returns success true and only errs on a create result (call_from.rs). Return data has no size cap; its encode gas is 100 plus 3 per word. revert_subcall_checkpoint (1249-1258) takes a dummy checkpoint to raise the depth and calls checkpoint_revert(saved), which lowers it again, truncates logs and the selfdestruct list to the saved lengths and undoes every journal entry after journal_i newest first (inner.rs 595-613). On main the same calls are made in the same order (main evm.rs 1039-1040 and 1228-1237); only argument passing and the ABI decoder changed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/v0.8.6/crates/evm/src/evm.rs

- Arc, cycle 38. L-1338: the continuation map keyed by depth, with a child that makes its own CallFrom, a CallTooDeep child and an inspector. Result: The continuation is stored at the precompile call's depth p and taken only when a frame that ran to completion finishes at depth p+1 (evm.rs 756-758, 1114-1117). The child runs at p+1 and no other frame can sit at p+1 until it ends, because the precompile itself pushes no frame at p and every frame the child starts is at p+2 or deeper; a nested CallFrom from the child stores its continuation at p+3. An immediate child (CallTooDeep, empty code) never stores one: completion runs at once, and frame_return_result skips the lookup for results that did not come from a finished frame (746-756). Under an inspector, inspect_frame_run takes the continuation and completes it before frame_end (around evm.rs 1410-1428), so frame_return_result finds none. The model's depth chains and its sibling-key fault exercise these cases. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/v0.8.6/crates/evm/src/evm.rs (lines 729-785, 1111-1117)

Result: Every one of these writes is a journal entry (transient words, token storage, native balance move), so a revert to the saved checkpoint undoes the debit, the payout, the swap's slots, the ERC-6909 mint, the sync words and the lock together, and a commit keeps them together. Because the release is built with a PGO profile, the bodies of ADD, MUL, SUB, DIV, MULMOD, SIGNEXTEND, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO, AND, OR, NOT, SHL, SHR, SAR, the PUSH and DUP and SWAP cases, JUMP and JUMPI are inlined into that one function and are different machine code from the out-of-line op functions; MUL, DIV, MULMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SLT, SGT, SHL, SHR and SAR still call holiman/uint256 routines, and validJumpdest is called. SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, EXP, BYTE and the rest go through the per-fork table to the out-of-line handlers. ## Reading of the source (theme-frame-checkpoint-and-commit-lift)

- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arc, cycle 38. Static census of every inlined journal checkpoint in eight shipped reth-derived binaries (op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and v2.8.1, Base v1.5.6, world-chain v2.8.2, conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, celo-reth v1.0.10, xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1, arc-execution v0.8.6): every place that raises the depth word J+0x118 and saves the three journal lengths, found by byte pattern and read in objdump text (scan.py, classify.py). Result: Accepted sites: celo 21 of 22, op-reth v2.10 56 of 60, op-reth v2.8.1 50 of 52, Base 229 of 234, World Chain 48 of 49, Zora 48 of 49, X Layer 18 of 18, Arc 25 of 40. Each accepted site loads logs J+0x10, journal J+0x28 and the third list J+0x40 from the same journal base as the out-of-line copy, stores them as one record in that order and raises the depth by exactly one, and every revert call after it in the same function passes that record. The sites not accepted were read by hand: op-reth make_call_frame 0x456e2d5 reloads the host pointer from [rsp+0x8] for each load and stores the record at rsp+0x238, which the revert at 0x456f364 receives; the 15 Arc sites in 0x295e140 and its copies keep journal_i in a register and copy the record to rsp+0x310 before the revert at 0x295eb06, in the right order; the rest have another depth offset and are not journal code. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/038/theme-frame-checkpoint-and-commit-lift.work/out/cls-celo1010.json and cls-*.json; scripts/scan.py, scripts/classify.py

- all 21 networks, cycle 38. What a transient leak across transactions would hand the next transaction, read in src/. Result: unlock sets the flag, calls back, requires NonzeroDeltaCount to be zero and clears the flag before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, Lock.sol:10-21). A successful transaction therefore ends with the flag false and the count zero, and a reverted one is undone by the journal. Only the synced currency and reserves (CurrencyReserves.sol) can be left set by a successful transaction, which is the A1 case earlier cycles closed. No path between two transactions was found that skips the clear. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114

## Reading of the source (theme-tempo-credit-region-lift)

- Tempo, cycle 38. Task 1 (L-1318). The TIP-1060 storage credit region of the v1.19.2 x86_64 SSTORE handler (0x42b46b8 to the exit 0x42b5095, with the out-of-line blocks 0x42b50f1 to 0x42b5175), run from its disassembly in the cycle 28/29 x86-64 model, followed by the dynamic gas, the EIP-8037 block and the refund routine 0x2d26f80. The PoolManager write and its journal entries came first from the handler's own segments 0x42b44c4 to 0x42b46b8. The transient credit state calls 0x1e8fd10 (tload) and 0x1e8feb0 (tstore) ran from the binary on real transient tables, the SstoreTransitionFlags block 0x4b632b9 to 0x4b633e7 of the outlined host sstore ran from the binary, and the credit slot reads and writes went through the handler's own warm, write and StorageChange segments. Cases: PoolManager slot shapes (slot0, liquidity, a tick word, fee growth, a position word, protocolFeesAccrued, an ERC-6909 balance), original zero or not, present and new each zero, equal to the original or another value, warm and cold PoolManager and credit slots, gas at, one below and one above every check, credit words 0, 1, 2, 20, 2^64-2, 2^64-1, 2^64, 2^64+5 and 2^256-1, transient credit words in Refund, Preserve and Direct mode with budgets 0, 1, 5 and 2^64-1 and invalid mode bytes 3 and 255, pre-T7 spec, EIP-2200 off, the credit precompile itself as owner, and injected database errors on the credit load and the credit write. Seed 2026112838, 71,328 cases, and seed 2026112839, 6,133 cases with a Preserve word that carries a budget. Result: No input makes the handler write a different PoolManager word, change the original word, skip or add a journal entry, or succeed or fail where accounting.rs, instructions.rs and gas_params.rs at the pinned revisions say otherwise. 0 mismatches in 77,461 cases on stored word, original word, return code (44,153 normal returns, 20,843 OutOfGas halts and 6,332 fatal returns through state.fail in the main run), gas left, refund, persistent credit word, transient credit word and the ordered journal tags (StorageWarmed 5, StorageChange 3, transient 4). The binary tests occupancy on present against new (0x42b479d to 0x42b4803), skips the precompile's own address (0x42b4809), charges the warm read before the credit load and the cold surcharge after it with skip_cold taken on the gas left after the warm charge, refuses a credit word of 2^64 or more as fatal, adds one with saturation on a clear (0x42b4b71 to 0x42b4b7b), takes the mode from the low byte of limb 0 and refuses modes above 2, charges 245,000 gas (0x3bd08) in Refund and Preserve mode, decrements credit and budget in Direct mode and leaves an unlimited budget alone, writes the transient word as [mode, budget, 0, pending], and charges the clean update cost only when the credit write changes a clean slot. - Tempo, cycle 38. Who gains from credits the PoolManager accrues. Every clear of a PoolManager slot by any caller (a burned ERC-6909 balance, a cleared tick, a closed position, collected protocol fees) mints one persistent credit to the storage-owning account, the PoolManager. In the default Refund mode each later creation of a PoolManager slot pays 245,000 gas and records a pending refund, which settle_storage_credit_refunds pays back at the end of a successful transaction by spending the PoolManager's credits. Result: This moves gas cost between users of the PoolManager and never moves funds. A user who creates a slot is refunded from credits that earlier users minted, and an account that drains the credits only makes later creators pay the full creation price, which is the price without credits. The refund goes to the transaction's gas accounting (result.gas.record_refund, config.rs:483-485) and touches no PoolManager slot or token balance. The mode word belongs to the account that calls the precompile (set_mode and set_budget take msg_sender, storage_credits/mod.rs), so no other account can switch the PoolManager to Direct mode. Information only. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/c0c9372/crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/c0c9372/crates/precompiles/src/storage_credits/mod.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/c0c9372/crates/precompiles/src/storage_credits/accounting.rs

Proofs older than the node's proof window are refused (code 4444), so the history before the window rests on source. apply_pre_execution_changes rejects any block with withdrawals and makes only the EIP-2935 history system call and the committee call (crates/evm/src/block.rs:815-866 and 554-591), and the test at block.rs:1507-1557 shows the Ethereum block reward and DAO paths apply only before T13 and only on a chain spec without Paris. - Tempo, cycle 38. Task 4 (L-1337). Do pools with address(0) as a currency exist on the Tempo PoolManager 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029, and what could a position in one do. eth_getLogs over blocks 0 to 51,157,365 in ranges of at most 31,250 blocks (the endpoint caps a query at 100,000) for Initialize logs, all of them and those with topic2 (currency0) equal to zero. Result: The PoolManager has 168 Initialize logs and none has currency0 = address(0); since currency0 < currency1, no pool on Tempo uses the native currency. If one were created, its native side could never be paid in: settle credits msg.value, which is always 0 on Tempo (src/PoolManager.sol:349-354), and a native take needs a value call the PoolManager cannot fund (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). A position in range would need native that nobody can deliver. A one-sided ERC-20 position outside the range can be added and removed. A swap that pays ERC-20 for native output leaves the swapper with a native credit it can only clear or mint as claim id 0, which no take can redeem; such claims could be burned to pay the native leg in another address(0) pool, so ERC-20 sitting in such pools could be bought only with native claims that someone first bought with ERC-20. No value appears from nothing, and no such pool exists today. ## Reading of the source (theme-never-run-sites-shared-balance)

- MegaETH, HyperEVM, Monad, cycle 39. Site A, the exact-input fee mulDiv (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:64-65, PoolManager pcs 22445 and 22513), never run with a product of 2^256 or more by the MegaETH and HyperEVM producers inside the PoolManager. Entry condition, cost, whether the call completes, and every place the word goes. Result: Entry: amountSpecified < 0 and |amountRemaining| * (1e6 - fee) >= 2^256, that is |amountRemaining| >= 2^236.068 at fee 0 and 2^236.073 at fee 3000 (python3). Hooks.beforeSwap returns amountSpecified unchanged for a hookless pool (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:252-253) and nothing bounds its size before Pool.swap. Any account reaches it in any existing pool with liquidity: the step aims at the next tick or the price limit, the amount consumed is only amountIn + feeAmount of the steps up to the limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:379), and the settled amount (params.amountSpecified - amountSpecifiedRemaining) passes the cast at Pool.sol:452-460. Cost: the tokens of an ordinary swap of a few ticks plus swap gas. The word amountRemainingLessFee is used in three places only: the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69, and in the else branch as amountIn (:77) and as the input of getNextSqrtPriceFromInput (:78-80). A wrong word that is still >= amountIn changes nothing, because the target branch takes amountIn and feeAmount from getAmount0Delta or getAmount1Delta and mulDivRoundingUp (:66-74). A wrong word below amountIn sends the step into the else branch, where feeAmount = |amountRemaining| - amountIn (:82), so the step consumes the whole remaining amount, amountSpecifiedRemaining becomes 0 at Pool.sol:379 and (amountSpecified - 0).toInt128() at Pool.sol:455 or :459 reverts because |amountSpecified| >= 2^236. When the correct word is below amountIn (exhaust branch with a wide amount, which already reverts at the same cast), a wrong word above amountIn makes the step reach its target with the amountIn and fee that the price move costs (:69-74), which is the honest price for that move. No wrong word at this site raises amountOut, feeGrowthGlobal (Pool.sol:404-405, :446) or a delta the caller may take. Every wrong word ends in no change or in a revert. Evidence: src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:64-82
- MegaETH, HyperEVM, Monad, cycle 39. Site C, the Position fee copy of mulDiv (src/libraries/Position.sol:93-96, pcs 22316 and 22378), never run wide by the MegaETH and HyperEVM producers inside the PoolManager. Result: Entry: (feeGrowthInsideX128 - feeGrowthInsideLastX128) * liquidity >= 2^256, which is the same as fees owed of 2^128 units or more in one currency, since the result is the product divided by 2^128. Fee growth only rises by fees and donations actually paid in: UnsafeMath.simpleMulDiv(feeAmount, Q128, liquidity) per swap step (src/libraries/Pool.sol:404-405) and simpleMulDiv(amount, Q128, liquidity) per donate (Pool.sol:473-478), and a position earns at most its share of them, so the operand needs 2^128 or more units of one currency paid as fees through one position. That is 3.4e38 base units; whether any asset other pools hold has such a supply was not checked (token sweep out of focus), and a token the account mints itself gets there. The conclusion below does not depend on which token it is. With the correct word the call always reverts, because feesOwed >= 2^128 fails feesOwed.toInt128() at Pool.sol:192. A wrong word above 2^127 reverts at the same cast. A wrong word below 2^127 credits that many units through feeDelta (Pool.sol:192) and callerDelta (src/PoolManager.sol:171, :183), but in the currency in which the account itself paid at least 2^128 units of fees, so the credit is smaller than what that pool received in that currency. The other currency has its own mulDiv with its own narrow operands (Position.sol:95-96). Every wrong word ends in a revert or in a loss for the caller. Evidence: src/libraries/Position.sol:91-101
- MegaETH, HyperEVM, Monad, cycle 39. Site D, the copies for an amount above uint160 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97, pcs 22721 and 22763, and :105, pc 20958), never run by either closed producer. Result: getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown takes the mulDiv path only when amount > 2^160-1 (SqrtPriceMath.sol:95-97 and :103-105). It is called from getNextSqrtPriceFromInput in the exhaust branch of an exact-input step (SwapMath.sol:77-80), where the step then consumes the whole remaining amount (:82), and from getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput in the capped branch of an exact-output step (SwapMath.sol:96-98), where amountOut = amountRemaining and the step uses the whole remaining output. In both cases amountSpecifiedRemaining becomes 0 (Pool.sol:373 or :379) and the cast of amountSpecified - 0, more than 2^160 in size, reverts at Pool.sol:455 or :459. A wrong price word cannot avoid that cast, so every wrong word at these sites ends in a revert. Evidence: src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:93-119
- MegaETH, HyperEVM, Monad, cycle 39. SqrtPriceMath.sol:52, the fallback divRoundingUp of the amount0 add path (pcs 23924 and 23928), which the censuses of cycles 33 and 37 show never executed on MegaETH or HyperEVM. Result: The fallback runs when amount * sqrtPX96 overflows or numerator1 + product overflows (SqrtPriceMath.sol:42-49), in the exhaust branch of an exact-input zeroForOne step. The exhaust branch needs amountIn to the target above amountRemainingLessFee, about L*2^96/target > 2^256/sqrtP, so with L <= 2^128 the step must span a sqrt price ratio of 2^32 or more, and the remaining amount must stay below 2^127 for the cast at Pool.sol:459, which forces sqrtP >= 2^129. The range then holds at least about 2^96 units of currency1 and the input is at least 2^127 units of currency0. Neither is payable in an asset others hold, so the account must use its own tokens on both sides, and a wrong next price there moves only the account's own tokens. Recorded as caller-only. Evidence: src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-52
- MegaETH, HyperEVM, Monad, cycle 39. Fee growth update in the swap loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:400-407) uses UnsafeMath.simpleMulDiv without overflow check; can feeAmount * 2^128 wrap in a swap that completes?. Result: No. In every completing swap the settled input amountSpecified - amountSpecifiedRemaining passes toInt128 (Pool.sol:452-460), and each step adds amountIn + feeAmount to it (Pool.sol:379, or :375 for exact output), so feeAmount < 2^127 and feeAmount * 2^128 < 2^255. Larger fees only arise in steps that consume the whole remaining amount, and those swaps revert at the cast. The same bound holds for donate (Pool.sol:471-478), where amount0 and amount1 pass toInt128 first. The swap copy runs on both closed producers (pc 20231: 120,548 runs on MegaETH, 2,710 on HyperEVM, cycle 33 out/pm-sites.json). Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:400-407

- Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM, Arc, cycle 39. Task 5 for the closed or unsimulated producers: which still have no mined proof that transient storage is cleared between transactions, and what a missing clear would expose. Result: None of the four has a mined pair. The reason is the code, not the sample: the only transient words of the PoolManager that a successful transaction can leave set are the synced currency and reserves (unlock relocks at src/PoolManager.sol:113 and requires the delta count at zero at line 112). Routers sync immediately before settling, so a successful transaction that ends with an ERC-20 sync open needs an account that calls sync(X) and stops (P3, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). No account did so in 4,375 traced Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM blocks here plus 4,000 in cycle 33. The mined pair can only come from such a call, which this review may not send. Per cycle 34, a leaked sync would make a later native settle revert (src/PoolManager.sol:356) or credit the next settler with the rise of X's balance (lines 357-361), so the hazard is a freeze of one settle or a gift to the next settler, not a path for the leaving account. The producers of Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM and Arc stay covered by source and replica evidence only. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-288
- Polygon, cycle 39. Task 2 (L-1358): key kinds of bor's multi-version stores and whether transient storage, logs, the access list or the refund counter are among them; read in v2.11.2, v2.11.1 and develop (core/blockstm/mvhashmap.go, mvstore.go, mvbalance_store.go, v2_executor.go, core/state/parallel_statedb*.go; the files are byte-identical across the three revisions except core/parallel_state_processor.go and core/vm/instructions.go in develop). Result: The block import path (core/blockchain.go:969-975, NewV2StateProcessor) runs V2: blockstm.MVStore keyed by a 54-byte Key of address, slot hash, subpath byte and type byte (mvhashmap.go:82-150). FlushToMVStore writes exactly five kinds: NoncePath, storage slots (NewStateKey), CodePath, CreatePath and SuicidePath (parallel_statedb.go:495-524); balances go to MVBalanceStore as per-address add and sub deltas (flushBalanceDeltas). Transient storage, logs, the access list, the refund counter and preimages are plain fields of the ParallelStateDB (parallel_statedb.go:111-118), cleared by Reset at the start of every incarnation (lines 256-281) and again by Prepare (lines 1277-1279), and SettleTo copies only nonces, storage, code, balances, logs and the account set into the final StateDB (parallel_statedb_settle.go:16-33). GetTransientState and SetTransientState touch only the local map and the journal (lines 1139-1150). The older MVHashMap (V1) holds address, state and subpath keys (Balance, Nonce, Code, Suicide; statedb.go:1036-1044) and its own comment calls V1 test-only (mvhashmap.go:429). Neither store has a transient key kind. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/state/parallel_statedb.go
- Polygon, cycle 39. Task 2 (L-1358): one execution of a transaction by a V2 worker: where writes are buffered, when they are flushed, what an inner revert, an aborted incarnation and an invalidated reader do. Result: SetState writes localStorage and only records the key (parallel_statedb.go:1040-1065, whose comment says storage writes are always deferred). The executor calls Execute with deferWrites true and FlushToMVStore only after the whole message has run (v2_executor.go:426-455, line 447), so no other worker can see a value from inside a running frame. An inner revert undoes journal entries before the flush: revertStorage restores or deletes the localStorage entry (parallel_statedb_journal.go:73-78) and jkTransient restores the local transient map (line 56), so a reverted write is not in the flushed set. A transaction that panicked is never flushed (line 496-498). On a validation failure dispatchReexec marks the old incarnation's keys ESTIMATE, re-executes into a freshly Reset state, and CleanupEstimate deletes the entries the new incarnation did not rewrite (v2_executor.go:571-612, mvstore.go:137-169). A reader that meets an ESTIMATE falls back to the base state in incarnation 0 and waits for the writer's final version later (parallel_statedb.go:332-393); every store read is recorded and Validate rejects it unless the writer and incarnation match or the value is equal (parallel_statedb_validate.go:115-133), and the failed reader is re-executed. A wrong parallel result cannot be kept: ProcessBlock checks it against the header and falls back to the serial result (blockchain.go:1308-1420), and the block producer runs transactions one by one through core.ApplyTransaction (miner/worker.go:1713). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/blockstm/v2_executor.go
- Polygon, cycle 39. Task 2 from the shipped bor v2.11.2 amd64 binary (cycle 31 download, GitCommit a4afe5a9, sha256 prefix 6d85c1aea6d89c06): the ParallelStateDB storage path run in the cycle 32/33 x86-64 model with blockstm.(*MVStore).ReadVersionFull answering from a preloaded table (scripts/stmv.py, seed 39_1358_01): another transaction's committed value, an ESTIMATE marker with a stale value, and a committed value that is replaced after its first read. Static check of the transient path in the same binary (out/objdump-calls.txt, out/objdump-transient.txt, out/objdump-FlushToMVStore.txt). Result: 5000 sequences, 135232 SLOADs, 48973 SSTOREs, 6668 reverts, 256887 store reads (61712 committed, 36814 estimate, 14072 changing), 165632 GetCommittedState checks, 623505 write-set checks, 11171 reads of a changed entry: 0 mismatches, 0 errors. Committed values are read as the pre-state, ESTIMATE entries fall through to the base word, a changed entry is read afresh on each SLOAD of an unwritten slot (no SLOAD result cache in front of the store), and the local write set that FlushToMVStore publishes never holds a reverted write. Two planted faults are caught: a stale committed value (200 of 200 sequences) and an ESTIMATE handed back as committed (194 of 200). In the binary, (*ParallelStateDB).GetTransientState and SetTransientState call only runtime map functions and appendJournal and contain no reference to core/blockstm, opTload makes one indirect call to the StateDB interface, and FlushToMVStore calls MVStore.WriteInc at exactly five sites plus flushBalanceDeltas, matching the source. A transient word cannot be read from the store because no code path puts one there or reads one from it. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/039/theme-transient-across-transactions-and-workers.work/out/stmv-5000.json

Result: None. opSload and opTload in all four call StateDB.GetState and GetTransientState directly (bor core/vm/instructions.go:577-584 at v2.11.2, 616-623 at develop, core/vm/eips.go:218-226 in both; bsc instructions.go:514-520 and eips.go:201-207; libevm instructions.go:514-520 and eips.go:197-203). Behind them are the standard layers: dirtyStorage (journaled), pendingStorage (earlier transactions of the block) and originStorage (database) in bsc and libevm (state_object.go GetState and GetCommittedState), and in bor's V2 worker localStorage (journaled), the MVStore and the base state, plus committedCache for the original value only, which is fixed for a transaction and whose source read is validated. The interpreter structs of bor (v2.11.2 and develop), bsc and libevm hold no storage cache; bor develop adds a keccak result cache and a MULMOD memo, not a storage cache. The binaries agree: opSload and opTload of bor v2.11.2, bsc v1.8.2 and avalanchego v1.15.3 make only the StateDB interface call (plus libevm's Contract.Address call) and uint256 SetBytes (out/objdump-calls.txt, out/objdump-bsc-avax.txt). With no cache, the cycle 36 reentry sequences have nothing to run against. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/vm/eips.go
- Polygon, cycle 39. Task 4: Polygon mined blocks in which two senders call the PoolManager and at least one PoolManager transaction reverts or has a failed frame under unlock, against a serial re-execution (debug_traceBlockByNumber callTracer and prestateTracer diffMode at polygon.drpc.org, receipts and logs from polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com, committed words by eth_getStorageAt; scripts/syncpairs.py, scripts/poststate.py). Result: 600 blocks with PoolManager logs (98088298 to 98090900), 44066 transactions, 989 PoolManager transactions, 135 blocks with two or more, 53 blocks that meet the condition. Status, gas used and logs of every PoolManager receipt equal the traced serial execution; the 202 reverted transactions carry one receipt log more than their frames, the LogFeeTransfer event of 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 that bor adds to every receipt (out/polygon-reverted-log-check.txt). For the 53 blocks, all 384 PoolManager storage words written by the serial re-execution equal the committed state at the block (0 differences). 70 times a failed unlock is followed in its block by a successful one. The receipts endpoint reported bor v2.11.1-private builds f2a2d63e69f6 and cb3d19c5f690 (host names) and the trace endpoint Geth/v10.0.0/drpc, whose backend is not named. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/039/theme-transient-across-transactions-and-workers.work/out/poststate-137.json
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Tempo, cycle 39. Whether this theme (producers without block simulation, and a parallel executor that could share transient or reverted words between transactions) applies to the other sixteen networks. Result: It does not. Their producers are open clients whose transient clear between transactions was tested by eth_simulateV1 at the real PoolManager address in an earlier cycle (fifteen of them; OPCODES.md 'Reading from the source' row), and none commits a transaction from a parallel or speculative run without running it again (OPCODES.md 'Speculative execution' row: reth's reuse path is off by default, BNB Chain discards its prefetch runs). Avalanche has no eth_simulateV1, but its C-Chain runs libevm serially and its transient storage and journal revert ran from the v1.15.3 binary in cycle 32. Evidence: research/network-risk/OPCODES.md:537
